title: Saudi Aramco tells staff to evacuate Dhahran as clashes with Yemen's Houthis continue
body: Saudi state oil company Aramco 2223.SE has told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf, six people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Thursday, as fighting between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensifies.Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognized government have raged since the group pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping ​chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.The instruction to staff to evacuate the building and work remotely follows a wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, targeting the company and Saudi airports. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment on what would be the first evacuation since the start of the Iran war.It was unclear what the reason for the evacuation was.The kingdom's benchmark index.TASI dropped 2.5% on Thursday following the Aramco news, according to LSEG data. Oil prices rose to their highest since May on Thursday on concern over an escalation of the Middle East conflict and its impact on crude oil supplies from the world's key exporting region.Houthis target Aramco facility in YanbuHouthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a televised speech that the group had launched attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and the Saudi defense ministry in the capital Riyadh. Saudi authorities did not confirm the attack.The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday it had intercepted drones over Riyadh and Islam's holy city of Medina, which is near Yanbu.The renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthi militias in recent weeks ended a 2022 UN-brokered truce, which had largely halted cross-border attacks, and opened another front ​in the US-Israeli ⁠war on Iran.The Houthis caused extensive damage to Aramco's headquarters earlier this month when they struck the building, with fire spreading across several floors.Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.Saree said that Saudi attacks on Yemen have killed and wounded 562 people since mid July, when the Houthis imposed a naval blockade on the kingdom, which then drew a warning from the Saudi-led coalition that it ​would respond "firmly."Separately, he said earlier on Thursday that the group is rescuing a boat carrying 14 Indians that was attacked off Jabal Zuqar island near the strait, one of the territories the group seized in an advance in September.Saree blamed the attack on Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.Houthis strike King Fahd airportA Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil hub of Dammam near Dhahran on Wednesday evening killed two people, a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, and wounded eight others.Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday that operations at the airport had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal.The ​Houthis had warned airlines this month against using Saudi airspace ⁠as they have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, including Riyadh's international airport and the southern airport of Abha.Brent crude futures LCOc1 climbed $3.06, or 2.81%, to $111.88 a barrel by 1104 GMT on Thursday. They hit $112.55 a barrel earlier in the session, the highest since May 18.

title: Hezbollah recruiting convicts in Latin America for revenue, relaxing ideological requirements
body: Hezbollah is increasingly recruiting convicted felons in Latin America, targeting individuals with financial difficulties who harbor resentment toward the courts – while relaxing its requirements for ideological alignment – according to a new Washington Institute for Near East Policy assessment. The report was written by Lucas Gualtieri, a Brazilian federal prosecutor who specializes in organized crime and Hezbollah's use of criminal networks.Operation Trapiche, a counterterrorism operation launched by Brazil's Federal Police in November 2023 with support from Israel's Mossad, has shed light on Hezbollah's efforts to outsource operatives, as well as on criminal revenue generation and financial services in Latin America, building capabilities the terrorist group can plausibly deny if confronted.Hezbollah has long outsourced operations in Latin America, as illustrated by the 2021 expulsion of two criminals hired by the Iran-backed group to target an Israeli in Bogotá.The investigation has uncovered what amounts to an assembly line for operatives. Rather than simply contracting hitmen, Hezbollah recruits men with no prior ties to the group, flies them to Lebanon for training, and sends them back to their home countries to scout for potential Israeli and Jewish targets.Gualtieri said Hezbollah was specifically seeking to recruit financially vulnerable convicted felons with no prior ties to the group or Lebanon. In intercepted audio, recruiters discussed looking for aggrieved individuals who had been “locked up” and felt they “owe the courts,” he said.By recruiting men without prior ideological or personal ties to Hezbollah or Lebanon, Gualtieri said, the group could deny involvement in attacks, allowing any resulting unrest to be dismissed as hate crimes committed by fringe extremists.Lucas Passos Lima, whose conviction was reinstated by Brazil's Superior Court of Justice last month after a federal court ruled that his role in a network targeting Jews and Israelis was motivated by financial gain rather than terrorism, had returned from Lebanon with more than $5,000 in untraceable cash.Had the court failed to convict Lima of terrorism, Gualtieri said, Brazil could have been viewed as a permissive environment for the group, and individuals who support terrorism for personal gain could have escaped more severe sentencing, despite their knowing involvement in plots.Hezbollah relying on Latin American criminal network revenueHezbollah has also increasingly relied on revenue generated by criminal networks in Latin America, he added, as in, for example, the discovery of Brazilian tobacco shops that helped fund plane tickets for recruits. The shops were initially identified by tax inspectors investigating a tobacco shop in Belo Horizonte's Mercado Central that was selling banned electronic cigarettes.The case was referred to counterterrorism police in October 2023 after an FBI warning about a criminal financial network funding Hezbollah raised alarm among Brazilian officials.Although the shops were registered to an individual identified as Hussain Abdulmajid, investigators found that the real operator was his brother, Mohamad Khir Abdulmajid, a Syrian-born naturalized Brazilian. The FBI memo also flagged Haissam Houssin Diab, a Lebanese-born naturalized Brazilian whose passport and travel bookings were later found in Abdulmajid's cloud storage.Abdulmajid is believed to have approached at least five Brazilians through social media and paid for their short trips to Beirut, including stays in upscale hotels. There, they allegedly received operational instruction and training in clandestine communications. This included learning a physical recognition signal and how to use shared email accounts as dead drops, leaving messages unsent in draft folders. They were also instructed to photograph Lebanese tourist sites to support a cover story that they had traveled for leisure.Lima was among those recruited through Abdulmajid's network; he was flown to Lebanon twice in 2023.After his first trip, researchers found that he had geolocated and filmed three synagogues, a Jewish cemetery, the Israeli embassy, and a rabbi in and around Brasília. He had also trained with firearms, purchased untraceable radios and surveillance equipment, and approached a pilot about exfiltration routes that would bypass migration controls.Hezbollah, IRGC using cryptocurrency for money launderingAlthough Hezbollah's use of criminal enterprises for fundraising is not new, the significance of these cases is that the group did not need to launder its own money to evade sanctions, Gualtieri said.Dante Felipini, a São Paulo cryptocurrency broker arrested in a separate money-laundering case as part of Operation Colossus, was able to establish three separate cryptocurrency wallets for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Hezbollah. Prosecutors charged him with money laundering, currency evasion, membership in a terrorist organization, and terrorism financing.Gualtieri said that Felipini's case showed that Hezbollah views outsourcing as both a tactic and an opportunity for recruitment. After the cryptobroker traveled to Baalbek in January 2023, where he fired rifles in the hills with Hezbollah terrorists, Felipini told a contact that the trip had been his “baptism” into the group.Gualtieri argued that the cases highlighted the need for authorities to pursue terrorism-related charges alongside other criminal offenses where the evidence supports them. He noted that such charges can lead to longer sentences and that relying solely on formal terrorism charges can understate the extent of Hezbollah's activities.He also highlighted a precedent set by Brazil's Superior Court of Justice, which affirmed that financial motivation does not preclude terrorism liability when suspects knowingly participate in a terrorist plot, even if they do not share the group's ideological motives.Finally, he said authorities should strengthen financial monitoring to identify suspicious cryptocurrency transfers and shell companies, continue tracking networks after assets are frozen, and expand national mechanisms for designating terrorist organizations.While international cooperation was crucial to Operation Trapiche, Gualtieri argued that domestic enforcement tools remained essential to disrupting Hezbollah's networks and prosecuting those involved. In Spanish, trapiche means “shady business.”

title: Iran deploys heavy weaponry to Kurdish regions amid fears of renewed conflict with Israel, US
body: Iran has deployed artillery and more weaponry to its northwest Kurdish regions, which border Iraq, while it has been increasingly cracking down on the Kurdish Iranian opposition group Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK). Recent clashes have been reported in the Shaho mountains and other areas near the border with the Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq. Millions of Kurds live on both sides of the border. They are part of the large Kurdish community that also lives in Syria and Turkey.According to the Kurdish media outlet Rudaw, “Iran has deployed artillery and heavy weaponry to Kurdish areas in the west of the country amid growing fears of a wider conflict with Israel and the United States, as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) intensifies operations against armed opposition groups along the country's western and southeastern frontiers.”Meanwhile, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) said that IRGC forces have been moving convoys of forces into the areas of Sanandaj, Kamyaran, Sarvabad, Marivan, and Baneh. This comes as Iran has demanded that Iraq expel Kurdish Iranian opposition groups. Iran's ambassador to Iraq claimed this week that Baghdad had agreed to do so.Iran has long demanded Baghdad rein in the Kurdish groups. The regime has also carried out hundreds of attacks on these groups.In the past week, Iran targeted groups from the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), PDKI, Komala, and Khabat, notably attacking a PAK camp near Mount Harir using drones. The four Kurdish groups, along with PJAK – a left-wing group linked to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) – are all part of a Kurdish Iranian opposition coalition formed at the start of 2026.Iran views Kurdish opposition groups as potential regional threatIran views the Kurds as a potential threat. It has wanted to pre-empt any uprising among the Kurds by essentially spreading the war in Iran to Iraq.Iran has deep influence in Iraq. Now, with reports circulating that Israel and the US could return to operations against Iran, Tehran appears to be making some new moves ahead of any looming new round of conflict.Rudaw reported that “an informed source in Kamyaran told the rights network that “hundreds of IRGC special forces, believed to be members of the entity's Saberin Unit, have been dispatched over the past few weeks in military convoys to areas surrounding villages on the slopes of Mount Shaho in Kamyaran County.”The situation in the Kurdistan region of Iran is complex. Some Kurds also work with Iran, which has often attempted to recruit Kurds to its units. As such, Rudaw says that the IRGC has also mobilized Kurdish fighters. From the Iranian regime's point of view, it is preferable to get Kurds to fight one another, not only because Kurds know the terrain but also because any blowback would fall on Kurdish communities, rather than on Tehran.Iran has also been using drones to attack PJAK forces in Iraq. The group said that drones had been used in the mountainous and forested areas of Marivan “with two suicide drones, followed by more than 30 mortar shells and heavy weapons on Sunday.”

title: What does the text of Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Turkey defense pact say? - explainer
body: This week, several media outlets in the Middle East published the text of the Makkah Defense Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. The texts are largely the same across media, with a few minor differences.This pact matters more than ever because the region is becoming more unstable due to the war with the Islamic Republic of Iran. Saudi Arabia is being targeted by the Iranian-backed Houthis. The United States is said to be supporting Saudi Arabia with advice or other non-kinetic means. This essentially means that the US is not currently willing to bomb the Houthis. The United Kingdom is sending warplanes to Saudi Arabia. Egypt may also send forces to assist in their defense. Reports even indicate that Israel could help Riyadh if the kingdom agrees.The Makkah Defense Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan was signed in Mecca on August 7, 2026, by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. It established a trilateral defense agreement under which an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all three. This is similar to the concept of NATO. However, so far the pact has not been activated.The text of the Makkah Defense Pact is now circulating because it has been presented at Turkey's parliament. It provides for joint military training, intelligence sharing, defense industrial cooperation, and a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia.What does the pact say?The text published by The National on October 21 reveals that the pact between the three countries is more than a mutual defense agreement. In its 16 articles, it envisages a permanent military and political structure, intelligence sharing, joint defense production, and other plans.The Jerusalem Post examined various versions of the text that had also been published by Middle East Eye and the newspaper Dawn in Pakistan. The texts were very similar. The articles focus on key points such as protection against threats to sovereignty, an attack on one considered attack on all, joint training, exercises and deployments, defense industry cooperation, establishing a permanent committee, and secretariat in Saudi Arabia, and having a first secretary-general from Pakistan, as well as the possibility of admitting additional countries. It also envisions intelligence sharing and logistical support.Several points in the text are worth noting. Article 2 notes that an attack on one is considered an attack on all. It contains a NATO-style collective defense clause. However, the three countries retain discretion over the extent and nature of the assistance they provide, including military support.The pact discusses threats, as well as actual attacks. Article 1 says the countries will use all necessary means when another member's sovereignty, territorial integrity, or recognized borders are threatened or endangered. This, potentially, demands more than mutual defense. In addition, Article 6 calls for joint training, military exercises, personnel exchanges, and deployments during both peacetime and wartime.Article 7 focuses on industrial cooperation as a central pillar of the pact. It comes as Qatar, Indonesia, Turkey, and Pakistan have agreed to a deal to expand cooperation in their defense industrial base. Article 7 of the pact focuses on joint weapons production, research and development, specialized technologies, defense innovation, and training personnel.Meanwhile, Article 8 creates a “Strategic Political and Defense Committee” involving the foreign ministers, defense ministers, and military chiefs of all three countries that will meet twice a year.Articles 9 and 10 focus on intelligence sharing and the provision of weapons, ammunition, fuel, spare parts, and other military supplies during peace, war, and other contingencies.What matters most for the Middle East is whether this pact will actually fulfill many of these visions.Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey have also discussed whether more countries might join. Article 8.4 establishes a method for admitting additional members, subject to consensus among the three countries. This implies an ambition to build a larger security organization rather than simply maintain a trilateral alliance.The initial concept is that Saudi Arabia will host the permanent secretariat, while Pakistan gets the first secretary general. In addition, Article 8.5-6 establishes the secretariat in Saudi Arabia, with a secretary general appointed on a rotating three-year basis. Pakistan will hold the first term in this significant institutional commitment. This is a meaty part of the agreement, laying out specific bureaucratic functions.Articles 6 and 10 cover military deployments, joint work, and logistical support during “wartime and peacetime.” This could enable the countries to establish regular joint military activities rather than cooperate only during emergencies. This would be similar to NATO drills or the frequent large joint exercises the US backs around the world.Article 13 of the deal prohibits sharing confidential information with outside governments, companies, or individuals. This raises interesting concerns about how the arrangement would interact with existing intelligence partnerships, particularly Turkey's NATO relationships and Saudi Arabia and Pakistan's relationships with Washington.In Article 16, there is a sentence noting that any party “may withdraw from this agreement after 10 years have elapsed from its entry into force, by giving the other parties written notification of its intention to withdraw through diplomatic channels at least three months in advance.” This is a strong long-term commitment. To avoid issues with NATO, the agreement notes that existing treaties are protected.Does the pact represent the beginning of a new regional military alliance?The permanent secretariat, rotating leadership, regular ministerial meetings, and provision for admitting new members suggest something more ambitious than an ordinary defense cooperation memorandum.There could also be an impact on the balance of power in the Middle East. Turkey brings a large defense industry and NATO experience, while Pakistan brings major military capabilities and nuclear weapons. All the countries are partners or allies of the US.The only differences in the texts published by the various media that the Post could identify were in Middle East Eye and The National.The Middle East Eye translation stated that the countries will support “technology sharing among defense-industry institutions, joint technology development, joint production.”The National version mentioned defense co-production, research and development, and exchanging expertise, but does not explicitly use the phrase “technology sharing.” It was not clear why there is this slight difference in wording.

title: Mandatory evacuation zone for families with children expanded to cover entire Sloviansk community – City Military Administration
body:
Donetsk Regional Military Administration has decided to expand the zone for the mandatory, enforced evacuation of families with children to cover the entire territory of Sloviansk community, due to a deteriorating security situation, Vadym Liakh, head of Sloviansk City Military Administration (CMA), announced on Thursday.

"This is a correct and important decision, as the security situation in our community is, unfortunately, constantly worsening. Just yesterday, two children were wounded in Sloviansk," he noted in a post on Facebook.

Liakh urged parents not to delay their departure, emphasizing that the lives and well-being of their children are of the utmost importance.

title: Netanyahu, Katz's warnings of Iranian strikes could spur regime into attacking first, officials say
body: Israel has intelligence indicating that Iran and its proxies are considering attacks against Israel ahead of the election, considering that a major security incident could undermine public confidence and influence voting, senior Israeli officials told Maariv on Thursday.According to the officials, public warnings by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz about potential attacks during the election period are intended primarily to deter Israel's enemies and prevent them from carrying out their plans.The defense and prime ministers have repeatedly warned of a potential Iranian strike in the days leading up to the elections, with Katz saying that any attack would be the fault of the opposition for ignoring his warnings.Defense officials have expressed concern that repeated statements by political leaders about the possibility of an imminent attack, coupled with the extensive media coverage they have generated, could lead to a miscalculation by Iran.One concern is that Tehran could interpret the warnings as preparations for an Israeli attack and consequently decide to strike first.Likelihood of another confrontation with Iran growing, defense source saysDespite a recent Financial Times report indicating that Israel had canceled a planned strike on Iran earlier this month at US President Donald Trump's request, Netanyahu has denied that the IDF had planned to attack first.A defense source told Walla that the sensitive period and the tense wait for decisions in the White House and Jerusalem center on the possibility of a strike against Iran. “As time passes, it is increasingly likely that we will have to go through a confrontation with Iran. Everything could change, but between a reality in which we reach an agreement with Iran and one in which we attack, the likelihood of war is growing.“There are two central questions: What will the Iranians do until then, and what will happen in parallel, regarding the acceleration of various processes? We are prepared for all scenarios in coordination with the US and countries in the region.”The source emphasized that the alert level remains extremely high, with the IDF's directorates, branches, and corps conducting situational assessments accordingly, alongside US Central Command (CENTCOM).“Coordination and updates take place daily,” the source said, adding that Israel is monitoring not only Tehran but also its proxies, amid concerns that Iran could force them to join the fighting if another military campaign breaks out.Concerns about an escalation triggered by miscalculation also explain that military officials have sought to calm public discourse and clarify that no specific intelligence warns of an imminent attack.Senior Israeli officials strongly rejected those briefings.“We don't care what one official or another is briefing. The truth is different,” they said.According to the officials, “The question that concerns us is whether the enemy will decide to attack or not. We know that it is currently considering this possibility. The statements by the prime minister and the defense minister are intended to deter.”The officials stressed that, in their view, the existence of intelligence concerning possible enemy intentions warrants public warnings, even without a specific intelligence alert regarding the timing or nature of an attack.“If certain officials, including within the IDF, are giving briefings for political reasons, that's their problem. The reality is different,” they said.Reports have also indicated an increase in Israeli fighter jet training exercises in the country's skies amid growing speculation about a possible military campaign against Iran.Israel's political leadership would have to order the IDF to strike targets across Iran to destroy remaining components of its nuclear program and defense industries producing ballistic missiles that threaten Israel's home front, with all the implications such an operation would entail.Defense officials assess that a decision on the matter will be made after the election, depending on the results, and in coordination with the United States.Shir Perets contributed to this report.

title: Czech president: Europe must close “gap” and play more active role in Ukraine peace talks
body:
Czech President Petr Pavel made this statement during a panel discussion at the Berlin Global Dialogue conference in Berlin on Thursday, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“I personally believe that our American allies do not necessarily represent European interests in the best way. That is precisely why I am firmly convinced that Europe must become more actively involved in the negotiations, have a clear vision of what the outcome should be and what the limits of the negotiations are, and propose alternatives that will make it possible to conduct the negotiations,” Pavel said.
According to him, Europe needs to develop a common position on ending the war and the future security architecture in order to become a full-fledged participant in the diplomatic process.
“Currently, these are merely negotiations between three parties—the United States, Russia, and Ukraine—in which Europe is not represented. I consider this a gap,” the Czech president noted.
At the same time, he acknowledged that European countries still lack a sufficiently coordinated vision for the continent’s future security architecture: “We do not have a single, clear European position. We have certain positions within the EU, but the EU does not represent all of Europe .”
In his view, without a strong, unified position, neither Russia nor the United States will regard European countries as full-fledged partners in negotiations.
At the same time, the Czech president emphasized that diplomatic contacts with Moscow are necessary, but they must be based on specific conditions and results. He also pointed out that Moscow is currently not showing any willingness to pursue a genuine peaceful settlement.
“They have not yet expressed any willingness to engage in peace talks, with one exception—Ukraine’s surrender and President Zelensky’s resignation. This is impossible for Ukraine. It is impossible for us on principle,” Pavel noted.
He also suggested considering future negotiations not only in the context of ending the war in Ukraine but also within the broader postwar architecture of European security.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 20 in Oslo, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks with U.S. Special Presidential Envoy Steve Witkoff, with the participation of Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gar Støre. European representatives also joined the preparatory consultations.
The parties discussed issues related to territory, security guarantees, and Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction. The following day, Witkoff traveled to Russia to continue diplomatic contacts.
On October 21, a meeting took place at the Konstantinovsky Palace in St. Petersburg between U.S. Presidential Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Russian dictator Vladimir Putin.
After the meeting, Witkoff stated that discussions on ending the Russian-Ukrainian war would continue in the format of trilateral talks at the technical level.

title: A communications edge helped Ukraine win Operation Vivaldi. US throttling of Starlink is now wearing it down
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi may have begun as early as March The counteroffensive seemingly inflicted more damage on a pair of Russian field armies than previously thought But the gains could be fleeting if a new speed cap on Ukraine's military Starlink terminals stays in place The Ukrainian 3rd Army Corps' Operation Vivaldi—its secretive counteroffensive east of Sloviansk in northern Donetsk Oblast—started earlier than first reported , and by the time it ended on 14 October it had cost the Russians more than 8,000 troops, by the 3rd Army Corps' count . It was a major Ukrainian victory in one of the most important sectors of Russia's 56-month wider war on Ukraine. But it could prove to be a temporary win, one the Russians may be able to partially reverse, if the administration of US President Donald Trump continues to throttle Starshield, the military version of Starlink that Ukraine's drones and commanders rely on. The Ukrainians' former command and control advantage, largely attributable to once-reliable Starlink and Starshield access, was pivotal as Operation Vivaldi played out in the Donbas region in stages starting in March. That advantage shrank practically overnight on 14 October, when a new speed cap began cutting off Ukraine's Starshield terminals whenever they moved faster than about 160 km/h (100 mph). The 3rd Army Corps attacked east of Sloviansk and north of Lyman as early as March, analyst and mapper Clément Molin concluded after scrutinizing official videos and interviews the Ukrainian defense ministry recently released. "The operation began much earlier than initially thought," Molin wrote. We are now 5 months after the start of Ukraine's Vivaldi operation and it has now officially ended A month after the operation was revealed, we know have much more information on the biggest Ukrainian success of the year. THREAD 1/18 pic.twitter.com/MgCoSv7Yhr — Clément Molin (@clement_molin) October 20, 2026 The timing was probably no accident. In early February, SpaceX, working from a Ukrainian defense ministry whitelist, switched off the thousands of stolen and smuggled Starlink terminals the Russians had been using. That had the effect of grounding many Russian drones and blinding many Russian commanders. Taking advantage of the Russians' confusion, Ukrainian troops attacked in several key sectors: in Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk Oblasts in the southeast, and east of Sloviansk in northern Donetsk. The Donetsk attack expanded into a full-blown counteroffensive under conditions of strict secrecy as the 3rd Army Corps probed for weaknesses along the flanks of the Russian 20th and 25th Combined Arms Armies, then overextended along the axis between the Zherebets River in the east and the outskirts of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk urban conglomeration in the west. The Russians had been threatening to lay siege to Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, the last two big free cities in Donetsk Oblast, from two directions: the north and the south. Operation Vivaldi eliminated the northern threat—and at great cost to the Russian 20th and 25th CAAs. A Ukrainian Hornet drone about to hit a buhanka, the UAZ van Russian forces use to haul troops and supplies to the front. Drones like this one have been choking Russian military supply lines. Via WarTranslated. Drones lead Aerial drones and unmanned ground vehicles led the attack, taking the Russians by surprise. "For an offensive operation, the Ukrainians sustained relatively few casualties compared to previous engagements," Molin explained. "Conversely, the defending Russian forces suffered significantly higher losses, largely due to the rapid encirclement of at least three regiments, not all of which managed to escape the area." It's unclear how many casualties the Russians suffered, but they might number in the thousands. The 20th and 25th CAAs were particularly fragile because the 3rd Army Corps and supporting drone units had been bombarding their supply line with so-called "middle strike" drones. But many middle strike drones rely on civilian-style Starlink satellite terminals or the more rugged, better-performing Starshield. Now that the 3rd Army Corps has wrecked Russia's 144th Motor Rifle Division, which the Institute for the Study of War assessed on 20 October has effectively ceased to exist as an organized fighting force, and pushed the Russian survivors back to the far bank of the Zherebets River, the Ukrainians are probably "consolidating their gains and adopting a defensive posture," according to Molin. Operation Vivaldi. Map: Euromaidan Press But that defensive posture, protecting Sloviansk from a northern attack, depends on reliable communications and responsive drones. On 14 October, a new speed cap hit Ukraine's Starshield terminals, cutting the link on any drone flying faster than about 160 km/h. Who ordered it is disputed. Sources told Reuters the order came from inside the White House, and that Pentagon leaders were told the service needed to be slowed. The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk himself ordered the slowdown, and that he and Trump discussed it soon after it became public. While Trump has denied ordering the speed limit, it's worth noting that the American president has become more overtly friendly toward Russia as his Republican Party looks likely to lose control of the US Congress in the November mid-term elections. The speed limit renders many of the faster middle-strike drones unflyable. As a result, "Ukrainian drone strikes have diminished significantly following yesterday's crippling of Ukraine's Starlink/Starshield connections, Russian sources report," the military history account ChrisO_wiki wrote on X on 15 October, the day after the speed limit took Ukrainian operators by surprise. Settlements Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps says it liberated during Operation Vivaldi north of Lyman, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine, as of 28 September 2026. Map: ISW Explore further Russia is back at Dobropillia a year after it failed there. Now it’s the southern jaw of a pincer on Donbas’s last big free cities A reduction in middle strikes on Russian supply lines could help Russian field armies recover from recent setbacks, including their retreat back across the Zherebets River. And if the communications confusion resulting from the partial loss of Starlink/Starshield connectivity persists, it could give the Russians the same kind of opportunity the Ukrainians had back in the spring. An opportunity to go back on the attack—and an Azov communications engineer warned Euromaidan Press in February that the shoe might be on the other foot. That's the worst-case scenario for the Ukrainians now that Operation Vivaldi has ended. The best case is that they get full Starlink and Starshield access back—or find command and control alternatives—and duplicate, in other sectors, the same success they enjoyed in northern Donetsk. "Now that the northern flank of Donbas is secured, at least for some time, the focus will concentrate on the southern flank," Molin predicted. Explore further Starlink crackdown cripples Russians—but American engineer warns Ukraine is just as vulnerable

title: Boxer built with room to upgrade its weapon station
body: The British Mechanised Infantry Vehicle was designed with capacity for future upgrades including to its remote weapon station, though no decision has been taken to replace the current system, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked the Secretary of State for Defence what assessment he had made of the potential merits of upgrading from the Kongsberg RS4 to the Kongsberg RS6 remote weapon station on Boxer. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “The United Kingdom Mechanised Infantry Vehicle was designed with capacity for future upgrades, including to its Remote Weapon Station. The Army continues to assess capability, priority and affordability options across the Mechanised Infantry Vehicle Programme and wider Armoured Fighting Vehicle fleet. No decision has currently been taken to upgrade the current Remote Weapon System.” Boxer entered British service with the Kongsberg Protector RS4, a stabilised mount carrying a 7.62mm or 12.7mm machine gun with a day and thermal sight, operated from inside the vehicle. The RS6 is a heavier station in the same family, rated to carry a 30mm cannon or a 40mm grenade launcher along with anti-tank missiles, and Kongsberg has marketed it to armies wanting a protected weapon fit without the cost and weight of a full turret. Australia selected the RS6 for its own Boxer order under Land 400 Phase 2, mounting a 30mm turret on its reconnaissance variants, and Germany has fitted heavier stations and turrets to Boxers for several customers. The post Boxer built with room to upgrade its weapon station first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
body: Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation. You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.” In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.” In interviews since , Gates has called AI “the most dangerous thing that humans have ever gone near,” and that AI “makes nuclear weapons look like nothing.” It is clear he does not think the current policy response from the White House, or the lack of coordinated efforts from the AI industry itself, is sufficient to combat this threat. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . So I wanted to know: Is Bill Gates an AI doomer? I also had a series of questions downstream from what he’s been arguing about AI. How can we ever hope to control AI, and align it to humanity, if we can’t even agree on what it is and whether it’s conscious ? How would you even technically construct a solution to alignment that could be enforced, not just for closed-source models but open-source ones, too? Bill gave us a big chunk of his time to dig into these issues with him, and the resulting conversation is a really illuminating one. He thinks we need to prepare for roughly two decades of AI disruption, and he says this period could be so painful it might split society in two — between people comfortable living near the technological frontier, and those who reject it. But assuming you solve the alignment problem- This feels like a big assumption. It’s an assumption, yes, and not guaranteed. But then the other problem you have is a problem of abundance and purpose at that point. I’ll leave it to younger people to figure out at that point in time how they choose to deal with that. You could literally say, “Let’s be like the Amish, and let’s only use AI for certain things.” I proposed in my memo the idea that some professions — childcare, food preparation, art, sports, a variety of things — might get chosen to be human-reserved. Even though the AI could do those things better, we would choose to do that. But that’s going to be a policy question people will have. Their freedom of choice, once you have that abundance, is very different from the shortage we have today, where in countries in Africa, most people never meet a doctor or almost half the kids are malnourished and don’t develop their brain. My big concern is this 20-year transition period, where they’ll have winners and losers and a lot of disruption, and we have to get through that in order to get to that period of abundance You want to say, even though that has challenges, you’ve eliminated a lot of the things that are tough about life today. My big concern is this 20-year transition period, where they’ll have winners and losers and a lot of disruption, and we have to get through that in order to get to that period of abundance. title: The movies, the media and the messy truth
body: It’s been a decade since Spotlight won Oscars for best picture and best screenplay at the 2016 Academy Awards, with the film recognised for its heroic portrayal of journalism. This newspaper described it as the “best film about journalism since All the President’s Men ”, which was quite the compliment, for its dramatisation of the Boston Globe ’s journalists working to expose historic child abuse cases within the Catholic church. Ten years later, Spotlight remains one of the great industry movies and presents a powerful case for investing time, patience, teamwork and shoe-leather into the stories that matter. The Social Reckoning , released earlier this month, attempts to cover some of the same ground, unravelling a time-hopping dialogue between an investigative journalist at The Wall Street Journal and a marginalised Facebook team member-turned reluctant whistle-blower, as the two work together to explain the algorithmic harm that social media is known to be capable of. Like Spotlight , The Social Reckoning is an advert for slow-burn reporting work, although journalism is very much the side order to the main-course dissection of the mores of digital platforms where billions of people spend good chunks of their daily lives. The contrast between those two worlds and the articulation of processes at work in their respective silos are everything you’d expect from a film by Aaron Sorkin, although it appears global audiences have not been especially convinced. The movie has to date underperformed its predecessor, The Social Network , as well as its reported pre-release revenue estimates. The Abu Dhabi cinema I saw the film in had few patrons in attendance on a recent weekend afternoon screening. One wonders if audiences genuinely want to sit and be instructed on the ills of social media in a darkened cinema when most will already instinctively recognise on some level that these digital platforms have a level of user-induced toxicity about them. Even armed with that knowledge, we remain broadly happy to scroll passively through our feeds morning, noon and night. And those who paid to watch the movie might have been absentmindedly flipping through their feeds right up until the point the opening credits rolled, an unintentionally amusing state of affairs given the film’s central argument. Media industry practitioners may still nod sagely at the love-letterish portrayal of investigative reporting, however. Time magazine called it a “brisk, old-school journalism thriller”, which in itself is an energetic hat-tip to a film that, in part, celebrates what is described in one scene as “the last two minutes of print journalism”. The Wall Street Journal ’s review, the title at the core of some of the film, describes it as a sequel that “no one saw coming and no one asked for”, in part, it says, because our societal concerns have shifted towards artificial intelligence in recent years. By comparison, social media might occupy the same place as the legal vices of society, such as excessive use of tobacco or alcohol or overconsumption of processed foods. Most would recognise the ability of these substances to do harm to the individual, but seem to have made an uneasy peace with their own habits. Given the above, The Social Reckoning seems unlikely to claim a spot on those “best films about journalism” lists that regularly circulate, which usually push the aforementioned Spotlight and All the President’s Men to the upper reaches of their rankings. Who knows if the film will be remembered affectionately a decade from now or even if it will be talked about at all? Anyone seeking a less glorious portrayal of the industry could do worse than seek out Devil Wears Prada 2 , a box-office high-performer earlier in the year that can now be found on streaming platforms. It offers a surprisingly accurate portrayal of journalism in its post-imperial years, although most people will have been attracted to it for its all-star cast and affection for the 2006 original. The 2026 comedy drama begins with layoffs at Anne Hathaway’s fictional newspaper and quickly progresses to the story at the centre of the film’s light plot being broken all over Instagram and the mea culpa that follows it through push notifications and alerts. The death of print is very much to the fore, too. The fictional fashion title at the centre of the film “stopped being a magazine years ago … we are digital, downloadable, we are in the ether … [we are] content that people scroll past while they eat”, which is quite the stinging epithet. In this world, digital stories are judged on optics and cut through to a niche audience by one segment of the organisation and on clicks and hard numbers by others. “Did anyone read the piece?” asks Meryl Streep’s Miranda early in the film at an editorial meeting. It is a question that sits at the heart of audience behaviour discussions in every newsroom, because on many occasions, what is perceived as good work does not line up with genuine high-performance and carry through. It is always a wonderful day in a newsroom when they do. As such, DWP2 probably captures the moment better than Sorkin’s admirable film. Process, production and dissemination of information at speed, as well as the definitive shift of print to being one form of story presentation rather than the only form, are to the fore. Outsiders may still wonder which is the more accurate portrayal? Insiders, meanwhile, may be locked in to interrogating what their audience wants, in what format and where.

title: How a fake pollster may have moved some 2026 elections
body: A new company whose polls had influenced campaign decisions and helped shape the midterms narrative admitted that it was faking its polling data on Tuesday night, setting off a firestorm in the electionsphere. Wedgewood Polls, facing an imminent publication of an investigation from FiftyPlusOne showing it was fabricating its numbers, declared late Tuesday night that it had been an “experimental project” to show how an “entirely fabricated polling firm” could sway public opinion while painting themselves as the good guys.They’d left an impact and been included by multiple credible polling aggregators including The New York Times — and mentioned twice in POLITICO's Morning Score polling roundup. Speculation is flying about what, exactly, Wedgewood was trying to achieve, and there’s still little public information about the defunct company that had crowdfunded thousands of dollars for its fake data. Was it an effort to boost progressives Democrats in primaries? If so, were progressives or Republicans really behind it? Was it being used to game betting markets? Were top operatives using the bogus data to make spending decisions? Were aggregation accounts too quick to jump on posting the data? An email to the account listed on Wedgewood’s X account bounced back, and previous PDFs of polls that were tied to the account are no longer available online. Regardless of what Wedgewood said it was trying to achieve (they remain adamant the project “was never intended to sway an election or permanently mislead the public”) — pollsters, operatives and candidates alike said there were real world implications for posting fake data online. Mallory McMorrow, the unsuccessful Michigan Democratic Senate candidate who dropped out before her primary, said a fake Wedgewood poll that showed her crashing to single-digit support against Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens “dried up” donations, “devastated” volunteers and led to numerous calls to exit the race. “It killed us,” McMorrow wrote on X . “These were some of the absolute worst days on the campaign. Especially for my team. There are no words to explain the morale blow, and nothing I could do or say to my team to fix it.” Jennifer Holdsworth, a Democratic operative who ran a super PAC supporting McMorrow, said the Wedgewood poll “was used by several donors to pull back funding at a time we were being outspent by $80 million.” The account also posted a poll showing democratic socialist Francesca Hong leading in Wisconsin gubernatorial primary, when there was scant public polling, something that contributed to the narrative she was ahead before the election (which she lost). They also posted a poll showing the Mississippi Senate race within reach, just before Democrats plowed money into the state. Scott Colom, the Democrat running for the seat, blasted the poll to his press list as proof there was “massive momentum” behind him. That led election watchers to argue that Wedgewood’s data was being used to make spending decisions in top outside groups, which elicited a response from Democrats’ main Senate super PAC. “Absolutely not. We don’t make spending or strategic decisions based on external polling,” Lauren French, a spokesperson for Senate Majority PAC, said on X . In its investigation, FiftyPlusOne said it had included Wedgewood in its aggregator because the firm was founded by people who had worked in the polling industry previously. There’s also been broad finger pointing at the aggregator X accounts that post polls frequently — and sometimes without verifying their accuracy. “You posted our polls multiple times. If you suspected it was fake, why did you post our results?” Wedgewood’s account shot back after Polling USA wrote that “my suspicions about Wedgewood were correct.” The whole ordeal illuminates just how big a problem polling could be in 2028, where both parties will have presidential primaries and polling can shift the narrative on a dime. “What I’m concerned about is essentially information pollution, things that are either intended to skew prediction markets or just straight misinformation flying around,” Charlotte Swasey, a pollster for the Democratic group Searchlight, told POLITICO Magazine recently. “It would be really difficult, especially in a primary, to tell people that what they’re seeing about their preferred candidate isn’t real.” A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. Want to receive the newsletter every weekday? Subscribe to POLITICO Pro. You’ll also receive daily policy news and other intelligence you need to act on the day’s biggest stories.

title: Ukraine’s key energy facilities damaged more than 170 times in 11 days, Kiev says
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Ukraine’s key energy facilities sustained damage more than 170 times over the past 11 days, Vladimir Zelensky said on his Telegram channel.
According to him, the figures cover the period starting October 11.
Earlier, Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergey Koretsky said that 2,147 explosions had occurred at the country’s energy facilities over a three-month period. According to him, this figure was several times higher than last year’s. Zelensky himself has also repeatedly reported damage to a number of key energy facilities and substations in the country.

title: Russian, Chinese governments to continue working on bilateral ties — prime minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. The governments of Russia and China will continue to work in a coordinated manner to develop relations between the two countries, Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said at a government meeting.
Mishustin mentioned that he had held talks yesterday with Chinese Premier of the State Council Li Qiang on the sidelines of the 31st regular meeting of the heads of the Russian and Chinese governments. He noted that this year marked the 25th anniversary of the Treaty of Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation between Moscow and Beijing. By decision of Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the fundamental document has been extended for another five years.
"The governments of Russia and China will continue to work in a coordinated manner to steadily develop interstate relations in the spirit of comprehensive partnership and strategic interaction, and to implement the agreements reached by our leaders at the highest level," Mishustin emphasized.
The prime minister said that priority areas for cooperation with Beijing included expanding bilateral trade, promoting partnerships in e-commerce, the platform economy, energy and transport connectivity. Developing humanitarian ties in science, innovation, technology and a number of other sectors also remained important.

title: Ukrzaliznytsia adds Kyiv City Express trips between Kyiv's banks amid Southern Bridge disruption
body:
Ukrzaliznytsia JSC is scheduling additional Kyiv City Express trips between the left and right banks due to traffic disruption on the Southern Bridge in Kyiv, Deputy Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport Volodymyr Shemaiev has said.
According to his Telegram post, the first additional trip from Pochaina station (transfer from the blue metro line) toward Troieshchyna will depart at 16:56, and from Vydubychi (transfer from the green metro line) toward Berezniaky at 18:02.
From 16:40, intervals between trips from the right bank to the left bank will be from 15 minutes.
In total, the trains will run on a half-ring route of Kyiv-Demiivskyi - Vydubychi - Berezniaky - Darnytsia - Rusanivka - Livoberezhna - Mykilska Slobidka - Voskresenka - Raiduzhnyi - Pochaina and in the opposite direction.
"In this way, Kyivans will get additional connections via both bridges, the Southern and the Northern," the deputy minister stressed.
Train tickets are available in the Ukrzaliznytsia app, he noted.
As reported, traffic on the Southern Bridge in the direction from the right bank to the left bank has been restricted in Kyiv due to an enemy attack on the capital.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko added that part of the metro infrastructure on the Southern Bridge was damaged by the shelling.

title: Hitz Praise Zone earns nomination at 2026 Praise Achievement Awards
body: Hitz Praise Zone, the gospel programme on Hitz 103.9 FM, has been nominated for the Christian Radio Programme of the Year at the 2026 Praise Achievement Awards. The programme is among 10 nominees in the category, which recognises radio shows that contribute to Christian broadcasting in Ghana. Other nominees represent stations including Spice FM, Sunny FM, Energy Radio, No. 1 FM, Sweet Melodies, Starr FM, Zed FM and Kristocentric. The nominations were unveiled on Sunday, October 18, at the African Regent Hotel in Accra, ahead of the fifth edition of the awards. Scheduled for Sunday, December 13, 2026, the ceremony will be held under the theme “Honouring Greatness, Celebrating True Excellence.” The nomination of Hitz Praise Zone recognises its place in Ghana’s gospel broadcasting space, where radio remains an important platform for sharing gospel music, promoting Christian expression and engaging listeners through faith-centred programming. The nomination also puts the Hitz 103.9 FM programme in contention for one of the awards celebrating contributions to christian radio in the country. The winners are expected to be announced at the December ceremony.

title: Court begins trial over kidnap of 20 NYSC members
body: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — An Imo State High Court, presided over by Justice Emeka Orafu, has commenced hearing in the case involving the kidnap of 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). Three defendants — Usman Aliyu, alias Chonge; Babangida Aliyu; and Mohamed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper — are facing a three-count charge of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms in suit number HOU/22C/2026. The Imo State Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Martins Udolwu, led the prosecution team, while Nnaemeka S. C. Adipo and Paschal Ofoma appeared for the defendants. Testifying before the court, the first prosecution witness, Ikechukwu Emmanuel, a staff member of the Department of State Services (DSS), said he investigated the incident. Emmanuel told the court that on October 1, 2026, at about 6.30am, 20 prospective corps members travelling in two buses from Ibadan to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states were attacked by suspected kidnappers armed with AK-47 rifles. “Twenty corps members from both buses were taken hostage and moved into the bush,” he said. The witness said security agencies in Imo, including the DSS, immediately deployed human and technical resources to track the attackers and secure the victims’ release. He told the court that the victims were released after the payment of the ransom demanded by the suspects, but investigations continued. According to him, intelligence reports indicated that the suspected kidnappers had relocated to Rivers and Abia states, leading to the arrest of the three defendants between October 10 and 14, 2026. Emmanuel also narrated how the DSS conducted an identification parade involving the three defendants and 10 other people. He said the released victims and one of the bus drivers identified the defendants during the exercise. The witness further told the court that Usman Aliyu, in a confessional statement, allegedly admitted that 11 people participated in the kidnapping operation. After the proceedings, Justice Orafu adjourned the case until October 27, 28 and 29, 2026, for continuation of hearing. The judge said he did not want the case to extend into the new year, directing the defence to be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately after the conclusion of his evidence-in-chief. “The defence must be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately he is done with his evidence-in-chief,” the judge said. The post Court begins trial over kidnap of 20 NYSC members appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NATO reconnaissance aircraft spends nearly five hours flying around Kaliningrad Region
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. A US-registered NATO reconnaissance aircraft spent nearly five hours circling the Kaliningrad Region, operating in the airspace of Lithuania and Poland, a source in air traffic control services told TASS.
"A Bombardier Artemis II reconnaissance aircraft, permanently based at an airfield in Constan·a, Romania, arrived near the Kaliningrad Region earlier today and spent nearly five hours flying in a circuit around the area," the source said.
According to the source, the aircraft operated in Polish and Lithuanian airspace, as well as over international waters in the Baltic Sea, at an altitude of approximately 12 kilometers.
The source noted that this was the second time the aircraft had circled the Russian region since the beginning of the week. The same aircraft was also spotted over international waters in the Black Sea, where it spent several hours flying back and forth between the western and eastern parts of the southern sea.
"The aircraft has now completed its mission and is heading back to its home base," the source added.

title: Potential Zaporozhye nuke plant accident could rival Chernobyl, Fukushima, director warns
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. The consequences of a potential accident at the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP), which could be triggered by blackouts caused by Ukrainian attacks, would be comparable to those of the Chernobyl and Fukushima disasters, the facility’s director, Yury Chernichuk, warned.
According to him, the ZNPP has lost external power 26 times since the conflict began, forcing it to switch to emergency diesel generators.
"In fact, this is the last barrier against accidents whose consequences could be compared to those of the disasters that occurred at the Chernobyl plant in the Soviet Union in 1986 and at the Fukushima plant in 2011," Chernichuk said during an international video conference, hosted by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which was dedicated to the Ukrainian army’s terrorist activities in the Zaporozhye Region.

title: Defense Forces strike electronic warfare assets in Bryansk region, several other Russia-held targets in occupied territories – General Staff
body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that it has struck an enemy electronic warfare (EW) station near the settlement of Hulevka in Russia’s Bryansk region, as well as a number of other targets in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine.

title: Euronaval 2026: Global Naval Shipbuilding Surges 50%
body: The Euronaval 2026 report on global naval shipbuilding reveals a 50% surge in global naval shipbuilding, with China now vastly outproducing the US. The report also details buildups in submarines and autonomous drones, and hypersonic arms races. For nearly sixty years, Euronaval has been at the forefront of major naval defence developments and is nowadays the largest naval defense exhibition, worldwide. Held from November 3 to 6, 2026, at Paris Nord Villepinte, the 30th edition unfolds against an unprecedented backdrop of geostrategic upheavals, the resurgence of high-intensity conflicts, and rapid technological change. Driven by this global naval rearmament and industry vitality, the exhibition is set to cross the 700-exhibitor mark, representing a 45% increase compared to 2024. Against a backdrop of profound strategic realignment and the return of high-intensity naval warfare, global military shipbuilding is experiencing an unprecedented boom. According to the newly released World Defense Shipbuilding 2026 study, unveiled ahead of the Euronaval 2026 tradeshow, the global market for military and paramilitary shipbuilding surged by 50% in the 2024-2025 period, reaching a staggering $122 billion. In terms of volume, global production jumped from nearly 1 million tonnes in the previous period to approximately 1.5 million tonnes. China Outpaces U.S. Industrial Output The most striking takeaway from the report is the rapidly widening production gap between the world’s two largest navies. Over the past two years, China has produced more than double the tonnage delivered by U.S. shipbuilders, churning out 636,208 tons compared to 270,509 tons for the United States. This massive industrial output allowed the Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) to take delivery of nine nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSNs) and ten destroyers in 2024-2025, compared to just three SSNs and four destroyers for the U.S. Navy. Additionally, the Chinese fleet commissioned its newest aircraft carrier—the 80,000-ton Fujian , equipped with electromagnetic catapults—and an amphibious assault ship during this period. A Surge in Submarine Construction The undersea domain remains a critical priority for major powers, driving a massive surge in submarine construction globally. Global production of nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSNs) nearly tripled, jumping from six units in 2022-2023 to 17 units in 2024-2025, representing a $27.3 billion investment. Conventional submarine deliveries also saw a significant increase, rising from 11 to 18 units globally. The Drone Revolution and Asymmetric Warfare Beyond traditional blue-water platforms, the modern naval battlefield is being fundamentally reshaped by autonomous systems and asymmetric threats. Drawing direct lessons from the war in Ukraine—where low-cost, explosive-laden surface drones like the Magura V5 successfully sank several Russian warships—navies worldwide are rushing to integrate unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) into their fleets. The Euronaval report highlights a broader doctrinal shift: navies are moving away from purely platform-centric approaches toward munitions-centric warfare . In response to the growing drone threat, advanced navies are being forced to rapidly develop and field complex, multi-layered counter-drone defenses, including interceptor drones, lasers, and rapid-fire gun systems . Hypersonics and the Parallel Space Race Traditional power projection platforms, such as U.S. carrier strike groups, are facing unprecedented vulnerabilities due to the proliferation of hypersonic anti-ship missiles. Russia’s Mach 9 Zircon missile and China’s extensive arsenal of hypersonic weapons—including the DF-17 and ship-launched YJ-21—are designed to neutralize traditional naval air defenses. Because these extreme-speed weapons cannot be tracked reliably by traditional over-the-horizon radars alone, the naval arms race has sparked a parallel competition in space . Nations are heavily investing in low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations dedicated to maritime surveillance, electromagnetic emission tracking, and early missile detection to protect their fleets . As the global strategic environment continues to fracture, the 2026 shipbuilding data makes one reality abundantly clear: the era of expeditionary crisis management has ended, replaced by an urgent, high-stakes arms race to prepare for high-intensity, peer-to-peer maritime conflict . title: Ebola: South-East governments step up containment measures
body: — Place health workers, border teams on alert — Abia prepares isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear — Enugu, Anambra intensify surveillance across LGAs By Anayo Okoli, Steve Oko, Vincent Ujumadu, Ugochukwu Alaribe, Jeff Agbodo and Emmanuel Iheaka Governments across the South-East have stepped up measures to prevent the spread of Ebola Virus Disease, following a reported case in Abuja, with Abia State preparing isolation facilities and seeking funds to procure protective equipment for health workers. Although no case of Ebola has been confirmed in any state in the zone, authorities said they were strengthening disease surveillance, alerting health workers and border teams, and improving emergency response capacity to contain any potential outbreak. The measures include heightened monitoring of suspected cases, public health awareness campaigns, infection prevention and control, and preparations to isolate and manage suspected cases. Abia races to prepare isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear Abia State Government said it had begun emergency preparedness measures against a possible Ebola outbreak, including plans to equip isolation facilities, procure personal protective equipment and intensify disease surveillance. The Permanent Secretary of the Abia State Ministry of Health, Dr Blossom Uma-Kalu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, assured residents that no case of Ebola had been recorded in the state. Uma-Kalu said the ministry had initiated consultations involving relevant departments and agencies to assess the state’s preparedness and identify gaps requiring urgent intervention. She, however, said additional funding was needed to procure personal protective equipment, PPE, thermometers, hand sanitisers and other essential supplies. According to her, the state was preparing a budget to determine which needs could be met through federal support and which would require state funding. “We have held meetings following communication from the Federal Ministry of Health about the case in Abuja. Health workers and relevant public health teams have been alerted to maintain a high index of suspicion,” she said. The Permanent Secretary said the government was also considering an additional isolation facility, while work continued on existing centres. She disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital (IDH) in Aba was nearing completion, while the isolation facility at a specialist hospital in Umuahia was undergoing remodelling. According to her, the state was also assessing a proposed facility that could be adapted for isolation if necessary. Uma-Kalu explained that establishing isolation centres required trained personnel, adequate funding and appropriate treatment and monitoring facilities, making it impractical to establish such centres in every local government area. She said the ministry was preparing a public health advisory to educate residents about Ebola, its symptoms and preventive measures. The advisory, she added, would include designated emergency telephone numbers for reporting suspected cases. Uma-Kalu urged health workers, particularly those in private hospitals and laboratories, to remain vigilant and pay attention to patients’ travel histories and symptoms that could suggest Ebola infection. She said public health teams working in communities and at entry points into the state had also been alerted to watch out for possible cases. The Permanent Secretary advised residents to remain calm but vigilant, avoid unnecessary contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected cases, and observe appropriate infection-prevention measures. She cautioned against dismissing suspicious symptoms as ordinary malaria without proper medical assessment. “People should not be afraid, but they need to be vigilant. Health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion and ensure that cases with symptoms suggestive of Ebola are properly assessed,” she said. She urged residents to rely on verified public health information rather than panic, adding that the state was taking steps to prepare for any eventuality. Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs Enugu State Government said it had intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following the reported Ebola case in the country. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, reassured residents that no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in the state. “Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said. Ugwu said the government was strengthening preparedness in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners. He noted that Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance necessary. According to him, surveillance had been reinforced across the state, while rapid response teams and technical personnel remained on standby to respond to suspected cases. The commissioner urged public and private health facilities to remain alert, promptly isolate suspected cases in line with established protocols and report them to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre. He also advised health workers to maintain strict infection prevention and control measures, including the use of appropriate protective equipment. Ugwu urged residents to remain calm, practise proper hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons and promptly report suspected cases to health authorities. He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising the public to rely on verified information from the state Ministry of Health, the NCDC and other recognised health authorities. He assured residents that the government would continue working with relevant agencies to strengthen Ebola preparedness, surveillance and response. Anambra to deploy surveillance officers at airport, motor parks Anambra State Government announced plans to deploy surveillance officers at strategic locations, including the Chinua Achebe International Airport, Umueri, motor parks, banks and other public places to strengthen efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Ben Obidike, who disclosed this while briefing reporters in Awka, said the officers would screen passengers arriving in the state from Abuja, Lagos and other African countries. He urged residents not to panic, assuring them that the government was taking measures to prevent an outbreak. Obidike said the state had monitored 40 persons of interest, with 33 completing their monitoring period and being cleared, while seven remained under active follow-up. He said all seven were stable. According to him, Anambra had developed an Ebola preparedness and operational plan covering surveillance, rapid response, infection prevention and control, laboratory coordination, referral arrangements, risk communication and logistics. He added that the state’s surveillance network across the 21 local government areas, the airport, motor parks and other public places would be strengthened to ensure early detection and reporting. The commissioner said state surveillance officers had participated in a two-day online training organised by the NCDC on monitoring persons of interest. He urged disease surveillance officers, health facilities and community reporting networks to promptly report unusual illnesses or deaths. He also advised healthcare workers to observe infection-prevention protocols and obtain patients’ travel and exposure histories. Residents who developed fever or other concerning symptoms after relevant travel or contact with a suspected Ebola patient were advised to contact health authorities and call ahead before visiting a health facility. Obidike urged the public to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with the blood and body fluids of sick persons, and refrain from handling the bodies of people who died from unexplained illnesses. He cautioned against spreading rumours or circulating the identities of people under monitoring, stressing that early reporting, public cooperation and trust were essential to containing the disease. Ebonyi on alert, warns against risky burials The Ebonyi State Commissioner for Health, Dr Moses Ikenna Ekuma, said there was no confirmed case of Ebola in the state, assuring residents that the government was prepared to respond to any outbreak. Ekuma said the Ministry of Health had activated precautionary measures, established an equipped isolation centre and trained health workers on infection prevention and control. He urged residents to avoid contact with bodily fluids, observe proper hygiene, cook bush meat thoroughly and exercise caution during burials where the cause of death was unknown. The commissioner also advised residents to avoid unnecessary travel and seek prompt medical attention if they developed unusual or severe symptoms. He attributed the state’s preparedness to Governor Francis Nwifuru’s investment in health facilities and equipment. Meanwhile, efforts to reach the Imo State Commissioner for Health, Dr Chioma Egu, were unsuccessful, as neither she nor the ministry’s Permanent Secretary was available when our correspondent visited the ministry. Calls to the commissioner’s telephone line also went unanswered, while she had yet to respond to a text message sent to her as of the time of filing this report. title: Four energy company employees killed, over ten injured in Zaporozhye Region in 2025-2026
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. Ukrainian attacks on the Zaporozhye Region claimed the lives of four energy company employees and injured more than ten others in 2025-2026, the region’s Acting Energy Minister Yevgeny Paramonov said during an international teleconference on the Ukrainian army’s terrorist activities in the Zaporozhye Region.
"One of the most flagrant examples of such an attack was recorded this year, when a district power grid chief and an electrician were killed by a drone strike on their way to a work site. A total of four employees of the regional power grid company were killed on duty in 2025-2026, with more than ten others sustaining injuries of varying severity," Paramonov said.

title: Museum of Ukrainian Diaspora in Kyiv damaged by Russian shelling
body:
The Museum of the Ukrainian Diaspora has been damaged as a result of Russian shelling in Kyiv, the Museum of the History of the City of Kyiv reported.

"Last night, the Museum of the Ukrainian Diaspora—a branch of the Museum of the History of the City of Kyiv—was damaged by Russian shelling of Kyiv. Windows in the building were blown out, and the facade and roof sustained damage. Fortunately, no one was injured," the institution stated.

It is noted that the museum is currently addressing the aftermath of the shelling; consequently, it will remain closed to visitors for the coming days.

title: Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
body:
IGUAZÚ NATIONAL PARK, Argentina — Few times in my life have I felt the enormity and power of nature. Standing at the edge of Iguazú Falls, on the Brazil-Argentina border, was one of them.
Iguazú isn't just one imposing fall, but a complex of cascades spanning more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October in Brazil has sent near-record volumes of water surging over its towering cliffs. Scientists link the relentless rains to this year's Super El Niño , causing extreme weather events across the globe.
But what a spectacular force of nature for the lower-than-average number of tourists who braved the deluge this month. The roar of the rushing Iguazú river under your feet penetrates your body; your eyes strain to keep up as the rusty swells disappear over the steep precipice. One day during my recent visit, officials registered nearly 12 million liters (more than 3 million gallons) of water per second tumbling over the falls. That's 10 times the normal flow. As the Iguazú river's red, muddy waters raced furiously toward the falls' edge, they lapped the bottom of the narrow metal catwalks that usually hover a few feet above the falls during normal-rainfall years. Officials closed the spectacular walkways as the river level kept rising. When asked why access was shut off, the national park's director simply said, "It just keeps raining." That's an understatement. I'm still drying out.
