title: Russia’s international reserves fall by $0.3 bln over week to $723.2 bln — Central Bank
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Russia’s international reserves stood at $723.2 bln as of October 16, 2026, down $0.3 bln over the week, according to materials published by the Bank of Russia.
"International reserves changed only slightly over the week, standing at $723.2 bln as of the end of October 16, 2026," the regulator said.
As of October 9, the reserves totaled $723.5 bln.
International reserves are highly liquid foreign assets held by the Bank of Russia and the Russian government. They consist of foreign currency assets, special drawing rights, the reserve position in the International Monetary Fund, and monetary gold.
Western countries imposed sanctions on the Bank of Russia after Russia launched its special military operation in Ukraine. In addition to freezing Russia’s gold and foreign exchange reserves, they banned all transactions related to the management of the Central Bank’s reserves and assets, as well as transactions with any legal entity, organization, or body acting on behalf of or at the direction of the Central Bank.

title: Chikadibia family awaits justice 18 months after alleged police raid
body: . RULAAC seeks compensation over demolished home, missing valuables . We need time to investigate – Police , request fresh petition By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – Eighteen months after Mr Sunday Chikadibia and his three daughters were arrested during a controversial police operation in Abia State, the family is still awaiting a government decision on its demands for justice and compensation over the alleged demolition of their home and loss of property. The Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre, RULAAC, which has pursued the case, is demanding an investigation into the April 12, 2025 operation, restitution for missing valuables and cash, and assistance to enable the family rebuild its life. RULAAC in a statement by its Executive Director, Okechukwu Nwanguma, yesterday demanded the disclosure of the investigation’s findings, accountability for any officials found culpable, compensation for the demolished home and the recovery or restitution of missing property and money. It also sought a thorough investigation into the alleged removal and sharing of the victims’ cash, including an examination of relevant police records and financial transactions. Chikadibia and his daughters, Glory, Ngozi and Ogechi, are from Mbaise in Imo State but residents of Alaukwu in Osisioma Ngwa Local Government Area of Abia State. According to the family, the operation began when one of the daughters, a slippers trader, was allegedly lured to a meeting with a purported supplier and arrested by plain cloth detectives. Her sister was subsequently summoned and taken away before operatives moved to their family home, where their father and another daughter were arrested. The family alleged that the operatives broke into rooms, removed cash and household belongings, and demolished the house without presenting relevant warrants or providing an inventory of the items seized. The missing property reportedly included electronics, laptops, a generator, furniture, clothing, land documents and construction tools. The family also alleged that substantial sums were withdrawn from their bank accounts while they were in custody. The claims have yet to be independently verified. Confirming the allegations in a phone interview with Vanguard, one of the victims, Glory Sunday Nwamaka claimed that over N3.5 million was withdrawal from their bank accounts, adding that details of the brutality meted out to them were contained in their statements. The family members were arraigned on May 13, 2025, before Chief Magistrate Court 1, Aba North, in Charge No. MAN/114C/2025, over allegations relating to kidnapping, murder, armed robbery, terrorism and conspiracy. A subsequent High Court case was identified as Charge No. HU/8C/2025 before the High Court at Obehie. Following sustained advocacy by RULAAC and media attention, government intervention eventually led to their release. However, the organisation insists that their release has not resolved questions surrounding their arrest, detention, prosecution, the alleged demolition or the missing property. The family’s ordeal was compounded by the death of their mother, Mrs Chioma Chikadibia, on August 8, 2025. The family attributed her distress and deteriorating health to the events, although an independent medical determination would be required to establish a direct causal link. On March 6, 2026, RULAAC petitioned Governor Alex Otti, seeking compensation for the demolished home, restitution for missing property and money, housing assistance, educational support for Ogechi and psychosocial assistance for the surviving family members. Following a further appeal, the Abia State Ministry of Justice requested additional information, which RULAAC supplied on July 29. At a meeting with the Ministry’s Citizens’ Rights Department on August 4, the family’s lawyer reportedly presented the allegations and supporting information. The Ministry according to RULAAC, requested photographs of the demolished property, bank statements relating to the alleged withdrawals and a list of missing items. RULAAC said the requested materials were subsequently submitted. However, the organisation said no formal decision had been communicated as of September 5. The family’s lawyer returned to the Ministry on October 6 to seek an update. RULLAC urged Abia State Government and relevant agencies of Government to intervene and get justice for the Chikadibia family. It also demanded immediate prosecution of the police personnel involved in the act. When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Maureen Chinaka, said she had no details about the matter but added that it needed to be properly investigated. She said that time had passed since the incident reportedly occurred, adding that “if they are alleging anything, they have to write to the command”. “Time has passed. I have to make inquiries. The affected officers or even the DPO must have gone on transfer since 2025. They should write to the Command for proper investigation to commence”. title: Ukraine steps up strikes on civilian infrastructure by 3-4 times — Russian envoy
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Ukraine has increased the intensity of strikes on civilian infrastructure by 3-4 times, Rodion Miroshnik, Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Foreign Ministry for Issues Related to the Crimes of the Kiev Regime, said at the international teleconference "Zaporozhye Region: Escalation of the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ Terrorist War."
"The statistical data we have confirms that it was the allocation of the first funds from the EU’s 90 billion euro military loan that triggered the escalation of the Kiev regime’s terrorist actions against the civilian population of Russia," he said. "At that time, Brussels and Kiev announced the creation of an alliance between the EU and Ukraine in the field of unmanned aerial vehicles."
According to Miroshnik, Vladimir Zelensky, inspired by the same ideas, announced a 40·day plan to force Russia to negotiate, but in practice this meant that the Ukrainian regime had agreed with its sponsors to use the funds allocated by the West to commit war crimes and terrorist acts.
"Throughout the front·line zone, this immediately manifested itself in a three· to fourfold increase in the intensity of strikes against civilian facilities and infrastructure," the diplomat said.

title: Battlegroup Center air defense crew evaluates effectiveness of new F-1 interceptor drone
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Servicemen of the Battlegroup Center’s air defense missile brigade destroyed more than 20 Ukrainian drones in four days, employing the new F-1 interceptor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for the first time, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"This F-1 drone, which has been put into service with the air defense missile brigade’s anti-UAV unit, has demonstrated high effectiveness in destroying high-speed targets. Over four days of combat use, the crews destroyed more than 20 enemy attack drones of various types, including the PD-2, Rubaka, and Bliskavka," the ministry said.
In addition, according to its data, the interceptor drone crew destroyed two new enemy Anubis unmanned aerial vehicles for the first time.
The ministry emphasized that with the F-1 interceptor drone, Russian troops effectively counter enemy strike and reconnaissance UAVs as they approach, preventing their attacks on military units. They operate in close coordination with air surveillance posts and radar station crews, ensuring the timely detection and elimination of aerial targets.

title: Ebola: Tomori faults Nigeria’s response timeline, demands full disclosure
body: …Warns against complacency By Sola Ogundipe Renowned Virologist and chairman of the West African National Academy of Scientists, Professor Oyewale Tomori, has raised concerns over the time it took Nigerian health authorities to confirm the country’s Ebola case, warning that delays in diagnosis and incomplete public information could undermine confidence in the national response. Tomori’s concerns come amid questions about the circumstances surrounding the confirmed case, the patient’s travel history and the adequacy of Nigeria’s preparedness to contain the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus disease. He warned that Nigeria must combine transparent communication with effective surveillance, rapid diagnosis, comprehensive contact tracing and adequate treatment and isolation capacity to prevent the outbreak from escalating. Speaking during a television interview, the virologist said he was more confident about Nigeria’s preparedness after hearing the health minister outline measures being taken to contain the outbreak, but stressed that the country must not become complacent. Tomori said the interval between the time the patient’s reported onset of symptoms and confirmation of the infection was a cause for concern, stressing that Nigeria must strengthen its disease surveillance, improve early diagnosis and prepare for the possibility of additional cases. He called on the Federal Government to provide comprehensive information about the case, including the patient’s movements before diagnosis and the extent of contact tracing, warning that gaps in official communication would inevitably fuel rumours. “The government must be completely transparent about matters like this. We don’t want to hear information in bits and pieces from different sources. Initially, we were told that the woman came from Uganda, later I heard the Ugandan authorities say she was a transit passenger. We need complete information, and when the government fails to provide it, the gaps are filled with rumours. “Tell us where the samples were tested and provide the relevant details. We are now hearing that the woman is a diplomat’s wife, among other reports. Certain information may need to remain confidential, but this is a national emergency, it concerns all of us, and we need the facts. We also need a clearer explanation of how the woman entered the country and what happened after her arrival. “Where did she stay? Where did she go? How many people did she come into contact with?” he asked, stressing that these details were essential to establishing the extent of possible exposure and reassuring the public,” he queried. Tomori warned that the time taken to confirm the infection highlighted the need for healthcare workers to maintain a high index of suspicion when treating patients who have travelled from areas experiencing Ebola outbreaks. On the timeline, Tomori said the period was still within the incubation period. “However, the fact that it took until the 20th (October) to confirm the case is a concern and we need to improve on that. By the time the woman had moved between different locations, the opportunity for further exposure might already have arisen. “We faced a similar problem in 2014, when Patrick Sawyer arrived in Nigeria. It took about three or four days to diagnose him. Samples were initially being sent for malaria testing. When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. “The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment. Our healthcare workers need to understand this. Their own lives are also at risk, so they must remain alert. “If I hear that someone has arrived from a country experiencing an Ebola outbreak, or from an area close to one, my first question would be whether the person could have Ebola before considering other possibilities. “We need to move beyond routine thinking before concluding that someone has malaria, healthcare workers should be up to date on diseases circulating in the places from which their patients have travelled,” he noted. On contact tracing Tomori said the health authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. “We should have more details than we currently have. For now, there is no reason to panic, the authorities are putting the necessary measures in place. What we need to do is prepare for the worst-case scenario. Suppose two or three of those contacts test positive. What happens next? “Do we have the hospitals, isolation facilities and other resources needed to manage additional cases? Those are the questions we should be asking now, rather than assuming that everyone will die because Ebola has entered the country. There are 44 people reportedly under quarantine. If one, two or three become infected, we must be ready to respond. According to him, healthcare workers must look beyond common illnesses such as malaria when a patient’s travel history suggests possible exposure to a dangerous infectious disease. “When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment.” He warned that failure to recognise the possibility of Ebola early could expose healthcare workers and other patients to infection. “I think the authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. We should have more details than we currently have,” he said. He said Nigeria should plan for the worst-case scenario without creating unnecessary public alarm. “For now, there is no reason to panic. The authorities are putting the necessary measures in place,” he said, adding that preparedness would be critical if the outbreak expanded. Further, Tomori also cautioned against relying exclusively on geographical distance to assess Nigeria’s risk. He said although the World Health Organisation had reportedly classified the country as being at low risk, he argued that regular travel between Nigeria and affected regions needed to be considered. “Hundreds of Nigerians travel to the region for business and other activities before returning home. That makes the risk more complicated than simply measuring the distance between two locations,” he said. On the strain responsible for the outbreak, Tomori explained that Ebola viruses differ in their characteristics and severity, even though they belong to the same broader group. “The Zaire strain has recorded fatality rates approaching 90 per cent in some outbreaks, while the Sudan strain has recorded rates of around 60 per cent. Bundibugyo has recorded fatality rates of about 50 per cent in some outbreaks,” he said. He cautioned against interpreting the comparatively lower fatality rate as evidence that the strain was harmless. “When we say Bundibugyo is less severe, however, that does not mean it is harmless or that it cannot kill people,” he said. title: Reps pass bill for National Children’s Hospital in Imo
body: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish a National Children’s Hospital in Ideato, Imo State, to expand access to specialised paediatric healthcare and reduce child mortality in Nigeria. The bill, sponsored by the member representing Ideato North and South Federal Constituency, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, scaled the second-reading hurdle after lawmakers considered its general principles during plenary. Leading the debate, Ugochinyere said the proposed hospital would provide specialised medical services for children, strengthen the country’s capacity to manage complex childhood illnesses and improve access to quality healthcare. The lawmaker said the proposed legislation was in line with the constitutional responsibility of government to protect the welfare of citizens, particularly children, who remain among the most vulnerable members of society. He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government. According to him, the provision places an obligation on government to prioritise accessible, affordable and quality healthcare for Nigerians, including children. Ugochinyere also expressed concern over Nigeria’s child mortality burden, noting that preventable conditions such as malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoeal diseases and neonatal complications continue to threaten the survival and healthy development of children. He argued that a dedicated national paediatric hospital would improve the diagnosis and treatment of complex childhood diseases while supporting medical research, professional training and early intervention services. The lawmaker further referenced Section 13 of the Child Rights Act, 2003, which recognises every child’s right to the best attainable state of physical, mental and spiritual health. He said the proposed hospital would provide an institutional framework for advancing child-centred medical care and improving health outcomes. Drawing comparisons with specialised paediatric institutions in other countries, Ugochinyere cited Children’s National Hospital in Washington, D.C., United States, and the Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa. He said Nigeria needed to invest more deliberately in specialised healthcare facilities capable of delivering advanced treatment and life-saving interventions for children. The proposed hospital in Ideato is expected to serve children from Imo State, the South-East and other parts of the country, subject to its eventual capacity and service arrangements. The bill was passed for second reading following a voice vote by the Deputy Speaker and referred to the relevant committee for further legislative consideration The post Reps pass bill for National Children’s Hospital in Imo appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: IPOB member pleads guilty, jailed 20 years for belonging to proscribed group
body: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Thursday, convicted and sentenced a self-confessed member of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Mr. Paul Okechukwu, 48, to 20 years in prison for belonging to a proscribed organisation. The defendant pleaded guilty to one count of a two-count charge the Federal Government preferred against him. The Federal Government alleged in the first count that the defendant, who is from Nnewi South in Anambra State, had in 2021, while in Imo State, committed an offence by belonging to IPOB, a proscribed organisation, contrary to and punishable under Section 16 of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. In the second count, the Federal Government alleged that the defendant participated in an attack in which two security operatives were killed, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 2(1) of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. After the charge was read to him, the defendant pleaded not guilty to the second count. In view of this development, and following an application by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who was in court to lead the prosecution, the court struck out the second count after it was withdrawn. Relying on Section 72 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022, the Attorney-General applied for the court to allow a witness from the Department of State Services (DSS) to review some facts of the case. The witness, whose name was given as “ABC” for the purpose of the trial, identified the defendant as a member of IPOB, which he said had since been outlawed. He told the court that the defendant was involved in acts of terrorism, which he said included attacks on security agents. The witness, who said he was part of a team that investigated the defendant, tendered a copy of the report, which was admitted as Exhibit A. While applying for the defendant to be convicted, the AGF argued that the law prescribed a minimum sentence of 20 years for the offence. “We therefore urge my lord to impose the maximum sentence, at least to serve as a deterrent to others and to also show that the nation cannot condone any act of terrorism,” the AGF added. Meanwhile, immediately after the AGF made the application, the defendant broke down in tears in the dock, begging the court to temper justice with mercy. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Hawa Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 20 years. The court said it took note of the charge against the defendant and “the ripple effect it has on the nation.” It held that the defendant should be remanded in any correctional facility chosen by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service to serve his sentence, which should count from the day he was arrested. The court held that the convict should be rehabilitated and redecalised upon the completion of his prison sentence. title: Trump Could Force Putin to Negotiate but Hasn’t, Zelensky Says
body:
US President Donald Trump has the leverage to bring Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table but has yet to use it, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
“Trump could very easily bring Putin to the negotiating table, because he has the means to do so. The way he speaks about me – President Trump should speak about Putin in the same way,” Zelensky said in an interview on The Diary of a CEO podcast.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Zelensky pointed to sanctions approved by the US Congress as one tool Trump could use to pressure the Kremlin.
“Sanctions are sitting on his desk. He didn’t vote for them – Congress voted for strong sanctions. He has the power to act,” Zelensky said.
Asked why Trump had not taken such action, Zelensky said he could only speculate about the reasons, including the relationship between Kremlin and US administration leaders and possible economic interests. He said:
“I don’t know why. Perhaps they have a special relationship. Perhaps it’s something else. I can’t say for sure; I don’t know everything. I can only speculate – perhaps there are some economic deals, or something of that nature.”
The podcast host suggested that Trump might be more concerned about domestic energy prices ahead of the US midterm elections than about Ukraine.
Zelensky rejected the idea that American fuel prices depend on how much Russian energy is sold, arguing that the US exports its own energy resources. The president explained:
“I can tell you with 100% certainty that diesel prices do not depend on the volumes Russia sells. They don’t. The Americans export energy resources. There is no ban on American energy exports; it is American companies that are doing the exporting.”
Zelensky added that he saw little reason for Trump to restrict private companies’ energy exports when those businesses were making money from them.
“And why would he do that, when ‘it sells, and the money keeps coming in?’” Zelensky said.
He also expressed confidence that the truth about the war and the decisions surrounding it would eventually emerge. Zelensky said:
“ All secrets, all mysteries eventually come to light. It just takes time. Time is definitely on the side of those who are open and ready for an honest dialogue and a struggle. This means that time will be on our side.”
The host also asked Zelensky about Trump’s repeated claims that Russia would not have launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine had Trump been president at the time. Zelensky replied:
“To be honest, no one knows the answer. The fact remains: this happened during Biden’s presidency. That is a fact. It is also a fact that it did not happen under Trump. But it is equally a fact that it was Putin who chose the moment for a full-scale occupation.”
He acknowledged that Trump’s relationship with Putin might have influenced the Russian leader’s decision-making, but argued that personal ties between presidents would not resolve the underlying threat to Ukraine.
Zelensky said Putin would continue pursuing his goal of occupying Ukraine regardless of who held the US presidency:
“Neither I nor Trump will hold the presidency forever. Sooner or later, Trump’s presidency would have come to an end, and Putin still would not have abandoned his primary objective – the occupation of Ukraine.
“Therefore, frankly speaking, it does not matter who exactly is president, as long as Putin remains in power.”
Zelensky warned that surrendering Sloviansk and Kramatorsk in the Donetsk region could open the way for further Russian advances toward Dnipropetrovsk region, including Pavlohrad and Dnipro.
He described the area as a key industrial and machine-building hub that supports Ukraine’s economy and said its defenses had been heavily fortified. Zelensky said:
“If we surrender these cities of ours to them, the risk is enormous. If he decides to push further, he could capture a vast number of our cities. The risk is real. There are no guarantees.”
He also questioned what security guarantees could mean if Ukraine were required to withdraw from additional territory to meet Russia’s demands.
“While everyone is talking about security guarantees and we are open to such talks – the Russians, for their part, want us to withdraw even further,” he said. “If we withdraw, where are the security guarantees? Not to mention the fact that it would be unjust.”
Zelensky estimated that Russia currently controls approximately 18-19% of Ukrainian territory. He also said Moscow presents different maps to its domestic audience and continues to pursue territorial objectives beyond the areas it currently occupies.
According to Zelensky, Russia wants to capture the city of Zaporizhzhia but has been unable to do so. He added that Zaporizhzhia and Mykolaiv remain Russian targets, even if Moscow does not explicitly acknowledge those ambitions.
He also pointed to the situation in Kherson, where the Dnipro River divides the city, with Ukrainian-held territory on one bank and Russian forces on the other. The positions allow Russian troops to shell the city, he said.
Zelensky said Trump had repeatedly urged both sides to seek a compromise, but argued that Ukraine was already making a significant concession by agreeing to stop fighting along the current front line.
“The biggest compromise we are already making is a ceasefire. Let’s just stop this war,” he said.
Zelensky added that he had repeatedly urged Trump to understand the scale of the concession Ukraine was prepared to make by agreeing to halt the fighting without first resolving every territorial issue. Zelensky stated:
“I have tried to tell the US President many times: just understand us. It is a huge compromise – simply holding the lines where they are right now.”

title: The Pentagon wants ketamine wafers as a battlefield medicine option
body: The Pentagon wants ketamine wafers. And it seems to want them now. Earlier this year, the Defense Department awarded a nearly $41 million development contract to Singapore-based iX Biopharma to develop Wafermine, a small, ketamine-packed wafer that dissolves under the tongue. Recently, the drug’s manufacturer announced that it is pursuing an emergency authorization that could make the medication available to troops before it receives full Food and Drug Administration approval, citing a September U.S. declaration of a military emergency that justifies the emergency use of drugs deemed necessary by the Pentagon. A federal emergency use approval declaration by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Sept. 3 opened the possibility of early official authorization , giving the FDA a route to use unapproved medications to treat war wounds. According to the notice, on July 15, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth determined “a military emergency, or significant potential for a military emergency, involving a heightened risk to U.S. military forces of an attack with a chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear agent or agents,” or an attack with agents that would cause life-threatening injuries. The declaration continues: “Injuries arising from these attacks may cause those forces to experience moderate to severe acute pain and place them at risk of developing life-threatening hemodynamic instability, including shock or respiratory distress.” Because of Hegseth’s determination, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr. declared that “circumstances exist justifying the authorization of emergency use of drugs” identified by the Pentagon. The notice did not elaborate on the emergency circumstances or state which drugs would be identified for emergency authorization. A Politico investigation published Tuesday found that iX Biofarma’s domestic manufacturing partner lacks the Nevada license required to operate. iX Biofarma called the non-opioid medication the “world’s first sublingual ketamine for acute moderate to severe pain,” and said the wafer enables a different delivery mechanism, letting patients absorb the ketamine through the mucous membrane into the bloodstream. Typically administered via injection, ketamine can alleviate pain, increase euphoria and cause dissociation and amnesia. A 2023 study found that opioid use to alleviate battlefield injuries decreased between January 2010 and December 2019, while ketamine use increased. The researchers found that “ketamine is generally used first for more severely injured patients and has increasingly been employed by the U.S. military as the primary analgesic for combat casualties.” The company said it received a “sole-source” award for Wafermine development, meaning it did not solicit other vendors.

The declaration continues: “Injuries arising from these attacks may cause those forces to experience moderate to severe acute pain and place them at risk of developing life-threatening hemodynamic instability, including shock or respiratory distress.” Because of Hegseth’s determination, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr. declared that “circumstances exist justifying the authorization of emergency use of drugs” identified by the Pentagon. The notice did not elaborate on the emergency circumstances or state which drugs would be identified for emergency authorization. A Politico investigation published Tuesday found that iX Biofarma’s domestic manufacturing partner lacks the Nevada license required to operate. iX Biofarma called the non-opioid medication the “world’s first sublingual ketamine for acute moderate to severe pain,” and said the wafer enables a different delivery mechanism, letting patients absorb the ketamine through the mucous membrane into the bloodstream. Typically administered via injection, ketamine can alleviate pain, increase euphoria and cause dissociation and amnesia. A 2023 study found that opioid use to alleviate battlefield injuries decreased between January 2010 and December 2019, while ketamine use increased. The researchers found that “ketamine is generally used first for more severely injured patients and has increasingly been employed by the U.S. military as the primary analgesic for combat casualties.” The company said it received a “sole-source” award for Wafermine development, meaning it did not solicit other vendors.

title: Kiev troops almost fully blocked ZNPP personnel transit to work — director
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. The armed forces of Ukraine have almost completely paralyzed the movement of personnel to and from the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP), the facility’s Director Yury Chernichuk said during an international video conference on Ukraine’s attempts to terrorize the Zaporozhye Region.
"The movement of personnel is virtually completely blocked, both from the outside, from the Novorossiya highway toward the city, and for employees, who work at the ZNPP and reside within the city limits or in neighboring settlements," he said.
"Their transit to and from work - elementary things - has become virtually impossible," Chernichuk added.

title: Harry Brook smashes fastest ODI double century and breaks Shubman Gill's record
body: Harry Brook broke a number of records as he smashed a double century in a tri-series match against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. Brook hit 202 off just 116 balls to help England post a mammoth 429-4. It was the first time an England batter had hit an ODI double century. Not just that, Brook's maiden ODI double century was also the fastest 200 in the format's history – from 114 balls – breaking record of India captain Shubman Gill who had scored one off 127 balls last month against the West Indies. On Thursday, Brook cracked 21 fours and 10 sixes to reach the milestone in the final over of the innings. The England captain also became only the second batter in history, after Caribbean great Chris Gayle, to hit a Test triple century, ODI double ton and T20 hundred. Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. The moment Harry Brook brought up his double 💯 💥 Fastest double hundred in ODI history and the highest individual ODI score on Pakistan soil 🏏 #SLvENG | #CricketKaJashan pic.twitter.com/WcJM6TvBm0 — Pakistan Cricket (@TheRealPCB) October 22, 2026 Brook's scintillating knock ended with the final ball of England's innings when he ​was caught by ‌Sahan Arachchige off ⁠the bowling of ​Janith Liyanage. Joe Root provided good support with 69 from 66 balls, ​finishing as England's second-highest scorer of the day. Will Jacks finished unbeaten on 66 off just 30 deliveries. It was the highest score ever conceded by Sri Lanka and the biggest total scored in Pakistan. Brook is already among top five Test and T20 batters and should now find himself in the top 10 in ODIs as well. The right handed batter has emerged as one of the best batters in the world, and among the few all-format players.

title: Ogun schools shut again as toxic gas sends over 100 pupils to hospital
body:
Schools in parts of Ogun State have been forced to close on Wednesday after more than 100 pupils were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure to an offensive gaseous substance, renewing concerns over recurring emissions in the Ijebu part of the state.
The affected pupils are from schools in ljebu Ode, Ago Iwoye and ljebu Igbo and were taken to the State Hospital in Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital in Ijebu-Igbo and other health facilities after some reportedly experienced breathing difficulties and fainted.
Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode and Itamerin Comprehensive High School in Ago-Iwoye.
The Ogun State Government, in a statement by the Special Adviser to Governor Dapo Abiodun on Information and Strategy, Kayode Akinmade, said it has involved relevant authorities to intensify investigations into the incident, saying the situation is under control.
“Findings from the affected students and information provided by the attending doctor revealed that the symptoms after inhaling this odour included shortness of breath, stomach disorders and drowsiness, among others,” the statement read.
Kehinde Bello, a senior special assistant to Mr Abiodun and general manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, also linked the latest occurrence to the underground gas emissions previously reported in the area.
Mr Bello said the government believed the phenomenon was associated with geological and tectonic fault lines rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. He assured residents that the government would work towards a lasting solution and said affected pupils were expected to recover after receiving medical attention.
According to the Punch report , a teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly, said the incident began at about 10am on Wednesday, when pupils and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties.
“Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day around 11am. when the situation was becoming horrible and unbearable,” the teacher said, adding that some parents also rushed to pick up their children amid uncertainty over the source of the emissions.
The latest incident is the fourth reported occurrence of gaseous emissions affecting schools in the Ijebu area since April, despite previous investigations and assurances by the state government that it was working to establish the source.
In April, about 30 pupils and a teacher were hospitalised after a similar incident at Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School in Ijebu-Ode. In May, more than 100 pupils and teachers were reportedly affected in another occurrence, while a June incident led to 69 pupils being hospitalised.
Following earlier incidents, the state government said preliminary monitoring had detected elevated methane levels in the affected area.
In May, the Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said air-quality monitoring equipment had recorded peak readings of about 13,500 parts per million in surrounding locations.
The government subsequently announced plans for a multi-agency assessment to investigate the source of the emissions and assess possible exposure risks.
In June, the government also disclosed that investigators were examining possible links to an underground rock fracture and a gas pipeline located several kilometres from the affected schools. At the time, officials said the investigation was ongoing, and the pipeline was reportedly shut temporarily pending further inquiries.
The repeated incidents have heightened anxiety among parents, pupils and school staff, with a teacher calling on the government to establish the precise source of the emissions and prevent further exposure.

title: Russia’s Shnaider through to quarterfinals of 2026 WTA Ningbo Open tennis tournament
body:
BEIJING, October 22. /TASS/. Russia’s tennis star Diana Shnaider reached the quarterfinals of the 2026 Ningbo Open tournament in China by defeating on Thursday Alexandra Eala from the Philippines.
In the match that lasted for 1 hours 55 minutes the 6th-seeded Russian, who is playing under a neutral status at the tournament, defeated unseeded Eala in straight sets 7-5; 6-4 and is now set to play in the quarterfinals round against 4th-seeded Iva Jovic from the United States.
It was the first-ever encounter between Shnaider and Eala at WTA tournaments and speaking after the match the Russian player said: "You expect the slice serve into the body, definitely a little more variation and a different type of ball strike."
"You just gotta get used to the ball - I guess the first few games you just get used to the spin, where are her strengths, what is her weakness," the official WTA website quoted Shnaider as saying after her match against Eala.
"You just gotta give yourself a little more time to adjust, then it becomes a bit easier as the games go on," she added.
Shnaider, 22, is currently ranked 13th in the WTA Rankings. She holds five WTA titles. Her best result in Grand Slams was reaching the semis at 2026 French Open. At the 2024 Summer Olympic Games in Paris, she captured a silver medal in women’s doubles with partner Mirra Andreeva.
The 2026 Ningbo Open is the WTA 500 class tournament played on hard courts at the Yinzhou Tennis Center in China on October 19-25 and it offers $1.2 million in prize money. Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina is the tournament’s reigning champion.
On February 28, 2022, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) issued recommendations to international sports federations to exclude athletes from Russia and Belarus from taking part in international tournaments, citing Moscow's special military operation in Ukraine as the reason.
Following the IOC's recommendations in late February 2022, the majority of global sports federations decided to exclude athletes from Russia and Belarus from all international sports tournaments.
The International Tennis Federation (ITF) ruled on March 1, 2022 to suspend the membership of the Russian and Belarusian national tennis federations while also scrapping all previously scheduled tennis tournaments in the two countries.
On March 14, 2022, the ITF also confirmed its prohibition on the Russian and Belarusian national tennis teams from taking part in the 2022 Davis Cup and 2022 Billie Jean King Cup.

title: Regions Calling: More Questions Than Answers After Latest Black Sea Oil Spill
body:
Hello and welcome to Regions Calling , your guide to developments from beyond the Russian capital by The Moscow Times.
In this week’s edition, we are putting the spotlight on the southern Krasnodar region , home to Russia’s vast Black Sea coast, which is reeling from the environmental fallout of a Ukrainian drone attack on the Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio tanker — while officials have offered few details.
For more of the latest news from the regions, subscribe to our biweekly email newsletter here or on Substack .
On the evening of Oct. 6, apocalyptic photos of a thick plume of smoke rising from the burning sea against a bright dusk sky flooded the Russian internet.
These images showed the result of one of Ukraine’s most successful drone attacks on the energy infrastructure along Russia’s Black Sea coast as the 247-meter, Liberian-flagged Afromax Rio oil tanker had been hit off the shore of the resort city of Sochi.
Environmental specialists were quick to sound the alarm over the fire's potentially catastrophic consequences, saying its ecological impact could exceed that of the massive 2024 spill near the resort city of Anapa, which left beaches coated in heavy fuel oil and mobilized thousands of volunteers.
Two weeks after the attack, as locals find oil-covered birds and pollution builds up along the coast, there are still more questions than answers.
“I would be a bad expert if I were to outline the [exact environmental] consequences right now,” one prominent environmentalist told The Moscow Times. “Why? Because it is not known how much oil has spilled as a result of this attack. And that is the main problem.”
Though regional authorities initially denied that the attack had caused an oil spill, Krasnodar Governor Venyamin Kondratyev warned of a potential emergency in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk one week after the attack.
The regional Emergency Situations Ministry also said it “detected minor oil spills” along the shoreline near Novorossiysk last week, but denied they were linked to the Aframax Rio.
The environmentalist, who requested anonymity for safety reasons, said officials’ reluctance to publicize details of the attack’s environmental impact comes amid mounting evidence of a spill and contradicts Russian legislation that “prohibits classifying information about the environment and environmental pollution.”
The Afromax Rio was towed to Novorossiysk, Russia’s largest Black Sea port, the day after the attack — a move decried by prominent local environmental campaigner Tatiana Tribat, who pointed to the already heavy environmental burden borne by the city.
Satellite images analyzed by Greenpeace showed the damaged vessel leaving an oil slick that covered around 25 square kilometers by Oct. 8.
Independent environmental monitor Prozrachny Mir also dentified an oil slick stretching along the coast from Novorossiysk toward the town of Arkhipo-Osipovka some 70 kilometers (43 miles) south in images dated Oct. 10.
Meanwhile, residents of Novorossiysk, Sochi and smaller coastal towns along the tanker’s route have reported finding oil-covered birds and traces of pollution washing ashore.
“Every day we receive reports [of contamination] from Yuzhnaya Ozereevka, Limanchik, Dyurso and elsewhere. If it wasn’t the Aframax Rio that fouled the coastline, then who is responsible for the pollution?” Tribat told a local newspaper.
For coastal residents who remember the Anapa disaster, the images were causes for concern. Yet evidence available from local media and volunteers “suggest that the spill from Afromax Rio was, in fact, significantly smaller” than that disaster, the environmental expert told The Moscow Times.
The Anapa spill happened in December 2024 when two Russian-flagged oil tankers were damaged during a storm, releasing over 9,000 tons of heavy fuel oil, known as mazut, into the Black Sea. Pollution from the spill stretched from annexed Crimea to Georgia, though Russia’s Krasnodar region was hit the worst.
“What we see now is incomparably smaller coastal pollution,” the Russia-based expert said.
“Back then, hundreds — even thousands — of birds were affected. In this instance, the number is in single digits. Back then, about 60 kilometers [37 miles] of coastline was covered in…a continuous strip of fuel oil,” he said.
Though the Afromax Rio can carry up to 100,000 metric tons of oil — nearly 10 times the combined load of the two tankers that caused the 2024 Anapa spill — this leak’s less pronounced impact on the environment is likely the result of the apocalyptic fire documented in the initial images.
“Of course, burning oil pollutes the air, then the combustion products…fall into the sea,” the expert said. “But this amount of damage and consequences are incomparable to what would have happened if all that oil poured out unburnt into the sea.”
Authorities reopened beaches affected by the 2024 Anapa spill this summer, but the disaster is far from over.
Images analyzed by satellite imagery monitor Sky Eye in July identified a fresh oil slick coming from the sunken bow of the Volgoneft-239 tanker in the Kerch Strait.
Meanwhile, authorities have long denied any ongoing leaks coming from the wreckage — sometimes in statements accompanied by photos of divers emerging from inspections covered in oil.
The consequences of the Afromax Rio spill could be shorter-lived, as some reports suggest authorities have already started pumping the remaining oil out of the tanker.
But the ongoing war in Ukraine, which has seen an escalation in maritime drone activity in recent months, means that a new oil disaster threatening the Black Sea’s ecosystem could be just around the corner.
“In recent months, Ukraine has significantly intensified its attacks on civilian vessels [in Black Sea], including tankers. While there do not appear to have been any major spills…some level of pollution has nonetheless occurred,” the expert said.
“And yet no damage from a military strike can compare to a disaster caused by negligence of officials and vessel operators, corruption and the like — which is precisely what led to the 2024 accident,” he said.
Authorities in the Far East port of Vladivostok removed a statue of Nobel Prize-winning writer Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn from the city’s central embankment on Tuesday to relocate it to the city outskirts.
Vladivostok city hall had ordered the Soviet dissident’s statue to be relocated earlier this year after deeming its presence among the warships “inappropriate.”
But just a day later, the 2.5-meter-tall monument reappeared on the embankment after it was found to be too large for its new location. It is unclear if the authorities will proceed with the plan after this week’s mishap.

These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .

title: Kremlin spokesman weighs in on upcoming trilateral talks with Ukraine
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. At this point, Abu Dhabi is considered the main platform for trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine, Russian Presidential Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov said.
In a comment to Vesti journalist Pavel Zarubin, the spokesman said Vladimir Zelensky can hardly redeem himself for Ukraine’s current neo-Nazi policies even by invoking memories of his grandfather fighting against Nazi Germany in World War Two.
Below are the Kremlin spokesman’s key remarks.
Abu Dhabi is now being considered as a venue for trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine: "At this point, we are talking about Abu Dhabi."
"Wait, you are getting ahead of yourself, do not do that," the Kremlin spokesman said, when asked to comment on whether Russia’s negotiating team was preparing any written documents or proposals.
Zelensky’s recollection of his grandfather, a veteran of the Great Patriotic War, strangely coincided with the worsening of Polish-Ukrainian relations triggered by Kiev’s neo-Nazi policies and the halting of arms deliveries: "It coincided with the climax of the scandal between Poland and Ukraine. The city council of Lvov passed a resolution declaring this to be the year devoted to an infamous Nazi military unit."
"This is what triggered the scandal. It was hushed up somehow, but Poland has already halted weapons deliveries in protest against Nazi manifestations. Simply highlighting this contrast will be a sufficient comment on Zelensky’s remarks."
Zelensky is trying to redeem himself through this recollection: "Since we are constantly speaking about neo-Nazi manifestations in Ukraine and the need to eradicate them, he is probably trying to ‘redeem’ himself in some way."
"But this is hardly possible in light of current events in Ukraine.".

title: Mandatory evacuation of children extended to all areas of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities
body:
Vadym Filashkin, head of the Donetsk Regional Military Administration, announced this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“We are expanding the mandatory evacuation zone for families with children—it now covers all settlements in the Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities… The lives of children are an absolute priority,” the regional head wrote.
He noted that the security situation in this area is constantly deteriorating; the Russians are attacking Kramatorsk and Sloviansk daily, striking residential neighborhoods, civilian vehicles, and areas where people are gathered.
“Staying there with children is an unjustifiable risk. I appeal to parents: do not put your children in danger, and do not wait until a Russian strike hits near your home. Evacuate now,” Filashkin emphasized.
He added that specialized police and State Emergency Service units are involved in this evacuation, and upon arrival at the transit point, families will receive assistance with their onward relocation to safer regions of Ukraine.
As previously reported, as of October 15 , approximately 71,300 civilians remained in the Ukrainian-controlled territory of Donetsk regio n, 60,000 of whom were located in areas of active combat operations across 21 territorial communities.

title: Russia kept sneaking troops through gas pipes behind Ukrainian lines. Now Ukraine has gone more than 15 km underground to do the same to Russia
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine's Defense Forces advanced more than 15 km through underground utility tunnels into Russia's rear on the Kupiansk axis in Kharkiv Oblast, the Khartiia Corps of Ukraine's National Guard reported on 22 October. The corps called it Operation Veles. The underground advance was paired with attacks on the surface and drone strikes, hitting Russian forces from two directions, the corps told Militarnyi. Russian troops have repeatedly crawled through gas pipelines around Kupiansk to get behind Ukrainian lines, even after Ukraine reported confident control of the city in February. This time, Ukraine went underground itself. The operation took away Russia's chance to get into Kupiansk's rear, the corps said . The corps reported more than 30 Russian soldiers captured and Russian losses of more than 100. Militarnyi, citing the unit, put the number of Russian troops killed at over 100. Khartiia studied how Russian troops moved through pipes before going underground itself, the corps commander, Brigadier General Ihor Obolenskyi, said. "We watched how the enemy works underground and studied how they do it. The Russians intended to use gas pipelines to get into the rear of our troops. So we went underground ourselves. We anticipated the enemy's actions and mastered the tactics of underground combat," he said. Boots under ground! Asymmetric breakthrough in the Kharkiv Region: Khartiia Corps conducts the subterranean counteroffensive Operation VELES, advancing 15 km underground. Corps Commander General Ihor Obolenskyi explains a unique operation. pic.twitter.com/qRQ93kckpK — Khartiia Corps in English (@khartiia_eng) October 22, 2026 For the operation, troops trained physically and psychologically to fight in confined spaces, sappers and engineers prepared the underground route, and special communications, navigation, silent logistics, and life-support systems were put in place, Khartiia told Militarnyi. The operation was named after Veles, the Slavic pagan god of the underworld. Khartiia's brigade, the R.U.H. assault regiment, the Lava drone regiment, the Achilles drone brigade, and units of Ukraine's military intelligence, including the Freedom of Russia Legion and the Russian Volunteer Corps, took part, the corps said . Russia has used pipelines to infiltrate before By September 2025, Russian forces had used pipelines to move troops behind Ukrainian lines three times, Ukrainian monitoring project DeepState reported on 12 September 2025. The first was in Avdiivka, the second near Sudzha, and the third near Kupiansk, where groups crossed the Oskil River through a gas pipe. Near Sudzha in March 2025, Russian special forces walked through a pipeline that until recently had carried Russian gas to Europe, the Associated Press reported . A pro-Kremlin blogger claimed they covered about 15 km and that some spent several days inside. Russian troops kept using the pipeline near Kupiansk this year. On 27 September, Khartiia's reconnaissance drones recorded Russian forces leading nine civilians, including children, elderly people, and a person on crutches, through the gas pipeline out of the Kupiansk community. Men of military age in civilian clothes walked alongside them, and the corps believes they were Russian soldiers using the group as cover to withdraw. Ukrainian troops held fire because of the civilians, the corps said, adding that the case has been documented for a war crimes investigation. Civilians led through a gas pipeline out of the Kupiansk community, Kharkiv Oblast, by people the Khartiia Corps identifies as Russian forces, 27 September 2026. Screenshot: Khartiia Corps Why the war is moving underground Drones, constant surveillance, and AI-assisted targeting have made the battlefield surface transparent and deadly, argue John Spencer, chair of urban warfare studies at West Point's Modern War Institute, and Col. Drew Craig, principal military engineering staff officer at NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. In an August analysis , they write that soldiers in Ukraine describe a "death zone" of some 30 km, where moving above ground can draw an attack within minutes. When firepower makes the surface too dangerous, armies have historically gone underground, as they did in World War I and Vietnam, and more recently in Gaza and Lebanon. "Armies that cannot survive above ground must adapt below it," the authors write. Fighting in tunnels brings its own requirements, the authors write: detecting the enemy by sound and vibration, and specialized unmanned systems that cannot rely on GPS or stable radio links. Long stretches underground also take a severe psychological and physical toll on soldiers. Western militaries are not ready for this, Spencer and Craig write. No NATO partner maintains even general capabilities for large-scale underground warfare, and US and British efforts focused mainly on detecting and clearing tunnels rather than occupying and operating in them. title: Finns Party unveils €8b cuts list, spares small pensions
body:
The Finns Party has presented its wish list for the next four years.
The Finns Party on Thursday presented its cuts list for the next parliamentary term, amounting to eight billion euros in cuts, plus a further one billion in other measures, including taxes.
The package is the party's plan for meeting the ' debt brake ' that the majority of parliamentary parties agreed upon earlier this year. The next government will decide the actual savings in coalition talks after next April's parliamentary elections.
The savings would hit areas such as immigration, social security, the wellbeing services counties and development aid, while small pensions would be spared.
The new levies include a higher tax on data centres as well as a sugar tax. The party would also impose an index brake on pensions above 2,000 euros a month in 2028-2031, with pensions below this threshold spared.
"We will address immigration significantly, especially by reforming social security," Finns Party leader Riikka Purra said, adding that the party still wants to make the entire social security system citizenship-based at some point in the future.
The party would also raise income thresholds, restrict social security, end humanitarian immigration, and abolish the refugee quota and municipal integration compensation.
The party would eradicate Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, which would free up some one billion euros. Purra said this is a capital transfer, not a saving, and the money would go to growth measures and reforming basic education.
"In the spirit of Sitra, the sum would be used for the future of Finns. In other words, for growth measures and especially for reforming basic education," Purra said.
The Ministry of the Environment and the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) would be merged into other state administration, and the National Agency for Education abolished, saving 10 million euros.
Public broadcaster Yle would lose 200 million, and its index linkage would be removed.
Parliamentary group leader Jani Mäkelä said development cooperation would end entirely.
"New commitments will be ended and existing commitments will be terminated as far as is possible, however, within the coming parliamentary term."
Support for Ukraine, crisis aid and disaster relief would be unaffected.

title: Western partners view Ukraine’s defense industry as collection of individual manufacturers due to lack of state strategy – Zaluzhny
body:
Western partners perceive Ukraine’s defense industry not as a cohesive system, but as a collection of separate manufacturers, because the state lacks a unified policy, a national strategy, and long-term funding for the sector. This was stated by Valeriy Zaluzhny, Ukraine’s Ambassador to the United Kingdom and former Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (2021–2024), during the fourth annual export forum hosted by Ekonomichna Pravda in Kyiv on Wednesday.
According to him, any defense sector rests on three core pillars: research and personnel training, production, and controlled operation—all of which must be supported by a unified state approach. Currently, Ukraine has around 500 manufacturers, each independently pursuing development within its own narrow niche.
"Is this really how we should describe the perception of the Ukrainian defense industry? Let’s be honest: we are viewed merely as a group of manufacturers trying to push their own specific products under various guises. I can tell you, as a citizen of Ukraine, that this no longer resembles what one would typically call an 'industry,'" Zaluzhny remarked.
He emphasized that, given the lack of independent resource backing and technological capabilities, Ukraine’s defense sector will likely follow a "niche" model. Under this approach, the country would focus on meeting specific, targeted needs essential for achieving victory—in part through cooperation with foreign partners.
"Clearly, given that we have certain achievements but lack the necessary technological capabilities and resources, we will likely adopt a 'niche' model, filling specific niches essential for achieving our political objective: ultimately, Ukraine’s victory in the Russia-Ukraine War. For instance, the British could supply the Ukrainian defense industry with missile engines, while another nation might provide space-related capabilities, and so on," he said.
As previously reported, Zaluzhny expressed skepticism regarding the possibility of a rapid breakthrough for Ukraine’s defense-industrial complex into foreign markets. He noted that the large-scale export of domestic weaponry and technology is complicated by the absence of relevant military doctrines among NATO member states, as well as the fact that many new technologies are still in the developmental stage.

title: Russia-US-China summit could be little Yalta, former Italian PM says
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. A potential trilateral summit between Russia, the United States and China in the Chinese city of Shenzhen could become a second Yalta conference, Italy’s former Prime Minister and ex-president of the European Commission Romano Prodi argued.
"Everybody is talking about the Shenzhen meeting next month, a meeting of great powers <...>. This could become a meeting where rules for the future will be set and red lines that must not be crossed will be laid down. I’d jokingly call it a 'little Yalta,'" Prodi said, addressing the XIX Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
He repeatedly described excluding Europe from global geopolitical and economic processes as a mistake, arguing that the United States, Russia and China would have no interest in this for the sake of a balance further down the road. At this stage, Prodi admitted, Europe is being left out because of internal fragmentation and weaknesses. According to him, Europe and Russia have grown apart because of external pressure, while the Ukraine conflict has made the divide seemingly insurmountable for now.
Earlier, US President Donald Trump proposed holding a trilateral meeting in China with his Russian and Chinese counterparts, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, respectively. Kremlin Aide Yury Ushakov told reporters on October 21 that Putin discussed the possibility of holding trilateral talks with Trump and Xi at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, scheduled for Shenzhen on November 18-19, during a meeting with US special presidential envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday.

title: Black Stars qualifying for AFCON 2027 will be a ‘miracle’ – Laryea Kingston
body: Former Ghana international Laryea Kingston believes the Black Stars could miss out on qualifying for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) for the second time in a row. According to him, the results after two games make it difficult for Ghana to bounce back and get into the conversation to qualify for the tournament to be staged in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. Ghana sit bottom of the group after no points from their two games against Cote d’Ivoire and Gambia, losing to the latter at the Accra Sports Stadium despite taking a two-goal lead. The Black Stars, who are hoping to return to the continental tournament after missing the last edition, have a doubleheader against Somalia up next in the qualifying series but Kingston believes Ghana making next year’s tournament will be a miracle. “Looking at the situation now, it will be a miracle for us to qualify,” he told 3Sports. “Two teams have six points; it means Ghana will have to win all games. For me, it will be very difficult, and it will take a miracle to turn things around.” The Black Stars have failed to win an AFCON qualifier since September 2023 and failed to register a victory in the qualifiers for the last edition of the tournament.

title: Humanitarian mission carried out in Belarus to reunite Russian, Ukrainian families
body:
MINSK, October 22. /TASS/. A humanitarian mission to reunite families from Russia and Ukraine was carried out in a border area of Belarus on Thursday, the BelTA news agency reported.
According to the report, 11 people crossed into Ukraine via the Novaya Guta border crossing to reunite with their families, while another three traveled to Russia.
While in Belarus, members of the group, which included elderly people and people with disabilities, were provided with hot meals before continuing their journeys.

title: High Court dismisses Mustapha Hamid’s application to travel abroad amid OSP trial
body: The High Court has dismissed an application by former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) CEO Mustapha Hamid seeking permission to travel abroad while standing trial in a case involving allegations of extortion in the petroleum sector. The application by Hamid, the first accused in the case of The Republic v Mustapha Hamid & 7 Others, was opposed by the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP). In its ruling on Thursday, October 22, 2026, the Court held that an accused person on bail whose movement is restricted must demonstrate compelling reasons for the restriction to be temporarily lifted. The Court found that the grounds presented by Hamid did not justify granting the request and consequently dismissed the application. Hamid, a former Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) and former Minister for Information, is standing trial alongside seven others over allegations of extorting money from players in the petroleum sector. The accused persons had previously applied to have the charge sheet struck out, but the Court dismissed the application, allowing the pre-trial process to continue. The proceedings have also seen disagreements over scheduling, including an earlier adjournment request by Hamid’s lead counsel, Joseph Kpemka, which the Court rejected. The trial is expected to proceed with the case management conference. Following the latest ruling, Hamid’s movement restrictions remain in place, subject to any further orders by the Court.

title: Normalization of Russia-US ties underpins European development — senior diplomat
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. Normal relations between Moscow and Washington are, contrary to what the West’s current ruling elites believe, a fundamental prerequisite for Europe’s peaceful development, as only with security and predictability between Russia and the US can Europeans become an independent pole of power, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said, addressing the Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
"Strange as it may seem, the West’s current ruling elite views the prospect of better or healthier Russia-US ties as one of the key threats to its own security," the senior diplomat noted. "Even from the standpoint of formal logic and the history of the continent’s development, normal relations between the US and the USSR, between the US and Russia are a fundamental condition for Europe’s peaceful development and, I would like to add, for its prosperity in the multipolar world."
If Europe continues to live amid geopolitical tensions between the two great powers, its political, economic, military and other weight will decrease exponentially, Grushko said. "And only under conditions of security and predictability can Europeans fulfil their potential as an independent pole of power," he noted.

title: Closing arguments set in trial of man accused of killing UNC student in 2012
body:
Closing arguments are expected in the trial of a man accused of killing a North Carolina college student 14 years ago
Closing arguments are scheduled for Thursday in the trial of a man accused of killing a North Carolina college student 14 years ago.
Faith Hedgepeth was a 19-year-old sophomore at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill when she was beaten to death in her off-campus apartment in September 2012. Miguel Salguero Olivares was arrested nine years later after being pulled over for driving while intoxicated and providing a DNA sample that prosecutors say matched evidence from the crime scene.
He has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder, rape and burglary charges.
Testimony began Oct. 7 following eight days of jury selection. Salguero Olivares did not testify and his attorneys rested their case Wednesday without calling any witnesses. Nearly two dozen witnesses testified for the prosecution, including Hedgepeth’s roommate and other friends, crime scene technicians, state and local law enforcement and a DNA expert.
Early testimony focused on Hedgepeth’s life and her last night alive, when she and her roommate returned home from a club around 2 a.m. Karena Rosario testified that she was drunk and sick when Hedgepeth drove them home but later called a friend to pick her up and she went out again, leaving Hedgepeth in the apartment alone. She returned hours later that Sept. 7 to find Hedgepeth’s body.
An autopsy showed Hedgepeth suffered extensive skull fractures and cuts to her face and head, and she was also badly beaten on her arms and legs.
Prosecutors allege Salguero Olivares, now 33, was a stranger who killed Hedgepeth in a fit of rage. They said his DNA was found on a rum bottle covered in blood that investigators identified as the weapon in the killing, in Hedgepeth's body and on a note written on a fast-food bag found at the scene.
Erin Ermish, a forensic scientist with the state crime lab, testified that she could never say with 100% certainty that a DNA sample came from a particular person. But she said DNA swabbed from Hedgepeth’s body was 170 septillion times more likely to be a mixture of DNA from Hedgepeth and Salguero Olivares than from Hedgepeth and an unknown individual. One septillion is a 1 followed by 24 zeros. In contrast, NASA estimates the entire universe contains only 1 septillion stars.
Ermish also said the mixture of DNA from the top of the rum bottle was 48.6 tredecillion times more likely to be from Hedgepeth and Salguero Olivares than from two unknown, unrelated individuals. One tredecillion is a 1 followed by 42 zeros.
In cross-examining witnesses, defense attorneys questioned Rosario’s account of that night, the processing of the crime scene and the reliability of some DNA evidence. They pointed out that police failed to search some areas of the apartment and later lost some possible blood evidence.
Several jurors cried after viewing autopsy photos of Hedgepeth, according to local media accounts. Salguero Olivares, meanwhile, cried when prosecutors played video of a jailhouse call between him and a friend who has since died.
The story has been updated to correct the spelling of Faith Hedgepeth’s last name in one reference.
Ramer reported from Concord, New Hampshire.

title: Communist Party Leader in Komi Republic Arrested for ‘Justifying Terrorism’
body:
Russian law enforcement authorities have arrested former State Duma lawmaker from the Communist Party Oleg Mikhailov on charges of publicly justifying terrorism, his regional party team said Wednesday.
Mikhailov has headed the Communist Party branch in the northern republic of Komi since 2014 and served as a State Duma member between 2021 and September 2026. In last month’s parliamentary elections, he lost his seat to a rival from the ruling United Russia party.
Komi’s Communist Party branch said in a social media post that Mikhailov was arrested at a Moscow airport after returning from a vacation.
The charge against Mikhailov of publicly justifying terrorism stems from old social media posts in which he allegedly supported jailed sociologist Boris Kagarlitsky and leftist activist Sergei Udaltsov .
“We believe the charges are revenge by Goldshtein and United Russia,” the party wrote on the VKontakte social media platform, referring to the regional head of Komi, Rostislav Goldshtein.
A court hearing where a judge will decide whether to place Mikhailov in pre-trial detention is scheduled for Thursday. He could face up to seven years in prison if found guilty.
Mikhailov’s arrest follows the August detention of Communist Party firebrand Nikolai Bondarenko in the southern Saratov region on “extremism” charges over an old social media post featuring a photo of the late opposition activist Alexei Navalny.
