title: Germany arrests Ukrainian national suspected of spying for Russia
body:
Germany's Federal Criminal Police arrested a Ukrainian citizen in the state of Brandenburg, surrounding Berlin, for suspected espionage on behalf of a Russian intelligence agency, Germany's Federal Prosecutor's Office said on Oct. 22.
The suspect, identified as Vadym Y., was arrested in the Oder-Spree district of Brandenburg a week after an investigating judge issued a warrant on Oct. 15, the prosecutor's office said .
Vadym Y. had been in contact with Russian intelligence through an interlocutor since at least July 2025, the prosecutor's office said. He allegedly collected relevant information in connection with Russia's war against Ukraine, including on the production of armored vehicles, ammunition, and explosives, as well as on military personnel and facilities on NATO's eastern flank.
While some of the information was publicly available, according to the prosecutor's office, the suspect allegedly also obtained details by deliberately approaching people working in the European defense industry.
The information on the suspected spy comes primarily from Germany's domestic intelligence service (BfV).
This incident comes a day after Germany's military for the first time classified Russian sabotage threats against its troops and facilities as "significant," German news outlet Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported on Oct. 21.
Reviewing internal documents from Germany's armed forces, Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported that this is the military's second-highest threat classification.
"We are noting that we face a ​significant sabotage threat overall for [Germany's armed forces]," said a defense ministry spokesperson, according to Reuters.
Germany's reclassification of Russian threats comes as experts warn Russia is testing how far it can push Europe without triggering open war — from drones crossing NATO airspace to sabotage and cyberattacks across the continent. Europe has strengthened its defenses since 2022, but key gaps remain, including in air defense, communications, intelligence, and joint command, experts say.
On Oct. 5, Martin Jaeger, head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, told lawmakers that Germany is in a "shadow war" with Russia and risks being drawn into a violent conflict with Moscow.

title: Senior diplomat sees no Russia-EU normalization without radical changes to bloc’s policies
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. Discussing any normalization between Russia and the European Union (EU) cannot take place without radical changes to the policy course being pursued by Europe which is preparing for war, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said, addressing the XIX Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
"There can be no discussing any bringing our relations back to normal without radical changes to the EU’s current foreign policy course in which the economy, military construction, military planning, weapons purchases, the situation in society and the preparation of society pursue the sole task of preparing for war with Russia and actually waging a hybrid war already today," the senior Russian diplomat argued.
"Today, the demonization of Russia and the Russian threat, given the crisis the European Union itself is facing, is effectively the only thing that keeps these EU countries in some kind of tense unity."

title: FG launches five-year plan to eliminate lead poisoning
body:
The federal government has launched a five-year strategic plan to eliminate lead poisoning in Nigeria, with a focus on strengthening prevention, surveillance, regulation and coordinated action against exposure.
The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, announced the plan in Abuja on Wednesday during the commemoration of the 2026 International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, themed “From Detection to Prevention”.
Lead poisoning occurs when lead, a toxic heavy metal, accumulates in the body over time.
There is no known safe level of lead exposure, and even low levels can harm human health, particularly in children. Exposure can damage the brain and nervous system, impair learning and development, and increase the risk of cardiovascular and kidney diseases.
Mr Salako described lead poisoning as a major public health and environmental challenge, identifying children, pregnant women and women of childbearing age as particularly vulnerable groups.
Sharing strategies, Mr Salako said the government was moving beyond identifying cases to tackling lead exposure at its source.
He highlighted the establishment of the Inter-Agency Working Group on Lead Poisoning Prevention and Elimination to strengthen collaboration among ministries, departments and agencies, as well as development partners.
Citing experiences in Lagos, Ogun, Sokoto and Zamfara states, the minister said interventions must be tailored to local sources and pathways of exposure.
“At the subnational level, we have identified the development of state-specific lead prevention and control action plans for Lagos, Ogun, Zamfara and Sokoto States as an important next step,” he said.
“These plans will reflect the specific sources and pathways of exposure within each of the states while remaining aligned with the national framework.”
He said finalising the Lagos State action plan was particularly important, as it was informed by assessments of blood lead levels and children’s environmental health.
According to the minister, the five-year plan provides a framework for multisectoral action, including environmental and occupational surveillance, improved laboratory capacity, stronger regulation and enforcement, and clearer referral pathways for people with elevated blood lead levels.
He added that a three-year national roadmap was being developed to translate the strategic plan into measurable interventions.
Mr Salako called on state governments, development partners, industries, civil society organisations, professional bodies, traditional and religious leaders, and the media to support the plan’s implementation.
He also urged Nigerians to take preventive measures, including avoiding contaminated soil and dust, using lead-safe products and observing safety precautions during battery recycling and painting.
Other measures he recommended included keeping work clothes away from living areas, wet-cleaning floors and children’s play areas, and maintaining diets rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C.
Mr Salako said the Federal Ministry of Health and Social . was committed to leading efforts to shift Nigeria’s response to lead poisoning from a reactive approach to a comprehensive, preventive and sustainable strategy.

title: 2027: PRP alleges multi-million naira plot to break its ranks, sabotage opposition coalition
body: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) has alleged a plot by senior members of the ruling party to destabilise its ranks, sabotage its grassroots structures and undermine efforts to build a credible opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party said the alleged scheme involved hundreds of millions of naira to compromise its officials, exploit former members and create divisions capable of weakening its electoral fortunes. In a statement by its National Chairman, Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, the PRP alerted its members and the public to the alleged plot, warning supporters against inducements to work against the party. It alleged that some disgraced former members were being deployed to create the impression of internal division, while strategically placed party officers were being used to undermine its grassroots support. The PRP specifically warned against attempts by unauthorised persons to recruit polling agents in its name, urging members to resist and expose any financial inducements intended to divert their support. “The persons in the governing party involved in this scheme have been advised to steer clear of the PRP and distance themselves from attempts to create a fictional PRP with their party’s funds and their names,” the statement said. The party warned that serving officers found to be involved would face disciplinary action, insisting that neither financial inducements nor internal sabotage would make it abandon its political commitments. “The leadership of the PRP wishes to assure its candidates and Party supporters that it will not sacrifice their commitments and loyalty at any price,” Baba-Ahmed said. The PRP said it remained committed to challenging the continuation of the Tinubu administration beyond 2027 and playing a role in building a potentially winning opposition coalition. title: Uganda steps up Ebola screening at airport as Nigeria heightens vigilance
body: Uganda has intensified Ebola screening at the Entebbe International Airport following reports that a woman who tested positive for the disease transited through the airport earlier this month. The Ministry of Health said this in a post on X on Wednesday, adding that its Permanent Secretary, Diana Atwine, had visited the airport to reinforce public health screening procedures. Atwine also conducted a spot inspection at the airport’s border entry point to assess screening arrangements and identify potential gaps. The ministry said it had received thermal scanners donated by the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) to strengthen screening at key points of entry as part of efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola. It said Uganda had no confirmed active Ebola cases following reports that the woman had transited through Entebbe International Airport. According to the ministry, the woman travelled to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) for business before passing through Uganda in early October. She reportedly showed no symptoms while in Uganda but developed them after arriving in Nigeria. NAN reports that Nigeria’s health authorities have confirmed an imported Ebola case involving a woman who arrived in Abuja after travelling from Uganda. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) confirmed the diagnosis through laboratory testing. The case has prompted heightened public health vigilance, including efforts to trace contacts and strengthen surveillance to prevent further transmission. Ebola is a severe viral disease that can spread through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, or with contaminated materials. Early detection, prompt isolation and contact tracing are critical to containing outbreaks. Nigeria previously recorded an Ebola outbreak in 2014 after an infected traveller arrived in Lagos from Liberia. The country contained the outbreak through coordinated surveillance, contact tracing and infection prevention measures. (Xinhua/NAN)

title: Elbit Systems Expands Underwater and Maritime Autonomy Capabilities with Acquisition of ISE
body: Elbit Systems Ltd. has completed the acquisition of International Submarine Engineering Ltd. (ISE), a Canada-based company specializing in advanced autonomous underwater and remotely operated systems for the maritime domain. The acquisition was completed for a purchase price that is not material to Elbit Systems. Elbit Systems press release Headquartered in the Vancouver area, ISE is a high-technology company engaged in the development and manufacture of undersea vehicles, including Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) and Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), as well as computer control systems and robotics. With more than 50 years of experience in subsea robotics, ISE has delivered over 250 underwater vehicles to customers in more than 20 countries worldwide. Elbit Systems ’ naval portfolio includes unmanned surface vessels, underwater systems, integrated command-and-control (C2) suites, electro-optical and sonar systems, communications and electronic warfare technologies. Through its subsidiaries and global centers of excellence, Elbit Systems delivers proven naval capabilities supporting missions ranging from coastal security to blue-water operations. The addition of ISE’s underwater autonomous technologies is intended to expand Elbit Systems’ capabilities in underwater Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), Mine Counter Measures (MCM) and Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), further strengthening the Company’s end-to-end maritime offering. “This acquisition marks another milestone in Elbit Systems’ strategy to expand its offerings in the naval domain. Combined with our existing capabilities in naval electronic warfare, autonomous systems, naval precision munitions and maritime mission systems, ISE’s underwater technologies will further strengthen our position as a global provider of comprehensive, integrated maritime solutions.” Bezhalel (Butzi) Machlis, President and CEO of Elbit Systems – End – The post Elbit Systems Expands Underwater and Maritime Autonomy Capabilities with Acquisition of ISE appeared first on Naval News .

Apple is rolling out a new badge in the App Store to indicate whether an app is optimized for its new foldable. The new “Made for iPhone Duo” badge will appear across apps and games that work with the device’s extra screen real estate.
Though Apple doesn’t include an image of what this badge might look like, it highlighted some of the ways apps are taking advantage of the Duo’s inner and outer screens. Netflix, for example, will display shows and movies that take up the whole inner display, while allowing you to watch its feed of short-form clips on the outside. Amazon’s Prime Video will let you watch shows and movies with the Duo partially folded, with the content on top and details about the cast on the bottom.
Meanwhile, Apple says Microsoft Word and Outlook will offer a “desktop-class” experience on the Duo, with Word placing its formatting tools alongside a document, and Outlook displaying your inbox next to a full email. Zoom can also display a video conference alongside shared content across the iPhone Duo’s inner screen. Other apps optimized for the Duo include Paramount Plus, NYT Cooking, Yelp, Lyft, and United Airlines. But, as The Verge ’s Nilay Patel found during his Duo testing , some apps “optimized” for the device, like Instagram, still have some bugs.
Apple says it’s going to launch editorial collections for the iPhone Duo on Friday, “with additional app updates rolling out throughout the year.” The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and launches on Friday, with “limited” quantities available on a walk-in basis .

Following a decade-long saga of delays, name changes , and Atari having to assure backers of a crowdfunding campaign that its retro console wasn’t doomed , the Atari VCS platform is being retired early next year. On February 1st, 2027, the Atari VCS software store is shutting down, according to an announcement posted to the Atari Club Discord and shared by Tom’s Hardware .
With a design loosely inspired by the original Atari 2600 — minus a cartridge slot — the VCS was a Linux-based, AMD-powered mini PC that could emulate a large collection of pre-loaded classic Atari games, but its functionality could be expanded through an online software store that included access to streaming platforms and, in recent years, game streaming platforms like Xbox Cloud Gaming and Nvidia GeForce Now.
Atari VCS owners will still be able to download and add software to their libraries through Atari’s official online store up until January 31st, 2027. After that, the store will officially shut down, but previously downloaded apps and games will still be usable. Atari says that following the store’s closure it plans to “make an OS update available that allows you to migrate all functionality to your local machine, removing any dependencies on Atari infrastructure for authentication and software.” The company also plans to release an Atari Home Brew app allowing owners to continue to add new games to their console’s library shared to the community by third-party developers who still want to develop and support the VCS.

title: Ukrainian OSINT analyst: Russia’s Yandex data center in Sasovo burned out inside, though its roof shows almost no significant holes
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russian tech giant Yandex's data center in Sasovo burned out from the inside, a Ukrainian OSINT analyst wrote on 22 October. On cloud-free satellite images, he saw almost no significant holes in its roof. Ukrainian drones hit the site overnight on 8 October. Sasovo was the first strike on a data center in Russia. It came two weeks after Russia destroyed data centers in Kyiv. Drones then hit Yandex sites in Vladimir and Kaluga, a Sber data center, and a VK data center near St. Petersburg , which VK acknowledged. In occupied Donbas, monitoring channels reported hits on buildings housing telecom operators. What the analyst sees The analyst, who goes by Harbuz, runs the Ukrainian OSINT channel Dnipro Osint. His roof reading comes from the images. His interior claim comes from what he called available information: he wrote that a fire broke out inside and put part of the equipment out of action. Cloud-free satellite image of the damaged Yandex data center in Sasovo, Ryazan Oblast, posted 22 October 2026. Image: Dnipro Osint In an earlier post , Harbuz wrote that a third of the data center had burned out. In the new one, he writes that the building burned out from the inside. He does not say whether he revised the earlier figure. Russian outlet Agentstvo studied Airbus images from 12 October. It found damage on about a third of the building. Unlike Harbuz, though, Agentstvo described a blackened western roof with damage resembling holes. What Yandex says On 8 October, Yandex stated that the attack caused a fire and forced it to suspend operations at the site, which hosts tens of thousands of servers, Reuters reported . Yandex Cloud and the Disk and Documents services that run on it ran with major disruptions that morning, Russian outlet The Bell reported . Later that day, the company stated: "The scale of the damage to the infrastructure is still being assessed. For the moment, we cannot confirm whether it is possible to restore the data centre equipment in Sasovo." Two of Yandex's three supercomputers, used to develop its AI model, are housed there. The same day, journalists asked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy whether Ukraine was targeting Russian data centers. He did not refer specifically to the Yandex strike, Reuters noted , but said: "We always respond in mirror-like fashion." title: Number of Ebola infections in DR Congo surpasses 9,700
body:
PRETORIA, October 22. /TASS/. The number of laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 9,700, the National Institute of Public Health, which is part of the DRC Ministry of Health, reported.
"The number of people infected with Ebola has reached 9,704. The death toll stands at 4,687, with a case fatality rate of 48.3%," it said.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Communications and Media Affairs reported that 937 patients with symptoms of the disease were receiving treatment in hospitals and medical isolation centers. The contact tracing rate for infected people is 76.9%.
The Ebola outbreak began on May 15 in the DRC and Uganda and became the second-deadliest in Africa since records began. Cases and deaths have been reported in eight provinces of the DRC. On July 28, Ugandan authorities announced that the outbreak had ended. On August 25, the World Health Organization confirmed the announcement. On October 6, Kenyan authorities reported the country’s first Ebola case. On October 20, Nigeria’s Ministry of Health reported the first confirmed case of Ebola infection in the country.

title: Ebola: Africa CDC urges African ownership, accountability in outbreak response
body:
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has urged African governments to take greater ownership of disease outbreak responses, invest in their health systems and hold development partners accountable as the continent battles the Ebola virus outbreak.
The agency’s Director-General, Jean Kaseya, said governments must ensure that non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and other partners receiving donor funds were accountable to national authorities and aligned their activities with government-led response plans.
Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Mr Kaseya said stronger African leadership and coordination were essential to containing outbreaks and preventing future health emergencies.
“We need to invest in our own system,” Mr Kaseya said.
Mr Kaseya said the Africa CDC declared the outbreak a regional and continental concern on 15 May because of the risk of cross-border transmission.
He explained that while an outbreak confined to one country fell primarily under that country’s authority, an outbreak affecting multiple countries required a coordinated regional response.
“When we have an outbreak in one country, it is the sovereignty of the country. But when we have it in more than one country, it becomes the mandate of the Africa CDC,” he said.
He said insecurity, humanitarian challenges and population movements in the area where the outbreak began informed the agency’s assessment.
According to him, the affected area was a mining hub where the movement of people increased the likelihood of the virus spreading across borders.
Mr Kaseya said Nigeria was not among the countries initially identified as being at risk because the outbreak was then concentrated in the eastern and central parts of Africa.
Nigeria’s first confirmed case has since heightened concerns about the country’s preparedness and the need for effective surveillance, contact tracing and infection prevention.
Mr Kaseya called for greater accountability from international organisations and NGOs involved in outbreak responses, particularly those receiving funding from external donors.
“We don’t want to see NGOs and partners getting money from donors and not being responsible vis-à-vis the government. That one would never happen again in Africa,” he said.
He said governments must ensure that all organisations involved in an emergency response work under a unified plan established by national authorities.
Mr Kaseya argued that stronger coordination would help ensure resources were directed towards urgent needs and that governments maintained oversight of response activities.
He cited funding commitments following a meeting with African heads of state, supported by development partners, as an example of efforts to strengthen African ownership.
He also referred to a task force convened by Nigeria’s president on Wednesday, which he said had decided to provide funding for the outbreak response.
However, he warned against focusing on blaming international partners rather than addressing the weaknesses exposed by the outbreak.
“Otherwise, if we want just to blame our partners, we will not resolve any issue,” he said.
Nigeria confirmed its first case of Ebola virus disease on 20 October, prompting health authorities to activate response measures.
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has been coordinating surveillance and other public health interventions to limit the risk of further transmission.
PREMIUM TIMES previously reported the NCDC’s warning about the risk of the virus being imported into Nigeria following cases reported in East Africa.
The risk of cross-border spread has highlighted the importance of regional surveillance and cooperation, particularly as people travel between countries for work, trade and other activities.
According to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 related deaths as of 19 October, based on data available up to 18 October.
Kenya had also reported nine confirmed cases, including one death, as of 20 October, following an imported case involving a person who had travelled from the DRC through Uganda.
Uganda recorded 20 cases between May and June. The WHO declared the outbreak there over on 25 August after 42 days without a new confirmed cases.
Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola virus disease that can cause severe illness and death. It spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.
There is currently no licensed vaccine specifically approved for Bundibugyo virus disease, making early detection, isolation, contact tracing and infection prevention central to outbreak control.
Mr Kaseya said African countries must use the current outbreak to strengthen their health systems and establish clearer accountability among governments and their partners.

title: Neither Russia nor Belarus wants war, but must be ready for it — Lukashenko
body:
MINSK, October 22. /TASS/. Neither Russia nor Belarus wants a war on their western borders, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said during a meeting with Russian Defense Minister Andrey Belousov.
"We are preparing for war, but are trying to avoid it in every possible way. No one wants it. But we should always be prepared so that it does not happen," Lukashenko said, according to the Pul Pervogo Telegram channel, which is close to the presidential press service.
"That is why our joint group of forces on the western flank will always be necessary, and today it is fully operational," the Belarusian leader added.

title: Zelensky: Russia used three ballistic missiles with cluster warheads in attack on Kyiv
body:
According to Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky reported this on Facebook .
“There were reports on the cleanup efforts following the Russian attacks on our cities and communities. Last night, the Russians launched, among other weapons, three ballistic missiles with cluster warheads against Kyiv. What makes these missiles unique is that they explode in the air as they approach their target, striking everything within a 400-meter radius,” Zelenskyy said.
According to him, one of these missiles struck Pechersk—the historic center of Kyiv—specifically the area between the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra and the Holy Vvedensky Monastery. The strike damaged monastery buildings, homes, stores, cafes, and other civilian infrastructure in the city.
“This is yet another extremely telling strike—telling in that it is not accidental. It is a deliberate choice of weapon, a deliberate choice of target area, and a deliberate attempt to inflict as many casualties and as much damage as possible on civilians. There wasn’t even a single military facility nearby, even in theory, and the weapon was designed to cause widespread destruction. Russia has not changed its approach to waging this war and is not taking any steps that might indicate a genuine desire to stop the war,” Zelenskyy emphasized.
He added that air raid alerts and strikes continue throughout the day in Kyiv and many other cities. In Kharkiv, a commuter train was hit. Dnipro, Marhanets, Mykolaiv, Kherson, and cities and villages in the Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Donetsk, Kharkiv, Chernihiv, and Rivne regions were all targeted.
Attacks on the energy sector continue. Since October 11, there have been more than 170 strikes on critical energy infrastructure—and this, Zelensky noted, despite the fact that a significant portion of the “Shaheds” and some of the missiles are being shot down. The president thanked all of Ukraine’s friends who are helping with the restoration of the energy sector.
“We know from our intelligence that the Russians have set priorities for further terror against Ukrainians in the coming weeks. Clearly, Russia is taking advantage of the slowdown in the delivery of air defense systems from our partners. And it is equally clear that the easing of pressure on Russia by certain partners only convinces Putin that his goals are seemingly achievable. We need different signals, different steps—stronger ones,” Zelensky emphasized.
He instructed the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense, together with the military command and the Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to inform partners about all aspects of the actual situation and existing threats, based on information provided by intelligence agencies.
“It is important to expedite the delivery of defense aid packages that have already been agreed upon. Thank you to all the leaders and countries that are helping!” Zelensky noted.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian invaders launched strikes on 12 regions on the night of October 22, killing two people and injuring 34.

title: Death toll from Israeli attacks on Gaza reaches 74,498
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 22 (MNA) – The Israeli regime’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,498 people and injured 175,616 since October 2023.
The Israeli regime's genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,498 people and injured 175,616 since October 2023, the enclave’s Health Ministry says.
Since the so-called “ceasefire” in October, the Zionist regime has killed 1,538 Palestinians and wounded 5,498.
In the latest 24-hour reporting period, four people were killed and 12 injured, it added.

title: FCT police arrest SUV occupant over fake presidency plate
body: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man after intercepting a Lexus LX570 SUV allegedly bearing a concealed presidential number plate in Maitama District, Abuja. The vehicle was intercepted at about 8pm on October 20, 2026, with the occupant taken into custody for investigation and possible prosecution, the police said. The command’s spokesperson, SP Josephine Adeh, said preliminary investigations revealed that the concealed number plate bore the inscription “PRESIDENCY” and registration number 10B218 FG. Adeh said further investigations, following the suspect’s claim that he was the legitimate holder of the plate, allegedly revealed that the registration documents were forged. She added that the suspect was also allegedly impersonating a permanent secretary attached to the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation. “Investigations are ongoing, and the suspect will be charged to court upon their conclusion,” the police spokesperson said. The command urged residents to remain law-abiding, cooperate with police operations and promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station. It provided the following emergency contact numbers for reports: 08032003913 and 08061581938. The post FCT police arrest SUV occupant over fake presidency plate appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Pizza Fan Owner and Employees Arrested in €25 Million Greek VAT Probe
body: Greek authorities have arrested the owner and several employees of Pizza Fan, one of Greece’s largest pizza delivery chains, as part of an investigation into alleged tax fraud involving at least €25 million in unpaid value-added tax (VAT). Nine people were arrested during a large-scale police operation on Thursday, October 22, targeting an alleged criminal organisation suspected of manipulating sales records to conceal revenue and evade tax payments. According to Greek media reports, the suspected scheme had been operating since 2022 and involved a nationwide network of approximately 140 stores. Pizza Fan owner among nine arrested The arrests were carried out by Greece’s Directorate for Combating Organised Crime, commonly referred to as the “Greek FBI”. Those taken into custody reportedly include Pizza Fan owner Konstantinos Antaras, a senior company executive, accountants, a computer programmer and several store managers. Investigators are examining the alleged roles of those involved and how transaction records may have been manipulated to reduce the company’s declared taxable revenue. The allegations have not been established in court, and the investigation remains ongoing. More than €500,000 in cash seized During searches of business premises and private residences, authorities reportedly seized more than €500,000 in cash, luxury vehicles, jewellery and other evidence believed to be relevant to the investigation. The operation involved the Financial Crimes Investigation Subdirectorate, working alongside Greece’s Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) and the police’s Directorate of Criminal Investigations. Authorities are continuing to examine the evidence to determine the full extent of the suspected tax evasion and whether additional individuals were involved. The investigation centres on alleged VAT liabilities of at least €25 million, although the final amount and the responsibilities of those arrested will depend on the findings of the authorities and any subsequent court proceedings. title: Information Minister: Media must avoid temptation to sacrifice accuracy for speed
body: Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has urged the media to rise above sensationalism, misinformation, unsubstantiated allegations and the temptation to sacrifice accuracy for speed, for commercial advantage ahead of the 2027 general elections. Idris made the call at Media Trust’s corporate office in Abuja, during the launch of the company’s Converged Newsroom, on Thursday. Speaking at the event, the minister said that the National Values Charter under the Ministry of Information and National Orientation, championed by the National Orientation Agency, reinforces the importance of integrity, responsibility, patriotism, and mutual respect. PRP alleges plot to weaken opposition coalition ahead of 2027 2027: Don’t sell your votes, Islamic scholars warn Nigerians He added that the aim is to inspire a media culture that promotes national cohesion without compromising the independence and critical scrutiny essential for journalism to thrive. He urged the Media Trust Group to make the convergence a center of innovation, investigative excellence, and responsible storytelling. He said the months ahead will undoubtedly witness an intensification of political activities accompanied by competing claims and counterclaims that must be subjected to rigorous fact-checking. Idris said, “With less than 90 days to our election, we will see much of that coming into play. At moments such as this, journalism must rise above sensationalism, misinformation, unsubstantiated allegations, and the temptation to sacrifice accuracy for speed, for commercial advantage, or even for narrow parochial interests. There is a need for journalists and media players to have a deep reflection, especially at a moment like this.” He noted that while press freedom must be protected, it is also important that the right atmosphere be created for journalists to thrive and for them to have a sustainable business. He said, “For media organizations to function optimally and discharge their duties and responsibilities, the business models that they depend on must be sustainable in the face of challenging times, in the face of technology, and also in the face of consumer expectation. Any business model of any newspaper or any media organization that is not responsible for this will certainly face extinction.”

title: Protection of Union State borders, gratitude to Russia: Lukashenko’s statements
body:
MINSK, October 22. /TASS/. Neither Belarus nor Russia needs a war in the western direction, President of the republic Alexander Lukashenko told Russian Defense Minister Andrey Belousov.
He said that Belarus is fulfilling its obligations to protect the borders of the Union State.
Lukashenko also thanked Russia for its assistance in organizing monitoring with the use of various technical means along the borders of the Union State, as well as those with Ukraine and Western countries.
TASS has compiled the key statements made by the president of Belarus.
Neither Minsk nor Moscow wants a war on their western borders: "We are preparing for war, but we are trying to avoid it in every possible way; neither we nor you need it. But to prevent it from happening, we must always be ready. This is why our joint forces in the western direction will always be needed, and it is in order today."
Belarus adheres to its obligations to protect the borders of the Union State: "The Belarusian army is fulfilling its role. We are fulfilling all our obligations from the Russian side to Belarus and from Belarus to Russia.
"Our opponents - we probably don't have any enemies here yet - they know about it, they see it. We have good cooperation in other departments and areas. This is why you don’t need to worry about our obligations to protect the borders of the Union State.".
Belarus is grateful to Russia for its assistance in organizing monitoring using various technical equipment along the borders of the Union State and along the borders with Ukraine and Western countries: "And you have them [such means], given the conflict in Ukraine, very advanced. Radars and the like. Russian experience was taken into account, and there are many Russian tools."
The Union State controls the entire territory along the border: "And that’s about 3,000 km, if you take the West and Ukraine into account. Of course, it must be protected by control and surveillance systems. We’re doing a good job here."
Control of the Union State’s borders with Ukraine and the West was discussed with Russian President Vladimir Putin: "President Putin and I have recently considered this topic at a meeting. He did a good job, he made a promise, he said: ‘We’ll help you with this, we’ll help you with that.’ We’ll need that. And we see that we do need it."

title: WATCH: President Herzog hosts ceremony commemorating 31 years since Rabin's assassination
body: President Isaac Herzog called for the assassin of former prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, Yigal Amir, to spend the rest of his life in prison without any possibility of pardon or a reduced sentence, warning on Thursday that growing tolerance of political violence threatens Israel's existence as a Jewish and democratic state.Speaking at a memorial ceremony marking 31 years since Rabin's assassination, Herzog condemned public calls for Amir's release and warned against the continued incitement and threats directed at elected officials in Israel."Thirty-one years do not constitute a cooling-off period for the murder of a prime minister. The passage of time does not diminish the severity of the crime," Herzog said."The national imperative that must be passed from our generation to those that follow is clear and unequivocal: The murderer must never be released. He must spend the rest of his life in prison. He must never receive any reduction of his sentence or any form of pardon. This must not be challenged under any circumstances."Herzog described his shock at encountering a billboard calling for Amir's release while driving on Highway 1 between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, saying the public must not dismiss such messages as ordinary political provocation."The very possibility that such a call could appear in a public space and be met with a shrug of indifference should keep us awake at night. We must not dismiss it as just another provocation," he said.The president warned that calls to release Amir reflected the danger of Israeli society gradually losing its absolute rejection of political assassination.His remarks come amid renewed controversy over public campaigns advocating Amir's release. In August, an activist was hospitalized after an altercation while removing a sign calling for Amir's freedom, highlighting the tensions surrounding the issue.Herzog warns political violence threatens Israeli democracyHerzog said Rabin's assassination was not simply the murder of a political leader but an attempt to overturn democratic decision-making through violence."The despicable murderer did not aim his weapon at Yitzhak Rabin alone. He aimed it at the heart of the nation," he said."The murderer of the prime minister sought to place his weapon above the will of the people, to resolve a disagreement through violence, through murder, threatening our very existence here as a Jewish, democratic, and sovereign state."Herzog emphasized that the assassination represented a threat to Israel's democratic institutions and that the lessons of the murder remained relevant more than three decades later."He murdered our beloved Yitzhak Rabin. We lost our leader. And we came perilously close to losing ourselves," he said.The president also criticized the continued circulation of threats against politicians and other elected officials, including on social media."Thirty-one years after that horrific assassination, there are still people in the State of Israel who dare to utter, or type on their keyboards, appalling threats to murder elected officials, whoever they may be," Herzog said."Others settle for 'merely' inciting political violence against their opponents."He called for an unequivocal rejection of violence across the political spectrum, arguing that its normalization could endanger the state itself."There is no place for political violence in a properly functioning state. There is no place for violence, period."Thirty-one years since Rabin's assassinationRabin was assassinated on November 4, 1995, after addressing a peace rally in Tel Aviv's Kings of Israel Square, subsequently renamed Rabin Square.The Jewish calendar date of the assassination is Heshvan 12, which this year falls on Thursday, October 22, and Friday, October 23.Amir, a Jewish extremist who opposed the Oslo Accords between Israel and the Palestinians, shot Rabin as he was leaving the rally. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment, along with additional prison time for related offenses.The possibility of Amir's release has periodically resurfaced in Israeli public discourse. In 2023, right-wing commentator Ari Shamai publicly called for Amir to be freed, sparking controversy and prompting Channel 14 to announce that he would no longer appear on its broadcasts."Three bullets. Three bullets fired 31 years ago sought to destroy the State of Israel, the Third Temple," Herzog said.Concluding his address, Herzog said the memory of Rabin's murder must serve not only as a tribute to the former prime minister but also as a continuing warning against political extremism."The candle we light here is a memorial candle for prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, a great leader who loved his people and was murdered by a criminal," he said."But it must also serve as a warning light. A warning drawn from that terrible tragedy, a warning that echoes the lesson that must remain before us and be passed down from generation to generation."Addressing the Rabin family, Herzog said the passage of 31 years had done little to diminish the national trauma or the sense of loss."Even after 31 years, the shock has not subsided. But 31 years have done nothing to ease the longing," he said."Yitzhak will forever remain in our hearts."

title: Ukraine’s population falls to 28.5 million, demographers say
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Ukraine’s population fell to 28.5 million as of mid-2026, the News.Live TV channel reported, citing Ella Libanova, head of the Ukrainian Institute of Demography and Social Research.
"A couple of days ago, we completed a population estimate for the middle of the year. The figure stands at 28.5 million. We have recently lost half a million people who left the country," she said.
Meanwhile, other experts have offered even lower estimates. Economist Alexey Kushch claimed that the country’s population was approaching 20 million. Former Ukrainian Prime Minister Nikolay Azarov cited the same figure in an interview with TASS.

title: Russia and Ukraine exchange bodies of fallen soldiers
body: Russia and Ukraine conducted another exchange of fallen soldiers’ bodies, the Russian business news outlet RBC and BelTA reported. The exchange took place at the Novaya Guta checkpoint in Belarus, where Russia returned 252 bodies to Ukraine and Ukraine handed over 25 fallen soldiers’ bodies to Russia. Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War confirmed the exchange. It was the first such exchange in more than a month. The two sides last swapped bodies of fallen soldiers on September 17, when Russia handed over 252 and Ukraine handed over 23. The two sides last exchanged prisoners of war in August, when 10 POWs returned to Russia and Russia handed over to Ukraine 10 civilians who had been detained in Belarus for legal violations. title: Terrorism: Court jails man 40 years for spying for late Benue militia leader
body: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced a man, Sunday Frank, to 40 years in prison after he confessed that he served as a spy for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana. Gana, who reportedly began as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, was killed in September 2020 by security operatives. In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents. It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states. Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release. He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader. Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted. Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant. He mounted the witness box and reviewed the facts of the case. The witness, simply identified as “AAA” after the court gave the FG permission to shield his real name, said the defendant had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana. He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons. According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written. The FG’s application to tender the statement in evidence was not opposed by the defence lawyer, Mr Y. Y. Shullai. Consequently, trial judge Hawa Yilwa admitted and marked the defendant’s statement as Exhibit A. The witness further told the court that his team investigated the defendant’s activities and filed a report. The report was tendered and admitted as Exhibit B. In his submissions, the AGF stressed that, in view of the defendant’s confession and the exhibits, he should be convicted on count 4 of the charge, to which he pleaded guilty. The AGF described the offence as very serious, noting that the law prescribes a punishment of at least 20 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. “I urge my lord to hand down a sentence of not less than 30 years. This is a very serious offence. “If it is not nipped in the bud, a whole generation of our security operatives can be wiped out by people like this providing information about their movement,” the AGF added. He further drew the court’s attention to the fact that count 4 of the charge related to section 13 of the TPPA. The defence counsel, who is from the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN), said he was not opposed to the AGF’s submissions. Therefore, Justice Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 40 years in prison, starting from the day of his arrest. The court held that the convict should, upon completing his prison term, be subjected to a rehabilitation and deradicalisation programme. The case is part of the ongoing mass trial of detained terror suspects. The post Terrorism: Court jails man 40 years for spying for late Benue militia leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: FG urges media to tell inspiring stories about Nigeria
body: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has urged Nigerian media organisations to give greater prominence to stories that highlight the country’s achievements and inspire national unity, saying journalism should not focus exclusively on criticism and negative developments. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, made the call on Thursday at the launch of the Media Trust Converged Newsroom in Abuja. Idris said positive stories showcasing Nigeria’s progress could also make newspaper headlines, urging journalists to use their platforms to promote national unity and inspire hope, particularly among young people. He described as a misconception the notion that journalism must always be adversarial, stressing that the media could hold public institutions accountable while reporting developments that encourage national aspirations. “Every headline does not always need to be critical. You need a headline that inspires us as a nation, a headline that promotes unity and headlines that inspire aspirations in our young people,” he said. Speaking at the unveiling of the artificial intelligence-powered newsroom, the minister described the initiative as a significant milestone in the evolution of Media Trust Limited, one of Nigeria’s established media organisations. He congratulated the management and staff of the company on the investment, noting that it had grown from modest beginnings into a multimedia organisation comprising Daily Trust, Aminiya, Trust TV, Trust Radio and digital platforms. According to him, integrating the organisation’s various platforms into a converged newsroom would enable it to deliver credible information seamlessly across print, broadcast and digital channels. Idris urged Media Trust to make the facility a centre of innovation, investigative journalism and responsible storytelling, capable of highlighting national challenges, celebrating achievements and contributing to informed public discourse. The minister also emphasised the importance of fact-checking, warning that advances in artificial intelligence, including AI-generated content and manipulated videos and images, had made information verification increasingly critical. On the 2027 general elections, Idris said the credibility of Nigeria’s democratic process depended partly on the integrity of the information available to voters. He urged journalists to uphold fairness, transparency and accuracy, avoid sensationalism and unsubstantiated allegations, and clearly distinguish facts from opinions and fiction in election-related reporting. The minister reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to press freedom, describing the media as an indispensable partner in national development and democratic governance. In his remarks, Jigawa State Governor, Mallam Umar Namadi, commended the Media Trust Group for its contributions to national development, noting that the organisation provided livelihoods for many Nigerians. Namadi urged media professionals to maintain the ethical standards of the profession and deploy their platforms to promote national unity. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Media Trust Group, Mallam Kabiru Yusuf, recalled that the organisation was established in Kaduna State in 1998 and had since recorded significant growth, including its transition from print journalism to media convergence. Yusuf urged media professionals to uphold fairness in their dealings with everyone, including those who considered them adversaries. He acknowledged that the organisation was not perfect but said it remained committed to maintaining professional standards. The post FG urges media to tell inspiring stories about Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Inside the institution where Ukraine races to counter Russia's evolving drones
body:
From a Canon camera to a magnetometer, wreckage reveals how Russian weapons keep advancing and why Ukraine’s countermeasures struggle to keep pace.
A Ukrainian soldier inspects the remains of a Russian Geran drone in a cornfield in Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine, on Oct. 12, 2026. (Jakub Laichter / The Kyiv Independent)
In a government office, researchers of drones and electronic warfare gather around a small metal device recovered from a Russian Geran drone. Its purpose — to measure the Earth’s magnetic field for navigation.
"This is the most recent component we found, about a week or two ago," said one of the researchers.
Outside, a Russian drone’s jet engine roared — a sound that has become almost constant in Kyiv in recent months as advances in drone technology allow Russia to strike farther, more often and with greater precision. The small metal sensor on the table could make that threat even more vicious.
If it works as the researchers suspect, it could keep drones on course even when their satellite navigation is jammed, making the prospect of a winter under near-constant Russian attack even grimmer.
The researchers work at an institution under Ukraine’s Defense Ministry, and its work is rarely seen by outsiders. Here, specialists dismantle Russian weapons recovered from the battlefield or attacks to identify vulnerabilities, help develop countermeasures, and anticipate what Russian engineers might try next. The Kyiv Independent was given rare access on the condition that neither the institution nor the people inside be identified.
Their work is a race against time. The researchers estimate that developing an effective countermeasure usually takes four to six months, while Russia can introduce further modifications after two or three.
Regarding the sensor they found — in technical terms called a magnetometer — the researchers said they were still investigating its purpose and whether Russia might deploy it at scale.
But finding a new component is not the same as understanding it, and understanding it is not the same as having a way to counter it. And the Russian engineers who put the magnetometer in the drone face a similar gap. Fitting it to a handful of drones is not the same as being able to deploy it at scale.
Inside the institution, the fluorescent-lit hallways were filled with pieces of missiles, drones, fuzes, and motherboards, all neatly organized and labeled. People move in and out, some in camouflage, others in jeans and plain shirts, some carrying paperwork, others pieces of military hardware.
There is the nose of a North Korean missile , taller than a grown man, and a large section of a Russian Oreshnik missile, its cylindrical body roughly as wide as a passenger car. On the other side of the hallway were several Russian Geran drones, their triangular bodies resembling black paper airplanes enlarged to more than three meters long (9.8 feet), with wings spanning roughly three meters.
Outwardly, the Russian Gerans still resemble the Iranian drones Russia began using to terrorize Ukrainian cities in the fall of 2022. Inside, however, successive modifications had made them markedly different from those early aircraft, and even from the first Russian-made Gerans that appeared by the summer of 2023.
To trace the drones' evolution, the researchers work backward from the ones they recover. They begin by identifying and documenting each drone’s basic features, then dismantle it to map its internal systems, trace its components to their manufacturers, and reconstruct how each part contributes to the aircraft’s operation.
The researchers explained that changes inside the drones often reflected the success of Ukraine’s defenses. A navigation system that had once guided an aircraft to its target could become vulnerable to jamming, prompting Russia to try something else.
"When the Russians see that the effectiveness is decreasing, they introduce other technologies," one researcher said.
But the two sides don't take turns. Russia can introduce another modification while Ukraine is still working out how to defeat the previous one.
On one of the tables lies a Canon camera recovered from one of the first iterations of Russian drones from late 2022 used for attacks on Ukrainian cities. Still in its original casing, it looked much as it would in a shop, except that its settings had been glued in place against the vibrations of flight.
The next example they recovered a few months later, a Sony, had been stripped of its casing, leaving its lens and colorful wiring exposed. "You can already see that it’s quite a development compared to the first sample," a researcher said.
Such details helped the specialists judge how far an adaptation had progressed. You can tell a lot from the workmanship and the way it’s put together, one researcher explained. Specialists look for whether a part was improvised and attached to a drone or whether the drone was built to carry it — a sign that an experiment might be entering regular production.
Sometimes the clue is simpler. Sometimes there are letters "E" or "EE" on a drone’s tail fins, which the researchers believe stands for "experiment."
Other clues had been deliberately erased. The researchers showed antennae chips with their identifying markings scratched off, an effort, they said, to hide the supply chains bringing American and European electronics into Russian weapons despite sanctions .
"Removing markings does not make identification impossible," one researcher said. But it can turn what might have been a glance at a label into an investigation requiring specialized equipment and scarce time.
Reconstructing Russian technology can take months or even years, hampered by a lack of specialized equipment, resources, and expertise in Ukraine, and even with help from foreign partners, some electronic components remain nearly impossible to decipher without access to manufacturers’ proprietary information, which they are often unwilling to share.
Hanging in the stairwell was a completely intact Geran-3 that had reached the institution in 2025, well before this autumn’s urgent calls to accelerate production of interceptors capable of catching jet-powered drones . It had run out of fuel and landed in sand without detonating.
At its rear was a silver jet engine, roughly the size of a large melon, replacing the propeller-driven engine that gave earlier iterations of these drones their familiar moped sound. Faster flight and higher operating altitudes made jet-powered variants harder for mobile teams armed with machine guns to engage.
A message written on the black body of the drone in white marker read "greetings to Serhii from the engineers." The researchers believed it was addressed to Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov, an adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky on defense technology. One researcher found a small consolation: the Russians had misspelled "engineers."
The same recovered aircraft had carried another indication of what was coming this summer beyond the jets: a camera and a mesh modem. "(That meant it was) able to send back video footage and receive control signals," a researcher said.
The researchers have a collection of the palm-sized mesh modems in their office, which they identify as Chinese-made. Mesh modems allow drones to relay video and control signals through one another, extending communications beyond an individual aircraft’s direct connection to its operator.
One researcher compared the technology to repeaters used to extend Wi-Fi coverage through a house. Here, the repeaters are other drones. This allows operators to change targets during flight and pursue even moving targets, such as trains , rather than simply sending a drone toward fixed coordinates, the researchers said.
The video feed allows the Russian operator to watch a civilian building draw closer while continuing to steer the drone toward it. He is far from the people inside but can see who he is targeting.
"If it is a civilian site, he knows what he is hitting and how," one researcher said.
The institution has possessed evidence of Russian attempts to implement jet engines and mesh relays since last year. But what a single recovered aircraft could not establish last fall was how soon or whether at all the same hardware would appear in large numbers.
Half a year later, it did. Since this summer, jet-powered drones have targeted Ukraine, particularly Kyiv, on a daily, constant basis, with the sound of explosions a regular occurrence in the capital throughout the day.
The researchers described the interval before an effective response to a modification became available as a "window of opportunity" for Russia. Once a change proved useful, Russia could concentrate resources on producing and deploying it while Ukraine was still developing a countermeasure.
"They don’t wait for us to come up with a countermeasure," one of the researchers said. The engineers attribute this problem mostly to scale. Russia likely has institutions similar to theirs, just several times larger with more resources.
The magnetometer the researchers recently recovered was still at an earlier stage of their investigation. "We can’t say for sure what it is, until we’ve completed all the necessary research," one said.
It might prove a modest refinement rather than a breakthrough. To become a widespread threat, its integration would need to be refined and its production scaled up.
But even a slight edge could be enough, helping more aircraft stay on course and tilting the balance of the war further in Russia's favor.
Jakub Laichter is a defense tech reporter at the Kyiv Independent. Before joining the Kyiv Independent, he reported from Eastern Ukraine as a freelance photojournalist since 2019.

title: DOCUMENTARY: Daily Trust; From Print To Multimedia
body:
A bereaved husband and five other persons conveying his wife’s corpse from Kano State to her hometown in Okpoga, Okpokwu Local Government Area of Benue State, have been abducted by armed men along Adoka Road in Otukpo LGA of the state.

Witnesses said that the incident occurred on Friday at about 8pm when the mourners, who had travelled from Kano, were approaching their destination, barely an hour drive from the scene of the attack.

Some residents of the area, alleged that they woke up to discover an abandoned corpse on the middle of the road and, upon closer inspection, realised that the occupants of the vehicle conveying the deceased had been whisked away by the attackers.

They alleged that officials of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) arrived at the scene on Saturday morning, evacuated the corpse and deposited it at a morgue in Adoka town.

 	Police gun down 2 suspected kidnappers, recover AK-47 in Delta

When contacted, the FRSC Information Officer, Ahula, said the officials were in a meeting but promised to obtain details of the incident and get back to our correspondent.

Meanwhile, an Idoma social media influencer, Meddy Olotu, claimed to have spoken with members of the bereaved husband’s family, who disclosed that the kidnappers had opened communication and were demanding N15 million for the release of the six abducted persons.

Olotu said the victims were intercepted and taken away while the corpse was abandoned at the roadside in their own homes state by the abductors after travelling all the way from Kano, just as the family members were preparing to receive the corpse for burial.

“They were heading to Okpoga to bury their dead when they were intercepted along Adoka road. The family members said they were in touch with the husband of the deceased and his friends until they lost communication with them while they were traversing the Adoka axis,” he said.

Confirming the incident, the Chairman of Otukpo LGA, Prince Maxwell Ogiri, acknowledged that the abduction took place along Adoka road, describing it as unfortunate and traumatic.

“Yes, it happened. Incidentally, the driver of the vehicle is my friend. This is the unfortunate incident we are witnessing. The kidnappers are demanding N15 million.

“But the security agencies are working to ensure that the kidnapped victims are rescued,” the chairman told journalists in Makurdi by telephone.

The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), DSP Peter Aondongu, also confirmed the incident, saying it occurred on Friday and that efforts were ongoing to rescue the victims.

title: Ukraine kills over 500 people in Zaporozhye Region since 2022 — Russian Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. More than 500 civilians, including 23 children, have died in the Zaporozhye Region from the actions of Ukrainian militants between now and February 2022, Rodion Miroshnik, Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Foreign Ministry for Issues Related to the Crimes of the Kiev Regime, told the international teleconference "Zaporozhye Region: Escalation of the Terrorist War by the Armed Forces of Ukraine."
"According to preliminary data, between February 2022 and October 20, 2026, 508 civilians were killed by Ukrainian militants in the Zaporozhye Region, which is under Russian control. These are only verified data. This includes 23 minors," the diplomat said.
"At the most conservative estimate, 2,207 people were injured. Of these, 114 are minors."

title: Pentagon ignored cybersecurity flaws before data breach, Marines’ lawsuit says
body: A pair of Marines filed a class-action lawsuit Tuesday against the Pentagon over a data breach at the Defense Manpower Data Center, or DMDC, arguing it allowed scammers to obtain and use their personally identifiable information, or PII. In the complaint filed in federal court in the District of Columbia, Marine veteran Tristyn Edwards and active-duty Marine Morgan Stampfli allege that they experienced fraudulent charges on their financial accounts and an increase in spam messages because of the breach. In September, the DMDC said it had discovered a vulnerability on July 16 in a file-sharing system that allowed unauthorized users to access unencrypted files containing personal information, including full names, Social Security numbers, birth dates and military occupations. According to the lawsuit, the vulnerability exposed millions of files containing information on service members and people affiliated with the military for approximately nine months before it was discovered. The lawsuit also alleges that the DMDC failed to “promptly notify” affected individuals, some of whom were informed two or three months after the breach was found. “The exposure of Plaintiff and Class members’ PII will cause various types of misuse in the coming months and years, including but not limited to, unauthorized credit card charges, unauthorized access to email accounts, identity theft, and other fraudulent use of their Private Information,” the lawsuit says. The lawsuit argues that the Pentagon violated federal privacy laws by failing to protect personal records and maintain compliant cybersecurity systems, despite internal warnings about issues in its systems. The complaint cites multiple reports from the Defense Department’s Office of Inspector General describing failures by both the department and the DMDC to implement adequate cybersecurity controls. In a report published days after the breach, the OIG said that “officials have not taken the necessary actions to demonstrate that they were operating at an effective level for 14 of the 20 [Inspector General Federal Information Security Modernization Act] core metrics.” News of the Defense Department breach emerged alongside reports of a cyberattack targeting FBI personnel files . However, the group responsible for the FBI incident has not been linked to the Pentagon breach. The department offered affected individuals 12 months of credit monitoring and identity-restoration services. “Had [the Defense Department] properly implemented standard cybersecurity controls — such as regular review of accounts, scanning for vulnerabilities, field encryption or tokenization of sensitive PII like SSNs, and routine monitoring of system logs for suspicious activity — the Data Breach could have been avoided,” the lawsuit says.

title: France orders four more SAMP/T NG systems to strengthen air and missile defence
body: The DGA placed the order through the Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation, OCCAR, with eurosam, the consortium comprising MBDA France, MBDA Italy and Thales. Eurosam said the French Air and Space Force would receive the units in a layered configuration combining Aster and MICA VL missiles. New radar and fire control SAMP/T NG succeeds the Franco-Italian SAMP/T, known as Mamba in French service. Development began in 2021 to address increasingly fast, manoeuvrable and stealthy threats in more complex operating environments. The programme introduces a new-generation fire-control system incorporating Thales’ GF300 radar. The radar is adapted to the capabilities of the Aster B1NT missile, which will extend the system’s interception capability. The DGA said SAMP/T NG, paired with the future Aster B1NT, would be the only European surface-to-air defence system capable of intercepting ballistic and hypersonic threats. It defined hypersonic speeds as exceeding Mach 5, or five times the speed of sound. Layered protection against air and missile attacks SAMP/T NG is designed to employ Aster 30 B1 and Aster B1NT missiles and coordinate short-range and very-short-range air defence assets. France’s Aster/MICA VL configuration will combine different missile capabilities within that layered approach. Eurosam says the system provides 360-degree protection and can simultaneously engage combinations of air and missile threats at distances beyond 150 kilometres. Its intended targets include aircraft, drones, cruise missiles and manoeuvring ballistic missiles. The system is designed for integration into national air defence networks and interoperability with NATO and coalition systems. It can also operate alongside friendly military aircraft in civilian airspace. Mobile firing units A firing unit can include up to six launchers carrying eight Aster missiles each, providing 48 missiles ready to fire. It also comprises an engagement module and a multifunction radar with an identification friend-or-foe module. According to eurosam, the radar can detect and identify targets beyond 350 kilometres. The mobile system can become operational in less than 30 minutes. The Aster B1NT incorporates a Ka-band seeker, new interception algorithms and updated electronics. Eurosam says these changes improve its performance against complex threats, including short- and medium-range ballistic missiles and hypersonic missiles. Export customers join France and Italy The DGA said Denmark and Ukraine had also selected SAMP/T NG for their air defence requirements. Other countries have expressed interest, although the agency did not identify them. The additional French order expands the programme’s domestic commitment alongside those export selections. Eurosam has served as industrial prime contractor and design authority for Aster-based air defence systems for more than 35 years.

title: Russian war veteran appointed mayor through Kremlin program ousted after raising corruption allegations
body: Nikita Gorelov, the mayor of the town of Sosnovka and a graduate of the presidential personnel program “Time of Heroes” for participants in the war against Ukraine, was dismissed, he announced on his Telegram channel. Gorelov was mobilized to fight in the war against Ukraine in September 2022. He served two years as a sniper, after which, on the recommendation of the Kirov region’s governor, he received an offer to head Sosnovka, the independent Russian news outlet Verstka reported . In October 2024, he took office as mayor and soon began accusing “crooks from previous administrations” of corruption. By December, he had already received orders to return to the front. The order angered local residents, who held a public rally in Sosnovka in his support. 4,000 people signed a petition backing him. In the end, Gorelov kept his post, but the Kremlin called his case the “most unsuccessful” example of appointing a war participant to a leadership position. Gorelov’s final dismissal was formally the result of a local government reform. In November 2025, authorities in the Kirov region passed a law abolishing municipal districts and creating new districts in their place, and Sosnovka, a town of about 8,400 people, lost its own administration as a result. Deputies in the newly formed Vyatskiye Polyany municipal district decided to remove Gorelov from office. Gorelov said he had been under pressure for two years and that officials had now decided to get rid of him “quietly.” As mayor, he secured a criminal case against the city council speaker over violations in the construction of housing for resettled residents and collected signatures opposing the local government reform. Gorelov accused regional authorities of using war participants for their own PR. “In essence, they use us like toy soldiers for hype, and then write us off,” he wrote. title: Repeated Ukrainian attacks could lead to a major regional tragedy — Rosatom CEO
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Ongoing attacks by the Ukrainian armed forces on the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) and Energodar could lead to a major regional tragedy, Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev told reporters.
"Constant strikes [by the Ukrainian armed forces on Energodar and the ZNPP], deliberate and calculated, targeting not military facilities but people and social infrastructure, have become part of everyday life," Likhachev said.
He stressed that the state nuclear corporation was continuing to seek a response from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and the international community to the situation. "We are drawing the attention of international organizations, countries and, as they say, all people of goodwill to the fact that this must stop; it is unacceptable. We are just a few steps away from a major regional tragedy," the Rosatom CEO said.

title: New nuclear sub design review finished ahead of schedule
body: The SSN-AUKUS Preliminary Design Review was conducted in June and concluded on 1 July, three months earlier than the September date it had been expected to meet, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked for what reason the scheduled September 2026 Preliminary Design Review date for SSN-AUKUS was missed and what the new date was. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “The SSN-AUKUS Preliminary Design Review was conducted in June 2026 and concluded on 1 July as part of the ongoing Detailed Design and Long Lead (D2L2) phase of the programme.” A Preliminary Design Review on a submarine programme locks the overall configuration before detailed design work proceeds at scale, covering the hull form, the compartment arrangement, the propulsion and combat system integration and the weight and stability margins. Passing it allows long lead items to be ordered against a stable design, which matters on a programme where reactor components and large forgings have ordering lead times measured in years. SSN-AUKUS is the replacement for the Astute class and the design Australia will also build, developed by BAE Systems at Barrow with Rolls-Royce providing the reactor plant and a trilateral arrangement governing the common elements. The boat is larger than Astute, carries vertical launch capacity and is intended to accommodate uncrewed systems alongside torpedoes and cruise missiles. Detailed Design and Long Lead runs to 2028, and the programme is midway through it, with Pollard confirming in a separate answer the same day that the number of boats will be settled before the phase closes. Steel will be cut on the first British hull next year, a milestone this publication has covered as it approached . Design reviews slipping to the right has been the pattern across large defence programmes for a generation, which is what prompted the question. Submarine design on this programme has run with a deliberately conservative schedule built around the Barrow drumbeat, and Dreadnought holds the priority on the same design and build resources. Australia’s Osborne yard in South Australia will build to the same design, and the Australian Submarine Agency has its own review gates aligned to the British ones, so an early conclusion on the British side gives both partners margin before detailed design work peaks. Rolls-Royce in Derby is producing reactors for both classes from a doubled site. Obese-Jecty’s question assumed a missed milestone and received a date that had already passed. The review closed on the first of July and the programme has been running on from it since. The post New nuclear sub design review finished ahead of schedule first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords. The aptly named 1Password for Agents doesn’t give bots free reign to access all of your connected accounts — you’ll still need to grant approval for sign-in requests — but should make it less cumbersome to use Agents for tasks that require them to log into various services.
”Agents are starting to do real work on our behalf. The old model where you hand over a credential and hope for the best doesn’t work,” 1Password chief product officer Aashish Tripathi said in a press statement. “An agent should be able to do the job it’s been asked to do without getting permanent access to everything behind the account, and 1Password provides the trust layer that makes this possible across personal agent experiences.”
With this new system, an AI agent uses a unique digital key to verify its identity to 1Password when it reaches a sign-in form. The app then sends you a notification about which account credentials it needs, and why. If you choose to approve the request, 1Password will fill in the required login information instead of handing it to the agent. Approvals are granted on your own device to ensure you’re behind the permissions, making this a similar process to two-factor authentication. After the agent is signed in, it’ll continue with its task, without ever having actually seen your password.
This 1Password access system is designed to work with a variety of popular AI agents, including Meta Muse, ChatGPT Work and Dots, Claude Duet, Grok Bot, and Town. 1Password says more partners are working to bring support to 1Password for Agents, including Browserbase, Browser Use, Dana, Instinct, Kernel, Perplexity, Ramp, Tomo, and Wajo, with “additional integrations to come.”
Correction, October 22nd : Aashish Tripathi is 1Password’s chief product officer, not CEO.
