US Special Envoy for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli said earlier in an interview with TASS that there was a chance of arranging an exhibition football match between the Russian and US national teams.
"As you may well know, we never come up with comments on talks regarding matches until final agreements are reached and documents are signed," Mitrofanov said, speaking on the sidelines of the 14th Russia: Country of Sports annual international sports forum.
"We are considering the possibility of hosting a match with the US national team; we have communicated with the [American] federation on this issue more than once, but it is too early to assess the effectiveness of this communication. All I can say at the moment is that the current situation is quite positive," he added.
The 14th Russia: Country of Sports annual international sports forum is taking place in Russia’s second-largest Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk on October 21-23 with the support of the Russian government and the Sports Ministry. The event is organized by the Roscongress Foundation with the support of the Krasnoyarsk Region government. TASS is the official information partner of the forum.
The annual forum was established in 2009 by a decree of the Russian president to promote physical culture and sport, international sports cooperation and a healthy lifestyle.
Russia’s national football squad played three friendly matches in late September and early October, namely against Iran (2-0), Namibia (6-0) and Nigeria (3-3).
The world’s governing football body, FIFA, announced on February 28, 2022, that the Russian national team and all professional clubs representing the country were barred from participating in FIFA tournaments.
In turn, the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) made a similar decision regarding the Russian national football team’s participation in UEFA tournaments.
Both FIFA and UEFA cited Russia’s special military operation in Ukraine as grounds for their respective bans on Russian teams’ participation in competitions.

title: Ghanaian boxers draw first-day byes at 2026 IBA Africa Elite Championships
body: All three of Ghana’s boxers have drawn byes on day one of the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Amadu Mohammed (bantamweight, 55kg), Ebenezer Ankrah (lightweight, 60kg) and Joseph “Jaguar” Commey (light welterweight, 63.5kg) will not fight on the opening day of the competition on Thursday, October 22. The championships have attracted a record 171 boxers, comprising 132 men and 39 women, making this the highest participation in the history of Africa’s premier boxing event. The turnout surpasses the 148 entries recorded at the 2024 Africa Elite Championships, which were also hosted in Kinshasa. That edition featured 101 male boxers and 47 female competitors. Seven bouts are scheduled to open the competition on Thursday as the championships get underway in the Congolese capital. Ghana will be hoping its three representatives can make a strong impression as the tournament progresses, with Commonwealth Games medalist Mohammed competing in the bantamweight division, Ankrah in the lightweight category and Commey in the light welterweight class.

title: Iran live updates: Iranian plotting against US citizens abroad in 'advanced stages'
body:
The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen are continuing cross-border strikes.
Talks between the U.S. and Iran have stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February.
The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.
Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military and oil infrastructure facilities.
Saudi Arabia's General Directorate of Civil Defense issued safety warnings on Sunday morning for the Riyadh, Khamis Mushait and Abha regions, amid ongoing cross-border attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
The directorate said that the danger had passed in all three regions shortly after the warnings were issued.
The U.S. intelligence community has gathered information through various channels indicating that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target American officials abroad, according to a memo sent from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
"The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," Clayton wrote.
Clayton also said that senior members of Rubio's staff had been briefed on the matter and that he would make every effort to downgrade as much of the intelligence as possible so that it could be shared more widely within the State Department.
A U.S. official confirmed the authenticity of the memo, which is unclassified and dated Oct. 23.
"When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment," the official said. "The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on restricted operating status in the region."
The existence of the memo was first reported by Axios.
A tanker reported being hit by an unknown projectile while transiting in the Strait of Hormuz Thursday afternoon local time, according to the UKMTO.
The tanker was able to continue its voyage to the next port of call, according to the UKMTO.
Asked about whether a the stalemate between the U.S. and Iran could continue for a year and if the U.S. is preparing for an extended conflict, President Donald Trump told reporters the U.S. "could end it very quickly."
"Iran is a failing nation. We're taking all the oil out that we want," Trump told reporters on Wednesday. "Everybody is taking oil out. In fact, last week we took more oil out than we have ever taken it out even before the war."
"They have no money, the question is do we want to finish it off or do we let it do we just want to let it wither because we're getting everything we want," Trump said.
Trump also pointed to Iran's rising inflation.
"Iran is not able to do much now. And we could if we wanted to just take all of the oil, we could take the whole country, we could take all of the oil," Trump said.

title: EU cannot be considered peaceful project as it seeks to counter Moscow — Russian diplomat
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. The European Union cannot be considered a peaceful project, as its strategic documents provide for countering the "Russian threat," Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said.
"Today, it’s not possible to speak of the European Union as a peaceful project. The main rationale for both the EU and NATO is the fight against the 'Russian threat,' which is enshrined in their strategic documents. Notably, EU and NATO documents initially described Russia as a direct and immediate threat but later added, after some deliberation, that the threat was also long-term," he pointed out, addressing the Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
According to Grushko, such an approach means that "no matter what happens in efforts to settle the Ukraine conflict, Europe will continue to see Russia as a threat." "Moreover, some hotheads even want to describe Russia as an existential threat in EU and NATO documents," the senior diplomat added.

title: Witkoff Meets Putin: Any Progress on Ukraine?
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin received Donald Trump’s chief negotiator on Ukraine, Steve Witkoff , in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday. According to Moscow, it was agreed that trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US would resume. Witkoff had met with European representatives and Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo before heading to Saint Petersburg. The media discuss the prospects of a peaceful resolution against the backdrop of Trump’s new hard line on Ukraine.
Kremlin giving no sign of being ready to negotiate
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Future meetings are also unlikely to yield any tangible results, The Spectator (UK) observes:
“There has been nothing to suggest yet that the Russian president is genuinely ready to make a deal or concede on his war aims. ... Facing the prospect of brutal midterm results for the Republicans in two weeks’ time, Trump is desperate for a win with Russia. Putin can sense this and appears to be using this to play for time ahead of a winter in which he hopes to make substantial progress on subjugating Ukraine. Not for the first time, it is Zelensky who is being forced to jump through hoops and show willing in the hope that doing so will save his country from a stitch-up by an enemy and supposed ally.”
The US’s policies of recent weeks are having repercussions across the world, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (Germany) points out:
“Putin and his inner circle are convinced that in the war against Ukraine and their struggle against the West as a whole, they will firstly have the greater staying power, and secondly be able to play the Americans and Europeans off against one another. Everything the American leadership has done in recent weeks confirms this belief. Consequently, the prospect of a ceasefire, not to mention peace in Ukraine, has become even more remote. Instead, the Kremlin is likely to feel emboldened to escalate the conflict even further. ‘Restoring justice of Russians’ takes place above all on the battlefield, Putin’s foreign minister has said.”
Unlike Trump, Putin is not in a hurry, notes Corriere della Sera (Italy):
“For five years now, Vladimir Putin seems to have been applying the old Russian proverb ‘The slower you go, the further you’ll get’ to a war that he originally thought would last no more than two weeks. … So Putin is biding his time, waiting to see how events unfold and what happens with the elections in the US and Europe – and taking whatever he can get without making any concessions. He has the chance to achieve in Washington what he is unable to achieve on the front line; but he also knows that this window of opportunity could be closed again by a single social media post in the middle of the night. ... What the Russian president needs to work out now is whether the path available to Trump will be long enough.”
The US President’s supposedly new stance on the war in Ukraine is not really new at all, argues Dagens Nyheter (Sweden):
“Some interpret this as the US changing sides with regard to Ukraine, and it’s easy to understand why Zelensky feels betrayed. Yet this development is nothing new. The difference is that Trump is no longer making a secret of what he has wanted all along: for Russia and his friend Vladimir Putin to win the war. ... Trump’s eagerness to help Putin now is particularly good news for the Kremlin. Russia is in a bad way, both on the front line and at home, where all its oil depots are burning. So it’s good that it has an ally in the White House.”
Experts will continue to puzzle over the US president’s policy on Ukraine, says Ilta-Sanomat (Finland):
“A clear intention can certainly be discerned behind Trump’s confused remarks on Ukraine and Russia. He wants to take credit for bringing about peace. But does anyone still believe he could actually achieve such a thing? After all this, can anyone still trust Trump’s word when it comes, for example, to security guarantees for Ukraine, which are a key safeguard for peace? ... When the war in Ukraine eventually ends and Trump is no longer president, a lot will be written about current events. Perhaps the most important question then will be: what on earth was going through Trump’s mind? It won’t make for pleasant reading.”

title: Evacuation of all families with children from Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities mandatory now – Regional Administration
body:
Vadym Filashkin, head of Donetsk Regional Military Administration, has announced the expansion of the mandatory, compulsory evacuation zone for families with children to include all settlements within Kramatorsk and Sloviansk territorial communities of Kramatorsk district, Donetsk region.
"The security situation is constantly deteriorating. The Russians are attacking Kramatorsk and Sloviansk daily, striking residential areas, civilian transport, and places where people gather. Staying there with children is an unjustifiable risk. I appeal to parents: do not put your children in danger, and do not wait until a Russian strike hits near your home. Evacuate now," Filashkin wrote on his Telegram channel on Thursday.
According to him, specialized police units and the State Emergency Service have been mobilized to assist with the evacuations. Upon arrival at a transit point, families will receive support for their onward relocation to safer regions of Ukraine.
As previously reported, the zone for the compulsory evacuation of families with children has been expanded several times over the past year within the city of Sloviansk alone, with new neighborhoods being added every few months.
Sloviansk and Kramatorsk communities share a border. In addition to the city of Sloviansk, the former includes the settlements of Bylbasivka, Sukhanivka, and Myrne, as well as the village of Torets. The second [hromada], in addition to the city of Kramatorsk, also includes the settlements of Yasnohirka, Kamyshevakha, Krasnotorka, Sofiyivka, Yasna Poliana, Shabelkivka, Ashurkove, Vasylivska Pustosh, Malotaranivka, Belenke, and Oleksandrivka, as well as the villages of Semenivka, Pryvillia, and Dmytrivka.
Prior to the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, the combined population of both hromadas was 300,000, and their total area spanned 534 square kilometers.

title: ‘Justice is hope’: Here are Leonen’s 9 promises as aspiring chief justice
body: MANILA, Philippines – Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen gave not one, not two, but nine promises on Thursday, October 22, as he vies to become the country’s 28th Supreme Court (SC) chief justice. Leonen was the first of five candidates to face the Judicial and Bar Council for its public interviews. Leonen said his plan includes a promise to enhance the expertise of judges and ensure that justice is accessible to everyone — especially the marginalized. Improvement of judges Continuation of Unified Legal Aid Service (mandatory free legal service of lawyers), developmental and social change lawyering, program of remote hearings and translation. More exposure for judges to jails and communities “Judges at every level must remain open to the possibility that their premises are mistaken,” Leonen said. Transparency in resolving cases When a case is submitted for decision, Leonen said the parties should be told the date by which the SC is expected to decide on it. If the date won’t be met, the parties should be told why. Continued digitalization of courts Leonen said the entire justice system should be digitalized — from the Department of Justice’s prosecution, trials at regional trial courts, to the appellate courts and SC. Accountability in public office Quicker resolution of corruption cases “Every case already filed by the Office of the Ombudsman arising from large-scale corruption decided at first instance before the end of 2027, the horizon of our Strategic Plan,” Leonen said. Consultation with business sector Review of regulatory actions and reporting of alleged exactions or extortions by any court official or employee Creation of more courts Leonen said at least 10 halls of justice should be built in the country’s poorest provinces. “Where no building will ever be close enough, our court will travel, as it did from Bongao to Simunul, Tawi-Tawi,” he added. Court’s independence If he becomes chief justice, Leonen said the SC will publicize any attempts at interference, who the court officials and employees met, about what, and what was asked. Creation of laws for those who need it Review Batas Pambansa Bilang 129 and consolidate the Rules of Court and the special rules into a Philippine Code of Pleading and Practice. Rules on the customary law of the indigenous peoples Writ of Kalayaan, which will compel “agencies responsible for a detention facility to act on its conditions, together and in the open” A review of the legal profession Review on the admission to the Bar Improvements for Shari’ah (Islamic law) counselors and lawyers Leonen said he will continue Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo’s plan to innovate the judiciary. “I offer all these, with my faults and weaknesses, which I constantly try to overcome. The ideas we debate today and the personalities who will appear before you pale in comparison to this: our people still suffer,” the aspiring chief justice said. “Whoever is appointed, this reality remains: our people still suffer. Yet they still come to our courts, holding their folders and their receipts, because they have decided that this is where their grievance belongs. On our watch, we cannot fail them. I will not fail them,” he added. Play Video What type of chief justice will Leonen be? Leonen said that in these times of political and economic challenges, the Philippines needs a chief magistrate who is independent and ready to make hard decisions for the people. He believes a chief justice should protect the confidentiality of SC deliberations, encourage other justices to speak up about their opinions, explain the Court’s decisions fully, and protect dissent. “All this because the judiciary should be where government is held to its conscience, the Constitution. A judiciary beholden to powerful interests — past, present, or future — does not deserve its name,” the senior magistrate said. Leonen said he will be, if ever, an independent chief justice, as proven by his track record. He said he has been senior associate justice for nearly 14 years and has worked with 5 chief justices and 37 associate justices. According to him, he has been an acting chief justice on many occasions and has chaired the SC’s 2nd and 3rd Divisions, among others. “I have voted, on principle, against the legal positions of the President who appointed me, and of every President who has sat since. I have also written unanimous decisions that clarified the framework and limits of the discretion of powerful departments and officials in government,” Leonen said. “I do not say this to my credit. It is the only assurance worth anything to the public,” he added Leonen said the court’s success will be measured by whether the poorest litigants can rely on it, if they can tell their families the justice system gave them a fighting chance in a case. He also believes that court decisions should reach and be understood by everyone. The chief magistrate added that lawyers should think of empowering people. As officers of the court, Leonen said they should explain what the law is, why the law is the way it is, and what could be done about it. “Justice is hope. Hope is honored when a remedy is owed to a named person, by a date, and then delivered. Anything short of that reduces hope to a mere sentiment. Our people have been offered sentiments for a very long time,” Leonen said. – Rappler.com

title: Kazakhstan Military Training Overhauled with New Drone Forces Planned
body: Less than a month after 14 service members died during military exercises in the Caspian Sea, Kazakhstan has approved plans to overhaul conscript training and introduce new safeguards against abuse in the armed forces. The reform plan was approved at a Security Council meeting on October 21, with the main changes scheduled for 2027. The September 24 tragedy prompted an investigation that uncovered serious failures in the planning of the exercises and measures to protect soldiers. A wider inspection of the Defense Ministry has since led to 13 criminal cases involving suspected embezzlement, abuse of authority, and other violations. New Training System Aims to Reduce Abuse Beginning in 2027, Kazakhstan plans to divide its mandatory 12-month military service into two stages. Recruits will spend their first six months at training centers and the remaining six months in military units, where they will continue combat training alongside their assigned formations. The change is intended to help conscripts adjust to military life and reduce the risk of hazing. Political analyst Gaziz Abishev believes that separating initial training from regular military service will make it easier for commanders to monitor abuse. “Amid the chaos of a regular military unit, it’s much harder to keep track of abusive behavior by people who are out of control. It will be easier at a training center. Officers will be personally accountable for the safety of conscripts,” he wrote on Telegram. The military also plans to appoint military counselors and an ombudsman for service members. The aim is to give soldiers and their families somewhere to turn when their rights are violated. Askhat Aimagambetov, a member of Kazakhstan’s parliament, the Kurultai, welcomed the initiative, citing cases of violations of service members’ rights and the difficulties their relatives have faced in seeking justice. “Now service members and their parents will have a direct, legally recognized advocate,” the lawmaker said . A New Drone Force The plan also calls for the establishment of dedicated drone forces and an expansion of the network of specialized military schools.. The move reflects the growing importance of unmanned aircraft in modern warfare, demonstrated particularly by the war in Ukraine, where relatively inexpensive drones have proved capable of destroying far more costly military equipment. Organizational preparations are expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with the main reforms planned for 2027. The wider inspection of the Defense Ministry is also due to be completed by the end of the year. Although preliminary findings have exposed serious failings, the commission’s full conclusions have yet to be published. Kazakhstan’s Military Capabilities in Central Asia Kazakhstan ranks 58th among 145 countries in the 2026 Global Firepower ranking, behind Uzbekistan, which holds 53rd place. Turkmenistan ranks 78th, Tajikistan 100th, and Kyrgyzstan 109th. According to Global Firepower estimates , Kazakhstan’s defense budget for 2026 is approximately $5.84 billion, compared with around $6.21 billion for Uzbekistan.

title: Overdependence on gold, cocoa leaves Ghana exposed to changes in global commodity prices – ISSER
body: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) has stated that the dependence on gold and cocoa leaves Ghana exposed to changes in global commodity prices and production conditions. The country’s external position strengthened considerably in 2025, with export earnings growing much faster than imports. The merchandise trade surplus widened from US$3.8 billion to US$13.8 billion, while the current account surplus rose from US$1.6 billion to US$9.4 billion. International reserves also increased, strengthening the country’s foreign exchange position, while the cedi appreciated against major international currencies. However, ISSER expressed worry in its 2025 State of the Ghanaian Economy Report that the improvement was heavily concentrated in primary commodities, particularly gold and cocoa. Minerals accounted for 68.2% of merchandise exports, highlighting continued export concentration. It explained that although non-traditional exports grew by 30.7%, Ghana’s export base remained relatively undiversified. “A strong trade surplus does not necessarily indicate that the economy has become more diversified or internationally competitive”, it warned. Policy Priorities ISSER called for diversification of exports through expand manufactured and processed exports to reduce commodity dependence. Similarly, it wants increased domestic value addition that is the strengthening of processing capacity and linkages between agriculture, mining and domestic industry. Finally, it urged the country to build external resilience via sustain reserve buffers and the strengthening of export competitiveness while reducing vulnerability to commodity price fluctuations.

title: No LNG overproduction on market — Novatek
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. No overproduction of liquefied natural gas (LNG) is on the market, CEO of the Russian gas producer Novatek Leonid Mikhelson said at the Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
"Sometimes there is even heard an opinion at present that LNG overproduction will be in coming years. As long as Novatek deals with LNG, we always hear this phrase. Nevertheless, the actual market practice shows that no overproduction takes place. If the price goes down, LNG simply starts substituting coal. On the other hand, LNG shortage may occur. It is because of that we see gas price spikes. This is what is taking place in the current year," Mikhelson said.

title: Dobrynya Nikitich cargo UAV to be entirely Russian-made — Svarog Center
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Production of components for the Dobrynya Nikitich cargo unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), used in Russia’s special military operation in Ukraine, is planned to be fully localized, a spokesman for the Svarog Research and Production Center told TASS.
"Work is currently underway to modernize the 15-inch Dobrynya Nikitich cargo drone. Our goal is to fully localize the drone production. So far, we have managed to make the drone almost entirely Russian-made: the Dobrynya Nikitich is equipped with a domestic frame, motors, propellers, a flight controller, and a speed governor. We are currently collaborating with partners, Russian manufacturing plants, to switch the digital communication system to domestic components," the company said.
The Svarog Center specified that the new version of Dobrynya Nikitich is also equipped with a remote control featuring a large screen, as requested by operators. "We are constantly working with units carrying out missions in the special military operation zone and receiving feedback on how to improve our products. We were tasked with simplifying the drone’s operation as much as possible. The current update allows users to plan missions using a controller with a large screen without needing a computer. Our software is intuitive, lets users plan routes and waypoints directly from the controller, and requires no special training," the company added.
The Dobrynya Nikitich drone is used to deliver cargo weighing up to 10 kg over distances of up to 12 km.

title: Dubai Design Week announces five new commissions for Abwab 2026
body: A seven-metre installation featuring red light and a structure inspired by the coded instructions used by Kashmiri weavers are among five new commissions announced for Dubai Design Week’s Abwab programme. Abwab , which means doors in Arabic, commissions new work by practitioners from across Asia and Africa. Dalia Rafeh, Grace Shieh, Kanaka Raghavan, Ubik and architecture and research practice Varussi have been selected to create this year’s commissions, under the theme In Other Words. The exhibition will run from November 3 to 8 at Dubai Design District. It forms part of the festival’s 12th iteration , with Abwab bringing the commissions together in an indoor group exhibition for the first time, moving away from the individual pavilions of previous years. Established in 2015, Abwab has supported more than 180 designers. This year’s works explore communication through lettering, textiles, paper and architecture, considering how meaning is conveyed through the materials and forms people encounter. Rafeh’s Shhhhhhhh takes the Arabic letter sheen – ش – and its association with the call for quiet as its starting point. The letter is repeated in a seven-metre installation using red light, which draws on the visual language of public and commercial signage. The work explores how the same call for quiet can suggest an order to remain silent, a pause for reflection or an invitation to listen. Dubai-based architecture and research practice Varussi, founded by Owais Asif Khan and Samreen Junaid Wani, draws on Kashmiri weaving traditions in Taleem . The installation takes its name from the traditional coding system used to design Kashmiri carpets and kani shawls. Varussi will translate that system into an architectural structure visitors can enter, exploring how craft knowledge is recorded and passed between generations. Dubai-based designer, educator and researcher Kanaka Raghavan turns to the construction of written language in Cheent Devanagari . Her work challenges the treatment of Latin typography as a universal starting point for design, drawing instead on Devanagari’s own structural and material traditions. Using block printing, ornament and layers of translucent textiles, Raghavan creates letterforms that separate and come back together as visitors move around them. Their changing appearance allows viewers to examine how the script is constructed. Writer and visual artist Grace Shieh explores the material qualities of paper in A Library of Paper Memories . Combining papermaking, poetry and experimental writing, the installation considers how fibres, textures and forms can carry memories and meaning alongside written words. India-based conceptual artist Vivek Premachandran, who works under the name Ubik, examines the interpretation of language in Non/Sense , a floor-based installation inspired by science-fiction writer Philip K Dick’s How to Build a Universe That Doesn’t Fall Apart Two Days Later . The installation uses translation, mistranslation, abbreviation and lorem ipsum – the placeholder text used in graphic design – to turn text fragments into patterns and spatial structures. The exhibition’s layout will allow visitors to move around, between and through the commissions, as well as view them from above. Entry is free. Three free curator-led walkthroughs with Alexie Glass-Kantor, Caoimhe CJ Reynolds and the participating practitioners will explore the research, materials and processes behind the works.

title: Russia’s New Filin Missile Uses US, Chinese Electronics
body:
Russia has begun using a new cruise missile against Ukraine that combines a Russian jet engine with American and Chinese electronics, Ukrainian military intelligence said, describing the weapon as part of Moscow’s push to develop cheaper long-range strike systems.
The missile, called Filin, entered use in late summer, according to Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR). The agency published an interactive 3D model, technical specifications, and a component breakdown on its War&Sanctions portal.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
HUR identified 35 electronic components associated with US manufacturers and 22 with Chinese manufacturers. It said the missile’s electronics resemble those found in other Russian missiles and drones, but feature a growing share of Chinese components and standardized designs across different onboard units and circuit boards.
Filin is produced by NPO Molniya, part of Russia’s Tactical Missiles Corporation. HUR described it as a continuation of Russian efforts to manufacture relatively inexpensive, ground-launched weapons powered by jet engines.
The missile has a carbon-fiber and fiberglass composite fuselage measuring 3.5 meters, or about 11.5 feet, with a wingspan of 3 meters (9 feet). Some parts are made using 3D printing.
Russian-advertised specifications cited by HUR give Filin a maximum speed of 800 kilometers per hour, or about 500 mph, and a range of up to 1,200 kilometers, roughly 745 miles. Those performance claims have not been independently verified.
HUR said the missile can fly at very low altitudes as well as at heights of up to 6 kilometers (3.7 miles). Versions carry either a 50-kilogram (130 lbs) or 100-kilogram (220 lbs) warhead. It launches from a ground-based platform using a solid-propellant booster.
The agency traced the missile’s onboard equipment to the Russian company PLAZ, which it said is also involved in producing the Garpiya attack drone, a variant of the Geran-2 manufactured by the Kupol electromechanical plant.
Filin and Garpiya equipment units share similar layouts and markings, HUR said, pointing to common design approaches across the two weapons.
For navigation, Filin uses a Chinese-made inertial navigation system alongside a 16-channel Kometa module. Inertial navigation tracks a weapon’s movement using onboard sensors, while the War&Sanctions portal identifies the Kometa unit as resistant to electronic interference.
Despite its foreign electronic components, the missile uses a Russian-made R500 turbojet engine manufactured by Reynolds, according to HUR. The agency said the same engine had previously been identified in Russia’s S-71K Kover and S-71M Monokhrom air-launched cruise missiles.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: IN BRIEF: Kremlin spokesman comments on Putin-Witkoff meeting, trilateral talks on Ukraine
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. The outcome of the meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President’s Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, trilateral talks on Ukraine and cooperation with China were the main topics of Thursday’s briefing by Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov.
TASS has summarized the key statements made by the Kremlin spokesman.
Russia has not yet decided whether President Vladimir Putin will travel to Miami for the Group of Twenty (G20) summit, but it will consider all circumstances when deciding whether to accept or decline the invitation: "There is an invitation to this summit, and it will be considered in light of all the circumstances."
Putin did not send any documents containing proposals for a settlement in Ukraine through US special envoy Steve Witkoff.
Mediation in a process as complex as the settlement of the conflict in Ukraine is difficult and is best conducted behind closed doors: "Of course not. Mediation in such a complex negotiation process is conducted behind closed doors."
"Megaphone diplomacy" and public discussion of proposals to settle the conflict in Ukraine can only harm the negotiation process: "Any kind of ‘megaphone diplomacy’ here can only be harmful. Public discussion of counterproposals can also only be harmful."
Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump are not currently planning a telephone conversation following the visit by US presidential special envoy Steve Witkoff. However, such a conversation could be arranged quickly: "At the moment, there are no plans for such a conversation. However, as you know, it can be arranged fairly quickly if necessary or if one of the parties desires it."
"The presidents constantly assure each other of their readiness to speak at a moment’s notice and at any time."
The US is making substantial efforts to settle the situation around Ukraine, while European efforts are aimed at provoking further hostilities: "The US administration is doing a great deal to promote a peaceful settlement. European countries are doing nothing to foster a peaceful settlement and doing a lot to provoke further hostilities."
Russia has yet to hear any constructive statements from Europe indicating a willingness to de-escalate tensions: "We have not heard a single statement that would indicate such an intention."
At the same time, Russia sees a positive development in the willingness of some European capitals to seek to understand what is happening: "We do indeed see increased activity in some European capitals in terms of efforts to understand what is happening -- this is a positive development, rather. But, of course, it still seems a long way off from such objective statements [on de-escalation]."
Russian President Vladimir Putin has not yet decided on the composition of Russia’s negotiating team for trilateral talks on Ukraine: "As for the composition of the negotiating team, that will be the president’s decision. And it has not been made yet. Let us not forget that this was only announced yesterday."
There are currently no definite plans regarding Putin’s participation in a meeting with members of the Russian negotiating team during the resumed trilateral talks on a settlement of the conflict in Ukraine: "No, there’s still time before this trilateral meeting. There are no specific plans regarding the president on this matter as of yet."
Putin and Chinese Premier Li Qiang did not discuss preparations for the Power of Baikal gas pipeline deal during their meeting in St. Petersburg: "No, it was not discussed. The topic of cooperation in the energy sphere was highlighted in general."
Russia-China energy cooperation still has significant untapped potential: "This cooperation [in the energy sector] is truly extensive. It has horizons that have yet to be explored. Both sides will continue working to make fuller use of the potential that exists."
Russia is guided exclusively by its own interests when making decisions concerning the assets of foreign companies: "In such conditions Russia, when making relevant decisions, is governed only by its own interests."

title: Kiev expects difficulties in EU accession talks in 2027 due to elections in Europe
body:
BRUSSELS, October 22. /TASS/. Ukraine wants to open accession negotiations with the EU on the two remaining clusters in December, believing that it will be much harder to do so in 2027 due to upcoming elections in EU member states, where Ukraine-related issues are unpopular, Politico reported.
The outlet quoted Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister for EU Integration Vsevolod Chentsov as saying that "It’s good to finish this" later this year, because next year "it gets super difficult politically." Ukraine is looking to a European Council meeting in mid-December "as an ideal date" to make that decision, he said.
Meanwhile, the European Commission’s roadmaps for candidate countries do not reflect Ukraine’s "progress on internal reforms," the senior Ukrainian official told Politico.

title: Why has B.C.’s snap election caught both main parties unprepared?
body:
When a snap election is called, at least one side would normally be prepared.
But that hasn’t been the case in British Columbia, resulting in a provincial election campaign like no other, political watchers say.
The campaign has seen interim B.C. Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson going without media availabilities on several days, including on Tuesday and Wednesday in the home stretch, ahead of Saturday’s final voting day.
The NDP has meanwhile pivoted its messaging from focusing on U.S. President Donald Trump, to affordability, to the need for a stable majority.
And campaigning has also been notably muted with relatively few large-scale rallies, although both major parties have events scheduled this week.
Even the NDP campaign bus, which was adorned with Eby’s smiling face in 2024, is an anonymous-looking coach, devoid of slogans.
Hamish Telford, an associate professor of political science at the University of the Fraser Valley, said he had noticed the “lack of preparation.”
“This is especially surprising since the NDP called this election. You would think, if they were going to call a snap election, that they at least would be prepared, and that they would obviously catch the Conservatives off guard,” said Telford.
“This was an election of their making, and they are not entirely ready for it,” he added.
Telford said the NDP had initially been anticipating Eby running against Kerry-Lynne Findlay, a divisive and unpopular leader of the Conservatoves. But Findlay resigned and was replaced by Doerkson.
Telford said he would have advised the NDP not to go through with it.
“They should have called the election off, but evidently things were too late, or they had built up too much momentum and couldn’t stop themselves.” said Telford.
Angelo Isidorou, who is chief strategist for the Conservatives, said snap elections can be messy compared with fixed-date polls.
“In this case, this is what makes this very unique … not only is it a snap election, but it was an election that took place at the same time as municipal elections, which never happens. So, it was all very chaotic,” said Isidorou of the Oct. 17 municipal polls across B.C.
He said the “biggest difference” between a snap election and a fixed-date election is the “predictability.”
“It’s difficult being in Opposition because you don’t know when the election is going to come, and when an election is called, you only have maybe over a week to recruit candidates and get them on the ballot because there’s a deadline. When there’s a fixed election, you can predict all of this,” said Isidorou.
“In this case, it wasn’t, and I think what surprised me the most is really how not prepared the NDP was,” said Isidorou, adding that otherwise, the NDP would have fielded a full slate of 93 candidates in every riding.
Elections BC said the NPD was one short of a full slate, after failing to nominate a representative in Peace River North.
But vetting may have suffered in the rush to field candidates.
While the Conservatives managed to fill their 93-riding slate, two candidates have since been disavowed by the party.
Jordan McIntosh, the 18-year-old former Conservative candidate for Vancouver-Strathcona, was dumped last Thursday over online posts that included saying Hitler killed “lots of Jews” not because he “hated them specifically” but because there were so many of them.
Another candidate, Joachim Agou, was ejected from the party earlier this month for online comments saying the driver of a car that rammed a pro-Palestinian protest group in Switzerland should have “reversed too.”
Political scientist Michael Prince said the election has “elements of some really unusual features.”
He said it was puzzling to see parties still fall into the trap of recruiting inappropriate candidates.
“They haven’t really thoroughly vetted their history of social media posts,” said Prince, the Lansdowne professor emeritus of social policy at the University of Victoria.
“We’ve seen, particularly on the Conservative side, candidates that have been removed by the leader or have stepped down very quickly,” he said. “So, that’s kind of the new unusual, but it’s been something that’s unfortunately pretty typical over the last several elections.”

title: Ukraine becomes global leader in black-market transplantology — envoy to OSCE
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. Ukraine has become one of the world’s leading centers of human trafficking and "black-market transplantology," Dmitry Polyansky, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE, said at a meeting of the organization’s Permanent Council.
"Unfortunately, we are compelled to note that human trafficking is on the rise across the OSCE region. We have repeatedly drawn attention to this problem in Ukraine, which has long since become one of the world’s leading centers of human trafficking and ‘black-market’ transplantology," he said.
Potential and confirmed victims of human trafficking from Ukraine have been identified across Europe, Polyansky added.
"According to the latest data from the International Organization for Migration, of the 39,000 human trafficking cases recorded in Europe over the past 20 years, 19,000 involved Ukrainians. With the connivance of the Zelensky regime, human trafficking for the purpose of harvesting human organs, cells, and tissues is flourishing," the Russian representative stated.

title: International Network Launched to Support Childhood Cancer Care in Uzbekistan
body: An international network to support children with serious and life-threatening illnesses, including cancer, was announced in Samarkand on October 21. The new initiative will bring together first ladies and spouses of heads of state. The network’s establishment was announced by Carlos Rodriguez-Galindo, executive vice president of St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital in the United States and director of St. Jude Global, which works to improve childhood cancer care worldwide. Uzbekistan’s First Lady Ziroat Mirziyoyeva was named chair for a two-year term. Participants in the initiative intend to share expertise and help expand children’s access to diagnosis, treatment, and quality medical care. The announcement came during the second International Congress on Pediatric Oncology, held on October 21–22 alongside the World Summit on Children’s Well-Being. The events brought together representatives from more than 100 countries, international organizations, and the medical community. Summit partners include UNICEF, the World Health Organization (WHO), and the World Bank. Mirziyoyeva also chairs the board of trustees of the Zamin Foundation, which co-hosted a UN event with St. Jude and the WHO in September 2025 aimed at improving survival rates among children with cancer and other serious illnesses. Uzbekistan is already participating in an international program to improve access to childhood cancer treatments. In February 2025, Uzbekistan and Mongolia became the first two countries to receive essential cancer medicines through a WHO–St. Jude initiative. The program aims to provide children in lower-income countries with a reliable supply of quality-assured cancer medicines free of charge. Uzbekistan is also preparing changes to its national cancer care system. As The Times of Central Asia previously reported , the country plans to reform its oncology services beginning in 2027, while a pediatric palliative care center is planned for the Samarkand region to support children with serious and incurable illnesses.

title: Ukrainian partisans claim sabotage of military communications near major Moscow data center
body:
Agents of the Ukrainian partisan group Atesh said they disrupted Russian military communication lines around IXcellerate, one of Moscow's largest commercial data center operators, to interfere with Russian air-defense coordination and help Ukrainian drones reach their targets, the group said on Oct. 21.
"We are disabling the enemy's channels, disrupting command and control, and helping UAVs reach their targets," Atesh said .
The group claimed Russia's Defense Ministry uses infrastructure linked to IXcellerate for military communications and air-defense command systems, while concealing that traffic within civilian server networks.
The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the claim, and Atesh did not provide details on the extent or duration of the disruption. There has been no public confirmation from Russian authorities or IXcellerate that military communications were affected.
IXcellerate operates several data centers across Moscow and describes itself as a leading commercial data center operator in Russia. Its facilities host telecommunications and other digital infrastructure used by banks, retailers, and business customers.
The partisan group has previously claimed sabotage operations against Russian military and defense-linked infrastructure inside Russia, including attacks on railway and energy facilities.

title: Normalization of Russia-West ties requires lifting of all sanctions — senior diplomat
body:
ISTANBUL, October 22. /TASS/. Normalizing Russia’s relations with the United States and Europe is contingent upon the removal of absolutely all sanctions, Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko told the 19th Verona Eurasian Economic Forum.
"We can start fresh with the US. We can move past this story [of sanctions], but, in order to forget it, the United States and Western Europe need to lift absolutely all sanctions. It is impossible to develop relations if we are navigating a minefield, not knowing where it will detonate, or where these sanctions will be applied," the Russian diplomat said.

title: Defense Forces strike EW station in Russia's Bryansk region and military depot in Luhansk region
body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
Among the targets struck was an electronic warfare station in the Gulevka area of the Bryansk Oblast in the Russian Federation.
“The destruction of electronic warfare assets expands the Ukrainian Defense Forces’ capabilities to effectively deploy unmanned aerial systems,” the General Staff emphasized.
They also succeeded in striking a command and observation post of a Russian army unit near Vyshneve in the Zaporizhzhia region and an enemy logistics depot near Zolotarivka in the Luhansk region.
Among the targets struck was a command post for the Russian invaders’ drones in the Lankove area of Zaporizhzhia region. The General Staff explains that striking such targets reduces the aggressor country’s ability to attack the positions of the Ukrainian Defense Forces and frontline communities with drones.
As reported by Ukrinform, in the Huliaipole sector, Ukrainian defenders destroyed two Russian air defense systems that were targeting Ukrainian aircraft.

title: Iran's floating oil reserves, used for China sales, completely depleted, analysts say - report
body: Iran's oil reserves, kept in tankers and sold to China over time, have been completely depleted, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing Kpler analysts.At their peak, these reserves consisted of almost 90 million barrels of oil, according to Kpler. By October 5, the reserves dropped to fewer than one million barrels, and have since been exhausted.“There's no more oil to discharge to China anymore,” Kpler's crude-oil analysis head Homayoun Falakshahi said.Other analysts, the WSJ reported, said Chinese payments to Iran may take up to two months to arrive, meaning the regime may still receive some funding from past sales.The consequences for Iran's already-struggling economy may be dire, with Falakshahi saying that the oil sales generally account for approximately 30-40% of its government revenue.“It looks like the US gamble is that the economy will either push the regime back into negotiations to accept a nuclear deal, or will spark protests internally which the regime will face challenges containing,” he said.Iman Nasseri, senior vice president of Middle East and Asia at energy-analytics company FGE NexantECA in Dubai and former worker in the research arm of Iran's oil ministry, said that the US strategy was working, but not to discount the Iranian regime's resilience. “Let's wait another year and see if the system can stand.”Iran-backed groups redirecting funds to IRGC, CENTCOM saysIran-backed groups including Hezbollah, Hamas, and Shiite militias in Iraq have been redirecting money to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as Tehran faces mounting economic pressure after nine months of war, US Central Command (CENTCOM) chief Adm. Brad Cooper said in a video statement released earlier this month.The United States' naval blockade has cost Iran an estimated $25 billion in lost oil revenue, he said.Additionally, CENTCOM and the US Treasury Department froze $350 million in Iranian cryptocurrency assets in recent weeks.Asher Smith contributed to this report.

title: Finnish PM visits Kyiv as Russia steps up attacks despite peace push
body:
Editor's note: This story is being updated.
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo arrived in Kyiv on Oct. 22 to finalize a number of agreements aimed at supporting Ukraine in the coming winter.
Orpo's visit comes amid a flurry of peace diplomacy, as Russia's mass overnight strike on Ukraine's capital underscored Moscow's unwillingness to cease its attacks.
Kyiv and Helsinki signed seven agreements on Oct. 22, worth a total value of 330 euros (over $336 million), President Volodymyr Zelensky said after meeting with Orpo. The deals include support for Kyiv's energy infrastructure and greater access to Finland's satellite networks.
"We agreed to utilize more of Finland's satellite capabilities," the president said. "This is important for our defense and for the resilience of Ukraine."
The agreements involve Finnish satellite companies Nokia and ICEYE, Zelensky said.
Ukraine relies heavily on intelligence gathered via satellite networks from foreign partners to monitor Russian missile launches and prepare for Russian strikes. In a press release from ICEYE, the companies said they wanted to go even further by helping Ukraine architect its own sovereign satellite communications system .
Zelensky also said Finland would provide support for Ukraine's power grid as Moscow begins its annual winter assault on energy . Since the beginning of the full-scale war, Russia has heavily bombarded key heating and electrical facilities during the cold seasons, attempting to plunge the country into darkness and maximize civilian suffering.
"Thank you for your willingness to support our logistics and energy sectors — these are key targets for Russia, and the fact that we will have more locomotives, more energy equipment, and more resources to protect our energy infrastructure will be a significant boost," Zelensky said.
Finland's Foreign Ministry also announced on Oct. 22 that Helsinki will allocate 2 million euros ($2.2 million) in humanitarian aid to Ukraine.
"The main purpose of the visit is to show Finland's strong support for Ukraine as the war of aggression continues and the country prepares for the winter," the Finnish government said .
Orpo's agenda also included meetings with top Ukrainian officials and opportunities to "show support for the reforms needed for Ukraine's EU membership."
Orpo's visit came a day after U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21. Witkoff had met with Zelensky and European partners in Oslo a day earlier on Oct. 20 to discuss peace proposals to present to the Kremlin.
After meeting with Witkoff, Putin said Moscow was ready to resume negotiations. Zelensky later reiterated that Ukraine supported trilateral peace talks involving the U.S. and Russia.
Hours after Witkoff lavished praise on Putin during their meeting, Moscow launched several waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, killing at least one person and injuring more than 20, according to Ukrainian officials.
Russia launched another ballistic missile attack on Kyiv in broad daylight on Oct. 22, while Orpo was visiting the capital. The Finnish prime minister visited a school damaged by a Russian drone during an earlier October attack, the Keskisuomalainen newspaper reported .
Finnish President Alexander Stubb has long called for Europe to play a bigger role in efforts to end Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine. He has said he would be ready to represent Europe in peace talks if asked.

title: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary.
body:
Using an AI agent to shop for you is a strange experience. Tech companies have marketed them as personal assistants — the democratizing of labor that ordinarily would only be available to the rich and powerful. In practice, at least for buying things, it’s more like sending an anxious and apologetic teenager out to the store: They require an inordinate amount of instructions and specifications, run into technical problems regularly, and come back with solutions that are not exactly what you asked for. They did, technically speaking, complete a task, just not the specific one you asked them to, and often not in the way you would have approached it.
Meta, Google, OpenAI, and others have all introduced some version of agentic shopping tools that promise to make buying things even easier than it already is. Demos show AI agents that can seamlessly book flights and hotels, browse billions of products to find the right one, and secure tickets to sporting events on a human’s behalf. But as AI companies — and their users — are finding out, buying things requires that the other party is willing to sell them in the first place.
The most prominent example of a retailer or service provider refusing to let an AI agent in has been Amazon. The retail giant sued Perplexity, with Amazon saying the AI company had ignored its requests to stop its agent from shopping on the site. More recently, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agent from shopping on Amazon. E-commerce sites aren’t the only platforms walling off agents: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said the bank wouldn’t allow outside agents to access accounts, saying it was “too risky” for clients and the company, and some users report they’ve been unable to use agents to book trips from providers like Delta and Amtrak. AI agents can also get caught in the web of general bot blocking systems, meaning that even if a site doesn’t have a blanket ban, existing firewalls can make agents inconsistent — and by extension, less useful for the types of tasks tech companies tout as the future.
Even without hard blocks, agents’ access to retailers is spotty. For example, Muse, which I instructed to look for a specific face moisturizer, was caught in Target’s bot check one day but was able to get through the next. It suggested a listing from a grocery chain that doesn’t ship to my address when I searched for the best price on granola bars. When I asked for mattress recommendations under a certain price point, Muse was once again blocked by Target, despite being able to pull from the site just a few minutes prior.
How successful an agent is at accessing a site may depend on how it went about the task and what safeguards are in place, Target spokesperson Loni Monroe told The Verge in an email. (Target has AI shopping partnerships with OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft.) Agents may be able to access one part of the site but not another, as a way to protect customer data and the shopping experience. In addition, Monroe said that Target has safeguards preventing unauthorized agents and bots from accessing customer accounts and initiating transactions on a human’s behalf.
The lack of Amazon options within agents is also impossible to ignore. Sometimes, the agents will say as much: When I asked Muse to find the best per-piece granola bar price, it offered options from Sam’s Club, Walmart, and Costco, but acknowledged a big caveat: Amazon might have had the lowest-priced option, but it was hard-blocked from browsing, so Muse couldn’t confirm. Between waiting for a response, directing Muse to search for more sites, and clarifying that a West Coast-based retailer wouldn’t ship to New York, it likely would have been faster to search myself. It also explains why agentic AI companies would really like to have Amazon on board — and why Amazon is so fiercely protective of how customers shop on its platform. It’s not that Amazon is against robots shopping in place of humans — the company has its own on-platform agentic shopping feature that monitors prices, automatically reorders items, and purchases products based on rules set by human users. Another feature that uses an agent to purchase products from other sites without leaving Amazon angered smaller businesses, who say they didn’t consent to having their storefronts scraped and featured on Amazon.
Amazon spokesperson Maxine Tagay confirmed that the company “requested that Meta remove Amazon” from Muse.
“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate,” Tagay said in an email.
It’s one thing for agents to offer comically spotty, disjointed services — but it’s another, potentially more frustrating experience when they actually do work, because of the implications for humans. In order to test a shopping task that I actually would like to automate, I unleashed Muse on The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion retailer. As secondhand shopping has exploded in popularity, shopping on The RealReal has gotten increasingly competitive, so much so that the company sells a $12-per-month subscription allowing shoppers to get early access to new items. On The RealReal, part of the shopping process is zero-sum: Placing an item in your cart reserves it for you for 20 minutes, making it impossible for other people to swipe it. I instructed my Muse agent to bulk-add all 10 of the newest listings from a favorite brand to my cart, effectively blocking other shoppers from purchasing them before I got the chance to review the latest selections. I had no intention of buying any of these items, but I prompted Muse to keep re-adding the items to my shopping bag each time the 20-minute hold had expired. On and on this went, all day (I eventually ended the task).
If I were a less honest, pure-hearted person, I would deploy an agent to run this personalized, technically allowed reserve system endlessly. But as I watched the items continuously pop back into my cart, exasperation flooded my psyche — on behalf of the other shoppers interested in these items, but also for my future self, who may soon be competing with someone else’s agent doing this same thing. Perhaps I already am.
The RealReal sees AI agents as an opportunity, and is investing in its own AI-powered services while protecting the integrity of the platform, chief technology officer Luke Friang told The Verge in an email.
“Our approach is to remain open to third-party AI agents, allowing them to browse, log in and interact with our marketplace, while maintaining safeguards against automated activity that could disrupt the customer experience,” Friang said. (Following publication of this article, Friang says that The RealReal updated its bot defense configuration to prevent this behavior from Meta’s Muse, while still allowing AI agents to direct shoppers to items on the app.)
To be sure, normal online shopping can be tedious, too — the endless array of options on the web can make finding the right thing feel like looking for a needle in a haystack. Agentic shopping is the inverse: It’s like looking at the world through a pinhole. If I don’t like the five options Muse has curated for me, I must ask it to find five more, and on and on. I must give the agent specific parameters and rules, and expand and tweak them as needed, little by little. A more rote task like finding the absolute lowest price on a product you already know you want is where an agent could be truly useful. Without Amazon, though, even that feels like the task was carried out with incomplete information.
If you have preferences about literally anything you spend money on — the price, the return policy, the shipping rates, the ethical standards of a company, the fabric composition — an agent is just another entity to express those preferences to. With the time and patience for hand-holding, Muse could help deepen a search for something specific: For example, I uploaded photos to Muse of a vintage dress I’ve been hunting for, along with the specific year it’s from, a list of keywords associated with it, notes about similar items, and secondhand platforms to start searches on. Muse could not find the dress for sale anywhere, but it did alert me to an upcoming auction of items from the same brand.
In an email, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton emphasized the partnerships the company has forged with retailers and the control human users have over the agent’s actions.
“Importantly, users can take over at any time, Muse is designed to always ask permission before buying, and it applies ethical browsing principles when asked to do things that a human could not - like buying all the tickets to an event,” Clayton said. “The response from retailers has been overwhelmingly positive, and we look forward to working with them as we continue to grow Muse and improve the purchasing experience.”
There’s another thing that nags at me no matter how long I tinker with agentic shopping: The joy and thrill of discovery is largely gone. Buying things is an American pastime. We do it in person, online, from strangers on Facebook, and from professional salespeople on livestreams. We buy things we need and we buy things we don’t, things we know we want and the things we’ve never seen until now that have suddenly become very important. It’s not a stretch to say that for many, shopping is a hobby — one that has become solidly entangled with another, more modern hobby of scrolling on a phone. We don’t just lust after material belongings; we imbue them with identity markers and social status. Buying things is intensive — in resources, in labor, in emotion. AI companies see this pastime as something that can be optimized. Many people would probably prefer that it not be.
Update, October 25th: This story has been updated to reflect a change in The RealReal’s bot defense system.

title: Netanyahu defense challenges Mandelblit over police questioning of key state witness
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's defense pressed former attorney-general Avichai Mandelblit on Thursday over his approval of police questioning of former Netanyahu aide-turned-state witness Ari Harow, arguing that investigators had exceeded the limits he set.The exchanges at the Jerusalem District Court focused on the scope of the early inquiries into Netanyahu and the evidence Mandelblit said led him to authorize a full criminal investigation into gifts from businessmen.Defense lawyer Amit Hadad contrasted Mandelblit's instructions with information investigators obtained from Harow. Mandelblit maintained that the early material had not justified a full investigation but that testimony from Hadas Klein, Milchan's personal assistant, describing a regular supply of gifts, subsequently changed his assessment.Mandelblit, who authorized the investigations and later approved the indictment, was called to testify by the defense.Under Basic Law: The Government, opening a criminal investigation into a sitting prime minister requires the attorney-general's consent. Hadad's questioning has focused on what that consent covered and when it was given.What is Case 2000, and how is Mandelblit connected?Harow, Netanyahu's former chief of staff, later became a state witness. Recordings of conversations between Netanyahu and Yedioth Aharonoth publisher Arnon Mozes, found on Harow's phone, became central to Case 2000.That case concerns discussions about a possible exchange of more favorable coverage for Netanyahu for steps against Yediot's rival, Israel Hayom. Netanyahu is charged with fraud and breach of trust in the case and denies wrongdoing.Hadad cited police investigator Koresh Bar-Nur's account that Mandelblit had approved stopping Harow at the airport and supplied questions. Mandelblit said he did not recall the details but considered it plausible that investigators had proposed the stop and he had approved it.Hadad also presented questioning that sought information about possible wrongdoing over a decade, arguing that it exceeded Mandelblit's authorization.Mandelblit said such questions could have arisen in negotiations over Harow becoming a state witness – a suspect who agrees to testify for the prosecution in return for concessions in his own case.But when Judge Oded Shaham asked whether that was what Mandelblit had envisaged when granting approval, he said no, explaining that the inquiry had a defined subject.Hadad then presented remarks recorded at a July 17, 2016, meeting, in which Mandelblit distinguished suspicions of substantial gifts from businessmen from information about cigars, champagne and a suit.Hadad argued that Harow had already described Netanyahu receiving packages of cigars from Milchan, challenging Mandelblit's characterization of the early information as concerning occasional gifts.Hadad argued that the summary of Harow's questioning had reached Mandelblit before the meeting. Mandelblit said he was unsure whether he had read it. He maintained that the material available then had not persuaded him to open a full investigation. He said he had authorized examining whether Netanyahu received gifts on a significant scale.The discussion concerned the development of Case 1000, in which Netanyahu is accused of receiving expensive gifts from wealthy businessmen. Netanyahu is charged with fraud and breach of trust in that case and denies wrongdoing.Mandelblit said Klein's testimony later indicated a regular supply rather than isolated incidents. That distinction, he maintained, changed his assessment of the evidence, strong enough, eventually, to file indictments.The defense said it would need additional hearing days to complete Mandelblit's testimony.Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: FG, Stakeholders Seek Promotion of Self Care in Tackling Public Health Challenges
body: *PHCs to play key role, says SFH Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The Federal Government has said there is need to imbibe the practice of Self-care as part of measures to address several public health emergencies including infectious diseases outbreak. At the same time, the Society for Family Health said there is a strong link between Self-care and the primary healthcare with sustainable financing, responsible use of technology, and meaningful community participation in advancing universal health coverage. Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Salako, stated this in Abuja on Wednesday at the inaugural National Self-Care Conference with theme “Self-care Puts Your Health in Your Hands: Test, Track, Thrive.” The minister said self-care is important in prevention and control of infectious diseases, including Ebola Virus Disease currently being contained following index case reported on Monday. “I use this opportunity to call on Nigerian public to observe self-care like hygiene, appropriate disinfection and cooperate fully with public health officials to contain reported Ebola index case,” he said. Salako said the theme captures fundamental principle of modern healthcare underscoring imperative of empowering people with knowledge, skills and tools to own their health. “Self-care extends healthcare beyond hospitals and clinics into our homes, workplaces and communities. It encompasses health promotion, disease and complication prevention, appropriate self-testing and responsible management of well-being. However, self-care does not replace professional healthcare nor absolve government of responsibility to provide accessible, affordable and quality services,” he said. He said government will continue to promote investment in health facilities, skilled personnel, essential medicines and functional referral systems, adding that self-care is opportunity to strengthen primary healthcare, advance UHC and improve outcomes through prevention, maternal health support, management of non-communicable diseases and extension of information to underserved communities. Salako explained that while Test allows individuals to know health status, with screening and approved self-testing helping early identification of hypertension, diabetes and other risks, Track requires consistent monitoring of blood pressure, blood glucose, physical activity and medication adherence guided by reliable information and linked to professional care. He said that Thrive is ultimate goal of healthier individuals, stronger families and resilient communities. The Minister said the benefits require integrating self-care into PHC, training workers, strengthening community education, improving access to quality-assured products and protecting public from unsafe practices, leveraging digital communication and AI. He called on states to integrate evidence-based self-care into policies, professionals to guide safe use, partners to support financing and capacity, private sector to prioritize quality and affordability, and traditional and religious leaders, civil society and media to build trust. Earlier, Group Director, Population, Health and Community Systems, SFH Donor-Funded Portfolio Directorate, Pharm. Emeka Okafor, said conference speaks directly to future of health by enabling people take more informed role in own care. He said Society for Family Health experience shows care becomes more effective when it responds to how people actually live, making decisions at homes, pharmacies, communities and through phones. Okafor said opportunity is to turn ambition into commitments with stronger links between self-care and primary healthcare, sustainable financing, responsible use of technology and meaningful community participation. He said that SFH looks forward to the time when more Nigerians can understand their health, act early and access support when they need it. In her remarks, the Special Adviser to the President on Health, Dr. Salma Anas Ibrahim said that Federal government laying special emphasis on Self Care as a means of further improving national health outcome and attaining the target of universal health coverage. Highpoint of the event saw minister being presented with an investiture as “The National Self Care Ambassador” by Dr. Salma Anas Ibrahim.

title: Bauchi mosque removes imam over alleged campaign for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election
body:
The management committee of Masjid Abdullahi Bin Zubbair in Madina Quarters, Bauchi State, has removed its imam, Dahiru Abubakar, over allegations that he used sermons to campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.
The committee also rejected an alleged proposal by Mr Abubakar to rename the mosque after the president.
The committee’s chairman, Abubakar Jibrin, confirmed the removal in an interview with Daily Trust, saying the imam had repeatedly been warned against using the mosque for political activities.
A source told the newspaper that Mr Abubakar had subtly campaigned for Mr Tinubu during sermons after obligatory prayers, telling worshippers the president was not responsible for the country’s insecurity and deserved another term.
The committee reportedly set up a panel after a similar sermon the previous weekend. It removed the imam after he repeated the remarks following the early morning Subhi prayer on Sunday, 18 October.
Mr Jibrin said the committee’s concerns went beyond the alleged campaign for Mr Tinubu to include the imam’s practice of gathering people in front of the mosque and sometimes inside it to discuss politics.
“We have warned him not once or twice but many times, but he didn’t heed our pleas,” Mr Jibrin said. “We vehemently rejected the use of the mosque for political meetings.”
Mr Abubakar, however, denied that his sermons amounted to partisan campaigning, saying he had urged worshippers to stop blaming Mr Tinubu for Nigeria’s insecurity and economic challenges, which he described as an “end times phenomenon.”
“I have been preaching to the people to stop castigating President Tinubu for the insecurity and economic challenges. They prepared to vote for him and give him another mandate in 2027 to continue his mandate,” he said.
He added that his sermons focused on the fear of God, prayer and daily conduct. He also cited insecurity in Sudan, Chad and Mali to argue that Mr Tinubu could not be held responsible for every security crisis.
Mr Jibrin further alleged that the imam had insisted on renaming the mosque from Masjid Abdullahi Bin Zubbair to Masjid Imam Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
According to the committee chairman, members rejected the proposal, saying that the mosque belonged to the community and its name should remain unchanged.
“All the committee members said ‘no’ because the mosque belongs to the community,” Mr Jibrin said. “When he insisted, we rejected the idea and resolved that the mosque name would remain Masjid Abdullahi Bin Zubbair.”
Mr Jibrin said the committee decided not to reinstate Mr Abubakar, stressing that it was not opposed to any political candidate but would not allow the mosque to be used for political activities.
He said political campaigns and meetings should be conducted through political parties and at their offices rather than in a mosque.
“Our prayer is to Allah to choose the best for the country, be it President Tinubu or any candidate among the presidential candidates who would become a blessing to the country,” he said.

title: Georgia Drops From ‘Free’ to ‘Partly Free’ in Freedom House’s Freedom on Net Report
body: Georgia’s score fell by two points in Freedom House’s 2026 Freedom on the Net report , changing its status from “Free” to “Partly Free,” with the watchdog citing an “extended crackdown” by Georgian Dream authorities on activism and “retaliation” against ruling party-critical online journalists and social media users. “Georgia’s status changed from Free to Partly Free, as authorities continued to suppress online activism and speech perceived to be critical of the ruling Georgian Dream party,” the report , covering June 1, 2025, to May 31, 2026, reads, assessing Georgia’s overall score at 68/100, down from 70/100 last year. “Although the country’s internet penetration rate improved, authorities extended its crackdown on online and offline activism related to protests over the ruling Georgia Dream (GD) party’s decision not to pursue integration talks with the European Union,” the watchdog said in its separate, Georgia-focused overview . “Online journalists and social media users critical of the GD increasingly faced retaliation in the form of fines, raids, summons, and investigations.” According to the report, Georgia lost points in the indicators of “Limits on Content” and “Violations of User Rights.” The country’s score in Limits on Content decreased from 5 to 4 “because authorities increasingly restricted the space for online and offline mobilizing and used facial recognition technology to track protesters,” Freedom House said. The score in the second indicator, Violations of User Rights, also fell from 5 to 4 because “an increasing number of fines, summons, raids, and other punitive measures were directed against internet users for their criticism of the government.” According to Freedom House reports, Georgia’s internet freedom has declined for the past four years, gradually dropping from 78/100 in 2022 to 68/100 in 2026. The drop in Freedom of Net score follows the Georgian government’s crackdown on public statements and social media posts that authorities and courts deem offensive. Since early 2025, authorities have gradually increased restrictions on the public statements they consider “insulting,” including through legislative amendments and legal actions against critics. 18/06/2025 – Court Fines GD Critics over Facebook Posts ‘Insulting’ Ruling Party MPs It has intensified since the Interior Ministry established its Division for Combating Hate Speech in June. The unit monitors “hate speech” in public spaces, including social media, and files complaints with courts, often without a request from the person deemed to have been “insulted.” It has been involved in dozens of cases leading to fines of 1,500 to 6,000 GEL over social media posts and comments, as well as administrative detentions. In the latest such case , Vakho Sanaia, the opposition-leaning Formula TV anchor and journalist, was sentenced to 30 days of administrative detention after the Interior Ministry filed another complaint against him over social media posts the Ministry deemed insulting to Georgian Dream figures.
