title: Officials to provide update on fatal fire at CFB Wainwright in Alberta
body:
Twenty-seven soldiers remain in hospital, including 13 in critical condition, following a devastating fire that killed four soldiers during a training exercise Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta.
Military officials said Thursday there have been no additional deaths and 12 soldiers have been discharged from hospital. The fire initially sent 39 injured soldiers to various hospitals in the region.
The decision to hold a live-fire training exercise later in the day during a high-risk fire month will be part of the investigation into the deadly blaze.
The base’s training-range standing orders caution that units firing between August and October should plan early morning shoots, when the fire risk is lower. The document says the fire-hazard risk is “normally low enough to permit the firing of most ammunition natures” before about 10 a.m.
Maj.-Gen. Wade Rutland of the 1st Canadian Division told reporters in Edmonton Thursday that the timing of the exercise will be part of the review, but cautioned against reading too much into the document’s recommendations.
“That’s a guideline and commanders on the ground have to assess multiple factors in order to decide whether or not to go ahead with shooting,” Rutland said, including the weather, dryness and the type of munitions involved.
“What needs to be looked at is what were the factors on that day, as opposed to general range guidelines.”
Canadian Forces Provost Marshal Brig.-Gen. Vanessa Hanrahan said the fire originated as a result of training on the grenade fire range.
She said the location prevented firefighters from suppressing the fire before strong winds suddenly swept up the flames and pushed the blaze in a new direction across the training range.
Military officials said the grass fire broke out on a grenade range in a permanent danger area, where it was being monitored before strong winds in the afternoon quickly pushed the flames toward soldiers conducting attack training.
Officials said the fire spread rapidly, bypassing fireguards and moving toward what’s called a pair’s range, where two soldiers work as a team to practice live-fire exercises. Officials had previously said the fire had leapt to the section attack range.
Roughly 84 soldiers of the Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry were taking part in a field exercise when the fire swept into their path.
Officials said they continue to believe natural gas infrastructure was not involved in the accident.
Hanrahan said 30 military police are on the ground investigating, but the information they can confirm at this time remains limited.
“What we can really say that we now know is that the fire initiated on the automatic grenade launcher range and that fire initiated as a result of routine military training that was happening on that range at the time,” Hanrahan said.
“Every other aspect of what happened, from the time that fire originated on that range to what we have today dealing with the tragic accident on a different range in that area, is still under investigation.”
Three investigations into the accident are underway: two led by the military and one civilian. Military police are conducting a police investigation, while a military-led board of inquiry will examine the broader circumstances and recommend measures to prevent a similar incident. The province’s chief medical examiner will investigate the fatalities.
Rutland had said Sunday that the investigation could take at least a month, but said Thursday he had “underestimated the scope” of the military’s board of inquiry.
He said the panel’s fact-finding investigation will take “as long as it takes to examine all facets of the situation.”
Rutland said the military knows it must review its safety regulations, but emphasized that Saturday’s fire was an anomaly.
“We’ll be reviewing things like our ammunition and our range and training safety standards. Concurrent and ongoing investigations will examine every aspect of what happened,” he said.
Training has resumed at the base, although officials said it is not the same type of training that was being conducted Saturday. The entire battalion is expected to redeploy in the coming days.
The military also helped transport 19 intensive care nurses and five operating-room nurses from Toronto who specialize in burn treatment to assist with the injured.
Chief of the Defence Staff Gen. Jennie Carignan said she was heartbroken by the tragedy and promised the military reviews would be carried out transparently.
“There are difficult questions about what happened,” Carignan said. “I am acutely aware of our responsibility to establish the facts, share the findings and act on what we learn.”
The four soldiers killed were Pte. Shaun Farrell, 23, of Prince Albert, Sask.; Pte. Aidan Goulding, 23, of North Vancouver; Pte. Hayden Lykkemark, 19, of Langley, B.C.; and Sgt. Morgan Wong, 26, of Edmonton.
Farrell is being remembered in his hometown of Prince Albert as a dedicated athlete who was admired by many.
Close family friend Andre Grobler said Farrell was born in South Africa before making Canada and Prince Albert his home in 2017. He described the 23-year-old as a vibrant young man who overcame many challenges in his life.
“While our hearts are shattered, we stand before you today not only in deep grief, but also with profound pride in the extraordinary young man Shaun became,” Grobler said.
Farrell’s mother, Patricia Farrell, spoke about facing a future without her son.
“What goes through any parent’s mind when they lose their child, their baby? I’m just wondering what my future is going to be like without him in our lives, without him being around,” she said.
Roughly 150 people attended a vigil late Wednesday at a church in the nearby town of Wainwright, where prayers were said, songs were sung and the names of those killed were read aloud, followed by a moment of silence.
“These courageous soldiers willingly placed themselves in harm’s way to secure our continued peace and freedom as Canadians,” said Pastor Dan Marchuk of the Wainwright Pentecostal Assembly.
Earlier Wednesday, about 300 flag-waving supporters gathered along an area highway to pay tribute to soldiers who were at the training area but were not injured.
Two buses carrying soldiers from the base drove slowly past the crowd as two military helicopters flew overhead. Many supporters held signs thanking the troops for their service.
“Wainwright stands with you,” read one sign. “Our condolences for your comrades and thank you for your service,” read another.
Mayor Bruce Pugh said the last few days have been difficult for the town of roughly 7,000 people, though activities at the base have started returning to normal.
“It’s a Highway of Heroes kind of thing in our own little community,” Pugh said.
“After the incident, they continued on with their training and continued to do their jobs. And so I think the least we can do is show a sense of pride in them and appreciation for what they’re doing.”
The fire continued to burn beyond the training base, but officials said it did not cause any lasting damage to base infrastructure.

title: 2027: Opposition has no alternative to Tinubu’s policies — Olabimtan
body: — Says president has laid foundation for better tomorrow By Dayo Johnson AKURE — The Director-General of the Ondo State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Victor Olabimtan, has challenged opposition presidential candidates to present credible and practicable alternatives to the policies and programmes of President Bola Tinubu’s administration ahead of the 2027 general election. Olabimtan, who is also the Ondo State Coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), said opposition candidates had yet to demonstrate how they intended to govern differently or improve on the current administration’s policies. He spoke days after the inauguration of the Ondo State PCC, insisting that Nigerians should assess the Tinubu administration based on its achievements, prevailing challenges and prospects for the future. “None of those aspiring to challenge the President has presented convincing and workable templates demonstrating what they intend to do differently or better if given the opportunity. “Instead, they continue to recycle familiar rhetoric without offering practical solutions,” he said. Olabimtan maintained that the Tinubu administration had taken significant steps towards addressing the country’s challenges and laying the foundation for sustainable development. He identified economic management, infrastructure development, education and youth empowerment as areas in which the administration had recorded what he described as significant milestones. According to him, the country’s current economic realities should be considered alongside the situation before the administration’s reforms and the prospects for future improvement. “The ongoing electioneering campaign should not be judged solely by where we are today. Rather, it should be assessed against three critical realities: where we were before now, where we are at present, and where we are heading. “We all know that we are not yet where we ought to be, but we are equally conscious of the fact that we have moved considerably beyond where we used to be. All indices point to the prospect of a better tomorrow,” he said. The PCC director-general said Tinubu had laid a foundation for a better future, particularly for young Nigerians, adding that the President had promised a second term focused on shared prosperity. “What is required of us now is to support and vote for him for a second term so that he can consolidate the gains already recorded and complete the good work he has started,” Olabimtan said. On the preparedness of the campaign council, which was inaugurated on Saturday, October 17, 2026, he said it was committed to mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state. He said the council was working to secure support for APC candidates contesting seats in the National Assembly and the Ondo State House of Assembly. “Our mission goes beyond delivering Ondo State massively for President Tinubu. We are equally determined to ensure that all APC candidates, from the State House of Assembly to the National Assembly, emerge victorious with unprecedented margins. “We are working towards this objective, and with the structures and strategies already in place, we are confident of a strong performance in 2027,” he said. Olabimtan commended Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, who also chairs the state PCC, for providing the structures and support required to strengthen the council’s operations. He said the council was confident that its mobilisation efforts would help it secure support from voters who, according to him, appreciated Tinubu’s achievements and commitment to national development. The PCC director-general also urged APC leaders, stakeholders and independent campaign groups across Ondo State to work together, warning that internal disagreements could undermine the party’s electoral objectives. “This is a clarion call on APC leaders and independent campaign groups in Ondo State to join hands with Mr Governor and the Ondo State PCC in the overall interest of our party. “We stand to gain more when we work together. Disagreements are inevitable in politics, but past differences should not be allowed to undermine our collective progress. This is the time to work as a united team rather than at cross-purposes,” he said. Under the campaign mantra, “One Party, One Message, One Campaign Mobilisation,” Olabimtan urged party members to set aside their differences, strengthen their grassroots structures and coordinate their mobilisation efforts. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Ondo State had recorded significant support for Tinubu and expressed confidence that the APC would seek to sustain and improve on that performance in 2027. He urged residents to continue supporting Tinubu and the APC, arguing that continuity would enable the administration to consolidate its reforms and development programmes in education, infrastructure, economic growth and youth empowerment. Olabimtan reaffirmed the PCC’s commitment to working with party leaders, stakeholders and grassroots mobilisers across the state to pursue the APC’s objectives in the 2027 general election. The post 2027: Opposition has no alternative to Tinubu’s policies — Olabimtan appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Diplomatic Ways to Critique AI Slop
body:
What do you say when a collaborator sends you AI slop to edit?
You can’t accuse them of AI slop, because you never really know.
But the thing is, we know that readers are suspicious of slop and will stop reading if they suspect that, whether its warranted or not .
So here’s a live list of coded ways I have of telling people to reduce the AI slop in their writing. Or maybe its human slop, either way it needs to go back to the author for more editorial work.
On lists : What is the argument you are trying to make here? Can you rephrase to make that point.
On contrastive language (‘not x, but y’): Tell us directly what you did do, not what you didn’t do.
On adjectives and adverbs : Avoid adjectives and adverbs in scientific writing.
On restatement : This conclusion restates the intro. Describe how your paper has advanced research in this topic.
On overuse of ‘critical’ and similar adjectives : Say how its important rather than relying on adjective to do the work.
On meaningless content : Is this sentence specific to your study, or could it be used in a study on another topic? If so, go back to the topic sentence of this paragraph and refine what you want to say.
On 5000 word drafts of discussions (I’m seeing this a lot!): This is long, let’s go back to the outline. Send me the topic sentences for each paragraph so we can work on relevance and flow, then you can move content over that’s relevant and cut unnecessary content.
Over-use of em-dashes … Now these are controversial. You could say to switch out for some colons instead, but I think the issue is often deeper. Probably the final point above ‘go back to the topic sentence of this paragraph and refine what you want to say’ will be helpful as well. I’ll think about it next time I see one in the wild.
And if your paper mentions goblins then I’m not reading it at all (unless its about goblin sharks !).

title: Amazon identifies Oct 17 PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure
body:
Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to Oct. 17, 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The exploit attempt originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network. While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure.
The PHP embargo window was set to be lifted on 2026-10-21 1400 UTC. On the day of the release, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified multiple proof of concept exploits for the vulnerability, with the earliest around 2026-10-21 0200 UTC. Subsequently, from 2026-10-21 0200 UTC to 2026-10-21 0800 UTC, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified additional exploitation attempts of PHP2Shell targeting MadPot from additional anonymized infrastructure. The actual payloads and choices in anonymization infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors. Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems.
The actual release of the embargo window was 2026-10-21 1400 UTC. Once the embargo was lifted and the patch was released, additional proof-of-concept exploits appeared within hours, and we saw them used against our sensors almost immediately. PHP2Shell is now seeing broad exploitation attempts in the wild.
Two lessons from this event apply well beyond this one vulnerability:
For security leaders, this changes several working assumptions:
AWS deploys multiple layers of protection to help safeguard customers. Our internal threat intelligence system automatically detected and restricted malicious scanning attempts targeting this vulnerability. We analyze over 200 billion events per minute and integrate threat intelligence from our MadPot honeypot network to identify and block known exploitation attempts in real time. Our honeypot system provides us with early detection of exploitation attempts, enabling rapid response and threat analysis.
The identified IP addresses include shared anonymization infrastructure and are not exclusive to this threat activity. Organizations should investigate any observations involving these addresses as opposed to blocking.
See how to use AWS Web Application Firewall to help reduce your exposure while you patch in our blog post Using AWS WAF to apply mitigations for PHP2Shell RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) .
If you have questions, start a new thread on AWS re:Post or reach out to AWS Support .
CJ Moses is the CISO of Amazon Integrated Security. In his role, CJ leads security engineering and operations across Amazon. His mission is to enable Amazon businesses by making the benefits of security the path of least resistance. CJ joined Amazon in December 2007, holding various roles including Consumer CISO, and most recently AWS CISO, before becoming CISO of Amazon Integrated Security September of 2023.
Prior to joining Amazon, CJ led the technical analysis of computer and network intrusion efforts at the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Cyber Division. CJ also served as a Special Agent with the Air Force Office of Special Investigations (AFOSI). CJ led several computer intrusion investigations seen as foundational to the security industry today.
CJ holds degrees in Computer Science and Criminal Justice, and is an active SRO GT America GT2 race car driver.

title: Canadian convicted in U.S. terror plot gets 50 more years for stabbing prison staff
body:
An Ontario man convicted of plotting a terrorist attack in the U.S. has been handed an additional 50-year sentence for stabbing two American prison staff.
The U.S. Department of Justice says Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy was an inmate at U.S. Penitentiary Allenwood in Pennsylvania when he stabbed two correctional officers in December 2020.
It says the weapon, made from part of a steel desk in his cell, was used to stab one guard’s hand and the other guard’s head and face, causing the latter to lose his right eye.
Officials also say a note in El Bahnasawy’s sock made reference to a terrorist attack for the Islamic State, and a pledge of allegiance to the group was found in his cell.
He has been serving a sentence for plotting bombings and shootings on behalf of ISIS in New York City.
The 28-year-old pleaded guilty in November 2025 to multiple counts of assault, assault with intent to commit murder, and possession of contraband inside a prison as well as providing material support to ISIS, a designated foreign terrorist organization. The additional sentence will be served consecutive to his previous 40-year conviction.

title: IDF probes alleged arson attack on Biblical High Priest Eleazar's tomb near Nablus in West Bank
body: The IDF is investigating a reported arson attack on a tomb believed to be the burial site of the biblical Eleazar the Priest in the Palestinian village of Awarta in the West Bank, the military confirmed.Footage of the alleged arson was shared online and circulated on Palestinian social media.“Troops searched for suspects, who fled the scene before they arrived,” the military said, adding that Israel Police officers and forensic investigators planned to enter the village under IDF escort to collect evidence and take witness statements.ראשוני: ערבים מכפר המרצחים עוורתא בשומרון הציתו את ציון קבר אלעזר הכהן. הסרטון פורסם ברשתות הערביות עם שירי האדרה לאויב. https://t.co/hpatL6woik— אלחנן גרונר (@elchanangr) October 21, 2026Yossi Dagan, head of the Shomron Regional Council, visited the site for repairs following the attack and condemned the perpetrators as “behaving like ISIS.”“Every enlightened person in this world, not only Jews, should be appalled by an act like this, the desecration of such a sacred place, such a holy tomb,” Dagan said. “These are our enemies. They choose darkness; they choose to burn. We choose light; we choose life. Light will always triumph over darkness.”Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu did not respond to The Jerusalem Post's request for comment on damage at the site.Eleazar, the son of Moses's brother Aaron, was the second High Priest of the Israelites and is a significant biblical figure in Judaism and the Samaritan faith.Eleazar's tomb repeatedly vandalized, desecratedDespite its religious significance, the site has been desecrated on multiple occasions. The Israelite Samaritan Information Institute has previously reported that members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) vandalized the tomb with graffiti bearing propaganda messages. As recently as last year, reports indicated that the PFLP's military wing had continued spray-painting the site.יש ב''ה גם חדשות טובות: שופץ שעות אחרי ההצתה: ראש מועצת שומרון תיקן את קבר אלעזר הכהן שעות אחרי שערבים הציתו את קבר אלעזר הכהן בכפר עוורתא שבשומרון, הגיעו הלילה למקום ראש המועצה האזורית שומרון יוסי דגן, מנהלת המקומות הקדושים של המועצה ולוחמי צה"ל — וסיידו וצבעו את הציון כדי למחוק את פגעי האש. דגן: "אנחנו כאן לא כאנשים פרטיים אלא כשליחים של כל עם ישראל. האויבים התנהגו כמו דאעש פעם אחר פעם. הם בוחרים בחושך, הם בוחרים לשרוף — אנחנו בוחרים באור, אנחנו בוחרים בחיים. האור תמיד ינצח את החושך. נעשה תיקון גדול גם בהתיישבות". קרדיט צילום: דוברות המועצה האזורית שומרון— נתנאל פרנקל (@Israel8251) October 21, 2026The Palestinian Authority (PA), which administers the area where the tomb is located, has not commented on the attack. However, the PA-controlled WAFA news agency reported on Thursday that “colonists barged their way into western Awarta town, south of Nablus, and fired live ammunition at a home. No injuries were reported.”“Colonists' violence against Palestinians and their property is routine in the West Bank and is rarely prosecuted by Israeli authorities,” WAFA claimed.Israel moves to take over archaeological sites from PAThe PA's alleged failure to protect religiously and historically significant sites has been a source of contention with Israel, which has recently moved to expand its control over archaeological sites, citing concerns over their preservation.In November, Israel sent a letter to Mahmoud Azem, the mayor of Sebastia, announcing plans to take control of the archaeological site there, and in July, the Foreign Ministry affirmed that Israel was seizing the site because of the threat posed by the “Palestinian Authority's own record of neglect and complicity, which has allowed the ancient ruins to suffer rampant vandalism, theft, and desecration.”

title: Sustain economic stability, expand productive employment and create better jobs – ISSER to government
body: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) wants government to sustain the economic stability while expanding productive employment, saying it will be critical to translating economic growth into improved living standards. In its State of Ghana Economic Report (SGER), ISSER said Ghana’s macroeconomic recovery gained momentum in 2025, but growth remained uneven across sector. Ghana’s economy grew by 6.0% in 2025, up from 5.8% in 2024 and above the global (3.4%) and sub-Saharan African (4.5%) averages. Growth was driven mainly by services (8.1%) and agriculture (6.8%). Industry slowed to 2.3%, largely reflecting a sharp contraction in oil and gas production, although manufacturing and gold production expanded. The macroeconomic conditions also improved considerably. Year-end inflation fell from 23.8% to 5.4%, the cedi strengthened, and interest rates declined. The fiscal deficit narrowed, while strong gold exports contributed to a substantial improvement in the external position and international reserves. ISSER said a lower inflation and a stronger currency provide relief to households and businesses, while improved fiscal and external conditions create a more favourable environment for investment. However, the stronger Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth does not automatically translate into better livelihoods. “Employment opportunities, the cost of borrowing and the distribution of growth benefits remain important concerns”, it argued. Policy Priorities In sustaining stability, ISSER urged the government to maintain fiscal discipline and low inflation while supporting productive investment. It also wants the government to creating better jobs whilst translate growth into employment opportunities, particularly for young people. Again, it called for strengthening resilience, saying, diversify production and exports, improve infrastructure and reduce dependence on commodity-driven gains.

title: EU still reeling from negative impact of sanctions against Russia — diplomat
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. Sanctions against Russia have dealt a blow to the EU economy from which it has yet to recover, Russian Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky said at a regular meeting of the organization’s Permanent Council.
"Sanctions have become an instrument of self-destruction for the European economy, dealing it a blow from which it has yet to recover. Record inflation, rising energy prices, deindustrialization, declining competitiveness, and an exodus of capital and manufacturing facilities. European taxpayers are ultimately footing the bill for a sanctions campaign that primarily hurts the European Union itself. Restrictions on energy supplies, financial transactions, and technology exports have backfired on European companies and households," he said.
The diplomat added that even in Europe, there is now a growing recognition that meeting Kiev’s increasing demands will require further cuts in domestic spending, including on social needs.

title: ‎’One Truth, Many Platforms’, Media Trust Deepens Newsroom Collaboration
body: ‎‎Media Trust Group has launched a converged newsroom that integrates its print, television, radio and digital platforms, relying on technology, collaboration and audience data to strengthen journalism and build closer relationships with readers, viewers and listeners. ‎ ‎The Group Editorial Director of Media Trust Group, Mallam Ibrahim Shehu, said the new newsroom would enable journalists and editors across the organisation’s platforms to work together, improve reporting and deliver verified stories in formats suited to different audiences. ‎ ‎Speaking at the launch ceremony in Abuja on Thursday, Shehu described the initiative as a major shift in how the media organisation gathers, processes and distributes news. ‎ ‎“This newsroom is one newsroom, many platforms,” he said. ‎ ‎The digital newsroom brings together the editorial operations of Daily Trust, Weekend Trust, Aminiya, Teen Trust, Trust TV, Trust Radio and Digital Trust under a unified system designed to promote collaboration and speed up news delivery. ‎ ‎Shehu said the arrangement would end the isolation that often separates newsrooms operating across different media platforms, allowing journalists to develop stories collectively and adapt them to the needs of different audiences. ‎ ‎“When something happens in Maiduguri, Kano, Lagos, Abuja or anywhere else, our journalists will no longer work in isolation and our platforms will no longer wait on one another,” he said. ‎ ‎He stated that a single investigation could generate a detailed newspaper report, a television documentary, a radio discussion, a podcast, a digital explainer and a data visualisation. ‎ ‎“Not the same content repeated everywhere, but the same truth told in the form each audience prefers,” Shehu said. ‎ ‎The Group Editorial Director said the organisation had deployed an artificial intelligence-enabled content management system to support the newsroom’s operations and make collaboration possible in real time. ‎ ‎Under the arrangement, reporters can file stories from the field or from home, while editors, television producers, radio presenters and digital journalists can access the material simultaneously and prepare it for publication across platforms. ‎ ‎Shehu said the system would help journalists work faster, strengthen verification and fact-checking, and give editors access to real-time audience analytics showing what people read, watch and listen to, as well as where they consume the content. ‎ ‎He, stressed that the technology would support rather than replace journalists, adding that editorial responsibility would remain with reporters and editors. ‎ ‎“This system does not replace a single journalist. It removes the wall between them,” he said. ‎ ‎He added that the organisation would prioritise accuracy, credibility and editorial independence as it adopts emerging technologies and new methods of news production. ‎ ‎“Our standard is clear. Speed without sacrificing accuracy, innovation without sacrificing credibility, and audience engagement without sacrificing editorial independence,” Shehu said. ‎ ‎The newsroom also seeks to deepen audience engagement by helping editors understand how people interact with news content and what encourages them to return to the organisation’s platforms. ‎ ‎Shehu said the organisation wanted to move beyond measuring success by the volume of content produced and instead use audience insights to improve its journalism and strengthen its relationship with the public. ‎ ‎“For too long, media organizations have measured success by how much they produce. This newsroom lets us ask better questions. What are people reading, watching and listening to? Where do they stop? What brings them back?” he said. ‎ ‎He added that audience data would inform editorial decisions without dictating the stories journalists pursue. ‎ ‎“These insights will not dictate the reports, but they will help us serve our audiences better,” he said. ‎ ‎The initiative also places emphasis on bilingual journalism, with English- and Hausa-language teams expected to work together from the beginning of the reporting process. ‎ ‎Shehu said the approach reflected Nigeria’s linguistic diversity and the need to make credible journalism accessible to audiences in the languages they use daily. ‎ ‎“Now in one newsroom, English and Hausa stand side by side. In this newsroom, Hausa is not an afterthought and English is not the only default,” he said. ‎ ‎He said the organisation would develop and report stories in both languages to ensure that audiences in different parts of the country receive accurate, contextual reporting in a language they understand and identify with.

title: Anambra deploys nurses to airport, activates Ebola hotlines
body:
The Anambra State Government has deployed nurses to Chinua Achebe International and Cargo Airport and activated emergency hotlines to strengthen surveillance and response to suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases.
The Commissioner for Health, Afam Obidike, disclosed this to the News Agency of Nigeria on Wednesday in Awka.
He assured residents that the government was strengthening measures to prevent the virus from entering the state.
Mr Obidike urged residents to report suspected cases through the emergency hotlines.
He said the ministry was collaborating with the World Health Organisation, UNICEF, Médecins Sans Frontières, and the Association of Public Health Practitioners of Nigeria and other partners.
According to him, the partnership will enhance surveillance, promote early detection and coordinate responses to suspected cases.
“The state has intensified surveillance at entry points, including the airport and border communities.
“We have intensified public awareness campaigns and refresher training for healthcare workers.
The commissioner cautioned residents against unproven preventive practices, including drinking or bathing with salt water, stressing that such measures could not prevent Ebola infection.
He explained that Ebola could spread through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of an infected person experiencing symptoms, contaminated materials and certain infected animals.
Mr Obidike advised residents experiencing symptoms such as fever, headache, weakness, muscle pain and joint pain, particularly after possible exposure, to seek prompt medical attention.
He noted that the symptoms could resemble those of malaria and other illnesses, making early medical assessment essential.
The commissioner urged residents to remain vigilant, avoid spreading unverified information and promptly report suspected cases through the designated emergency hotlines.
Nigeria confirmed an imported case of Ebola on Tuesday, involving a woman who recently arrived in the country on an international flight from Uganda.
The patient is receiving treatment in isolation at a private hospital in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), Jean Kaseya, subsequently disclosed that the patient is the wife of a diplomat who travelled to Uganda’s capital, Kampala, for a holiday.
Mr Kaseya said the woman, originally from Uganda but resident in Abuja, developed symptoms three days after returning to Nigeria on 3 October.
As reported by PREMIUM TIMES, contact tracing commenced after the confirmation, with 44 close contacts initially identified, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.
The government has urged health facilities to remain alert, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe infection prevention and control measures, and report suspected infections to public health authorities.
The confirmation followed months of heightened surveillance after Ebola outbreaks were reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda.
PREMIUM TIMES reported in May that the federal government had identified 21 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) as facing high or moderate risks of Ebola importation following a risk assessment prompted by the outbreaks.
In September, PREMIUM TIMES also reported that the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention had raised the country’s preparedness level and strengthened surveillance measures.
The agency said travellers arriving from countries with active Ebola transmission could be required to complete health declaration forms to support monitoring and follow-up.

title: Russia Expels 32 Uzbek Migrants as Deportations Rise in Novosibirsk
body: Russian authorities expelled 32 Uzbek citizens from the Novosibirsk region on October 16 for violating migration regulations. Court bailiffs escorted a reported total of 47 foreign nationals out of the country that day, including citizens of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Azerbaijan. Over the course of the week, 91 people were expelled from the region. The migrants were identified during police raids in two districts of Novosibirsk and the surrounding Novosibirsky district. Those expelled paid for their own tickets home. Violations of Russia’s entry and residence regulations can result in fines ranging from 2,000 to 5,000 rubles (approximately $25–62), as well as administrative expulsion. Under Russian law , expulsion generally also means a five-year ban on re-entering the country. Expulsions from the region have risen sharply. By mid-September 2026, authorities had expelled 1,524 foreign nationals from the Novosibirsk region, compared with 958 during the same period a year earlier, an increase of approximately 59%. Uzbek citizens account for a substantial share of those expelled. By July, authorities had removed 618 Uzbeks out of a total of 1,314 foreign nationals, or approximately 47%. Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan were the next most frequently represented countries. The increase in expulsions comes as fewer foreign workers are obtaining work permits in the region. According to figures presented to regional lawmakers, approximately 27,000 work patents were issued in the first eight months of 2026, down from 34,000 during the same period last year. Russia is also tightening national requirements for migrant workers and their families. In July, Russia enacted legislation requiring migrant workers to demonstrate that they can financially support themselves and dependent family members. The changes also require children covered by the provisions who turn 18 to obtain their own work patent or another legal basis to remain in Russia. The main provisions take effect on January 1, 2027. As The Times of Central Asia previously reported , work-related entries into Russia by citizens of Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan fell by approximately 15% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier.

title: Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC
body: By Ayobami Okerinde The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr Jean Kaseya, has blamed a lack of international interest for the absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, saying the situation might have been different if the outbreak were affecting Western countries. Kaseya made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he called for greater African investment in vaccine research and manufacturing. He said, “I can tell you, if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccine will already be available. Why this vaccine today is not available? Because some of our partners decided to consider this issue as an African issue, they were not interested.” The Africa CDC chief, however, said the agency was taking steps to address the gap, including supporting clinical trials of vaccine candidates. He disclosed that an African manufacturer in Egypt was conducting clinical trials of a potential vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Kaseya also said the agency was working with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to explore clinical trials and compassionate use of Ervebo, a vaccine developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola. He stressed that the continent had the expertise and capacity to advance vaccine development, adding that Africa should not continue to depend solely on external partners during public health emergencies. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind. We have the knowledge, we have people with intelligence, we have capacity to manufacture vaccines, and we need to move on,” he said. Kaseya also called for greater domestic funding and improved coordination among African countries and international partners. He said 28 African countries had contributed funding to support the response to the current outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. The outbreak, declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, has caused more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities The disease has also been detected in other countries, with the Kenyan Health Ministry reporting a ninth case in the country on Tuesday, prompting concerns over cross-border transmission. Nigeria also confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20. The patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, is receiving medical care, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring. The post Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola: Ebonyi lawmaker urges stronger surveillance
body: — Calls for emergency preparedness in schools, hospitals By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The member representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency, Ebonyi State, in the House of Representatives, Chinedu Ogah, has called on the Federal Government and relevant health authorities to strengthen Ebola prevention, disease surveillance and emergency preparedness in schools, hospitals and other healthcare facilities. Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on Reformatory Institutions, made the call in a statement following deliberations on a motion by the Chairman of the House Committee on Infectious Diseases, Amobi Ogah, seeking stronger preventive and emergency medical measures against the disease. The lawmaker urged Nigerians to remain calm, avoid panic and cooperate with public health authorities by observing recommended precautionary measures. He stressed the need for comprehensive preventive measures in primary and secondary schools, tertiary institutions, primary healthcare centres and general hospitals to minimise the risk of transmission and protect vulnerable populations. Ogah also urged Nigerians to adhere strictly to official health advisories and rely on verified information from the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). He called on federal and state health authorities to strengthen disease surveillance, screening at points of entry, laboratory testing, contact tracing and rapid emergency response mechanisms. According to him, sustained public awareness, adequate infection-prevention supplies, well-equipped healthcare facilities, trained health workers and sufficient funding are critical to effective disease containment. The lawmaker further urged the Federal Government to mobilise public and private healthcare institutions and ensure the timely release of outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies to improve their preparedness and response capacity. He warned that delays in identifying suspected cases, isolating infected persons and tracing contacts could undermine containment efforts and increase public health risks. Ogah said proactive prevention, coordinated action by relevant institutions and responsible public cooperation were essential to protecting lives and preventing a potential Ebola outbreak in Nigeria. The post Ebola: Ebonyi lawmaker urges stronger surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: West Bank Palestinian farmers face attacks, olive theft from settlers as violence continues
body: Ahmed Salem, a Palestinian man living in the West Bank, said he witnessed extremist Israeli settlers hitting his olive trees with sticks and taking off the olives, saying he feared being attacked if he attempted to intervene.Extremist settlers have intimidated Palestinians harvesting their olives in the West Bank for decades, but this year, not only has recorded violence increased sharply, but reports of theft have been widespread, according to Palestinians, Israeli rights groups, and the UN.The settlers dumped Salem's olives into sacks and then drove them to a nearby Israeli settler outpost to be pressed into olive oil, he told Reuters."How would you feel if something that belonged to you was being violated, and you could do nothing about it?" he asked.The couple living in the outpost, whose olive press settlers have urged Israelis to use for West Bank olives, declined multiple Reuters requests for comment, while the Yesha Council, which oversees Israeli settlements in the West Bank, did not immediately respond.The attacks have accelerated ahead of an election next week that opinion polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Right-wing coalition could lose to opponents who have taken a more critical stance against settler violence.The IDF has been reported to restrict Palestinian access to nearby areas, including many olive groves, particularly amid the establishment of hundreds of small settler outposts across the region."This creates a situation where Palestinians, in many of the cases, many of the lands, especially in proximity to settlements and outposts, cannot enter the land and harvest the trees," said Ziv Stahl, executive director of Israeli rights group Yesh Din."But settlers can come and go freely, and that's what they do."Rights group claims over 100 attacks on olive harvesters since start of seasonEven when Palestinians can access their trees, it is not without risk. Yesh Din on Wednesday reported 125 physical attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters over the 24 days since the season began and 168 incidents of crop theft, with the IDF present in at least a quarter of cases.An IDF official said it takes acts of violence, criminal activity, and attempts to undermine security very seriously. The official did not refer to settlers or comment on the reports of olive theft in the presence of the IDF, which has separately uprooted trees with excavators, citing what it said was a need to prevent Palestinian attacks.The removal of Palestinians' olives has met with widely differing responses from Israeli rabbis."I call it theft. From my perspective, I define it as theft or robbery, and it is forbidden," said Zev Weitman, the rabbi for Alon Shvut, south of Bethlehem.Prominent Orthodox rabbi Dov Lior said settlers should harvest across the West Bank, asserting in an open letter that Palestinians had no ownership rights to the land and that harvesting olives fulfilled "the commandment of conquering the land."Hundreds of acres of the land around Salem's village, Lubban al-Gharbi, including olive groves, were fenced off and seized between 2023 and 2026 by Avichai Farm, an Israeli settler outpost built on a nearby hill.Salem said villagers have seen settlers harvest olives from the seized land and take them to the outpost's olive press.At the start of the olive harvest, settlers posted on social media, calling on Israelis to harvest olives in the West Bank and bring them to Avichai Farm's press."Both fine oil and strengthening the Jewish hold on the vast expanses of our land!," read a message on a settler Telegram group. "It's either our enemy or us!"The press at Avichai Farm advertises "premium products produced by Avichai Farm," including olive oil at about $20 a bottle, on a website run by the Farms Association, a settler group Reuters has reported receives significant financial support from the Israeli government, which says the aim is to promote peace.The Farms Association did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the couple who live on the farm with their children declined to be interviewed by a Reuters reporter who approached the area on Sunday.On a road leading to Avichai Farm, Reuters spoke to a man who declined to be identified and said he had driven from a settlement around 90 minutes away to press 14 bags of olives from trees he said he grew himself.West Bank Palestinians accuse settlers of stealing olives from their landLubban al-Gharbi villagers are among those who say that the harvesting of olives from trees in groves seized from Palestinian land constitutes theft.During this year's olive harvest, Palestinian authorities say three Palestinians have been killed in daily settler attacks, which have also injured several journalists, European diplomats, and a French mayor.Stahl said the violence was "part of a campaign of ethnic cleansing, paving the way for the annexation of the West Bank without its Palestinian population."Israel said it is investigating some of the incidents.An Israeli government spokesperson said olives "picked by a Jew in the ancestral homeland of the Jewish people" did not constitute theft and that Jews owned and cultivated "millions of olive trees" in the area. No one should take the law into their own hands, the spokesperson added.Palestinian farmer Samer Ben Shamsi said masked settlers attacked him on October 9 in the Palestinian village of Beita near Nablus, then sped away in a pickup truck with his harvest of olives after he and other farmers fled."This year, they steal without fear because they have a state and a powerful force backing them," Ben Shamsi said, referring to the security forces.Within the past year alone, settlers had shot him in the leg, beaten him, and smashed his possessions, he said."We pay in blood for the olives."

title: Large calibre gun production returns to Britain
body: Rheinmetall has officially opened its UK Gun Hall at Telford in the presence of Wes Streeting, the Secretary of State for Defence, marking the return of independent production of large-calibre weapons to Britain, according to the company. The facility will manufacture 120mm and 155mm weapon systems, including those supporting Challenger 3 and future artillery platforms. It offers 11,500 square metres of production space and at peak capacity can produce up to 245 barrels a year across both calibres, along with more than fifty breeches annually. Wes Streeting said: “Britain is back in the business of making the weapons that our Armed Forces need to defend the nation against our adversaries. From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action. One hundred skilled jobs in world-class manufacturing and the return of large-calibre weapon production to UK soil for the first time in twenty years – this is what defence as an engine for growth looks like.” Rheinmetall turned an empty facility into an operational manufacturing capability in eight months, installing and commissioning advanced manufacturing equipment and transferring specialist expertise to the British workforce. Production of breeches and breech blocks began in May and barrel production followed in June. Armin Papperger, chief executive of Rheinmetall AG, who hosted the opening ceremony alongside Streeting, said: “Today’s opening is an important milestone for Rheinmetall and for the United Kingdom. In a remarkably short period of time, we have turned our commitment into a sovereign manufacturing capability that will strengthen Britain’s defence industrial base for decades to come. The UK has been a long-standing and valued partner for Rheinmetall, and today we are building on an already strong relationship. We are committed to investing in the UK for the long term, expanding our industrial footprint and working together to deliver the capabilities needed for the future. By combining Rheinmetall’s expertise with British skills, innovation and manufacturing, we are strengthening the UK’s sovereign industrial capacity, supporting the Armed Forces and contributing to the security of NATO and Europe.” Rebecca Richards, managing director of Rheinmetall UK, said: “The official opening of our UK Gun Hall is a landmark moment for Rheinmetall UK and for Britain’s defence industrial base. In just eight months, we transformed an empty facility into an operational manufacturing capability by investing in British people, British skills and British industry. From the outset, we have listened to what the UK needs and focused on delivering sovereign capability at pace. By transferring specialist knowledge from Germany and developing a highly skilled British workforce here in Telford, we are creating skilled jobs, supporting British businesses and building the industrial capacity needed to equip our Armed Forces while investing in the long-term prosperity of the UK.” The Gun Hall is expected to support more than a hundred highly skilled people as production develops. Rheinmetall currently employs around 685 people in Telford, thirty-five of them at the Gun Hall, and the facility forms part of more than £200 million the company has invested across its British operations over the past five years. British employees undertook training and knowledge transfer at Rheinmetall’s production facility at Unterlüß in Germany, gaining expertise in precision manufacturing, quality assurance and specialist weapon production before bringing it back to Telford. The company has also recruited specialist skills from across the Telford region. Rheinmetall said it intends to introduce British steel from Sheffield Forgemasters into production. This publication has reported on the wider work to rebuild Britain’s ability to manufacture large calibre guns and on the point at which the first British-made artillery barrels headed to Ukraine . The company described the Gun Hall as a concrete example of the industrial partnership between the United Kingdom and Germany established under the Trinity House Agreement. The investment complements Rheinmetall UK’s work on the Boxer Mechanised Infantry Vehicle and the Challenger 3 programme, both of which are built at Telford by Rheinmetall BAE Systems Land. Ministers confirmed in Parliament this month that there is no current requirement to procure new 105mm barrels for the L118 Light Gun, and consequently no plans to restore domestic production of that calibre. The post Large calibre gun production returns to Britain first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Trilateral summit on Ukraine, Russia’s unlikely isolation: MFA briefing
body:
NIZHNY NOVGOROD, October 22. /TASS/. A meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin, US leader Donald Trump, and Vladimir Zelensky is being discussed, but no final agreement has been reached yet, said Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov.
Speaking at the Nizhny Novgorod Economic Forum, he noted that the European countries’ position on the conflict in Ukraine is anti-Russian, extremely belligerent, and very dangerous. According to Ryabkov, Russia cannot be isolated "by definition."
TASS has compiled the key statements made by the deputy foreign minister.
Russia is reviewing the ideas and proposals brought by US negotiators: "We are currently analyzing the content of these additional considerations and ideas."
Russia hopes that the United States is now carefully examining what it heard on Wednesday from Russian President Vladimir Putin: "I very much hope that our American colleagues are currently engaged in the same work. They are carefully, attentively, and deeply delving into what they heard at the Konstantinovsky Palace directly from the president."
Russia expects that the Trump administration will be able to embrace the logic of resolving the conflict in Ukraine based on the situation on the ground: "Full consideration of the changed realities on the ground, our constitutional realities, and the current situation on the battlefield is an imperative. This is the basis on which we engage in dialogue with the United States, and we will not deviate from this approach. We expect the Trump administration to understand the logic behind such a settlement and the imperative of addressing these realities, and to act accordingly in its future dealings with both its minions in Kiev and the European bloc."
Russia keeps the settlement in Ukraine high on the agenda in its relations with the United States.
A meeting between Putin, Trump, and Zelensky is being discussed, but a full agreement is still pending: "The idea has been raised, but there is no final understanding on this yet. There is no full agreement at this point. Discussions are ongoing."
Finding ways to resolve the conflict around Ukraine is difficult, but Russia starts from the premise that any solution must ensure the most reliable resolution of the fundamental problems that made the launch of the special military operation inevitable: "Finding a way forward is no easy task. We cannot abandon the fundamental principle that any solution - whether political or military, should political and diplomatic methods fail - must ensure the most reliable settlement of the underlying problems that made the launch of the special military operation inevitable.
"It is absolutely essential to address the root causes and underlying factors of this conflict and to resolve the situation that led to the emergence of this acute crisis."
The European stance on the Ukraine conflict is anti-Russian, highly confrontational and dangerous: "The European group is currently taking the most anti-Russian, the most belligerent and, therefore, highly dangerous position."
Diplomacy is the art of reaching agreements. "We are not giving up. We are playing on many fronts and will continue to do so. We are open to peace.
"Russia cannot be isolated by definition: it is a continent in its own right and an integral part of Eurasia. Remember, everyone who thinks differently - you won’t succeed in your attempts to impose your will on Great Russia and its partners.
Russia firmly defends its national interests: "Russian diplomacy is guided by the country’s leadership towards resolute protection of national interests and towards creating favorable external conditions to ensure the country’s safe and steady development."
At the same time, Russia is building equitable cooperation with countries that are willing to cooperate. "Moreover, unlike those who, according to the Russian president, believe it is permissible to dictate their will, preach about life, and give orders by the right of strength, we are ready to develop equal and mutually beneficial relations with everyone who is open to cooperation on similar principles.
"In the face of unprecedented Western sanctions, in an environment where attempts to isolate Russia continue unabated, we are focusing our efforts on building a new infrastructure for foreign economic activity that is protected from destructive external interference, including production and logistics chains and transport corridors."
The share of payments in national currencies among the member-states of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) has risen above 90%: "We are working with the partners on creation of a new payment infrastructure, on integration of the national systems of financial information transmission," he said.
"We have already transferred a significant portion of mutual settlements to the national currencies and are continuing this work. Within the EAEU, the share of the national currencies in services and trade exceeds 90%."
Currently, a free trade agreement is in force between the EAEU and Vietnam, Serbia, Iran, Mongolia, and the UAE: "A similar document with Indonesia has been signed and will soon come into force. A non-preferential trade agreement is being implemented. Negotiations are underway on the parameters of trade liberalization with India. A decision was made to launch corresponding negotiations with Tunisia. The feasibility of such a step in relations with Pakistan and Jordan is being studied."

title: GES warns teachers against GH¢210 promotion scam
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has warned teachers applying for promotion to disregard demands for GH¢210 from individuals claiming they can facilitate their applications. The Service said it had received reports that some individuals were requesting the money from promotion applicants under the pretext of helping them secure approval. In a notice shared on Facebook on Wednesday, October 21, the GES stressed that the teacher promotion process was fair, transparent and entirely free of charge. It, therefore, urged applicants not to make payments to individuals who claim they can facilitate or influence the outcome of the process. “Applicants are, therefore, advised to ignore any demands and refrain from making payments to individuals who claim they can facilitate or influence the promotion process,” the Service stated. The GES further directed teachers to follow only the official procedures and guidelines communicated by the Service in pursuing their promotion applications. The warning comes amid concerns over attempts by individuals to exploit teachers seeking career advancement by demanding money in exchange for purported assistance. The Service’s advisory is intended to protect applicants from potential financial exploitation and reinforce the integrity of the promotion process. Teachers have been urged to remain vigilant and avoid unofficial payment arrangements, as the GES maintains that no fee is required to facilitate or influence their promotion applications.

title: Fog blinds Ukrainian drones. Russia resumes mechanized assaults in the south after months-long pause, military officials say
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russian forces are preparing to resume mechanized assaults in southern Ukraine after a pause of several months and are moving armored vehicles toward areas where they plan to launch offensives, Anastasiia Shevchenko, deputy spokesperson for the Southern Forces Grouping, told Ukrinform on 22 October. The Huliaipole axis remains the hottest in the Southern grouping’s zone, with 10 to 20 combat engagements reported on an average day, she said. On the Huliaipole axis, one of Russia’s largest force groupings is fighting Ukrainian forces, comprising units from several Russian combined-arms armies, the spokesperson says. Over the past week, as the weather worsened, Russian forces began local assaults there with infantry, motorcycles, and armored vehicles, seeking to break through toward Zaporizhzhia and blockade the city, Ukraine’s 7th Air Assault Corps reported , adding that the area is one of Russia’s key priorities in southern Ukraine. Russia has used fog this way before: last November, Russian troops moved under its cover to avoid detection by Ukrainian drones as they advanced on Huliaipole, the Institute for the Study of War assessed . Russian forces have abandoned large-scale assaults across a broad front and are attempting to infiltrate Ukrainian positions in small groups. They periodically use motorcycles and quad bikes for assaults, Shevchenko said, adding that these vehicles are fast and maneuverable. However, Russian forces should not expect to advance unimpeded, the spokesperson noted. Ukrainian units control Russian supply routes and systematically detect and strike Russian personnel and equipment while they are still moving toward their launch positions, she added. “Specifically, speaking in numbers, since the beginning of October alone, units of the Southern Forces Grouping (Forces) have destroyed more than 3,000 occupiers and 1,300 pieces of weapons and military equipment. Thus, the enemy is suffering significant losses in the operational zone of the Southern Forces Grouping (Forces),” the spokesperson concluded. Ukrainian drones disrupt Russian logistics Russian forces had stopped using military vehicles because Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces controlled their logistics, Shevchenko said in comments to Ukrinform on 16 September. Ukrainian drones spotted Russian troops and equipment in time and struck them mostly on their routes of advance, she said. Ukrainian air strikes destroyed bridges near Polohy in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, complicating Russian supply operations along the Huliaipole axis, Ukraine’s 7th Air Assault Corps reported on 21 September. Russian forces had used these bridges to move personnel, heavy equipment, and ammunition for their offensive toward Orikhiv. Disruptions to logistics have forced Russian units to rely more on motorcycles, which are more vulnerable to Ukrainian strikes, the corps said. Explore further Ukraine timed its Huliaipole operation around the weather — and it worked. Here’s why that won’t happen again soon Russian forces are also expected to use fog and rain as cover for assaults, Mykola Zinko, deputy commander of the unmanned systems battalion of the 5th Assault Brigade, said on 19 October. Russia has brought up reserves, and its heavy equipment will move out under the fog, he said. Read also Russia marched into Huliaipole in December. Now it can’t march out. title: Witkoff lauds 'humanitarian' Putin as Russia releases detained American
body:
Stephen Hubbard, 74, was arrested by Russian forces in Ukraine in April 2022.
LONDON -- Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan who had been in Russian detention since 2022, was released Wednesday.
President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Russia to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and oversee Hubbard's release. Witkoff landed in the Russian city of St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, a Kremlin aide confirmed, ahead of the planned meeting with Putin.
Trump's envoy thanked Putin for freeing Hubbard. Putin said that Hubbard -- who was detained in eastern Ukraine in April 2022 -- was taken to St. Peterburg's Pulkovo Airport.
"I want to thank you very much. The president sends his thanks," Witkoff said. "Because of you, he's going home to his family."
"You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian," Witkoff told Putin. "You are a humanitarian also, sir."
Witkoff said in a post on X later Wednesday that Hubbard was on his way back to the United States. He shared photos of himself meeting the former American teacher, as well as an image of Hubbard aboard what appeared to be a jet.
"Now, he is on his way back to a family who loves him, a President who never gave up on him, and a nation that proudly welcomes him home," Witkoff said in part.
Witkoff added that Hubbard's release "was not part of an exchange – and we extend our thanks to President Putin for releasing him on President Trump’s request."
President Donald Trump on Wednesday, during a roundtable event on cybersecurity, was asked whether he agreed with Witkoff calling Vladimir Putin a “humanitarian.”
“I guess you could say for that particular purpose” of securing Hubbard's release, Trump said, though he went on to add, “I wouldn’t say anything one way or the other.”
The president appeared to suggest that he wished to avoid antagonizing Russia amid the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
"You know, we're negotiating with Russia to stop the war with Ukraine, and we have been pretty happy with Russia that they have not gotten involved with Iran," Trump said. "So, the last thing I want to do is upset an apple cart where we're getting close to settling a war."
Vice President JD Vance, speaking at an unrelated event in Ohio earlier Wednesday, defended Witkoff calling Putin a "humanitarian" after some lawmakers, including Republican Sens. Thom Tillis and John Cornyn and Democratic Sens. Chris Coons and Mark Kelly , pushed back forcefully against the characterization. Cornyn in particular called Putin a "stone cold killer" while Tillis said Witkoff's statement was "embarrassing and outrageous."
“I agree with Steve Witkoff saying something nice to a person who just released an American hostage,” Vance told reporters. “I care much less about what Steve said and about the fact that he is bringing an American hostage home to his family, we should all be celebrating that, not be complaining about what Steve Witkoff said in order to get it done."
Hubbard's sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, told ABC News on Wednesday that she was thanking Trump "for being the hand of God and bringing Stephen Hubbard home."
"He's been gone a long, long time. Thank you President Trump for caring for everyday Americans," she said, adding that the development was "awesome" and that the "Lord has given me peace."
Fox said she had not yet spoken to her brother or to U.S. officials and that she learned about Hubbard's release from the media. Hubbard, she added, will be flown to San Antonio where there is a military base that released Americans are usually brought to for treatment.
Trump later wrote in a post to social media he asked Putin to release Hubbard in a phone call that took place last week. "Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family," Trump wrote.
The U.S. "was not required to give anything in return -- an unprecedented situation for Russia," Trump added. "There was no 'swap' necessary for this release."
The president then posted to social media again defending his recent decision to waive numerous sanctions on Russia.
"If sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt," Trump wrote of the discussions over Hubbard's release.
Witkoff arrived in St. Petersburg as the Trump administration was closing in on a deal that would see multiple Americans released from detention in Russia, two U.S. officials and another source familiar with the matter told ABC News.
The talks were centered on Hubbard and several other U.S. citizens held by Moscow on what the administration believes are dubious charges, the source said.
Hubbard had been living in eastern Ukraine as a civilian since around 2014, where he taught English and had a relationship with a Ukrainian woman, according to his family.
After he was detained, Russian authorities charged Hubbard with acting as a mercenary and fighting for Ukraine, sentencing him to nearly seven years in prison. Hubbard's family and U.S. officials said the charges were false and the State Department designated him as wrongfully detained.
During their meeting, Witkoff and Putin discussed the latest U.S.-led efforts to end Moscow's ongoing invasion, which the Kremlin launched in February 2022.
"One thing that I hope to accomplish today is to have some good conversation between us about resumption potentially of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States," Witkoff said.
Witkoff also touted U.S.-Russian "business and economic cooperation" as "an example of what the possibilities are in the future."
Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg following a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Norwegian capital of Oslo on Tuesday. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb also attended the talks, which focused on ceasefire proposals to halt Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Witkoff's latest round of shuttle diplomacy comes amid intensifying White House pressure on Zelenskyy to make concessions to secure a peace deal with Moscow.
In recent weeks, Trump waived a raft of sanctions on Moscow and again blamed Kyiv for the lack of progress in U.S.-sponsored peace talks, even suggesting that Zelenskyy should be replaced as Ukrainian president.
On Tuesday, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that the U.S. had received "nothing" for its support of Ukraine.
"Look, we have given tremendous amounts to Ukraine. We've got nothing back other than high diesel," Trump said. "We have given, probably, possibly, more money to Ukraine than almost anybody over the years, hundreds of billions of dollars. We've got nothing back, and the American taxpayers are tired of it. We want Zelenskyy to make a deal."
Following his meetings in Oslo on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said in posts to social media that he was "thankful to the American side" for its input on propose future security guarantees for Kyiv. The Ukrainian president also said he spoke with Secretary of State Marco Rubio by phone to discuss "sensitive issues such as Starlink, ballistic missile interceptors and intelligence."
On Wednesday, Zelenskyy said he continued to hold meetings in Oslo. "A lot depends on whether the American side manages to hear something new from Russia today -- about peace, not about continuing the war," he wrote.
ABC News' Joe Simonetti, Shannon K. Kingston, Fritz Farrow, Nicholas Kerr, Emily Chang, Anna Sergeeva and Justin Gomez contributed to this report.

title: Russian forces strike food production facility in Odesa region, fire extinguished
body:
Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"A civilian enterprise that produces food came under attack. The administrative building was almost completely gutted by fire following a direct hit," Kiper wrote.
According to him, no one was injured in the attack.
The Odesa regional office of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that the enemy strike damaged a two-story administrative building at the facility. More than 30 rescuers were involved in dealing with the aftermath of the attack.
The agency later reported that firefighters had extinguished the blaze at the facility.
According to the Bessarabia.UA news outlet, Russian forces attacked the Titan food production facility in the Kiliia community of the Izmail district for a second time overnight on October 22. The strike destroyed the facility's administrative building, which was constructed in 2007.
According to the facility's owner, Ihor Kapitan, Russian drones struck Titan's production workshop and storage facilities overnight on October 21, while the administrative building came under attack the following night. A fire broke out, affecting a total area of 650 square meters.
Kapitan said that the first floor of the administrative building housed a bakery and premises used to produce semi-finished food products. These areas were also damaged.
Kapitan stressed that no one was injured in the second attack.

title: Uganda Airlines enters Ghana aviation market with flights between Entebbe and Accra starting Oct 27
body: Uganda Airlines is entering Ghana’s aviation market from October 27 with a promotional return fare flight between Entebbe and Accra, raising the prospect of stronger price competition on travel between West and East Africa. The Ugandan national carrier will begin four-times-weekly services on October 27, 2026 offering travellers an additional option on a market currently served by established airlines connecting through their regional hubs. The promotional fare could put pressure on competing carriers to review their pricing, particularly for passengers travelling between Ghana and Uganda for business, leisure and family visits. Any sustained reduction in ticket prices, however, will depend on demand, available capacity and how rival airlines respond. For Ghanaian travellers, the entry offers a potential opportunity to compare more fares and schedules when planning trips to East African destinations. Businesses could also benefit if lower airfares make regional meetings, trade missions and commercial partnerships more affordable. The route is relevant to efforts to deepen trade between the two regions, where the cost and convenience of air travel can influence how frequently entrepreneurs, investors and service providers meet across borders. Improved connectivity could also support tourism exchanges, giving Ghanaian visitors another travel option to visa-free Uganda while helping Ugandan travellers access Accra’s commercial, cultural and hospitality markets. Uganda Airlines’ entry comes as African aviation stakeholders seek to improve intra-continental connectivity and reduce dependence on indirect journeys through European and Middle Eastern hubs. Better connections are also viewed as important to the African Continental Free Trade Area’s ambitions to increase trade among African economies. The passengers originating their travel from Accra, Ghana, the greater competition could benefit consumers. Ticket are now on sale for the new service which will operate via Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Moscow Court Upholds Detention of Political Analyst Alexander Kynev Despite Serious Injury
body:
A Moscow judge has rejected political analyst Alexander Kynev’s appeal against being held in pre-trial detention on drug trafficking charges despite growing concerns about a serious injury he sustained when he was arrested, the exiled news outlet Mediazona reported Thursday.
Kynev was arrested at his Moscow apartment last month on charges of attempting to sell a large amount of drugs. He was later hospitalized inside a Moscow detention center for bone fractures and other injuries.
A lower Moscow court ordered Kynev to be placed in pre-trial detention until Nov. 24, with details of the case remaining withheld from the public. He denies the charges, which carry a punishment of up to 20 years in prison if convicted.
Kynev appeared at the Moscow City Court appeal hearing via video link with his leg in a cast. Kynev’s defense team warned that he faces permanent disability without proper medical care and crutches .
“If Kynev doesn’t get medical help soon, he’s going to end up disabled,” his attorney Vera Goncharova told the judge.
However, the judge rejected the defense’s request for house arrest or other forms of restrictions, ruling that Kynev will remain in custody until at least Nov. 24.
Kynev, who wrote regular opinion columns for The Moscow Times before it was designated an “undesirable” organization in 2024, has worked as a political consultant since the 1990s, when he was first involved with the campaigns of the liberal Yabloko party.
Over the years, he has worked for a number of independent political organizations, including the now-disbanded election observer Golos.
He remained in Russia despite growing political oppression following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Kynev was a leading commentator on the Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections before his arrest
He estimated a far lower turnout and vote share for the ruling United Russia party than the official results, warning that the party’s record haul of 349 out of 450 seats could backfire on the Kremlin.
