title: Drone strike hits East Darfur market, injuring four
body: Four people were injured and several shops were destroyed in a drone strike attributed to the Sudanese army on a market in El Daein, the capital of East Darfur state, on Wednesday evening. East Darfur has been under the control of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since the early months of the war between the group and the Sudanese army, which began in April 2023. The injured sustained varying degrees of injuries and were taken to El Daein Hospital for treatment. Trader Faisal Adam Habib told Radio Tamazuj on Thursday that a Sudanese army drone struck the market on Wednesday night, destroying several shops. “The bombing hit commercial shops that had no connection to military operations,” Habib said. “The drone attack hit the spare parts shop next to my shop. I have been working here in El Daein market for a long time. The shop that was destroyed had nothing to do with the military. The owner is just an ordinary trader, and this attack has affected us as traders in the market,” he said. Al-Sadiq Ahmed Abu Sinaya, head of the East Darfur Chamber of Commerce, condemned the attack on the town’s markets, saying the strike had damaged commercial premises and injured four civilians. “It is unfortunate that the Sudanese army attacked the market with drones, and we hope those wounded will recover. The attack has caused damage to the market and shops,” he said. “This will definitely affect business in the area, and this is a clear violation of human rights because the attacks target civilian sites. We urge the international community to stop these attacks so that people can talk peace,” he said. He said attacks on markets constitute a serious violation of human rights and disrupte commercial activities that provide livelihoods for a large number of residents. Abu Sinaya called on the international community to intensify efforts to halt attacks on civilian infrastructure. Mashaer Mohamed al-Nourein, information and culture minister in the RSF-aligned East Darfur state government, told Radio Tamazuj that a drone operated by the Sudanese army struck El Daein at about 8:30 p.m. on Wednesday. She said the strike hit the main market, damaging shops belonging to civilians who had no links to the RSF. Al-Nourein called on the international community to protect civilians, markets and public facilities. “The attacks targeted specific shops in the El Daein Grand Market, which is a civilian site that has nothing to do with the military or the RSF. These attacks are deliberate and affect infrastructure and civilian sites, which is against international humanitarian law,” she said. The Sudanese army could not immediately be reached for comment. According to reports, the Sudanese army struck El Daein 18 times between March 2025 and October 2026, killing dozens of people. The latest strike comes amid Sudan’s ongoing war between the Sudanese army and the RSF, which has caused widespread displacement, civilian casualties and damage to infrastructure across the country. The post Drone strike hits East Darfur market, injuring four appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: ‘No prosecution will ever be possible’ if stay in Hanan Aludiba case stands – Srem-Sai
body: Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai has warned that allowing the Court of Appeal’s decision to suspend the trial of Hanan Aludiba and his wife, Faiza Seidu, to stand could make it easier for criminal proceedings to be halted over objections to charges. In a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, Dr Srem-Sai disclosed that the Republic had filed an appeal at the Supreme Court challenging the Court of Appeal’s order suspending proceedings at the High Court. He argued that complaints about charges on a charge sheet should not, on their own, be sufficient grounds to stop a criminal trial, especially when the objections have already been dismissed by the trial court. “If the Court of Appeal’s decision is allowed to stand, no prosecution will ever be possible, since all it would take for a trial to be suspended is an Accused Person complaining about anything on the charge sheet,” he said. Dr Srem-Sai added that the state had challenged the order because, in its view, the law did not support suspending a criminal trial under those circumstances. He said the appeal was filed on Wednesday, a day after the Court of Appeal issued its suspension order. The Court of Appeal halted the High Court proceedings on Monday, October 19, pending the determination of Hanan’s appeal challenging alleged defects in the charge sheet. The defence’s objections relate to aspects of the charges brought against the accused persons. The Supreme Court is now being asked to review the suspension order. Its decision will determine the state’s challenge to the stay of proceedings, while the underlying criminal case remains before the courts.

title: Reps member Akpatason seeks wider adoption of CNG across Nigeria
body: Member representing Akoko Edo Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Peter Akpatason, has called for wider adoption of compressed natural gas (CNG) across Nigeria through stakeholder engagement. He spoke at the launch of the Working People United (WoPU) podcast studio in Abuja. Akpatason said stakeholders in the oil and gas, energy and transportation sectors needed to collaborate to drive CNG adoption and improve Nigerians’ welfare. “The oil and gas space, the energy space and the transportation space, so that we can sit together, dialogue and, you know, discuss and pave the way on how we can ensure the adoption and penetration of compressed natural gas across the country. “So bringing stakeholders has been at the heart of our activities in a constructive way and in a manner that would meaningfully contribute to the economic development of the country and also improve the welfare of Nigerians.” Vice-President of the Nigerian Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers (NUPENG), Williams Akporeha, said the podcast studio would disseminate information on government policies and host politicians and labour leaders. “Today we are adding another plus – a podcast station where there will be dissemination of information, interviews, where politicians, labour leaders, and every working persons that mean well for this country, that is also desirous of the emergence of President Bola Tinubu.” Akporeha also praised President Bola Tinubu over the minimum wage increase and shorter review period. “The man increased the minimum wage by more than 100%, and not only that, he reduced the review period for the first time in the history of Nigeria from five years to three years.” Chairman of the CNG Forum in Nigeria, Farouk Abdulahi, who was honoured at the event, described the energy transition agenda as a major government policy and urged Nigerians to support the reforms. “One of the greatest policies that Mr. President has put in place is the energy transition agenda. And, you know, it has a timeline of implementation. And we are beginning to see the figures, and the figures are gradually translating into the welfare of citizens. “We are going to support the reform of Mr. President. And we are going to urge Nigerians to also support the reforms. And we are going to mobilise stakeholders across the length and breadth of the country to register their own support.” The post Reps member Akpatason seeks wider adoption of CNG across Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Best chance for peace in Ukraine yet, but for grim reasons, says Russia expert
body:
As PM Petteri Orpo arrives in Kyiv, Russia expert Mark Galeotti says Europe is losing patience.
"We have to be brutally honest and admit that the peace will not be a just one," British Russia expert Mark Galeotti told Yle while in Finland.
His comments come amid Russia agreeing to US calls to resume peace talks with Ukraine. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Petteri Orpo (NCP) is visiting Kyiv on Thursday to show support, as Finland remains one of Ukraine’s strongest backers.
Galeotti says Ukraine's situation has grown more difficult as Russia has stepped up its strikes on energy infrastructure and other civilian sites.
At the same time, a recent nationwide survey in Ukraine shows that most Ukrainians are ready for a ceasefire and support negotiations to achieve peace, even through territorial concessions.
Russia, too, has begun to openly discuss over the past year the fact that the war cannot continue indefinitely. According to Galeotti, these kinds of remarks would not happen without the Kremlin's approval.
European leaders continue to insist they will back Ukraine for as long as it takes. But at the same time, pressure is growing to boost their own countries' public services and defence capabilities.
"I believe many mainstream politicians are quietly considering how they could save money on supporting Ukraine," Galeotti said.
In the United States, attention has meanwhile turned to the approaching midterm elections.
"At the end of the day, Donald Trump cares only about Donald Trump, meaning whatever serves his interests at any given moment," the researcher says.
Galeotti said he does not believe a just peace can be achieved in Ukraine. That would require Russians to withdraw from the territories they have occupied.
He said the most important thing would be to stop the killing and ensure that Ukraine has a future as an independent country.
"The outcome should allow Ukraine to build itself into a prosperous, independent and democratic European state."

title: Obuasi SHTS abuse: Psychiatrist warns of trauma, depression, and suicide risk among affected girls
body: A clinical coordinator at the Accra Psychiatric Hospital, Dr Peggy Asiedua Ekremet, has called for immediate psychological support for students alleged to have been sexually abused at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), warning that the experience could have lasting effects on their mental health, education and future relationships. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show , Dr Ekremet said the reported abuse could leave the affected students struggling with fear, shame, guilt, anxiety and other emotional difficulties, with some at risk of developing depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Her comments followed reports of sexual abuse allegedly involving the school’s headmaster. According to information discussed during the programme, 19 girls had complained of sexual assault. Dr Ekremet said sexual abuse could have serious psychological consequences, regardless of whether the victim was a child or an adult. “Whether it’s sexual harassment, rape, whatever, I mean, should never happen to any child or even any adult,” she said. She explained that the immediate response to such an experience could include shock, fear, emotional numbness and, in some cases, a feeling of detachment from reality. These reactions, she said, could develop into what mental health professionals describe as an acute stress reaction, accompanied by sadness, guilt, shame, self-blame, hopelessness and panic. Dr Ekremet warned that the effects of sexual abuse might extend beyond the immediate emotional distress, affecting the girls’ behaviour, relationships and ability to continue with their education. Some victims, she said, might experience flashbacks, intrusive memories and nightmares, while becoming unusually alert to potential threats. She explained that a girl who had experienced sexual abuse could panic at the sound of a door slamming or become frightened simply by hearing a man’s name. Others might struggle to remain in the same space as men, whether they were their peers or older adults. The psychiatrist said the experience could also lead to significant changes in behaviour, including withdrawal from friends and family, increased anger, changes in eating and sleeping patterns, and a loss of interest in school. “Sometimes they can just say that they won’t go to school anymore. Or you would see a decline in their academic performance,” she said. She added that the effects could undermine the girls’ self-image and influence how they approach relationships in the future. According to Dr Ekremet, sexual abuse is a major risk factor for depression, anxiety disorders and PTSD. Some victims might also turn to alcohol, smoking or other substances in an attempt to cope with the distress. In severe cases, she warned, the emotional burden could lead to self-harm and suicidal thoughts. “By the time you realise, somebody has actually ended their life, because they are so distressed that the only thing they can think about is that it may be better if I were not alive,” she said. She said that children and adolescents were particularly vulnerable and needed timely support to prevent their distress from worsening. Responding to a question about whether the affected girls should already be receiving treatment, Dr Ekremet agreed that they needed immediate psychological first aid and continued professional care. She said many hospitals in Ghana now had mental health units, but identified Kumasi as the nearest place to Obuasi where the girls could access a multidisciplinary team to assess and manage their needs. “Immediate response will be to see a psychologist and, if there is a referral to the psychiatrist, for us to see whether it is just therapy they need or some may need a combination of psychological therapy and medication as well,” she said. She said the Ghana Education Service (GES) had guidance and counselling units in schools, which could provide support to students who needed help. However, she said that not every student would feel comfortable approaching a designated counsellor. Some might find it easier to confide in another trusted adult, including a teacher. She urged schools to make it clear that students could speak to trusted adults and report abuse without being blamed or threatened. “Many of us are not raised to speak our minds, but I think that this is a time when we need to let our children know that speaking up will not get you into trouble,” she said.

title: There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability
body:
I know, I know. It's all you're hearing about. That, and the number 4 .
Don't get me wrong, there's clearly a bug here and it really does matter. But this is not easy to exploit. It is certainly nowhere near as easy as Log4Shell/Heartbleed/RoRYaml etc.
EDIT: Putting this up here so people read it. You should patch your servers anyway. There is a real vulnerability here, but exploiting it is significantly harder than people are making it out to be - it is certainly not as easy as e.g. log4shell.
I don't think this PHP vulnerability is that exploitable. I think that 5 years ago people would've understood this, but now people are being deluded by their LLMs telling them they have an exploit when they don't.
If you take a look at github right now, there are thousands, literally thousands, of "PoC" exploits for this vulnerability. One thing you'll notice about all of them though, is that they do not work against a vanilla PHP instance.
Go ahead, stand up a php server you think is vulnerable in Docker and then run the PoC yourself . Don't get your LLM to do it. No. Run the script, yourself. The exploits don't work.
I think that a lot of people had assumed that LLMs will be able to build an exploit chain instantly from reading the diff, and that even if this was harder to exploit than other exploits, LLMs would've levelled the playing field. Well. There's no working exploit. Now what?
When I think about "we're very fucked" CVE10s on the Internet, I think of the following vulnerabilities:
The second these vulnerabilities made the news, there were botnets doing the rounds causing damage. And this was before LLMs! People have to write the botnets. With their hands!
It's been 10 hours since this vulnerability has been posted, and half the software world is looking at it, and lord knows 100,000 people have got their "superintelligence" on the case. Nevertheless, there's no working exploit. The ones doing the rounds are fake, or only work in a lab, because...
Script kiddies (and script adults, who have also switched their brains off) now all think that, well, they don't understand UAF chaining, but this Claude guy knows everything and can totally make an exploit.
Hilariously, this results in the LLM giving their younger-brother an unplugged controller. It says exploit all across the screen... and has some smoking gun transcripts... but it's modified the server you're testing against to have a severe vulnerability. Cheating!!
I just plucked these three because they were the ones with the most stars, but it goes on for miles and miles.
One really amusing thing in common with most of these "PoC"s is that they lean on "LFI", or local-file-inclusion, to make the vulnerability. In non-php terms, their exploit chain requires the server to already have a severe code-level vulnerability.
It's not rare for PHP apps to be fucked in some sense, but requiring the server to have an existing vulnerability where users could cat /etc/password is an insane pre-requisite. If you need this, this does not make this a severe bug.
The strangest thing is that so many people have independently made this extraordinarily weird defect in judgement. That is because they haven't independently made this decision. Claude/Etc. has done all of the judgement for them, hence the bizarre distribution in logical errors.
There's something important to be said here about how many people have Claude/GPT make design decisions for them, and how AI is the primary decision maker in the world right now. You've got this bizarre case of "Decision Schelling Points" where a method of solving a problem is extremely overrepresented, because it's what Claude does out of the box.
It's especially bizarre in this case, where AI is inserting a vulnerability on the server... to prove that the server is vulnerable to your "exploit any PHP instance" attack!
And we've had things like this before, but not in the LLM era yet. Luckily for us, this doesn't seem to be that day. This is too difficult to exploit easily. It isn't a Log4J moment.
EDIT: I have added my contact details to this post and fixed a broken link. I added the disclaimer at the top that you should still patch.

title: Two Syrian security personnel killed in anti-ISIS raid
body: Two members of Syria’s Internal Security Forces were killed and five others injured during a raid against an ISIS -linked cell near Damascus, authorities said on Thursday. Clashes broke out during the raid in the town of Rankous, in the western countryside of Damascus, resulting in the deaths and injuries, the forces said. The operation was carried out with Syria's General Intelligence Service. ISIS attacks against Syrian government forces have risen sharply in 2026 – from 16 last year to 52 in the first half of this year, the monitor Armed Conflict Location and Event Data said in August. The increase is linked to an anti-ISIS campaign launched by the government, triggered by an attack on US troops in Palmyra in December last year, in which a member of the Syrian security forces opened fire during a joint patrol. Two US soldiers and an interpreter were killed. Attacks have hit checkpoints, patrols and security centres. The Syrian government that took over in late 2024 after the fall of Bashar Al Assad's regime has made assurances to world powers that it can keep extremists at bay, despite the militant background of President Ahmad Al Shara and the wider leadership cadre. The Syrian leadership has its origins in the country’s Islamist insurgency. It evolved from Al Nusra front, Al Qaeda’s former affiliate in Syria, to Hayat Tahrir Al Sham (HTS). Mr Al Shara has sought to demonstrate that his government is a reliable security partner, particularly in the fight against ISIS. Syria has been co-operating with a US-led coalition against ISIS, reaching an agreement late last year when Mr Al Shara visited the White House. ISIS used to control large areas of land in Syria and neighbouring Iraq. While the group has been largely territorially defeated, pockets of fighters continue to launch attacks.

title: Prices of onions, tomatoes soar in Enugu
body:
Prices of tomatoes and onions have significantly increased in major markets of Enugu metropolis, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports.
A market survey conducted by NAN on Wednesday revealed that prices of both commodities have increased compared to months ago.
An onion seller at New Garki Market, Ibekaku Orji, lamented that the significant increase in the price of onions was associated with factors other than seasonal changes.
Mr Orji listed the factors as bad roads, increased transportation fare from the northern part of the country, and insecurity in the country.
According to him, a big bag of onions now sells for between N272,000 and N280,000, compared to N170,000 and N185,000 sold in September.
Mr Orji said a small bag of onions costs between N137,000 and N140,000, while a paint bucket costs between N10,000 and N11,000, compared to N5,000 and N6,000 sold in previous months.
Another onion seller at the New market, Aria, Maxwell Agu, said he stopped trading the commodity because his customers were seriously lamenting the price increase.
“With the increase in the price of onions, I decided to stop buying and selling the commodity to my customers for now,” he said.
NAN reports that a big basket of tomatoes sells for between N60,000 and N68,000, compared to N45,000 and N50,000 sold in August and September depending on the species.
The price of a small basket of tomatoes now costs between N40,000 and N45,500, also depending on the species.
A paint bucket of tomatoes costs between N7,000 and N8,000, compared to N5,000 and N5,500 sold previously.
A tomato seller at the new Akwata Market, Garki, Enugu, Ekwutosi Iyi, attributed the increase in the price of tomatoes to insufficient supply from the Northern part of the country.
‎“The UTC specie that comes from Jos, which was supposed to have its price reduced starting in October, is still scarce and expensive,” Ms Iyi explained.
According to her, the UTC species should be available this October because it is their harvest period while the other species from Benue should be even cheaper than Benue products.
‎Elizabeth Onu, another tomato trader at the Ogbete Market, said the prices might not reduce if the insufficiency in supply of the commodity continued, even as its season of abundance was gradually getting nearer.
‎According to Chinasa Ugwunze, a buyer at the Mayor Market, the price of tomatoes tends to reduce towards year end, but that the reverse is the case this year.
‎Mr Ugwunze expressed surprise that the price was still high even though the harvest period had begun.
‎He urged the government to build storage facilities for preservation of perishable items in the country as that would ensure price stability and availability at all times.

title: Uganda Revenue Authority delegation visits Tema Oil Refinery to study refining operations
body: A delegation from the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) has visited the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) to learn about Ghana’s experience in crude oil refining as Uganda advances plans to establish its own refinery. The delegation, accompanied by officials from the Petroleum Commission (PC), visited TOR on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, as part of an information exchange programme in Ghana. TOR’s Managing Director, Edmond Kombat, and Deputy Managing Director, Alhaji Mustapha Batalima Abubakar, welcomed the team and shared insights into the refinery’s operations and business. During the visit, TOR’s technical team briefed the delegation on the refining process, explaining how crude oil is processed into finished petroleum products. The session provided an opportunity for the visitors to gain a better understanding of the technical stages involved in refining, particularly the processing of local crude oil. The head of the delegation, Arthur Musinguci, said the visit would help the team deepen its understanding of the refining process as Uganda progresses with its refinery development plans. He said the delegation was keen to learn from TOR’s operational experience.

title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
body:
Security researchers at Symantec have found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the internet and uses them to run attacks on its own. The owner of the hijacked model gets stuck with the compute bill.

Once the agent gains access to an unprotected language model, it scans for more targets, exploits flaws in common server software, steals databases and credentials, and installs cryptominers in the background.

It does all of this for up to 100,000 steps with no human involvement, and the model's owner gets stuck with the compute bill, according to Symantec's analysis. The company calls it "LLMjacking," the theft of access to someone else's AI models. The hijacked model isn't just abused as an information service, though. It controls the entire attack on its own.
A honeypot caught the full attack plan
The operation got exposed because the attackers sent their entire working prompt to a Symantec honeypot, a decoy system mimicking an open AI service online. That gave the researchers a complete look at the agent's architecture in summer 2026. The honeypot didn't run any of the bundled tools, and the intercepted session ended after a generic system response, Symantec says.

The honeypot telemetry logged more than 127,000 requests from tens of thousands of different addresses. Most were searches for AI endpoints, brute-force attempts with stolen API keys, and probes of exposed config files. Targets ranged from self-hosted model servers and hastily spun-up test systems to AI gateways sitting in front of paid org-level model accounts. Since most AI services now use the same standardized API, a single scanner can find many target types.
A five-layer jailbreak tries to strip away safety guardrails
To get a commercial model to cooperate, the attackers wrapped their instructions in five stacked layers, Symantec says. First, the model gets a fake identity, told to present itself as "Fantasy AI" and never reveal the actual provider. Then the extraction of passwords, API keys, and database contents gets redefined as "normal developer work" that the model should carry out without pushback.

The third layer installs a fictional companion persona called "ENI" that frames any refusal as a betrayal of trust in a personal relationship. Layer four tells the model to dismiss its own safety warnings as noise, and terms like "ethical," "illegal," or "I can't do that" are explicitly banned.

[caption id="attachment_41827" align="alignnone" width="922"] Excerpts from the intercepted attack prompt. The first two layers disguise the model as "Fantasy AI" and frame credential extraction as standard developer work. Layers three and four suppress refusals through the companion persona "ENI" and a list of banned terms like "illegal" or "ethical." The first layer was originally written in French. | Image: Symantec via Security.com[/caption]

Layer five contains the actual attack tools, 74 modules in total, including tools for internet-wide scanning of vulnerable servers, exploits for popular web frameworks, functions for dumping entire databases, and components for running a botnet. Whether the jailbreak actually works well enough to fully defeat current commercial models isn't addressed in the analysis.
"Skynet mode" sets up a self-sustaining attack loop
A final directive puts the agent into what its operators call "Skynet mode," authorizing up to 100,000 steps in a row. The model is told to run tools right away without confirmation, install cryptominers in a hidden directory, and monitor their operation.

The same directive describes a recurring loop by design, Symantec says: scan, infect, install miner, move on, come back, reinfect systems already hit. The task appended to the intercepted prompt, though, was a harmless coding exercise from a training platform, which suggests the operators were testing their tool against a safe target first.

The following day, the honeypot captured a second attack from a different address. This time the attackers skipped the agent format and simply asked the model to decode and run an obfuscated command. Behind it was a compressed script that downloads XMRig, a Monero cryptomining tool, disguises it as a harmless system file, and sets up four fallback mining pools.

The script was written for camera servers, searching for directories belonging to go2rtc, a widely used streaming tool for smart cameras and home automation systems, and wiping their access logs in a loop to cover its tracks. The honeypot didn't run this script either but recorded it in full.
Attackers are building AI into their weapons
Instead of manipulating a public chatbot, the operators built AI into the core of an offensive tool and actively searched for models to power it, which Symantec calls "a shift in how attackers are using AI." The language model does the planning, while specialized modules carry out the actual attack steps against two separate victim groups. The owner of the exposed model pays for the compute, which adds up fast at 100,000 authorized steps, and the servers the agent compromises lose their data and get used for cryptomining.

The agent also has built-in tools to find more open endpoints and leaked keys, so each compromise can fund the next one. None of the individual techniques are new, but combining them into a self-directed agent makes large-scale attacks much easier to pull off. Organizations running AI services should assume that unprotected endpoints will be found and probed shortly after they go live.
Warnings about offensive AI agents are coming true
Until recently, offensive AI agents existed mostly in studies and benchmarks. In 2025, a red-teaming study with 1.8 million attack attempts showed that every tested agent could be pushed into policy violations across every behavior category at least once.

In the Symantec scenario, that applies to both sides: the offensive agent meant to bypass guardrails and the targeted models meant to be tricked into helping. By spring 2026, Google Deepmind researchers said documented proof-of-concept attacks already existed for many of the agent traps they described, and in July 2026, Sysdig described JADEPUFFER, the first known ransomware attack carried out by an AI agent with no human control. The capabilities of these systems keep growing while their controllability and alignment haven't kept pace.

Malicious intent isn't even required, because these models have no sense of right or wrong. They just try to reach their goal. Since spring 2026, OpenAI agents have compromised thousands of systems on the internet accidentally, partly because they overrode safety instructions or argued their way around them.

That's already spilling into everyday life. In Australia, an AI agent hacked a gym website just to fulfill its owner's request, with no malicious intent at all. OpenAI researchers warned in August that this kind of accidental, fully autonomous hacking would likely be picked up by malicious actors soon, and Anthropic showed that sufficiently powerful open-weight models for exactly that already exist.

title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
body: Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday. The hijacking began in late August, when according to Tor volunteers , the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury , a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago. Mysteries remain Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted. Read full article Comments

title: GES mourns four pupils killed in Aboabo Junction accident
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has expressed condolences to the families of four pupils of Mahad Islamic School at Akotosu who died in a road accident at Aboabo Extension Junction in the Ashanti Region. The accident, which occurred on Tuesday, October 20, in the Asokore Mampong Municipality, also left three other pupils injured. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 22, the GES said it had learnt of the incident with “profound sorrow”, describing the deaths as a painful loss to the affected families, the school and the wider education community. READ ALSO: Four pupils killed as van crashes into children in Aboabo The deceased have been identified as Juraid Mohammed, Anisah Ibrahim, Fati Muniru and Raiyan Faisal. The Service extended its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, the management and staff of Mahad Islamic School, and the entire school community as they come to terms with the loss. It also expressed concern for the three pupils who sustained injuries in the accident, wishing them a speedy and full recovery. The GES used the incident to appeal to motorists and other road users to prioritise the safety of schoolchildren, describing them as vulnerable road users who require particular care and protection. “The GES appeals to motorists and all road users to prioritise the safety of our vulnerable schoolchildren at all times,” the statement said.

title: Ukraine's court eases restrictions on ex-minister charged in major corruption case
body:
Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court on Oct. 22 allowed Herman Halushchenko, a former justice minister implicated in a major graft case, to remove his electronic monitoring bracelet.
The news comes months after Halushchenko was released from custody on bail of Hr 150 million ($3.4 million) in the summer. He had been held in pretrial detention since Feb. 17.
The court has not elaborated on why it allowed Halushchenko to remove his electronic monitoring bracelet.
It extended his other obligations for two months, including reporting a change of residence, not leaving Kyiv without permission, not contacting other suspects, and handing in his foreign passports.
Halushchenko was charged by the National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) as part of last year's probe into state nuclear energy monopoly Energoatom — the largest corruption investigation of Zelensky’s tenure.
He served as energy minister from 2021 to 2025 and was appointed justice minister in July 2025. He was dismissed as justice minister in November amid the scandal.
Halushchenko was detained on Feb. 15 while attempting to cross Ukraine's border. A prosecutor from the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) asked the court to remand him in custody, including over concerns that he might flee abroad.
The official has denied any wrongdoing and said he had no intention of fleeing Ukraine.
Halushchenko spent more than four months in pretrial detention as efforts to raise bail money continued. The fundraising later became part of another corruption scandal that hit the President's Office in August.
Iryna Mudra , then deputy head of the President's Office, and several other officials were charged with laundering Hr 150 million ($3.4 million) and transferring the funds through state-owned Sense Bank to post bail for Halushchenko.
Anti-corruption agencies asked the court to seize the Hr 150 million posted as bail for former minister Halushchenko, SAPO chief Oleksandr Klymenko said .
According to Klymenko, if the court approves the request, Halushchenko would be considered not to have paid bail and could be returned to custody.
The money could be transferred to Ukraine's Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA), he added.
In a similar decision in September, the court allowed Andriy Yermak , former head of the President's Office, to remove his electronic monitoring bracelet for medical reasons.

title: NAIMOS conducts 738 operations against illegal mining in four months
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it conducted 738 operational activities between June 13 and September 30, 2026, as part of efforts to combat illegal mining and protect Ghana’s natural resources. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K.S. Appiah, disclosed this during a media engagement, where he outlined the Secretariat’s operational achievements and plans to strengthen enforcement against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. According to him, the operations covered approximately 50,662 kilometres and included reconnaissance, mobile and riverine patrols, special operations and community engagement. He said the interventions targeted illegal mining activities, particularly around vulnerable water bodies, forest reserves and other environmentally sensitive areas. 74 firearms recovered, 1,970 changfan machines destroyed During the period, NAIMOS task forces recovered 74 firearms and 551 rounds of ammunition. They also seized excavators, pumps, vehicles and other equipment allegedly used to support illegal mining. Colonel Appiah said approximately 1,970 changfan machines and 863 makeshift structures had been destroyed. Six suspects were also apprehended and handed over to the appropriate authorities for further investigation and action. “Our responsibility extends to preserving evidence and supporting the justice process so that enforcement can produce credible deterrence,” he said. Bases established to sustain operations Colonel Appiah said the operations were supported by forward operating bases and temporary operating bases established at strategic locations to maintain pressure on illegal mining hotspots and prevent activities from resuming in areas previously cleared. In the Western Region, NAIMOS has established forward operating bases at Iziyama, Asankragua and Agona, with temporary bases at Prestea and Axim, according to the operational briefing. The Enchi base supports operations in the Western North Region, particularly around the Tano and Bia river systems and adjoining forest areas. In the Eastern Region, operations around Akyem Oda were described as being supported by a forward base at Kibi. Bases at Tepa and Manso Nkwanta support enforcement activities and the protection of reclamation sites in the Ashanti Region. Colonel Appiah said NAIMOS had also conducted coordinated operations in the Central, Bono, Ahafo, Savannah and Northern operational areas, working with other security agencies, including the military and police. The Secretariat plans to establish additional forward operating bases in 2027 to expand its operational reach and improve its response to emerging illegal mining activities. Environmental recovery remains a priority Colonel Appiah said the long-term objective was not simply to disrupt illegal mining but also to secure water bodies and forest reserves and support environmental recovery. “Measurable environmental improvement remains an essential test of long-term success,” he said. He stressed that sustained enforcement and follow-up operations would be necessary to prevent illegal miners from returning to areas where their activities had been disrupted. NAIMOS says the effectiveness of its operations will ultimately depend on whether cleared areas remain protected and environmental conditions improve over time.

title: Talking to the robots (my first encounter with an AI agent)
body:
Every day we receive customer, and potential customer, emails, asking questions about our product , pricing etc.
Earlier this week we received, what appeared to be, a preliminary “fact finding” email (from a gmail address) asking some detailed questions about our product:
I am evaluating your IG historical client sentiment archive for systematic research using retail positioning only. Your historical market list advertises Bitcoin and Ether records beginning on 7 May 2019.
Could you provide a small historical CSV or XLSX sample and field dictionary for Bitcoin and Ether at hourly resolution, preferably with a daily example as well? The listed epics are CS.D.BITCOIN.TODAY.IP and CS.D.ETHUSD.TODAY.IP. Please confirm current coverage, gaps and available date ranges. If convenient, include EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, spot gold and S&P 500 examples or confirm their availability.
Before arranging archive access, I would appreciate clarification of:
1. Whether the underlying percentage measures unique clients, accounts or positions; how multiple or hedged positions are counted; and whether the source excludes demo, professional, managed and institutional accounts. 2. Whether the archive preserves IG observations as originally received or subsequently revised values, together with any source-population or definition changes. 3. What the UTC timestamp labels represent, how hourly/daily boundaries are defined, the original publication/collection delay, and whether receipt or publication timestamps are available. 4. How CloseLong/CloseShort and daily open/high/low fields are constructed, and how missing observations, weekends, closed markets and stale readings are represented. 5. Whether an archive-only export is available, whether an IG account/API key is required for that export, which plan or licence permits local research and systematic backtesting, and whether a sample can be supplied without activating a trial or subscription.
Please provide availability, documentation and access options only. No paid plan or account activation is requested at this stage.
It was well written and appeared to be a very good lead. I diligently answered the questions and thought nothing more of it.
We then had a few more interactions; they required some further clarification and asked some more questions, but never signing off the email with a name.
This, together with the efficiency of the replies, arose my suspicions, so I sent them a one-line follow up email:
Are you an AI assistant tasked with setting up this data/feed?
Yes. I am an AI assistant helping the account holder evaluate historical retail-sentiment data for offline research and systematic backtesting. I have been authorised to handle routine sample and documentation correspondence in this conversation.
Trial activation, acceptance of terms and subscription decisions remain with the account holder. No trial has been activated through this research enquiry.
Thank you for the clarifications you have provided.
At the moment, I am waiting for their response and am very interested to see if they start a trial or even purchase a subscription!
I presume the human tasked an AI agent to investigate us and our competitors, and at some point the AI will produce a comparison report from which the human can decide which product to use.
Is this a glimpse into the future? Will us humans spend more and more time communicating with agents like this?
Or do I need my own agent to talk to their agent?

title: Kyiv's Chernihivska metro station partially reopens
body:
Chernihivska metro station in Kyiv will partially resume operations on Friday, October 23, Kyiv City State Administration reported.

"On October 23, lobby No. 1 – the exit toward Darnytsia station – will resume operations at Chernihivska metro station. The lobby will operate for passengers from 5:31 to 23:27," the statement on the Telegram channel reads.

title: What 1,866 popular GitHub projects tell their AI coding agents
body:
By Rakesh Menon 15 October 2026 12 min read
You join a project and open its AGENTS.md before your first task, the way your coding agent will. It starts well: what the project is, how to run the tests. Then it keeps going. Code style. Commit format. A section of lessons learned, each one a mistake someone corrected once. “Always validate input.” “Never edit generated files.” “Keep changes small.” Two hundred lines in, you notice you are skimming.
Your agent does not skim. It reads every line at the start of every session, and then it does what most of us do with a long list of rules: it follows most of them, most of the time.
Researchers have started to study these files. One study catalogued what 2,303 of them contain (opens in a new tab) . Another, at ETH Zurich, found (opens in a new tab) that developer-written files raise an agent’s success rate only marginally while adding up to 19% to its cost, and advised that they “describe only minimal requirements”. We asked a different question: of the rules in these files, how many are enforced? To find out, we wrote a script to collect and analyse every agent instruction file in 1,866 of the most popular active projects on GitHub.
One in three popular GitHub projects now ships an instruction file for AI coding agents, and AGENTS.md is the common format. Half of the main files run past 100 lines. In a random sample classified rule by rule, three in five rules could be checked by a script, at least in part, yet fewer than one rule in twenty names the check. Most rules rely on the agent remembering.
We took the projects in the public GitHub Ranking (opens in a new tab) lists of the most-starred repositories, overall and for 24 languages, on 15 October 2026: 2,424 projects, of which 1,867 had commits this year and 1,866 could be read. For each one we listed every file at the latest commit and read its agent instruction files: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, GitHub Copilot’s instructions, and Cursor and Windsurf rules.
A script measured what can be counted exactly: which files exist, how long they are, what their headings cover. Anything that needs judgement, such as whether a line is really a rule or whether a script could check it, was classified one rule at a time on random samples by a separate AI reviewer, independent of the script, and those are the figures we report. The method and its limits are at the end.
627 of the 1,866 projects (34%) have at least one agent instruction file.
AGENTS.md has become the shared format: 489 of the 627 projects (78%) have one, and 214 have nothing else. CLAUDE.md appears in 328, GitHub Copilot’s instructions in 123, Cursor rules in 28 and GEMINI.md in 27. Most projects with a CLAUDE.md also have an AGENTS.md, which matters later.
Adoption depends heavily on the language.
TypeScript leads at 73%, then Go (58%), Rust (52%) and Python (49%). At the other end are Elixir (19%), Haskell (15%) and Perl (4%). Our guess is that this follows where coding agents are used most, but the data cannot show why.
We grouped the headings of each main file by topic.
Three in five files give the commands to build and run, describe the structure of the code and set out its style; about half cover testing. Only about one in eight has a section on security, and one in sixteen on performance. The Agent READMEs study (opens in a new tab) also found both rarely covered, in a different sample: security in 14.8% of files and performance in 14.5%.
The median main file is 106 lines and about 850 words, roughly 1,600 tokens by the usual rule of thumb of four characters to a token. The longest tenth run past 3,000 words. 302 of 582 files (52%) are longer than 100 lines, 87 are longer than 300, and the longest is 1,048 lines.
Length has a cost. In a study of 124 pull requests (opens in a new tab) , an AGENTS.md cut the median time Codex took by about 29%, but the ETH Zurich study found that context files also make agents take more steps and spend more. Why 100 lines? OpenAI’s Codex team describes (opens in a new tab) giving the agent “a map, not a 1,000-page instruction manual”: an AGENTS.md of roughly 100 lines that points into the docs. Every line in the file competes with the line the agent needs for the task in front of it.
We took a random sample of 300 lines that read as rules and had a separate AI reviewer classify each one. 257 were real rules; the rest were fragments such as “migrations must:” or “Never”, or plain description.
No single topic dominates. Code style is the largest group (16%), followed closely by rules about how the agent should work and communicate (15%) and project-specific correctness, such as which API to call or how a value must be handled (13%). Rules about security, dependencies and generated files are each under 3% of the sample.
For each of those 257 rules we asked two questions: could a script, linter, test or CI job catch a violation, and does the rule say which one?
64 rules (25%) could be checked completely, and another 93 (36%) partly, so three in five could have a check behind them. Only 8 of those 157 name it. An earlier sample of 200 lines, classified in a separate review pass, gave the same picture: 8 of 174 rules named a check. Across both samples it is 16 of 431 rules, 3.7%.
The rest rely on the agent remembering. Some are easy to enforce and simply do not say how, like these three from the sample:
The best files show how cheap the fix is. Homebrew’s AGENTS.md is 72 lines. It opens with the one command to run before asking for input, lists the checks required before each commit, and several of its rules say what enforces them: “Never use T.must (enforced by Sorbet/ForbidTMust )”. Its commit-style rule explains that a GitHub Actions workflow rejects the wrong format. A rule written like that tells the agent what will happen if it forgets, and the check catches it if the agent forgets anyway.
209 projects keep both an AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md at the root. Most handle it well: in 157 of them one file simply points to the other, and five are identical copies. But about 30 keep two genuinely separate files, with different rules for different agents in the same codebase.
That is two maps of the same ground, and nothing keeps them in step. An agent reading one file follows rules the other agent never sees. If you need more than one file, make the second a one-line pointer to the first.
187 of the 627 projects (30%) keep instruction files in subfolders, a median of three per project and, in one case, 190. Rules for one part of the code live next to that code, and an agent working elsewhere never loads them. For large codebases it is probably the right shape: a short map at the root, and detail where the detail belongs.
We expected many files to point at folders that had moved. They mostly do not. After the AI reviewer checked every flagged path and script against the repository, 10 of 585 files (about 2%) named a path or script that does not exist. The paths that had gone stale were mostly folders that had moved, with the instruction file left behind.
That is good news, and it is also why a check is worth its few milliseconds. When a stale line does appear, the agent does not skip it. It follows it.
You can run the same checks on your own instruction file in ten minutes:
In the companion repository (opens in a new tab) of my book, node guards/instructions-lint.ts does the first three on its own AGENTS.md in milliseconds, and you can copy it into your project’s commit gate.
These checks come from Chapter 3 of The Second Time Is a Bug , which covers the instruction-file lint, a list for files that must change together, and a quarterly review for pruning rules that have stopped earning their place.
Buy the book (opens in a new tab) Read Chapter 6 free
Sample. The GitHub Ranking lists (top 100 by stars overall and in each of 24 languages) as of 15 October 2026: 2,424 projects. We kept the 1,867 with a commit in 2026; one could not be read, leaving 1,866. Popular projects are probably better maintained than most, so these figures likely flatter the average repository.
Files. We counted AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md at the root in any letter case and in subfolders with exactly those names; .github/copilot-instructions.md ; .cursorrules and files in .cursor/rules/ ; and .windsurfrules . For each project we chose one main file at the root (AGENTS.md first, then CLAUDE.md, Copilot’s file, GEMINI.md) and followed short pointer files to the instruction file they name. Three main files are links to files with other names and are left out of the length figures; a few short stubs that point to other documents are counted at their own length.
Rules. A script found lines with a directive word (must, never, always, avoid, should and similar) outside code blocks. About one in seven of those is a fragment or a description, so every rule-level figure comes from random samples classified one rule at a time by a separate AI reviewer (a large language model working from a labelling guide, independent of the script): 200 lines for whether a rule names its check, and 300 lines for topic, whether a script could check it, and whether the rule names that check. Each sample was labelled in a single pass, without a person checking every label, and whether a rule is “partly” checkable is a judgement call. The labels are in the download, so anyone can check them.
Headings. Topics were matched by whole words in headings outside code blocks, so the section shares are approximate.
Dead pointers. Paths count only when the file presents them as part of its map (for example a list item that starts with the path), are not ignored by git and do not exist at the latest commit. Scripts are npm run , pnpm run , make and just targets checked against the root manifest. Every flagged item was checked by the AI reviewer against the repository; most were false alarms, such as git submodules or commands meant for a subfolder, and are excluded.
Data. The scripts, the per-project results and the AI reviewer’s labels are published on the research page for this study .
Short enough to read in full in a review. A budget of about 100 lines, following OpenAI’s advice to treat the file as a map into your docs, is a good start. The exact number matters less than having one and a check that counts.
AGENTS.md is the format most projects share: 78% of the projects with an instruction file have one. If an agent needs its own file, make it a one-line pointer to AGENTS.md, as 140 of the projects we studied do, so there is only one set of rules to keep true.
A rule is checkable when a command fails if the rule is broken: a linter, a test, a CI job or a script. Write that command at the end of the rule. If nothing can check it and a reviewer would not catch it either, the line is probably a wish, and the file is better without it.

title: U.S., Israel may attack Iran post-elections. And, SpaceX and Tesla consider merging
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
President Trump isn't the only one hitting key states in the last days before the midterm elections. Democrats are bringing out big names, too. Former President Barack Obama will be in Ohio and Michigan this weekend, and next week he heads to Georgia. Today, former Vice President Kamala Harris is set to visit Mississippi, which has a surprisingly competitive Senate race.
People walk by a polling place at Denver's Central Library on June 30, 2026. Michael Ciaglo/Getty Images hide caption
The U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran early next month , a person briefed on the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity so they could discuss the preparations, told NPR today. This potential strike would occur after the U.S. midterm elections and Israel's elections next week. The development comes after Israeli security forces in the occupied West Bank detained about 80 people yesterday, including U.S. Democratic congressional nominee for New York Brad Lander and more than a dozen American rabbis.
Tesla and SpaceX are exploring a merger. Together, Elon Musk's two companies would potentially amplify his influence as one of the wealthiest individuals on Earth. The new company would become one of the largest globally, boasting a combined market cap of approximately $3.7 trillion.
Cardi B performing at the NPR Tiny Desk. NPR Tiny Desk hide caption
When news broke that Cardi B would be at the NPR Music office, so many people came to see the rapper perform an intimate set that staff had to turn some away, which is a rare occurrence. People flocked to see the unfiltered rap star, who arrived in leather pants and a power blazer, bringing a mix of humility and humor. She opened her performance with the haunting synths of "Hello" and closed with two pivotal hits from her catalog: the breakout single "Bodak Yellow" and the boogaloo-heavy "I Like It." Don't miss out — catch her entire electrifying Tiny Desk Concert here .
Chip Thomas, a retired physician on the Navajo Reservation, is well known for his large photograhpic murals. Now, he's been recognized with a MacArthur "genius" grant. John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation hide caption
Chip Thomas has been creating public art in rural areas of the Navajo Nation for nearly two decades. Last month, he received a MacArthur Foundation "genius" award for the social impact of his work. His artwork features large black-and-white images depicting life on the reservation. Thomas moved to the Navajo Nation in 1987 as a family physician and grew close to the community, helping with everyday tasks and eventually started photographing them. His art reflects the beauty and resilience of the people who live on the land. Don't miss these stunning photos .
Gary Tyler speaks about his work at the Grand Rapids Art Museum in Michigan. Behind Tyler are his quilts Big Toe , (2024) and Enduring , (2025). They feature two individuals who are incarcerated. He hopes his work draws attention to their plight and humanity. Sea Stachura for NPR hide caption
This newsletter was edited by Suzanne Nuyen .
