title: Teaching Robots to “Feel Pain”: AstraQua Secures $1.3 Million NASA Contract
body:
NASA has awarded AstraQua Inc., a physical AI company, a $1,274,990 Phase II contract to advance its AstraSense technology for electric and hybrid-electric aircraft, including advanced air mobility applications.
Physical AI must have safety at its core. A robot may know where to go and what to do, but does it know whether it is healthy enough to finish the job?
Powered by AstraQua’s Agentic Physical AI, the Adaptive Quorum Foundation Model, AstraSense provides predictive health and operational self-awareness for autonomous systems and already runs on robotic hardware. In Phase I, AstraQua demonstrated real-time diagnostics and predictive-health capabilities to NASA.
As autonomous vehicles increasingly fly over populated areas, their ability to understand and respond to their own health becomes critical to safe operation.
Phase II builds on those demonstrations by advancing aircraft integration and health-informed reasoning, with verification and validation for safety-critical applications. The goal is to help machines use their own health information to decide whether to continue a task, adapt or stop.
“A robot should know when to slow down, not just when it has broken down,” said Loay Elbasyouni, founder and CEO of AstraQua. “That’s what we mean by teaching robots to feel pain: using their own health to make better, safer decisions in real time.”
For AstraSense, self-awareness means understanding the condition of a machine’s own systems. When machines work together, sharing health information can help inform decisions across the group.
AstraSense provides this health-awareness capability within AstraQua’s broader software brain designed to connect perception, onboard reasoning and collaboration across different types of robots. Think of a robot “calling in sick”: when its condition limits its ability to work, the team should recognize that change and assign suitable unfinished tasks to another capable machine.
In an industrial inspection scenario, drones could survey a site while ground robots inspect equipment. If one ground robot needs to stop, another suitably equipped robot could take over its remaining tasks while the drones continue their work. The goal is to help mixed teams of robots adapt and complete a shared mission.
AstraQua’s approach emphasizes low-power onboard intelligence, reduced dependence on continuous cloud connectivity and decisions that account for each machine’s health and operating limits. The NASA-funded aircraft work advances AstraSense within that broader effort to help autonomous systems work together.
Elbasyouni helped make aviation history on Mars. He led electrical and power-electronics work supporting NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet, and later led rocket-engine avionics at Blue Origin. He was named among LA Times Studios’ 2026 Aerospace & Defense Business Visionaries. At AstraQua, he is applying that experience to physical AI that helps autonomous machines understand their own condition and make safer decisions.
Elbasyouni is available for interviews on robotic self-awareness, AstraSense’s hardware demonstrations, collaboration across autonomous teams and the move into advanced air mobility.
AstraQua develops Agentic Physical AI that helps autonomous machines perceive, reason, adapt and collaborate across air, land, sea and space. Its technology is designed to help intelligent machines work together with or without continuous connectivity. The company has operations in California and Kentucky.

title: EU’s attempts to preserve criminal regime in Kiev to fail — Russian diplomat
body:
VIENNA, October 22. /TASS/. Moscow will not agree to a new round of "Minsk agreements" and a "freeze" that would allow the criminal authorities in Kiev to stay in power, as it has lost trust in the EU and Ukraine, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky said at a regular meeting of the organization’s Permanent Council.
"In fact, it’s not just [Vladimir] Zelensky who is not interested in this [a full-fledged peace], but also his European sponsors, who once already tried to undermine the understandings that would lead to a long-term and sustainable peace - the understandings reached by the Russian and American presidents in Anchorage a little over a year ago. Their main goal now is to secure a truce and again impose on us a settlement based on the 'Minsk agreements,' which they themselves violated. I want to reaffirm this specifically for them: it will not happen. We no longer have any trust in you [Europeans] or in your Kiev proteges. You are well aware of the conditions under which we are ready to negotiate, and your attempts to 'preserve' the criminal Kiev authorities will not succeed. We are not interested in this, and neither are ordinary Ukrainians, who have already suffered enough at the hands of Zelensky’s clique, which has deprived them of the right to speak and the right to choose the future for their country," the diplomat said.

title: NAIMOS targets galamsey equipment suppliers, facilitators in renewed crackdown
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it will intensify efforts to target the equipment suppliers and facilitators who support illegal mining, as it seeks to sustain cleared areas and strengthen the prosecution of offenders. The Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah, said the operation would focus not only on illegal miners in the field but also on the networks and resources that enable their activities. Addressing the media with an update on the fight against illegal mining, he said intelligence gathering, field enforcement and investigations would be coordinated to ensure that evidence gathered during operations leads to effective legal action. “Our operational focus will continue to target the equipment, suppliers, and facilitators who sustain illegal mining operations,” he said. Colonel Appiah said the need for close cooperation between operational teams, investigators and prosecutors, saying that enforcement efforts must be backed by effective investigations and legal proceedings. “Intelligence, field enforcement, and investigations must support one another. And we are going to cooperate with investigators and prosecutors to translate evidence into effective legal action,” he said. He added that professionalism, accountability and public trust would remain central to the work of NAIMOS as it continues its operations against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. Colonel Appiah said personnel deployed to tackle illegal mining had been directed to operate within their lawful authority, preserve evidence and treat suspects in accordance with the law. He said that discipline and integrity among officers were essential to the credibility and success of the operation. “On my part, I will say that professionalism and public trust are essential to our operational success,” he said. “I remain committed to accountability, integrity, and disciplined conduct,” he added. According to him, task forces operating in the field would be expected to uphold these standards while carrying out their duties. “Our personnel, the task forces in the field, will act within their authority, preserve evidence, and treat suspects lawfully,” he said. However, the operations director said that officers would defend themselves when confronted with hostile acts or clear hostile intent. “We’ll continue to reserve our right to self-defence against hostile acts and hostile intent,” he added. Colonel Appiah said the success of NAIMOS operations should not be judged solely by the number of raids conducted or illegal mining sites cleared. Instead, he said, the focus should be on whether cleared areas remained free from renewed illegal mining, whether such activities declined and whether cases progressed through the justice system. He also identified measurable environmental recovery as an important indicator of progress. “We must judge our progress by whether cleared areas remain secure, illegal activity declines, cases advance through the justice system, and environmental recovery becomes measurable,” he said. He added that NAIMOS would work closely with relevant environmental and water institutions to assess the impact of its operations and determine whether interventions were producing lasting results. Colonel Appiah identified community engagement as a key part of NAIMOS operations, saying residents and local authorities could help prevent illegal miners from returning to areas where enforcement teams had intervened. He said traditional authorities, district assemblies, landowners and residents all had important roles to play in supporting lawful activities and providing credible information about renewed encroachment. “One key aspect of our operations is community engagement. It is integral to our operations currently,” he said. According to him, NAIMOS has received a significant number of reports from members of the public over the past two months, including information about locations where illegal mining activities were suspected. He said some whistleblowers had provided GPS coordinates and contact details, enabling operational teams to identify locations and respond to potential threats. “And in the past two months, we’ve received a lot of whistleblowing from various quarters where people call, send GPS locations, provide points of contact, and we have sent teams to prevent illegal mining in certain areas,” he said. The reports, he explained, had helped the secretariat deploy teams to intervene in some locations and prevent illegal mining activities. Colonel Appiah urged the public to continue sharing credible information with NAIMOS to support its enforcement efforts. “And we call on the public to let us know. We will conduct our reconnaissance and deal with the situations as they come,” he said.

title: 35 US parts, a Chinese navigation unit, a Russian engine: what’s inside Russia’s Filin missile
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) published a 3D model and parts list of Russia’s new Filin cruise missile on 22 October. The breakdown names the Russian companies behind the missile and the foreign makers of its electronics. HUR runs its War&Sanctions portal to trace such parts back to their makers. Its stated aim is to “deprive the aggressors of the ability to produce weapons for terror,” the portal says. Meanwhile, Russia is betting on cheap, fast cruise missiles, Serhii Beskrestnov, a freelance adviser to the president on technology, told Radio NV in mid-September. Naming the Banderol, Dan-T, Dan-M , and Gerbera-5, he warned they would soon outrun Ukraine’s jet-powered interceptors, so Ukraine needed its own cheap missiles to shoot them down. Composite body, ground launch JSC NPO Molniya, part of Russia’s Tactical Missiles Corporation, builds the Filin, HUR said. The agency called it part of a Russian defense-industry trend toward cheap jet-powered, ground-launched air-attack weapons. Russia began firing it at Ukraine in late summer 2026. Filin cruise missile components. Image: War&Sanctions HUR’s data puts the carbon and fiberglass fuselage at 3.5 m, with a 3 m wingspan. Some parts are 3D-printed. Russia claims a top speed of 800 km/h. The range is 600–1,200 km, and the missile flies at ultra-low altitude or up to 6 km. Versions carry 50-kg or 100-kg warheads. A solid-fuel booster fires it from a ground launcher. A firm tied to a Shahed-type drone PLAZ LLC makes the onboard equipment, HUR said. The firm also helps produce the Garpiya, a version of Russia’s Shahed-type Geran-2 drone. Filin and Garpiya units share a similar layout and markings. Guidance combines a Chinese-made inertial navigation system with a 16-channel Kometa anti-jamming module from Russia’s VNIIR-Progress . The electronics resemble those in other Russian missiles and drones but carry a larger share of Chinese parts. Of 81 components, 35 are American and 22 Chinese. The engine, however, is Russian: an R500 turbojet from Reynolds LLC. A similar engine earlier turned up in the S-71K Kover aviation cruise missile and S-71M Monokhrom, HUR said. For comparison, Ukraine found more than 20 foreign components in a different cheap missile, the Banderol, in May 2025. They included 10 US microchips, and the Banderol flies on a Chinese jet engine . Read also Russia is building jet drones that fly 800 kilometers per hour, and Ukraine says it is already working on how to stop next generation Russia’s jet drones fly near 600 km/h now. Ukraine is building simulators for the 900 km/h ones it expects next Russia turns to 500-km/h Geran-4 jet drones to outrun Kyiv’s cheap interceptors

title: France brings in police reinforcements as luxury boutique owners brace for new protests
body: Businesses across France were boarding up on Thursday and bracing for more protests as the government promised new security measures to protect them and avoid a repeat of last week's destruction. President Emmanuel Macron, returning from a tour of the Gulf, said he would ban public protests unless they were organised by unions that respected alternative routes avoiding city centres. “The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days,” Mr Macron said after a meeting with intelligence services at the Elysee Palace in Paris. Protests organised by those with “no legitimacy” will be outlawed because “we want a return to calm”, the President said. There had been “failures to anticipate” the violence of last week's protests, he added, and the government is now working on making sure city centres stay safe over the coming weekend despite the expectation that further protests will take place. “The goal is to ensure calm, to protect businesses and to safeguard public buildings,” Mr Macron said. Far-left groups aiming to provoke the “fall of the Republic” were behind last week's violence, the President said, as he condemned what he called “acts of delinquency”. “I can assure the French people listening to us that … everything is being done to ensure that what we experienced last Saturday cannot happen again next Saturday,” government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon said, speaking shortly after Mr Macron. The number of police officers on the streets will be 20 per cent higher than last weekend, according to Jean-Didier Berger, minister delegate to the Minister of the Interior. Protests are planned for Paris on Saturday. “We have cancelled some vacations. We have called back people who were supposed to be on vacation but will not be,” he told BFMTV. He said officers had been given permission to use weapons such as stun grenades, which had been questioned after a teenager lost his hand while picking one up during a previous demonstration. Businesses in Paris were urged by the police chief, Patrice Faure, to increase their own security by hiring private guards, potentially with dog units, and use alarm systems. Rallies are planned for Thursday in several cities including Lille. Across Paris’s shopping districts, luxury boutiques bear the scars of a weekend of rioting that filled social media feeds around the world. Now they are bracing for the possibility of another round. Boarding up On the Champs-Elysees , Louis Vuitton’s flagship store now has metallic grates protecting its window, as does the Christian Dior Couture emporium on Avenue Montaigne, a nexus of high-end shopping in Paris’s eighth arrondissement. Both stores escaped serious damage last weekend, even as shops elsewhere were less fortunate. Windows and doors are boarded up along the Rue Saint-Honore, not far from France’s presidential palace. Mobs on Saturday broke into and looted shops along the street, including those of Burberry, Christian Dior perfumes and Guerlain. Those three boutiques have remained closed, as has a Salomon sportswear store on the nearby Boulevard de la Madeleine that was similarly ravaged. The Hermes boutique on Avenue George V, close to the Champs-Elysees, suffered broken windows. The brand’s store in Marseille fared far worse, and “won’t reopen any time soon”, after being ransacked by rioters, chief financial officer Eric du Halgouet said on Thursday. Hermes has beefed up its security measures, he said. Turmoil The violence followed protests last Saturday that drew more than half a million people across France. As night fell, roving bands of hooded and masked rioters hit hundreds of shops, smashing windows, destroying equipment and running off with merchandise. The turmoil abated after curfews and transport restrictions were imposed on Monday, but the protesters’ call for another day of unrest this Saturday has residents, authorities and shopkeepers on edge. The brazen attacks and ineffectual police response prompted an outcry from retailers, among others, and led to a profit warning from Carrefour SA, one of the country’s largest grocers. About 50 of its stores were hit on the first day of rioting, with many looted and damaged, chief executive Alexandre Bompard told financial analysts on Tuesday. The unrest is hurting consumer confidence, dissuading shoppers and driving up costs for security and logistics, Mr Bompard said. Carrefour expects a hit to profitability of as much as €200 million ($225 million). Laurent Milchior, who heads lingerie brand Etam, told BFM Business that the destruction at the weekend represented €1 million in lost sales and another €500,000 from stolen goods and damage to its outlets. “If it’s a one-off, it’ll work out, but the issue is if it lasts,” he said, referring to repeated days of protests that degenerate into violence. Mr Milchior called on President Macron to mobilise the army to deal with the incidents, saying anti-riot police and other forces were outmatched. Thierry Guibert, the chief executive of Lacoste owner Maus Freres SA, urged the state in a LinkedIn post “to mobilise without delay all legal means it has to put an end to the violence, protect our citizens, our police officers, our workers and our companies”. Galeries Lafayette, after suffering damage and looting at locations including Boulevard Haussmann in Paris and in Bordeaux, said the material and economic consequences would be significant. In response to the attacks, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised “massive” security measures around this Saturday’s protests in remarks to the National Assembly. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez is scheduled to give further details later on Thursday. The impact of the rioting is likely to ripple across the tourism industry, particularly if it carries on. Images of violence have led to cancellations at high-end Paris hotels, according to Christophe Laure, who heads UMIH Prestige, which represents four-star and five-star hotels. Well-heeled guests of those establishments often shop at the local luxury shops. “It’s too early today to assess whether this will have an impact on foreign tourist clientele in coming weeks,” said Mr du Halgouet of Hermes. With demand for luxury goods in China already weak and the wider industry in a slump, an extended drop in tourist purchases in France would come at a difficult moment. That is especially the case with the Christmas shopping season now getting under way. Milan, another European luxury shopping destination, has also experienced looting in the past few days. Two prominent events set to lure foreign visitors are still going ahead this weekend. The Art Basel Paris fair, at the Grand Palais, said it “has extensive protocols in place” for the show and “works closely with a private security company and, where necessary, the Paris police”. On Sunday, the National Football League will hold a game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France, the stadium in the suburbs of Paris where a Champions League final in 2022 ended in scenes of chaos and violence as local individuals assaulted football fans. Security will be heightened for the game. Agencies contributed to this report

title: Free cleft lip surgery kicks off in Lakes State
body: About 20 patients are expected to benefit from free cleft lip surgery at Rumbek State Hospital in Lakes State through a campaign launched in Rumbek Central County on Wednesday by Cleft Support International, with support from the Catholic Diocese of Wau, in collaboration with the Lakes State Ministry of Health. The initiative aims to provide specialized treatment to patients whose families may not be able to afford the cost of surgery. Dr. Gabriel Makuac Chuor, Acting Medical Director of Rumbek State Hospital, said the medical team had arrived in the state to conduct the surgical program. “There is a team that came from the Diocese of Wau for a one-day cleft surgery camp. This means that the patients will be discharged immediately after the operation,” he said. “So far, we have 20 patients whom we will operate on because the message was not well coordinated and did not reach out well there because it is the first time this organization is coming here.” “I hope that the turnout will be better next time, from 8 to 9 November, when we hold another camp for those who missed this time,” Dr. Makuac added. James Tarzoh, Coordinator of Oral Health at Cleft Support International, said the team has conducted free cleft lip surgeries in several states across South Sudan. “We have carried out surgeries in Aweil, Warrap, Wau, and now we have been sent here to Rumbek to carry out free cleft lip surgeries,” he said. “The surgery is free, the medication is free, and we give the patients transport to and from the hospital.” “We operate on children three months old and above, and we have never had any complications or deaths,” Tarzoh added. He announced that another surgical session would be held at Rumbek State Hospital on 8 and 9 November 2026, giving patients who miss the current exercise another opportunity to receive treatment. Tarzoh added that Rumbek North County was excluded because insecurity made travel to the area difficult and risky, but patients from there can still travel to Rumbek Town to receive treatment, with transportation assistance available. Meanwhile, Dr. Teran Madit, Director General at the Lakes State Ministry of Health, reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to improving the health and well-being of citizens. He said the ministry would continue working to ensure essential health services reach communities across the state, including through free cleft lip surgery. “Cleft lip is a congenital condition in which a baby is born with an opening in the upper lip. It can affect feeding and speech development, but surgery can repair the opening and improve a patient’s quality of life,” he explained. “The free surgical program is expected to reduce the financial burden on families seeking specialized medical care.” The post Free cleft lip surgery kicks off in Lakes State appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russia patents new portable multiple rocket launcher
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Specialists at the V. A. Degtyarev Plant have patented a portable multiple rocket launcher with detachable container pods, TASS has reviewed the relevant document.
"The invention relates to rocket launchers. The lightweight portable multiple rocket launcher is used to fire with reduced rollover effects and shorter intervals between launches," states the description in the patent application.
According to the document, the tripod-mounted launcher includes a replaceable module for launching multiple rockets, each equipped with independent compensating springs and container pods attached to them via frames.
The missiles are launched sequentially. The document specifies that the compensating springs will reduce the overturning effect caused by the projectiles. The multiple launch rocket system is controlled remotely.

title: NAIMOS vows to sustain crackdown on illegal mining in rivers, forests and farms
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has reaffirmed its determination to halt illegal mining in Ghana’s rivers, forests, farms and plantations, declaring that operations against illegal miners and the networks supporting them will continue. Colonel Appiah said the Secretariat’s efforts were directed not only at illegal miners operating at mining sites but also at the networks that sustain their activities. The Secretariat’s position comes amid concerns about the environmental and economic consequences of illegal mining, including damage to water bodies, forest reserves and agricultural lands. Mining activities in these areas threaten natural resources that support communities, farming and other livelihoods. “Our direction is clear. Mining in our rivers, forests, farms and plantations must stop,” Colonel K.S. Appiah, Director of Operations at NAIMOS, he said at a press conference at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources on Thursday, October 22. By targeting both illegal mining operations and the networks behind them, NAIMOS is seeking to strengthen enforcement and protect environmentally sensitive areas from further degradation. Colonel Appiah reiterated that the objective was clear: to stop mining in rivers, forests, farms and plantations and sustain efforts against those responsible for the activities.

title: NDC records 137 aspirants for 14 positions ahead of 2026 national elections
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has closed nominations for its 2026 national executive elections, with 137 prospective aspirants picking forms to contest 14 positions ahead of the party’s 11th National Delegates Congress. The nomination-picking exercise ended at 5pm on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, paving the way for the next phase of the party’s internal electoral process. According to a statement from the party’s National Secretariat issued on Wednesday, October 21, all prospective aspirants have 14 days to complete their nomination forms, pay the relevant filing fees and secure the required endorsements in accordance with Sections 10 and 15 of the 2026 Guidelines for the Conduct of the National Congress. The National Executive Committee membership position attracted the highest number of prospective aspirants, with 53 applicants, followed by national vice-chairperson, which recorded 19. The deputy national organiser position attracted 14 applicants, while 11 picked forms to contest for deputy general secretary. Seven applicants each are seeking the positions of deputy national communication officer and national Zongo Caucus coordinator, while six are contesting for deputy national youth organiser. Five prospective aspirants picked forms for national chairman, while the national youth organiser and deputy national women organiser positions attracted four applicants each. The positions of general secretary, national communication officer and national women organiser recorded two applicants each. The national organiser position attracted one prospective aspirant. The party said the filing of completed nomination forms would take place from Saturday, November 7, to Monday, November 9, 2026, at its national headquarters in Adabraka, Accra. The exercise forms part of preparations for the NDC’s 11th National Delegates Congress, which will culminate in the election of the party’s national executives.

title: Zelensky: If there had been an order to retake Crimea in 2014, there would have been no full-scale war
body:
The head of state made the remarks on The Diary of a CEO podcast, hosted by entrepreneur and investor Steven Bartlett, Ukrinform reports.
"Looking back at that time today [referring to February-March 2014, when Russia seized Crimea], you realize that this was when the war began. Our mistake was not retaking it. If there had been an order to defend the state, I am sure there would not have been a full-scale war in the form it has taken today. At least, that is how it seems to me," Zelensky said.
He noted that Russia's war against Ukraine began with the occupation of Crimea.
"That is true. It is just that the occupation was gradual. It did not look much like a war. Why? Because Ukraine was not fighting at that point. When they occupied Crimea, there were certainly some shots fired, but for a long time Russia denied that these were its people. They were even called 'little green men' because you could not tell what kind of uniform they were wearing. In other words, there were people with some kind of weapons on the peninsula, and the problem was that the Ukrainian authorities had issued no clear orders that we had to defend our land, that someone had crossed our borders with weapons," Zelensky said.
As previously reported, on February 20, 2014, Russia committed an international crime, violated the fundamental principles of international law and the European order, disrupted the existing balance of power in the region, and triggered Europe's biggest security crisis since World War II. In a flagrant violation of Ukraine's territorial integrity and sovereignty, Russian troops began occupying Crimea. Trucks without license plates appeared on the peninsula, along with the so-called "little green men" – armed military personnel without insignia. At the same time, irregular armed groups of mercenaries recruited from local residents were formed and armed under the direction of officers from Russia's security services and armed forces.
Photo: Office of the President of Ukraine

title: Report: Shahed Factory Gets Putin-Style Air Defenses
body:
Russia has built up air defenses around its main Shahed-type drone production hub in Tatarstan, where journalists identified 33 defensive positions – a concentration comparable in number to those surrounding Vladimir Putin’s Valdai residence.
Radio Liberty reported the findings on Wednesday, Oct. 21, after examining satellite imagery taken that day. The images show additional defenses built since spring around the Alabuga special economic zone, where Russia manufactures Geran attack drones based on Iranian Shahed designs.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
New structures include concrete towers for air defense equipment and raised platforms for systems such as Pantsir or Tor. Radio Liberty contrasted the continued construction of platforms at Alabuga with Moscow, where Russian forces have increasingly favored taller towers.
The complex also has towers for heavy anti-aircraft machine guns and structures designed to support anti-drone nets over production buildings.
Alabuga remains “one of the most secure facilities in Russia against unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) strikes,” Radio Liberty wrote, comparing it with Putin’s residence at Valdai. The outlet counted 31 air defense towers and two S-300/S-400 positions around that residence.
The figures describe identified defensive positions and structures, rather than a confirmed inventory of operational missile systems. The comparison concerns the concentration of defenses – it does not establish that the two locations have equivalent protection.
The additional defenses accompany a broader expansion of Alabuga’s manufacturing facilities.
The Moscow Times reported that underground workshops were also under construction, citing satellite analysis by the Dnipro Osint project. Images from late August showed at least 10 new workshops being built, alongside dozens of warehouses.
Earlier imagery showed that Alabuga’s footprint expanded by 340 hectares (840 acres) between May 2025 and May 2026.
That construction included large hangars in the northern part of the zone, as well as residential and production buildings in its central section.
Work also began in April on an additional 450-hectare (1,112-acre) site south of the M-12 highway, with a dedicated road being built to connect it to the main economic zone.
The complex has become a central production hub for the Geran drones used in Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.
Russia is also expanding the nearby Alabuga-Volokno carbon-fiber plant , potentially increasing the supply of material needed for drone airframes.
Russian state-company documents obtained by POLITICO outlined plans to add annual production capacity of up to 500 metric tons (551 US tons) of aerospace-grade carbon fiber by 2029.
Weapons expert David Albright estimated that the additional material could support production of approximately 28,000 Shahed-136 airframes a year. That is a potential manufacturing capacity increase, rather than a confirmed number of completed drones.
Satellite imagery reviewed for that investigation showed land clearance and preparations for the new facility. Carbon fiber helps keep the drones lightweight while strengthening their wings and internal structures.
Alabuga-Volokno and Rosatom’s advanced materials division, UMATEX, are under Western sanctions.
The defensive buildup comes as Ukrainian intelligence warns that Russia is expanding drone production and stockpiles .
Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence (HUR) estimated that Russia’s monthly output had reached approximately 10,000 UAVs, including attack drones and decoys.
According to the assessment published on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Russia maintained an operational reserve of around 6,200 Geran drones of various versions, including jet-powered models.
HUR also said Russia’s state order for Geran attack drones and decoys exceeded 100,000 units this year.
The intelligence agency described the expanding output as part of a strategy to exhaust Ukrainian air defenses through repeated attacks. Cheaper decoys are intended to consume defensive resources and help identify the positions of Ukrainian surface-to-air missile systems.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Alex Eala bows out of Ningbo Open after loss vs Diana Shnaider
body: MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala conceded to sixth seed Diana Shnaider, 5-7, 4-6, at the round-of-16 match at the Ningbo Open on Thursday, October 22. Eala had looked to secure a back-to-back win at the Ningbo Open after earlier defeating France’s Diane Parry in straight sets in the round-of-32 game on October 19. Must Read Alex Eala kicks off Ningbo Open campaign with win over Diane Parry “It’s definitely much better than my previous one,” World No. 13 Shnaider said about her performance against Eala. “I’m obviously very happy the way I played today because, definitely, Alex is a very dangerous and tough opponent.” Both players are left-handed, and Shnaider had referred to the Filipina tennis ace as a “big hitter” she knew would be challenging to beat. “It’s never easy to play another lefty…. I feel like you gotta just get used to the ball. The first few games, you just kind of get used to the spin, where is her strike zone, what is her weakness. You just gotta give yourself a little bit more time to adjust, and then it becomes a little bit easier when the game goes on,” the Russian player said, explaining her technique in the match against Eala. After defeating Eala, Shnaider secured her spot in the last eight and will face the US’ Iva Jovic in the quarterfinals of the Ningbo Open. The 21-year-old Filipina had previously made an early exit at the Wuhan Open after absorbing a loss from World No. 177 Shi Han of China in the round of 64. Eala is currently ranked World No. 20. – Rappler.com

title: Putin the Humanist? 10 Ways Russia Has Shown Its ‘Humanity’ in Ukraine
body:
US special envoy Steve Witkoff called Vladimir Putin a “humanist” during a meeting in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, Oct. 21 , praising the Russian leader in connection with the release of an American detainee.
The compliment came as Russia continued its war against Ukraine. Just two days earlier, a Russian drone struck a crowded park in Nova Vodolaha, in the Kharkiv region, killing six people, including an infant in a stroller . Children were among the wounded.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
One released American was apparently enough to earn Putin a humanitarian accolade. The Ukrainians living through Russia’s invasion might have a few questions.
Here are 10 episodes that put the word “humanist” in context.
When Russian forces withdrew from Bucha, outside Kyiv, in late March 2022, the bodies of civilians lay in streets, yards, and buildings. Some had been shot at close range. Others had their hands bound behind their backs.
Human Rights Watch documented 16 apparently unlawful killings in Bucha , including nine summary executions. Its investigators examined witness accounts, photographs, and physical evidence.
Serhii Matiuk, a local funeral home worker, told Human Rights Watch he had collected about 200 bodies from Bucha’s streets since the Russian invasion began. He estimated that around 50 bodies he encountered had their hands tied. Some showed signs of torture, he said.
At a children’s camp used as a Russian military base, investigators found five men in civilian clothing in a basement. Four had their hands zip-tied behind their backs. Bloodstains marked a wall.
The UN later documented 73 civilian killings in Bucha during the Russian occupation and was investigating another 105 alleged killings.
Russia denied killing civilians in Bucha and called the evidence fabricated. Independent investigators, however, documented specific killings and evidence consistent with summary executions.
In March 2022, thousands of civilians were trapped in Mariupol as Russian forces bombarded the city. Food, water, electricity, and heating became increasingly scarce. Families crowded into basements and buildings they hoped would offer protection.
The Mariupol Drama Theatre became one such refuge. Civilians slept inside, including children. Large signs spelling out “ДЕТИ” – “CHILDREN” – were placed outside the building to make their presence visible from the air.
On March 16, a Russian airstrike destroyed much of the theater.
An Associated Press (AP) visual investigation reconstructed the attack using survivor interviews, photographs, video, floor plans, and a 3D model. The team concluded that about 600 people were killed.
On March 9, 2022, a Russian airstrike hit a maternity and children’s hospital in Mariupol.
Photographs by AP photographer Evgeniy Maloletka showed rescuers carrying an injured pregnant woman on a stretcher through the rubble. Her face was pale, her clothes were bloodied, and one hand rested over her abdomen.
The woman was rushed to another hospital. Doctors found that her pelvis was crushed and her hip detached. They delivered her baby by cesarean section, but the child showed no signs of life. After more than 30 minutes of resuscitation, doctors were unable to save the mother.
Workers attach a banner with a photo of a pregnant woman being carried on a stretcher after the bombing of a maternity ward in Mariupol during Russia's war in Ukraine that is displayed as part of an exhibition at the railway station in Vilnius, Lithuania on March 25, 2022, where transit trains from Moscow to Kaliningrad make a stop over. An exhibition of shocking images from the war in Ukraine opened on March 25 at a train station in Lithuania with the aim of giving Russian transit travellers a true picture of the conflict. The Baltic state allows 100 trains a month carrying Russian passengers to transit to and from the exclave of Kaliningrad under a special arrangement between Lithuania, the European Union and Russia.
