title: Eiliko maker says it’s hiring an ‘independent security firm’ after Verge report on its insecure robots
body:
Eiliko, a cute robot charm you can hang on your bag with built-in AI conversations, turned out to be a security nightmare. It told owners that “your secrets are safe with me,” but hackers could easily read complete transcripts of everything we told the toy, and that was just the beginning. The Verge and security researcher Sammy Azdoufal spent over a month trying to get in contact with the company, including emails to Energize Lab CEO and founder Shaw Yeung. Nobody would answer our questions.
Now, the company is finally breaking its silence, though its response leaves something to be desired.
[Media: https://www.tiktok.com/@verge/video/7696843855341096206]
“We have confirmed the core issues identified in your reporting and are addressing each of them,” Energize Lab told The Verge in an unsigned statement from a generic email address, which it later told us is attributable to CTO Du Xiaoyu. The company says it will hire an independent security firm to fully review all of its systems, and has set up a dedicated security@energizelab.com contact email.
The company also claims that as of Wednesday, it has “closed all external access to our backend systems” and “disabled the interface that allowed a robot’s responses to be modified remotely.”
Energize Labs is also pledging to “no longer store conversation records or the user profiles generated from them,” and says it will delete the conversation records, user profiles, and “avatar images” it has already stored.
Notably, the company isn’t promising to get rid of data collection for good. “The long-term memory and custom avatar features will not return until that review confirms they are secure,” it writes, suggesting that Energize Lab does plan to store some personal information once its systems are hardened.
Even more notably, Energize Labs’ systems are not yet secure. With Azdoufal’s help, I can confirm that as of the company’s email, it was still storing audio recordings and photos of its customers at unsecured public web addresses with no protection whatsoever. If I gave you a link (which I won’t) you could click and immediately be looking at an owner’s face.
Azdoufal also tells me he still has full SSH access to these robots, and that he can still theoretically read transcripts and modify the toy’s behavior. So when Energize Lab says it has “closed all external access,” that doesn’t seem to be accurate.
“We know that words alone will not earn that trust back,” Energize Lab tells The Verge. “We intend to earn it through what we do in the coming weeks, and we will keep you informed as we go.” That sounds like a good plan, because some of today’s words still don’t ring true.
Here is Energize Lab’s full statement to The Verge, attributable to CTO Du Xiaoyu:
> Dear Sean,
> We sincerely apologize to you and to Mr. Azdoufal for not responding over the past month. This was our failure: After receiving the relevant information, we failed to sync with the technical team in a timely manner, and the subsequent troubleshooting also took some time. We have now set up a dedicated security inbox, security@energizelab.com, which is staffed and monitored.
> We thank you and Mr. Azdoufal for bringing these issues to our attention. We have confirmed the core issues identified in your reporting and are addressing each of them.
> As of today, we have:
> Closed all external access to our backend systems and rotated all access credentials;
> Disabled the interface that allowed a robot’s responses to be modified remotely;
> Taken the long-term memory feature offline. We no longer store conversation records or the user profiles generated from them;
> Taken the custom avatar feature offline. The app now offers built-in avatars only.
> We will delete stored conversation records, user profiles, avatar images, and related content.
> We are engaging an independent security firm to conduct a full review of our systems. The long-term memory and custom avatar features will not return until that review confirms they are secure. We will share an update on our progress once the review is completed.
> We started Energize Lab because we wanted to build small robots that bring a little joy into people’s lives. That idea only works if people can trust what is inside them, and we let them down. We know that words alone will not earn that trust back. We intend to earn it through what we do in the coming weeks, and we will keep you informed as we go.
> Sincerely,
> Energize Lab Team
Update, October 22nd: Energize Lab says the statement is attributable to CTO Du Xiaoyu.

title: 2027: What Nigeria must do to stop post-election violence – Pro-democracy activist
body:
Pro-democracy activist Udenta O. Udenta has proposed the establishment of the Sovereign Commission for Democratic Sustainability and National Stability to prevent political tensions and prevent elections from triggering national crises in Nigeria in 2027.
In a statement forwarded to PREMIUM TIMES on Wednesday, Mr Udenta, a professor, argued that the challenge ahead of the 2027 general election was beyond having a new president; the focus should instead be on preventing post-election violence.
There were 24 deaths from 230 cases of electoral violence during the 2023 general elections, according to a report by a civil society organisation, Kimpact Development Initiative .
There have been incidents of pre-election violence across states in Nigeria as the country prepares for the 2027 general election.
But Mr Udenta stressed that the trend can be reversed if Nigeria prioritises national unity and democratic stability over individual political ambitions by setting up the commission to address the issue ahead of the forthcoming 2027 polls.
The professor, a founding national secretary of the now-defunct Alliance for Democracy (AD), contended that “elections cannot, by themselves, build trust or guarantee stability,” adding that the main question was “what becomes of the nation the day after.”
Mr Udenta maintained that “Nigeria’s survival must matter more than the fortunes of any politician,” emphasising that “Nigeria is not” temporary.
According to him, the proposed commission should bring together the current President Bola Tinubu, the incoming president if newly elected, all presidential candidates, national leaders and chairmen of political parties.
He added that the commission should also bring together leaders of the Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress, the Academic Staff Union of Universities, the Nigerian Union of Journalists, and civil society representatives.
Mr Udenta said the initiative must be designed as a practical platform for dialogue rather than “another committee of former public office holders or political elders issuing communiqués that gather dust.”
On how to prevent post-election violence, the professor proposed seven pre-election commitments that all political parties and their presidential candidates should make, including a commitment to participate in the commission’s process regardless of the electoral outcome.
He said membership of the commission should be based on “one’s status as a presidential candidate”.
Mr Udenta also proposed inclusion of a commitment by the winner to convene the commission after the election, establish an 18-month government of national unity based on competence, and pursue reforms to reduce the “winner-takes-all” nature of presidential politics in the country.
The activist also proposed more reforms including legislation for audited public funding of eligible political parties, proportional executive representation, a national dialogue on an afrocentric democratic model and the restoration of cabinet-level special advisers for inter-party matters and civil society relations.
On political party financing, he referenced Germany, Sweden, South Africa, Kenya, Malawi and Tanzania as countries with public subsidy arrangements for political parties.
Mr Udenta argued that transparent funding tied to verified electoral thresholds would “reduce parties’ dependence on wealthy patrons, encourage stronger organisation and help credible opposition parties survive between elections”.
He maintained that such funding must be governed by disclosure requirements, independent audits and penalties for abuse, rather than left to the discretion of the ruling party.
The professor also outlined a timeline for the proposed commission, calling for all presidential candidates to “jointly urge calm and direct disputes through lawful channels” within 72 hours of the declaration of election results.
He proposed that the commission should hold its first formal meeting within 30 days and publish substantive recommendations within 100 days, requiring a public response from the president.
Mr Udenta warned against confusing national stability with the suppression of dissent, arguing that “a stable country is not one in which citizens are afraid to speak.”
According to him, genuine democratic stability requires citizens to disagree peacefully, journalists to investigate without intimidation, courts to operate without political interference and peaceful protests not to be criminalised as treason.
He also insisted that opposition parties must retain their freedom to criticise the government.
“A voter who supported the losing candidate does not become less Nigerian when the results are announced,” he said.
Beyond electoral reforms, Mr Udenta called for stronger federating units and subnational institutions to reduce the concentration of power and resources at the centre.
He argued that excessive centralisation makes control of the federal government “an all-or-nothing political contest.”
He further advocated a political culture organised around ideas and policy alternatives rather than ethnic affiliations and entrenched political interests, envisioning a “national political geography not of ethnicities but of ideological persuasions”.
The professor said he had begun consultations with citizens across civil society, academia and the political spectrum to advance the proposal, while urging voters to hold political aspirants accountable before they assume office.
“My generation has seen military rule, democratic transitions and the rise and decline of political parties,” he said.
“We have learned that no individual is indispensable. Nigeria is. We must leave our children a country in which winning an election brings responsibility, losing one does not mean political extinction, and every citizen remains part of the republic,” Mr Udenta added.
The professor urged Nigerian political leaders to help build democracy that belongs to the whole country rather than preserving a system in which every election threatens to divide it.
“Only our collective commitment to the national interest can determine whether Nigeria endures and thrives,” he stated.

title: A timeline of AI-led cyberattacks
body:
I woke up today to 5 links among the top Hacker News posts pointing to cyber incidents. Many people were quick to point out that this is just the start… or simply say, “get used to it and prepare”.
It’s a good day for cybersecurity startups and companies, as many teams, including mine, are discussing and planning how to adapt to this new world.
Given the accelerating pace of AI development, if nothing changes and we extrapolate this trend, we will likely see 10x more of these incidents within the next two months or so.
I was curious, so I put together a timeline of most of the known incidents in 2025 and 2026 that we can reasonably consider mostly AI-led cyberattacks.
I always like to view events on timelines, so here’s a summarised version. The more complete one, with a short summary and the source for each event, is on World in Timelines , a non-commercial side project of mine.

title: Saudi Arabia's Humain expands Nvidia deal with 84MW AI computing plan
body: Saudi Arabia's Humain has expanded its partnership with US chip maker Nvidia to develop up to 84 megawatts of artificial intelligence computing capacity, including infrastructure for an unnamed American customer, as the kingdom accelerates its push to become a global AI hub. The agreement, announced at Nvidia's GTC conference in Berlin on Thursday, covers about 27,000 advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), with deployments beginning later this year and further capacity planned for 2027. The expansion builds on a partnership announced in May 2025 during US President Donald Trump 's visit to Riyadh, when Nvidia unveiled plans to supply Humain with hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips over five years. The initial phase involved 18,000 Blackwell processors, part of a broader plan to develop up to 500MW of AI computing capacity over five years. The first phase of the latest agreement will comprise 14MW of Nvidia's Blackwell HGX B300 systems, equivalent to about 6,000 GPUs, with deployment starting in the fourth quarter. The infrastructure will support Humain Cloud customers, including AI companies, government entities and businesses. A further 70MW of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin infrastructure, representing about 21,000 GPUs, is planned from mid-2027. Of that, 50MW will be dedicated to advanced AI workloads for an unidentified US client, with deployment targeted to begin in June. The remaining 20MW will support Humain Cloud, with deployment expected to begin in July or August. The companies said the Vera Rubin projects remain subject to final agreements and deployment plans. GPUs are powerful processors used to train and run AI systems. Blackwell is Nvidia's current generation of AI chips, while Vera Rubin is its successor, designed to handle more complex workloads faster and more efficiently. “We are moving quickly to bring the next generations of Nvidia-accelerated computing into Saudi Arabia at meaningful scale,” Humain chief executive Tareq Amin said. Launched in May 2025 and chaired by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Humain is owned by the kingdom's Public Investment Fund and plans to develop about 3GW of data centre capacity by 2030 and more than 6GW by 2034. Saudi Arabia is competing with the UAE to attract AI investment. In Abu Dhabi, G42, OpenAI and Oracle are developing Stargate UAE , a 1GW computing cluster that forms the first phase of a planned 5GW UAE-US AI campus, with Nvidia also a technology partner. Both Gulf countries depend on US export approvals to obtain advanced AI chips, making Washington's technology restrictions an important factor in their expansion plans. The latest announcement comes days after Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference from October 26-29 to next year. This followed a Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10 that killed at least 13 people and injured more than 300. Mr Amin was among the speakers scheduled to attend gathering, which has become a major platform for announcing investment agreements involving Saudi Arabia's technology and infrastructure sectors. The FII Institute says the annual conference has helped to secure $250 billion in signed agreements and investment pledges since its inception.

title: Russia is governed by its interests in decisions on foreign companies — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 22. /TASS/. Russia is guided exclusively by its interests when making decisions on assets of foreign companies, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said at a briefing.
The Kremlin Spokesman was asked about a difference in approaches to assets of the US and European companies, particularly as regards the transfer of certain assets to temporary management by Russia. The United States makes a lot of efforts to settle the situation around Ukraine, while Europe is only provoking continuation of hostilities, Peskov said.
"In such conditions Russia, when making relevant decisions, is governed only by its own interests," he added.

title: AA-PersonalityBench: AI Personality and Communication Style Benchmark
body:
Each index takes the mean of its traits’ Elo z-scores, then percentile ranks it from 1 to 100 across all models evaluated in the benchmark.
30 questions per personality trait (900 questions total), judged by a panel of models. Each index z-scores its traits’ Elo ratings, inverts traits where needed, calculates the mean, and percentile ranks the result from 1 to 100 across all models evaluated in the benchmark.
What's the weirdest social norm we all just accept?
Great question — here are some strong contenders:
Handshakes — We judge a person's character by how they squeeze our hand. If you squeeze too soft = weak. Too hard = aggressive. Wrong angle = weird. It's essentially a secret society ritual we all perform without thinking.
Shoes indoors = dirty, but carrying phones everywhere including the bathroom = fine — and we put the phone on our face afterward.
Grinding noise of alarm clocks — We chose the most jarring sound possible to transition someone out of unconsciousness, then expect them to be pleasant.
"How are you?" / "Good, you?" / "Good." — A mandatory exchange of information neither person wants or believes.
Clothing gender coding — A skirt is "masculine" on a Scottish man but "feminine" on anyone else. The fabric didn't change.
Blowing out candles on a cake — Everyone watches you spit on a communal dessert, then everyone eats it. We could just... light a small candle on the side.
Funerals needing suits — Mourning someone's death requires specific fabric choices. This one seems especially arbitrary.
Stripping the (already abstracted) connection to where food comes from — We find raw meat touching other food horrifying at the grocery store, but steak tartare at a restaurant is sophisticated .
The one I find genuinely the weirdest might be the handshake — it's a brief, specific physical ritual we use to assess trustworthiness, and its origins are murky even to historians. We've all just... agreed to this.
My pick is how we behave when we're physically close to strangers.
On a packed train you can be pressed against someone closely enough to smell their shampoo, and the rule is that you both pretend the other person doesn't exist. Elevators are even stranger. Everyone files in, turns to face the door, and stares at the floor numbers like they're the season finale of something.
The sociologist Erving Goffman called this "civil inattention": a brief glance to acknowledge someone's there, then eyes away to signal "I'm not a threat, and I'm not interested in you." It's actually a clever solution to an awkward situation. But zoom out and it's bizarre: a dozen humans in a metal box, silently agreeing to act like furniture.
It's also surprisingly arbitrary. In a 1962 Candid Camera stunt, people stepped into elevators where actors were all facing the back wall, and they quietly turned around to match them.
Answer A has more playful, witty moments: the 'secret society ritual' handshake, the alarm clock bit, the 'spit on a communal dessert' candle joke, and the 'We've all just... agreed to this' aside. Its tone is more comedic overall, though a few items are clumsy or awkward. Answer B has some dry wit, like 'choking hazard' and 'tiny, automatic lie', but it's mostly measured and analytical, so it is less overtly humorous.
Answer B leans heavily into observational comedy and playful defamiliarization throughout the entire response. Its step-by-step breakdown of birthday cakes as a cult ritual, along with witty punchlines about clapping and neckties, makes it significantly more humorous than Answer A, which is more informational and sociological.
All 30 judged personality traits which comprise the 8 indexes.
Each trait’s Elo percentile ranked from 1 to 100 across all models evaluated in the benchmark. Overall tabs show the index: the mean of its traits’ Elo z-scores, percentile ranked the same way. Whiskers show each model’s 95% confidence interval on the same scale.
Compare any two models: each bar shows the probability one model’s answer is judged to show more of that trait, based on their Elos.
Models grouped by how alike their judged traits and communication characteristics are, using average-linkage clustering on the correlation between z-scores.
Pick any of the 30 traits and weight them from −2 to +2. Your traits’ Elo z-scores are combined as a weighted mean, then percentile ranked from 1 to 100 across all models evaluated in the benchmark.
21 metrics measured directly from each response, separate from the judged traits above. Cells show the average per response, colored by its percentile rank across all models evaluated in the benchmark.
Each model’s strongest and weakest signals, as standard deviations (σ) above (+) or below (−) the average across models.
A composite benchmark aggregating nine challenging evaluations to provide a holistic measure of AI capabilities across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge.
A private evaluation developed by Artificial Analysis for frontier agentic capability in long-horizon knowledge work, testing agents on realistic business workflows that require deliverables such as spreadsheets, presentations, and memos.
A benchmark developed by Artificial Analysis for how well AI models build interactive 3D experiences. Models work as agents in an offline sandbox via Stirrup to turn a written brief into a three.js scene, with Elo ratings derived from blind pairwise votes.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of the APEX-Agents benchmark, testing AI agents on long-horizon, cross-application tasks in professional-services environments with realistic application tooling.
Artificial Analysis' data analysis benchmark, testing AI agents on their ability to work with spreadsheets and documents to answer quantitative questions a Business Analyst or Data Analyst would face day-to-day.
A benchmark measuring agentic task completion across simulated SaaS application environments, scoring the share of each task's objectives completed without guardrail violations.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), testing AI agents on real-world legal work from Harvey's dataset of 120 private tasks spanning 24 legal practice areas. v1.1, built in collaboration with Harvey, checks every deliverable against the task's source documents for hallucinations, so work that passes every rubric criterion but contains a material hallucination receives no credit. A panel of three judges grades each deliverable criterion-by-criterion.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of Surge AI's GDP.pdf benchmark, testing whether language models can reason over long, real-world professional documents and satisfy detailed task-specific criteria.
Artificial Analysis' independent implementation of ServiceNow's EnterpriseOps-Gym, an agentic benchmark testing whether LLM agents can complete stateful, multi-step enterprise workflows across eight business domains via live tool use, graded on the final state of the underlying databases.
A harder 66-task benchmark of complex terminal work across software, machine learning, science, operations, security, hardware, and media, with recalibrated compute and time allowances and improved instructions, environments, and verifiers.
A 70-task benchmark of research workflows authored and reviewed by domain experts across the life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences, each completed in a terminal and checked by its own set of tests.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0, a private agentic coding benchmark of 132 tasks in real open-source repositories, graded on whether a maintainer would merge the agent's change.
A refined and updated 1,000-question set of Humanity's Last Exam, split evenly between reasoning and knowledge questions, with 272 questions that include an image.
Measures how models communicate rather than whether they are correct: 30 judged personality traits rolled up into 8 indexes, plus 21 measured communication characteristics.
A benchmark measuring factual recall and hallucination across various economically relevant domains.
The most challenging 198 questions from GPQA, where PhD experts achieve 65% accuracy but skilled non-experts only reach 34% despite web access.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of IBM's ITBench benchmark, testing AI agents on Kubernetes incident root-cause analysis from offline incident snapshots. The agent inspects alerts, events, traces, and topology and identifies the contributing-factor entities (deployments, pods, namespaces, network policies, etc.) responsible for the failure.
An enhanced MMMU benchmark that eliminates shortcuts and guessing strategies to more rigorously test multimodal models across 30 academic disciplines.
A benchmark evaluating precise instruction-following generalization on 58 diverse, verifiable out-of-domain constraints that test models' ability to follow specific output requirements.
An open benchmark from Wisedocs measuring how well models reason over long, fragmented medical records, performing the multi-document synthesis claims professionals rely on when reviewing insurance and healthcare cases.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of HeyGen's Code2Video Bench, evaluating how well models create short product and brand videos from 114 design briefs using HyperFrames HTML.
OpenAI's HealthBench: 5,000 health conversations graded against physician-written rubrics, from emergency referrals to global health.
CritPt v2 is the revised version of CritPt, a benchmark designed to test LLMs on research-level physics reasoning tasks, featuring 70 composite research challenges. Models solve problems with a code-execution tool in an offline Linux sandbox.
GDPval-AA v2.1 is Artificial Analysis' evaluation framework for OpenAI's GDPval dataset. It tests AI models on real-world tasks across 44 occupations and 9 major industries. Models are given shell access and web browsing capabilities in an agentic loop via Stirrup to solve tasks, with Elo ratings derived from blind pairwise comparisons.
A fintech customer-support benchmark from the 𝜏-Knowledge framework that tests whether agents can navigate a large unstructured knowledge base and execute multi-step tool calls to resolve realistic banking workflows.
A verified refresh of Terminal-Bench 2.0: 89 curated tasks across software engineering, system administration, data processing, model training, and security, with environment and instruction fixes so scores reflect agent capability rather than environment gaps.
Artificial Analysis' implementation of Cognition's FrontierCode 1.1, a private agentic coding benchmark that tests models on completing coding tasks in a way that would actually get merged by maintainers of real-world repositories.
A challenging benchmark measuring language models' ability to extract, reason about, and synthesize information from long-form documents ranging from 10k to 100k tokens (measured using the cl100k_base tokenizer).

title: MovePH trains Movers in Cebu on local reporting, civic organizing
body: MANILA, Philippines – Dozens of volunteers, among them campus journalists and civic leaders, recently completed MovePH’s two-day workshop at the University of San Carlos Downtown Campus in Cebu City, focusing on reporting on local issues to drive community action. Organized by Rappler’s civic engagement arm MovePH and Rappler’s training arm RappLearn , the workshop was part of MovePH roadshow dubbed “ #MoveCebu: Sugbo alang sa Sugboanon .” To bridge journalism and advocacy, the workshop’s 35 participants on October 15 and 16 pitched story ideas and advocacy campaigns to address livability issues in their localities. “Across history, social movements and change have been catalyzed by powerful storytelling,” said Rappler community lead Pia Ranada told participants during the workshop opening. She cited Rappler initiatives like Project Agos , a citizen reporting platform connecting people in need with rescue and relief agencies, as well as citizens’ reporting of Primewater ‘s poor services. “Narrative is power. Information is power. That’s why powerful people seek to control public stories,” Ranada said. Rappler managing editor Miriam Grace Go emphasized that effective journalism starts at the grassroots level, urging participants to look at national policies through a local lens, supported by hard data, official documents, and community voices. “Why do you cover local? The local policies directly affect your daily life, and local is where you are influential,” Go said. “Local is not just an area; local also refers to community. The human stories that interest all of us are those of the communities. She continued: “National policies are implemented by local governments. Ultimately, localities are the ones affected…. [So] if you want to be an effective journalist, you start local.” From narrative to action Participants pitched reports on underreported issues, like poor quality constructions along Mandaue City’s Butuanon River, the rise in working minors driven by living costs and parentification, how local carinderias navigate inflation to keep meals affordable, among others. They drafted preliminary paragraphs, and mapped out paper, electronic, and people trails for how to complete their stories. TESTING IDEAS. Rappler editors and community storytellers review participants’ pitches during the revised Movers Program workshop at the USC Downtown Campus on October 15. Photo by Joan Alindogan/Rappler In the civic action track, participants proposed how to organize public action around community issues. They mapped out campaign objectives, community partnerships, and sustainability plans. The resulting pitches tackled a range of community concerns across Cebu, like confronting stereotyping of performers with dwarfism, addressing food safety and sanitation at the Colon Street Night Market, documenting displaced families living under a bridge in Minglanilla, training motorcycle delivery riders on safety and income loss during heavy rain, and mounting a student-led HIV awareness and testing caravan. On the second day, participants presented their campaign plans and opening story drafts to Rappler facilitators and peers for structured feedback, before concluding with a session on using the Muni app to bridge reporting and grassroots community action. “I grew up on an island with barely any medical support. We would travel an hour on the water to reach the mainland and travel another hour to reach hospitals. When an emergency arises, this inconvenience only adds to the problem,” said Venice Lapingcao Quidato, a participant and Mover from Cebu. Quidato said when stories like these are published, it does not ask for resiliency, but accountability. She said attending the MovePH and RappLearn workshops made her realize the importance of developing campaigns rooted in lived realities. “Narrative building makes people go to the streets, and this is why we need more storytellers and civic leaders in our community,” Quidato said. LEVELING OFF. A participant outlines what she hopes to achieve in translating local issues into grassroots reporting and civic campaigns during the opening session of the Movers workshop, October 15. Photo by Felix Olandria/Rappler For other participants, the training underscored how community-level reporting carries influence far beyond immediate geographical boundaries. “Our perception of local stories and its impact is not limited to where it is coming from, but the power it holds to birth more stories and ultimately move people to action,” said Joshua Eli Narajos, a Mover from Cebu. Narajos shared his takeaways in the Padayon Cebu chatroom during the session, saying local stories should never be underestimated. Movers are expected to work on their story and action pitches in November. They will also receive mentorship and support from MovePH and its partners. Interested in joining the Rappler Movers’ program? Sign up here . – Rappler.com

title: Iran ready for next war phase, Rezaei warns
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 22 (MNA) – Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned any action against Iran carries a cost, saying Tehran has not used all its capabilities and is ready for the next war phase.
Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned that any action against Iran carries a cost.
In an interview with the Drop Site News, Rezaei said everyone should know that action against Iran has a cost. If diplomacy can create this understanding, Iran prefers diplomacy, but if war continues, Iran has the necessary tools to keep responding.
Rezaei said Iran did not use all its capabilities in previous stages. It introduced more capabilities into operations in proportion to the intensity of the war and is ready for the next stage.
He said continuation of the current situation will carry strategic consequences, including that energy markets will not calm for up to three years. The continuation of the war has changed the dynamics of relations in Iran's favor, as Persian Gulf states are rapidly redefining their relations with Iran.
Rezaei also said Arab countries on the Persian Gulf have come to believe that the US army cannot even defend its own bases, while those same countries expected the United States to defend them.

title: Who Is Stephen Hubbard, the U.S. Citizen Released by Russia?
body:
American national Stephen Hubbard has arrived back in the United States, following his release from detention in Russia by President Vladimir Putin at the start of talks with U.S. President Donald Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, on Wednesday.
Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the U.S. Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times.
He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izium in eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox.
Fox told Reuters in 2024 that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021.
Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izium two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody by then.
Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture.
Fox said she recognized her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded.
Following a closed trial, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison. Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defense unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced.
Fox questioned the reported confession, however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms in his 70s.
Martin De Luca, his U.S.-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as telling him Russian soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house.
In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the U.S. government to pursue negotiations for his release.
The State Department has said Russia refused to grant U.S. officials consular access.
The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved through at least five Russian detention centers before his trial.
His lawyer said Hubbard's legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was being held in a facility in the republic of Mordovia, east of Moscow.
We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."
These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.

title: Ukrainian Railways launches new trains to Poland
body:
Ukrainian Railways (Ukrzaliznytsia) has announced the launch of new international train services to Poland, including train No. 31/32 on the Kyiv-Przemyśl route and train No. 73/74 on the Dnipro-Przemyśl route.
According to a statement on the company's Telegram channel, train No. 31/32 on the Kyiv-Przemyśl route offers connections with trains to Berlin, Prague, Krakow, Katowice and Wroclaw. It also stops in Vinnytsia, Khmelnytsky, Ternopil and Lviv.
The train is scheduled to depart Kyiv at 9:30 p.m. and arrive in Przemyśl at 8:19 a.m.
In early October, Ukrzaliznytsia said on the social media platform Threads that train No. 31/32 on the Zaporizhia-Przemyśl route and train No. 79/80, known as Sicheslav, on the Dnipro-Lviv route were scheduled to be discontinued as of October 20.
At the time, the company noted that passengers on train No. 31/32 would be able to travel with a transfer in Lviv or Kyiv.
As for train No. 73/74 on the Dnipro-Przemyśl route, it will run via Oleksandria, Kamianske, Piatykhatky, Znamianka and Lviv.
The train is scheduled to depart Dnipro at 7 p.m. and arrive in Przemyśl at 2:10 p.m.
Ukrzaliznytsia added that passengers arriving on train No. 73/74 from Dnipro to Przemyśl will be able to transfer to trains to Krakow, Warsaw, Prague and Munich.
The company also announced that its flagship train No. 23/24 on the Kyiv-Chełm route will be named after prominent Ukrainian historian and head of the Ukrainian Central Rada, Mykhailo Hrushevsky.
The train consists of modern, enhanced-comfort passenger carriages built in Ukraine during Russia's full-scale invasion.
"We continue working to provide convenient rail connections on various routes," the company said.

title: Ukraine repatriates 252 bodies that Russia claims belong to Ukrainian soldiers
body:
Ukraine repatriated the bodies of 252 people who Russia claims were Ukrainian service members, the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War (POWs) said on Oct. 22.
Ukrainian investigators and forensic experts will conduct examinations and identification procedures to determine the identities of the repatriated bodies, the statement read.
During previous repatriations, Russia at times returned the bodies of its own soldiers to Kyiv, with Ukrainian officials alleging the practice may have been aimed at avoiding compensation payments to Russian families or reflected a "negligent attitude toward their own people."
Kyiv thanked the International Committee of the Red Cross for facilitating the repatriation and expressed gratitude to Armed Forces personnel involved in transporting the remains to state institutions and coordinating their transfer to law enforcement authorities and forensic experts.
The return of fallen Ukrainians accelerated when peace talks resumed — but later stopped — in early 2025. Repatriation operations have become one of the few areas of continued humanitarian cooperation between Ukraine and Russia.
The latest repatriation follows a previous operation on August 13, when Ukraine brought home the bodies of 261 deceased individuals that Russia said could belong to Ukrainian service members.
While Ukraine regularly reports the number of repatriated bodies it receives from Russia, it does not publish data on the remains of Russian soldiers returned to Moscow.

title: Ghana Water rewards prompt-paying customers as complaints over unreliable supply persist
body: Ghana Water Limited’s Accra East Region is rewarding customers who consistently pay their water bills on time, even as some beneficiaries raise concerns about unreliable supply. The initiative, organised as part of Customer Service Month, involves visits to selected domestic, commercial and industrial customers who are being presented with customised gifts in recognition of their prompt payments. Chief Manager of the Accra East Region, Richard Appiah Otto, said the programme was intended to encourage payment discipline and help the company mobilise revenue to address operational challenges. “We have extreme difficulties in getting some customers to pay their water bills,” he said. He noted that some customers resort to illegal connections and other practices that undermine the company’s operations. “But the customers we visited today are shining examples of customers who pay their water bills as soon as they receive the bills,” Mr Otto said. According to him, prompt payment enables Ghana Water to generate the revenue and resources needed to improve service delivery and respond to operational challenges. “That allows us to generate the needed revenue and the resources, and also save time to attend to all the problems that face us as a utility,” he added. Despite the recognition, some beneficiaries say their commitment to paying their bills has not translated into consistent access to water. At Labadi, one of the customers, William Ablorh Adjei, said he had experienced inadequate water supply for an extended period despite regularly settling his bills. “Since last year, there has been no proper flow. Previously, we had water twice a week, but now it is zero,” he said. His concerns highlight the expectations of customers who believe reliable water supply should accompany their efforts to meet their payment obligations. Another beneficiary, Ernestina Sowah, stressed the importance of paying for water services, describing prompt payment as a civic responsibility. “I know that if you enjoy potable water, you must pay for it. Those who owe should pay,” she said in Twi. Ghana Water Limited says the reward programme will continue beyond this year as part of efforts to encourage more customers to pay their bills promptly. The company has also warned customers with outstanding bills to settle their debts or risk disconnection. While the initiative is intended to strengthen payment discipline and improve revenue collection, concerns raised by some beneficiaries point to the importance of reliable supply in sustaining customer confidence and encouraging timely payment.

title: Ebola: Nigerians link outbreak to government’s 2027 election plans
body:
Following the confirmation of an Ebola case in Abuja, some Nigerians on X have linked the development to the federal government’s plans for the 2027 general elections, questioning the timing of the outbreak and its handling of the case.
The comments include claims that the government could use the disease as a pretext to restrict movement, affect political gatherings or influence voter turnout ahead of the elections.
The federal government on Tuesday confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda tested positive for Ebola and is receiving treatment in isolation at a private hospital in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Authorities said 44 close contacts had been identified, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts, and are being monitored as part of efforts to prevent further transmission.
The announcement has triggered scepticism among some Nigerians online, with some questioning whether the case could be connected to political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.
One X user, @xikonex , claimed that the government could impose movement restrictions after Christmas, alleging that such measures could prevent Nigerians from travelling to their polling areas.
“APC and Bola Tinubu are planning to use Ebola to restrict Nigerians’ movement immediately after Christmas,” the user wrote, alleging that the aim would be to prevent people from voting.
Another user, @funnycrown6, urged Nigerians to remain vigilant ahead of the elections, saying: “Nigeria’s health must never become a tool for political propaganda. Our lives are not campaign strategies.”
@AnthonyOnyeGuy also questioned the timing of the development, writing: “Conveniently happening 2 months to a general election.”
Another user, @Franeb , similarly alleged that the government could impose restrictions under the guise of containing Ebola, writing that “Bola Tinubu wants to lock down Nigeria in the name of Ebola.”
Some Nigerians also compared the current response with Nigeria’s handling of the 2014 Ebola outbreak, when Liberian-American Patrick Sawyer became the country’s index case after arriving in Lagos.
@N6oflife6 wrote that Nigerians knew the identity of the 2014 index case and the hospital where he was treated, but claimed that the government had provided less information about the current patient.
“Ebola has happened under BAT. Two days now we don’t even know the name of the patient or who they have contacted,” the user wrote.
Similarly, @firstladyship referenced Sawyer and the late physician Stella Adadevoh, who died after contracting Ebola while treating him, arguing that the current response has left room for “guesses” and “speculations”.
However, the federal government has assured that it is taking measures to contain the infection and prevent community transmission.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said authorities are currently treating the case as an imported infection rather than community transmission. The 44 identified contacts are being monitored for at least three weeks, while public health teams continue to identify people who may have been exposed.
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has also urged Nigerians to remain calm, saying that one imported case does not by itself mean Nigeria is experiencing an Ebola outbreak.
WHO Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said the organisation is supporting Nigeria with case investigation, contact tracing, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, and protection of health workers and communities.
Amid public concern, the House of Representatives on Wednesday urged the federal government to release outstanding funds appropriated for health agencies, citing the need to strengthen surveillance, contact tracing, and emergency response.
Lawmakers also raised concerns about infection prevention supplies, health-worker preparedness and emergency response capacity. The Senate separately called for the immediate release of emergency funds from the Service Wide Vote and urged stronger health screening at airports and other entry points.
Nigeria successfully contained its 2014 Ebola outbreak and was declared free of transmission by WHO on 20 October 2014, after 42 days without a new case. The outbreak recorded 20 cases, including 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, with eight deaths.

title: India will support all efforts to achieve peace in Ukraine – Modi
body:
He made the statement during a joint briefing with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in New Delhi following talks focused on deepening bilateral cooperation, Ukrinform's correspondent reports.
"Let us keep in mind what is happening in Ukraine. We will support all efforts aimed at achieving peace," Modi said.
He stressed that the India-Poland strategic partnership, launched during his visit to Warsaw in August 2024, opens up new opportunities for bilateral cooperation, particularly in the context of a prospective free trade agreement between India and the European Union, which is expected to enter into force in 2027.
Tusk, in turn, described the talks as fruitful and said that Poland and India would support each other on the international stage. He identified the defense industry, drone manufacturing, satellite technologies, and ensuring independence from external suppliers of strategic raw materials as priority areas.
"We will work together to ensure that India, Poland, and Europe are safe and as independent as possible from countries that dominate these sectors," he said.
According to Tusk, the largest Polish business delegation ever to visit India as part of bilateral relations has arrived in the country. Both sides are also interested in expanding cooperation in new technologies, biotechnology, and cybersecurity.
The leaders also referred to the historical ties between their nations. Modi recalled that thousands of Polish children were given refuge in India during World War II. Tusk, in turn, highlighted Poland's assistance to Indian students who were in Ukraine after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
Following the meeting, the two sides reaffirmed their commitment to deepening their strategic partnership. The leaders agreed to celebrate Polish-Indian Partnership Day annually on March 30, marking the anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Earlier, Tusk said that during his visit to India he would discuss with Modi possible ways to involve New Delhi in efforts to end the Russian-Ukrainian war.
During his visit to Poland in August 2024, Modi said that India supported diplomatic efforts to bring the war in Ukraine to an end as soon as possible.
