title: JYSK store at Kyiv's Pochaina district completely destroyed
body:
A JYSK store in the Pochaina district was destroyed in a Russian attack on Thursday. No one was injured, JYSK Ukraine Country Director Yevhen Ivanytsia said.

"Unfortunately, another JYSK store in the Pochaina district was destroyed this morning during a massive missile attack on Kyiv. The store burned to the ground," he wrote on LinkedIn.

Among the positive developments, he said, was that neither employees nor customers had been injured.

"All customer orders will be delivered. All employees will keep their jobs and continue working at other stores in the chain. We continue to grow: today we will sign one new lease agreement, and tomorrow another," Ivanytsia said.

As reported, the Epicentr hypermarket and Retail Park Pochaina were damaged in a Russian attack on the capital overnight into Thursday. The most extensive damage was sustained by the premises of JYSK, Puma, Colin's and Nova Poshta stores, as well as the office of Nhood Ukraine, the retail park's management company.

title: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
body: Two women – a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi. Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. Libyan officials were reported as saying the women would be handed over to authorities in their respective countries after necessary procedures were completed. Libya’s al-Masar TV showed the two women entering what looks like an ambulance and later being attended to by a health worker. Speaking in French, the women thanked Khalifa Haftar, military commander of eastern Libya, and his son, Saddam Haftar, for their release. Gretzmacher was an aid worker who had lived for many years in Niger, while Abbt had spent several years living and working as a community worker in Agadez. A plane was expected to leave Benghazi on Thursday, first stopping in Vienna to transfer Gretzmacher to Austrian authorities before continuing to Switzerland with Abbt, privately owned Air Info Agadez news outlet reported. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 Nato-backed uprising that toppled long-time ruler Muammar Gaddafi. It is split between two administrations – one in the east backed by Haftar, and the other in the west in the capital Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah. Niger and the broader Sahel region have faced years of jihadist violence, including kidnappings and deadly attacks, carried out by different groups linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State. The country has been under military control since 2023 when Gen Abdourahmane Tchiani deposed the country’s elected President, Mohamed Bazoum.

title: Udenta Proposes Sovereign Commission to Prevent Post-election Crisis
body: Chuks Okocha in Abuja A pro-democracy activist and founding National Secretary of the Alliance for Democracy (AD), Professor Udenta O. Udenta, has proposed the establishment of a Sovereign Commission for Democratic Sustainability and National Stability to address Nigeria’s political tensions and prevent elections from triggering national crises. In a statement, Udenta argued that the challenge ahead of the 2027 general election goes beyond who emerges president, stressing that the country must prioritise national unity and democratic stability over individual political ambitions. For example, he said that while he is a fervent Peter Obi supporter and will vote for him, there are other players who will drive this project with him that are supporters of President Tinubu, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Gov Seyi Makinde, and the other presidential candidates. He further asserted that “elections cannot, by themselves, build trust or guarantee stability,” adding that the critical question is “what becomes of the nation the day after?” He stressed that “Nigeria’s survival must matter more than the fortunes of any politician,” because “Nigeria is not temporary.” The proposed commission would bring together the sitting president, all certified presidential candidates, national leaders and chairmen of political parties, leaders of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC), the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), the Nigerian Union of Journalists (NUJ) and civil society representatives. Udenta stressed that the initiative was designed to be a practical platform for dialogue rather than “another committee of former officeholders or political elders issuing communiqués that gather dust.” He proposed that all political parties and their presidential candidates make seven pre-election commitments, including participating in the commission regardless of electoral outcome. According to Udenta, membership would be based on candidacy, declaring that it “only derives from one’s status as a presidential candidate. Period!” Other proposals, he said, include a commitment by the winner to convene the commission after the election, establish a time-bound 18-month Government of National Unity based on competence, and pursue reforms to reduce the winner-takes-all nature of presidential politics. The proposed reforms also include legislation for audited public funding of eligible political parties, proportional executive representation, a national dialogue on an Afrocentric democratic model and the restoration of cabinet-level Special Advisers for Inter-Party Matters and Civil Society Relations. On political party financing, Udenta cited Germany, Sweden, South Africa, Kenya, Malawi and Tanzania as countries with public subsidy arrangements for political parties. He argued that transparent funding tied to verified electoral thresholds would “reduce parties’ dependence on wealthy patrons, encourage stronger organisation and help credible opposition parties survive between elections.” The professor maintained that such funding must be governed by disclosure requirements, independent audits and penalties for abuse, rather than left to the discretion of the ruling party. Udenta also outlined a timeline for the proposed commission, calling for all presidential candidates to “jointly urge calm and direct disputes through lawful channels” within 72 hours of the declaration of election results. He proposed that the commission hold its first formal meeting within 30 days and publish substantive recommendations within 100 days, requiring a public response from the president. Udenta warned against confusing national stability with the suppression of dissent, declaring: “A stable country is not one in which citizens are afraid to speak.” According to him, genuine democratic stability requires citizens to disagree peacefully, journalists to investigate without intimidation, courts to operate without political interference,e and peaceful protests not to be criminalised as treason. He also insisted that opposition parties must retain their freedom to criticise the government, noting that “a voter who supported the losing candidate does not become less Nigerian when the results are announced. Beyond electoral reforms, Udenta called for stronger federating units and subnational institutions to reduce the concentration of power and resources at the centre. He argued that excessive centralisation makes control of the Federal Government an all-or-nothing political contest. In his concluding challenge to political leaders, Udenta asked: “Will you help build a democracy that belongs to the whole country, or preserve a system in which every election threatens to divide it?” He stressed that although political rivalry and competition were necessary in a democracy, they must not undermine national institutions, adding that “only our collective commitment to the national interest can determine whether Nigeria endures and thrives.”

title: Prominent Rumbek Central Paramount Chief Madol Mathok dies at 87
body: The influential and long-serving paramount chief of Lakes State’s Rumbek Central County, Madol Mathok Agolder, 87, passed away in Juba age 87 years has passed away today in Juba on Wednesday after battling illness. Born in 1939, the deceased was popularly known as Agut-kec and succeeded his brother, Maker Mathok, as chief in 1976. He was venerated for contributing to the SPLM/A liberation struggle. Rumbek Central County Commissioner Manyiel Riak Manyiel confirmed the paramount chief’s death and said he had informed Governor Gen. Rin Tueny Mabor. “The untimely death of the paramount chief of Rumbek Central County has caused great shock to everyone in the community and across Lakes State,” he said. “The late paramount chief was a well-known community leader to the late Dr. John Garang de Mabior and the current president, Salva Kiir Mayardit, during the SPLA liberation struggle because of his immense contribution in terms of human resources and material contributions.” Commissioner Riak said the doctors who were treating the deceased will reveal the exact cause of death. For his part, Emmanuel Mading Manon, the chairperson of the Nyang Community of Rumbek Central County, said they have lost a great man. He revealed that the late paramount chief was called back from the Sudan Police Service in 1976 to succeed his late brother Maker Mathok following the latter’s death. “The late Paramount Chief Madol Mathok passed away today (Wednesday) from a heart attack in Juba”, he said. “My message to the greater Rumbek community is that we have lost a great man of peace. Unfortunately, we have lost a man who was our dictionary and a Bible and also a leader who was supposed to continue guiding us.” According to Mading, arrangements are underway to take the body of the late paramount chief to Rumbek for burial. He said a grave is being prepared near Bros Hotel in Rumbek. “The late Paramount Chief Madol Mathok was a great supporter of the liberation struggle and mobilized youth to join the SPLA, contributed food to the then rebels, and hosted several SPLA garrisons.” The post Prominent Rumbek Central Paramount Chief Madol Mathok dies at 87 appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: ‘Enough is enough’ – NDC’s James Agbey warns of backlash over ‘abandoned’ task force
body: A National Democratic Congress (NDC) operative, James Agbey, has warned that the alleged neglect of the party’s electoral task force could provoke a backlash, calling their treatment after the 2024 election victory a “recipe for disaster”. In a statement dated October 22, 2026, Mr Agbey accused the party and government of failing to address the welfare and employment concerns of operatives who helped mobilise supporters and protect ballots during the elections. “Enough is enough,” he declared, calling for jobs, empowerment opportunities and what he described as promised placements in national security. Mr Agbey said the concerns went beyond employment to include recognition and a meaningful voice in the party’s decision-making structures. He argued that some operatives felt the party had relied on them as campaign mobilisers and security personnel during the election, only to sideline them after victory. According to him, their frustration grew because some appointees who contributed little to the party’s electoral success benefited while grassroots campaign workers struggled. “As a leader and someone who actually deployed some of these boys for electoral politics, I’m aware of their plight,” he stated, calling for an end to what he termed “disgraceful self-sabotage”. Mr Agbey said it was particularly troubling that the party would need the same activists to strengthen its grassroots structures and mobilise support ahead of the 2028 general elections. He warned that overlooking their grievances could weaken that support as political activity builds towards the NDC’s internal elections. “The strength of the NDC always lies in the ability to protect its people from the savagery of capitalism. Sadly, the umbrella cannot protect its own,” he said. Mr Agbey also alleged that some task force members had been promised national security jobs that had not materialised. The statement did not identify who made those promises or provide details of the proposed placements. He urged party leaders and government appointees to address the complaints, warning against underestimating the resentment arising from unmet expectations. “Let those who have ears listen to the cries of the NDC electoral task force,” he said.

title: Robinhood picks DIFC for Middle East debut and targets 2027 launch
body: US financial services platform Robinhood is expanding to the Middle East, with the Dubai International Financial Centre becoming its regional headquarters. The company said on Thursday it had been approved by the Dubai Financial Services Authority to offer trading and custody services across all 10 asset classes approved by the regulator, including equities, cryptocurrencies, exchange-traded funds and investment tokens. “The DIFC is one of the world’s most important financial hubs, and our expansion there brings us closer to building a global platform that enables anyone, anywhere to own the highest quality financial assets,” said Vlad Tenev, chairman and chief executive of Robinhood. Robinhood plans to start offering its products in the region in 2027, giving investors access to a wider range of global financial assets. The company said its Dubai operations will be led by Salah Kaddoura as senior executive officer and president of Robinhood Mena . He will oversee the expansion of the regional team. “From our new home in Dubai’s premier financial hub, we’re looking forward to building Robinhood’s regional presence and expanding access to the global financial ecosystem for a new generation of investors,” Mr Kaddoura said. The move comes as Dubai strengthens its position as a financial centre , attracting international companies seeking access to the region’s growing investor base. The number of companies at DIFC grew at a record pace in the first half of this year, despite uncertainty over the Iran war, as the emirate’s financial hub continued to attract banks, wealth and asset managers, and hedge funds from around the globe. DIFC, one of the fastest-growing onshore financial hubs of the broader Middle East, North Africa and South Asia region, registered 2,318 new companies in the 12 months until the end of June, marking a 30 per cent annual increase, the regulator said in July. Global companies that set up their regional offices at DIFC during the first six months of the year include Allianz Trade Middle East, Arrowpoint Investment Partners, Bank of Canada, Blue Mountain Capital, Citadel, Gordian Capital, ICICI Prudential Asset Management, JP Morgan International Advisors, and Varenne Capital Partners. Arif Amiri, chief executive of the DIFC Authority, said Robinhood’s decision to establish its regional headquarters in Dubai reflected growing demand for technology-driven investment services across the Middle East. “With its proven ability to broaden participation in financial markets, Robinhood is well positioned to contribute to the continued development of the region's investment landscape and to connect a new generation of investors with opportunities across global markets,” he said. DIFC is among the key planks of Dubai's growth ambitions and is aligned with the Dubai Economic Agenda, the initiative known as D33, which aims to double the size of the emirate's economy to Dh32 trillion ($8.71 trillion) over the next decade and establish Dubai among the top three global cities. Dubai is also pursuing a Dh100 billion expansion plan for the second phase of the the financial centre, called DIFC Za'abeel District, which on completion will boost overall capacity to 42,000 companies housing 125,000 professionals across more than 1.5 square kilometres of floor space. Demand for office space continued during the first six months of this year with DIFC Square, which has 600,000 square feet of space, becoming 100 per cent pre-leased before completion.

title: ‘Humanitarian’: Trump Weighs In on Putin Praise Amid Backlash
body:
US President Donald Trump declined to give an unequivocal endorsement of Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian” on Wednesday, Oct. 21, suggesting the description could apply specifically to the Russian leader’s decision to release an American prisoner.
Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump responded to questions about his special envoy Steve Witkoff’s praise of Putin earlier that day.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Trump suggested the characterization could be understood in the context of freeing Stephen Hubbard, whom he described as having expected to remain imprisoned for life.
“But I wouldn’t say anything one way or the other,” Trump added. He also said the US had given nothing in exchange for Hubbard’s release.
The answer stopped short of either broadly endorsing Witkoff’s assessment or rejecting it. Trump tied his response to the individual prisoner’s release, rather than offering a general judgment of Putin’s conduct.
Witkoff made the remarks during a televised meeting with Putin in St. Petersburg, where the two discussed efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
Thanking Putin for releasing Hubbard, the envoy compared the Russian president with Trump and called him a humanitarian.
The comments prompted sharp criticism from Republican lawmakers , who pointed to Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian civilians and the deportation of Ukrainian children.
North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis urged Witkoff to reconsider the description and speak to Ukrainian families whose children had been killed or taken to Russia.
Texas Senator John Cornyn also rejected the characterization, describing Putin as a killer.
Nebraska Congressman Don Bacon called the episode embarrassing.
Vice President JD Vance defended Witkoff, arguing that thanking someone who had just released an American detainee was part of the envoy’s diplomatic work. He said Witkoff’s responsibility was to secure results, regardless of whether others agreed with the sentiment behind his words.
Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher, had been held since 2022 after Russian troops detained him in the Ukrainian city of Izyum.
Russian authorities accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine. His family and legal representatives disputed those allegations, and Washington designated him as wrongfully detained.
He was sentenced to six years and 10 months in prison following a closed trial. Trump said he had asked Putin to release Hubbard during a recent telephone conversation.
Hubbard’s sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, said her brother had believed he would die in prison. She described beatings and starvation during his detention and expressed relief after speaking with him following his release.
The controversy over Witkoff’s language comes amid Republican criticism of the administration’s broader approach to Moscow .
Utah Senator John Curtis warned in an opinion article published on Tuesday, Oct. 20, that sanctions relief, purchases of Russian diesel, and restrictions affecting Ukraine’s military capabilities were strengthening Putin’s position.
“Capitulating to an authoritarian dictator shows weakness and sets back the cause of freedom,” Curtis wrote.
The senator criticized Trump’s decision to suspend additional sanctions and tariffs, arguing that easing economic pressure would benefit Russia while its forces continued their invasion.
He also raised concerns about satellite communications restrictions affecting Ukrainian operations and interruptions in intelligence sharing used to warn of incoming ballistic missiles.
Drawing on his recent visit to Ukraine, Curtis argued that the country had become a strategic partner contributing battlefield innovations and combat intelligence to the US.
He called for continued support for Ukraine’s defense, stronger pressure on Russia’s war economy, and a clear message that invading a sovereign neighbor would not succeed.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Can business save Israel-Australia relations? Ambassador says there is still hope
body: Relations between Israel and Australia have been something of a roller-coaster, with diplomatic tensions, political disagreements, and growing antisemitism threatening a partnership that Israeli Ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman believes still has enormous potential.But Newman, who presented his credentials in February 2026, remains optimistic that the two countries can overcome their differences, and he sees business, innovation, and personal relationships as important parts of the solution.“It's really been like a roller-coaster journey, which has its ups and downs all the time,” Newman shared during a call with The Jerusalem Post ahead of the media outlet's November 19 Australia Summit in Sydney. “It's really upside down.”The event will bring together senior business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs, policymakers, innovators, and decision-makers from Australia, Israel, and beyond for a high-level gathering focused on business, innovation, and collaboration. The summit aims to strengthen relations between Australia and Israel by connecting people and ideas across two countries with strong cultures of entrepreneurship, innovation, and global engagement.Newman said Israel and Australia have always enjoyed “natural, excellent relations.”The countries share similar values, with historical ties dating back to before the founding of the State of Israel, when ANZAC forces fought alongside Jewish forces in the campaign against the Ottoman Empire.However, over the past several years, especially since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre and the ensuing war, there has been a “serious deterioration in relations,” Newman said. That deterioration was amplified by Australia's decision to unilaterally recognize a Palestinian state in the midst of the war.Still, Newman, who arrived in Australia less than a year ago, said that in nearly every meeting, even at the highest levels, he has encountered a stated desire to improve relations.At the beginning of the war against Iran, Australia stood with Israel and the US, with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government providing strong verbal and strategic support. But as the fighting continued and energy prices rose, public sentiment began to shift.Newman said he doesn't believe negative sentiment will last. Although “it's really difficult to assume how things will be when we have a new government in Israel and the war ends, I assume that things will improve dramatically.”One of the core challenges, as he sees it, is Australia's geographical distance from the Middle East. The countries are located more than 12,000 kilometers apart, and Australia, because of its relative isolation, “doesn't really perceive the threats the same way Israel does,” Newman maintained.Other major points of contention include the countries' differing perspectives on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the issue of expansion in the West Bank.Nevertheless, Newman believes trust can be rebuilt and stressed that Israel has both the desire and goodwill to improve the relationship.“It's up to Australia, really,” Newman said. “We say all the time that we must rise above the differences of opinion and the different issues.”Newman believes stronger relations with Israel would also benefit Australia, and he hopes The Jerusalem Post Australia Summit will help showcase those opportunities.“If we take it out of the political realm and we move toward community engagement and economic issues, business ties, things like that, there is wide support in Australia for Israel,” Newman noted. “One of our priorities has been to reach out to communities. We've reached out to Christian communities, Indian-speaking communities, Hindu communities, even Greek communities, and we see a tremendous amount of support within Australia for Israel.”He said there is even a strong Iranian community in Australia that supports Israel and regularly marches in support of the Jewish state outside the Israeli embassy.Beyond community engagement, Newman sees economic cooperation as one of the most promising ways to strengthen the bilateral relationship.“There's a saying that the economy can open the doors of diplomatic ties, and diplomacy can actually open the doors for economics,” Newman explained.To date, more than 150 Israeli companies are active in Australia, and Israel is one of the largest sources of foreign listings on the Australian Securities Exchange. An Israeli economic attaché in Sydney, along with two chambers of commerce, one in Israel and one in Australia, works to strengthen economic ties between the countries. Australia ranks high among Israel's export destinations, according to Newman.He also pointed to Israel's strategic location at the crossroads of East and West, which offers Australia potential connections to distant markets and regions, including Europe and Latin America.Moreover, Israel brings a unique combination of adaptability, innovation, research and development, cutting-edge technology, and resilience.Already, Australia is turning to Israel for expertise in fields such as defense and security, space, agritech, water technologies, and healthtech. Newman pointed to several well-known Israeli companies that have found success in Australia, including Netafim, Elbit, CyberArk, and Monday.com.He also sees considerable opportunities in industries where Israel itself has little direct experience. Australia, for example, is a global leader in mining, an industry in which Israel has limited expertise because it lacks natural resources. But Newman argued that Israeli technology could nevertheless play a significant role in improving mining operations.“When you go into a mine, and you see how many adaptations of technology can assist them, and Israel can be of tremendous benefit, whether it's sensors, whether it's thermal readings, whether it's drones… In just about every field that you talk about, even if it's not an expertise of Israel like mining, Israel can come in with its technology and provide solutions.”The opportunities also run in the other direction.Newman described Australia as an attractive partner because of its world-class research institutions, deep pools of investment capital, vast territory, and skilled workforce.“I would say Australia offers new frontiers, and we can also work with Australia and the Pacific Islands,” Newman said. “We can open up the whole Indo-Pacific region and work together, even in trilateral relationships like Israel, Australia, the Pacific Islands, or Israel, Australia, India.”He described the two countries as “like-minded” and said Israelis have repeatedly told him how easy it is to do business in Australia.However, Newman acknowledged that growing antisemitism in Australia poses another serious challenge to the relationship. Beyond the tragic Bondi Beach massacre last December, which claimed 15 lives, multiple reports have documented a rise in antisemitic incidents across the country.According to the Executive Council of Australian Jewry's report on antisemitism, released at the end of last year, there were 1,654 anti-Jewish incidents recorded in the country between October 1, 2024, and September 30, 2025. Between 2014 and 2023, the average was 342 incidents.“We can't ignore the fact that there are a lot of haters here in Australia,” Newman said. “There's a lot of antisemitism, and so we must work together to stand strong against these haters and give legitimacy to this relationship.”Despite these concerns, Newman believes most Australians recognize Israel as an ally and close friend and would “like to jump over the political issues and move straight towards cooperation. And that's where I think The Jerusalem Post Australia Summit can also play a big role.”The summit aims to bring together potential business partners, entrepreneurs, and innovators from both countries, alongside leading figures in security and geopolitics, to explore new opportunities for cooperation. For Newman, the personal connections that emerge from such gatherings may ultimately prove more important than any formal agreement.“If one gets the phone number and the personal connection, the chemistry with the person, it makes a big difference,” Newman said.“Each company that comes, and doesn't matter at which level, if it's a CEO, president, or just a worker in the company, and identifies the specific areas of cooperation, maps them out, they can work together later,” he added.While the political relationship between Israel and Australia may remain unpredictable, Newman believes the opportunities for cooperation are too significant to ignore. For him, rebuilding ties begins with people willing to look beyond their disagreements and find common ground.“I am always optimistic,” Newman concluded. This article is part of a special series leading up to The Jerusalem Post Australia Summit, taking place in Sydney on November 19. For more information, visit www.jpost.com/australia2026.

title: The outcome of the battle for Donbas — and the war itself — hinges on whether Ukraine can hold Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. How are two former Azov commanders leading the defense?
body: The Ukrainian command is trying to stop the Russian offensive — the decisive push in the battle for Donbas — on the approaches to the Kramatorsk-Sloviansk urban area. To do this, it has created two operational groupings, both led by veterans of the Azov Brigade: the “Center” grouping, tasked with holding Sloviansk, is commanded by Andriy Biletsky (former commander of the 3rd Army Corps), while the Azov grouping guarding the approaches to Kramatorsk is commanded by Denys Prokopenko (former commander of the 12th National Guard Brigade, which was reconstituted after the 2022 capture of its forces in Mariupol in 2022). Biletsky’s troops have already distinguished themselves with a successful offensive: they pushed Russia’s 20th Army back across the Siverskyi Donets north of Sloviansk, and are now trying to drive back the forces advancing on the city from the east and south. Prokopenko’s task is harder: he took up his new post in the midst of a fresh Russian breakthrough between Dobropillia and Kramatorsk. In this sector, Ukrainian forces are dealing with a full-blown crisis — possibly more serious than the one caused by the Russian breakthrough in the same area 14 months ago. Russian troops have already cut the Dobropillia-Kramatorsk road, are storming the first city, and are pushing toward the outskirts of the second. Dobropillia Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces had fully captured Dobropillia and released several videos of Russian assault troops in the city as evidence. Some of the footage shows clear signs of AI processing (a practice that is becoming more common), though other clips appear genuine. Ukrainian forces, meanwhile, have published videos of their own strikes on Russian forces in Dobropillia. Troops advancing from the south have reached the city center, while forces attacking from the east have reached the northern outskirts via the village of Hannivka. A third group is advancing between Dobropillia and the Pokrovsk–Dnipro road, threatening to outflank the entire area from the west. The apparent goal is to drive a wedge between the “Azov” group in Dobropillia and the forces defending the eastern part of the Dnipropetrovsk region, in the area around Mezhova. North of the Pokrovsk–Dnipro road, Russian forces have reached Hulive, while to the south they have captured Serhiivka. The main danger, though, comes from a Russian breakthrough east of Dobropillia. Russian command has moved additional forces there from the eastern part of the Zaporizhzhia region and repeated, on a much larger scale, a maneuver that failed last year: a large grouping has pushed through to the Dobropillia–Kramatorsk road and now threatens to break through to Kramatorsk’s southwestern outskirts. Russian forces have retaken Kucheriv Yar and part of the large village of Zolotyi Kolodiaz — the same settlements where a Ukrainian counterattack in August 2025, reinforced by large forces redeployed from the Sumy region, halted the well-known Dobropillia breakthrough. Both sides have simultaneously published videos meant to prove they control Zolotyi Kolodiaz, so it remains unclear which side holds the village. Russian forces, however, have already managed to get behind its Ukrainian defenders near Petrivka. Russian forces earlier reached Novoandriivka on the road to Druzhkivka farther east, raising a real threat of a breakthrough directly to Kramatorsk’s southeastern outskirts. At the same time, on the opposite flank of the area overseen by Denys Prokopenko’s group — along the front southeast of Kramatorsk — another Russian grouping continues to advance. It is moving around the northern outskirts of Kostiantynivka and Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, heading generally toward Bilokuzminovka. The terrain there is difficult: Bilokuzminovka is home to a park with cliffs dozens of meters high, backed by a ridge of hills. Even so, Ukrainian forces still have reason to fear a Russian breakthrough toward the airport on Kramatorsk’s southern edge. East of Bilokuzminovka, Russian forces have resumed their advance along the Bakhmut–Sloviansk highway, aiming to reach Kramatorsk’s northeastern outskirts. Ukrainian command also faces an additional problem: figuring out the plan behind the Russian offensive in the northern Donbas. Ukraine had previously been confident that Russian forces intended to swing deep around the Kramatorsk–Sloviansk urban area from the west and east, forcing Ukrainian troops to retreat under threat of encirclement while avoiding urban combat. Ukrainian command said the western Russian grouping aimed to reach Barvinkove in the Kharkiv region, while the eastern grouping aimed to reach the confluence of the Oskil and Siverskyi Donets rivers near Izyum. However, it now appears Russian command may have another plan as well (and perhaps not only one): to approach Kramatorsk from several directions at once and begin storming the city itself, whose prewar population was 150,000. In that scenario, the battle for neighboring Sloviansk, whose prewar population exceeded 100,000, would begin at the next stage. Sloviansk and Lyman Over several months, Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi eliminated the threat of a breakthrough by Russia’s 20th Combined Arms Army toward the confluence of the Oskil and Siverskyi Donets rivers near Izyum, as well as Russian attempts to cross the Siverskyi Donets near Sviatohirsk. Andriy Biletsky’s group has finally confirmed, with video evidence, a long-anticipated development: Russia’s 20th Army has abandoned a large area west of the Chornyi Zherebets River and is now trying to organize a defense along its banks between Torske and Zarichne. Ukrainian assault troops are already operating inside Zarichne but have not yet crossed the river. Russian command’s evident task is to defend not only along the river but also the northern flank of the 25th Combined Arms Army, which continues to control the area west of the Chornyi Zherebets all the way to the outskirts of Lyman. This sector matters even more to Russian forces than the 20th Army’s: beyond hopes of capturing Lyman, the 25th Army is meant to support the flank of another Russian grouping operating on the Siverskyi Donets’s southern bank and advancing directly on Sloviansk. For now, the 25th Army is holding its territory despite problems on its northern flank near Zarichne and Yampil, and is even trying to advance into Lyman’s residential areas. Biletsky’s group, meanwhile, is trying to address the Russian advance on the Siverskyi Donets’s southern bank more radically. The commander received reinforcements for this: two brigades that had previously been fighting in the eastern Zaporizhzhia region. Using these forces, Ukraine’s “Center” group launched a counterattack against Russia’s “South” group, which had previously been advancing on Sloviansk from the east. Ukrainian forces tried to retake Rai-Oleksandrivka from Russian assault troops, who had been infiltrating from there into the town of Mykolaivka, 6 kilometers (4 miles) east of Sloviansk, in recent weeks. Ukrainian units appear to have gained a foothold in central Rai-Oleksandrivka, but Russian forces continue to hold the village’s northern outskirts. South of Rai-Oleksandrivka, Ukrainian forces have not yet managed to turn the situation around: Russian troops continue to infiltrate between the Siverskyi Donets–Donbas canal and the Bakhmut–Sloviansk road. Zaporizhzhia region As noted above, Ukrainian command was forced to redeploy two brigades to the Sloviansk area from the Zaporizhzhia region — more precisely, from the junction of the Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. They had previously been part of a Ukrainian corps that had spent several months advancing on the northern flank of Russia’s “East” group, which in turn had been moving along the front toward the central districts of the Zaporizhzhia region. To organize this offensive, Ukrainian command had redeployed the 7th Air Assault Corps from the Dobropillia area back in late spring, a move that weakened Ukrainian defenses around the town. There was no choice at the time: after capturing Huliaipole in the winter, Russia’s “East” group was rapidly advancing toward Orikhiv, threatening to collapse Ukrainian defenses in the western districts of the Zaporizhzhia region and the eastern part of the Dnipropetrovsk region. The 7th Corps’ offensive achieved relatively modest results: the “East” group’s advance on Orikhiv slowed sharply, and Russian command was forced to redeploy forces to its northern flank. However, Ukrainian forces never managed to cut the “East” group’s supply lines or force it to retreat, and Ukrainian command is now being forced to gradually dismantle its strike grouping at the junction of the Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Russian forces have also attempted to storm Orikhiv. So far, only forces from the “Dnipro” group are directly involved, since Ukrainian attacks on the northern flank have delayed the “East” group from reaching Orikhiv from the east. About a month ago, Russian forces captured Novodanylivka south of Orikhiv, as well as the now-famous village of Mala Tokmachka to the east. Airborne forces redeployed to the area from the reserve simultaneously launched an offensive southwest of Orikhiv, reaching Novoandriivka and Novopavlivka. Ukrainian forces have responded with counterattacks. Russian airborne units reportedly may have been pushed out of Novopavlivka, west of Orikhiv, though there is no visual confirmation yet. At the same time, east of Orikhiv, Ukrainian forces again attacked Mala Tokmachka from several directions. Published videos show Russian forces holding only part of the village’s center and its southeastern outskirts, including the area around a penal colony whose ruins have already changed hands many times. The situation around Orikhiv continues to worsen for Ukrainian forces, however: Russia’s “East” group has resumed its offensive on a broad front toward Orikhiv and the Orikhiv–Novomykhailivka road, previously one of the main Ukrainian supply routes in the area. Troops from the “East” group have already infiltrated Omelnyk, north of Mala Tokmachka and 10 kilometers (6 miles) northeast of Orikhiv. Russian forces are advancing not only on Orikhiv itself and its supply routes, but also on Novomykhailivka to the north. So far, there are not many Russian assault troops along the Orikhiv–Novomykhailivka road. Ukrainian forces, however, are busy repelling the “Dnipro” group’s attempted storm of the city and apparently lack the strength to dislodge the Russian troops from their positions. title: Russia replaces its missiles as fast as it fires them, Ukrainian intelligence says. Its drone order this year tops 100,000
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); As of October, Russia has up to 700 ballistic and several thousand cruise missiles in reserve, and its 2026 state order for Geran-type drones and decoys such as the Gerbera exceeded 100,000 units, Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) told NV in figures the outlet published on 20 October. The missile stocks are roughly the same as HUR reported to NV in July, the outlet found. Ukraine enters the heating season facing what it says is a Russian plan to hit 60 infrastructure sites this winter. HUR’s figures suggest Russia has the weapons for it, even after its fall mass strikes . In June, HUR said Russia could fire up to 100 ballistic missiles a month while keeping its stocks steady. Its drone output, meanwhile, is shifting to jets that are harder to shoot down . Russia produces 110 ballistic missiles a month Russia can make more than 200 missiles a month, 110 of them ballistic, HUR said. About 115 of its ballistic missiles are Iskander-Ms, with production of up to 65 a month. A modernized Iskander with a projected range of 550 to 700 km is in development. At the same time, Russia holds up to 400 S-300PM and S-400 air defense missiles adapted to strike ground targets, and makes about 40 a month. Meanwhile, Kinzhal production has been temporarily paused over poor accuracy, and the capacity has gone to conventional ballistic missiles. Most new Kalibrs go into reserve Russia plans to make more than 80 Kh-101 cruise missiles a month and is exceeding that, though defects in releasing them from aircraft have sent some batches back to the factories. Russia has more than 450 Kalibrs and makes about 29 a month. Because Ukrainian air defense downs them effectively, Russia sends most new ones to its strategic reserve and to equip its fleets, HUR said. It also holds more than 600 Oniks anti-ship missiles, upgraded for ground strikes, and more than 120 Zircons. Explore further Ukraine recovers Russia’s undamaged Geran-3 jet kamikaze drone carrying camera and live-link equipment (VIDEO) Russia now assembles 4,000 jet drones a month Russia holds a reserve of about 6,200 Gerans and makes about 10,000 drones a month. Its main production hub is the Alabuga special economic zone in Tatarstan. Since summer, Russia has shifted toward turbojet drones. “The reason is the saturation of Ukraine’s Air Force with mobile fire groups that shoot down low-speed targets en masse,” HUR said. Russia now assembles about 4,000 jet drones a month, mostly Geran-4s and Geran-5s , which fly at 400 to 500 km/h. It also makes about 2,000 cheaper propeller-driven Geran-2s, which HUR said are used to wear down air defense and locate air defense positions. Read also Russia’s jet drones fly near 600 km/h now. Ukraine is building simulators for the 900 km/h ones it expects next Russia turns to 500-km/h Geran-4 jet drones to outrun Kyiv’s cheap interceptors Russia has a plan for Ukraine this winter, Ukraine says: intercepted document reportedly outlines up to 1,000 missiles, drones, and bombs targeting 60 critical infrastructure sites

title: SolGen to seek clarification, partial reconsideration of SC ruling on unprogrammed funds
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Office of Solicitor General (OSG) said on Thursday, October 22, that it will seek clarification and partial reconsideration of the recent Supreme Court’s ruling on unprogrammed appropriations (UAs). “With utmost respect to the Court, the OSG will seek clarification and partial reconsideration of certain aspects of the Decision, particularly the guardrails prescribed for the exercise of budgetary powers,” the OSG said in a statement. “The OSG agrees that safeguards are essential to ensure transparency, accountability, and fiscal discipline in the use of public funds. The complex challenge, however, lies in distinguishing the safeguards that are required by the Constitution from those whose formulation falls within the constitutionally provided powers of Congress and the Executive,” it added. The OSG noted that the 12 separate opinions accompanying the ruling “reflect the complexity of the constitutional questions presented and the differing judicial perspectives on their resolution.” “The OSG will carefully consider these opinions in its further action,” it said. “The OSG remains committed to assisting the Court in ensuring that safeguards governing public expenditure are firmly anchored in the Constitution, while preserving the powers entrusted to the political branches in service of the Filipino people,” the OSG added. In its ruling on Tuesday, October 20, the Supreme Court ruled that the 2024 and 2025 budgets are unconstitutional since Congress increased the president’s proposed national budget through UAs. UAs are standby appropriations that may only be used once specific conditions are met, such as when government revenues exceed targets or when foreign grants and loans are on the table. The Supreme Court did not rule that UAs are unconstitutional but clarified that UAs must be compliant with the following: There should be no lump sums in unprogrammed appropriations. The conditions for using new income and additional earnings from the government’s non-tax revenue incomes should be differentiated from programmed and unprogrammed expenditures. Congress should have sufficient standards in terms of prioritization for spending if there is more than one purpose under unprogrammed appropriations. The provision for the unprogrammed appropriations should be within the national fiscal program plan found in the budget and “consistent with its nature as a narrow contingent appropriation.” During the budget hearing of the Department of Budget and Management in the Senate on Thursday, Budget Secretary Kim De Leon said the DBM is closely working with the OSG to seek clarification before the High Court. De Leon said that there are a lot of issues that may arise from the recent Supreme Court ruling, like unreleased UAs, unobligated allotment, and unpaid obligations from previous years. Play Video The High Court had clarified that there was no need to return the money that had already been spent following the doctrine of operative fact. This means completed programs whose beneficiaries acted in good faith won’t be undone. The doctrine, however, “does not shield authors, proponents, or implementors from criminal, civil, or administrative liability unless the proper tribunals explicitly find that they acted in good faith.” – Rappler.com Must Read 5 practical effects of SC ruling on unprogrammed appropriations

title: Tinubu Commissions Section III Of Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Expressway
body: President Bola Tinubu has commissioned Section III of the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Expressway, covering the Zaria–Kano corridor. The expressway is a major transport route linking Kano with Kaduna and other parts of the country, serving thousands of commuters, traders, commercial drivers and transport operators daily. The completion of the Zaria–Kano section is expected to improve road safety by providing better driving conditions, reducing hazards associated with damaged road surfaces and helping to prevent avoidable accidents and loss of lives. The project is particularly important given the high volume of passenger and commercial traffic along the corridor, which plays a significant role in the movement of people and goods across Northern Nigeria, according to Tinubu, who was represented by the Kano State Governor, Alhaji Abba Yusuf, at the ceremony. Beyond road safety, the improved highway is expected to boost economic activities by facilitating the transportation of agricultural produce, manufactured goods and other commodities between Kano, Kaduna and neighbouring states. As a major commercial hub, Kano stands to benefit from improved access to markets, reduced travel delays and lower vehicle operating costs, creating better opportunities for traders, farmers and businesses, according to a statement by the Director General, Media and Publicity, Government House, Kano, Sunusi Tofa. The statement also noted that the commissioning underscores the Federal Government’s commitment to developing critical infrastructure that strengthens national connectivity, supports commerce and promotes economic growth. The Kano State Government urged motorists to observe speed limits, avoid dangerous overtaking and comply with traffic regulations to ensure that the improved road delivers lasting benefits to road users. The post Tinubu Commissions Section III Of Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Expressway appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Businessman, Animal Rights Activist Elizbarashvili Released Through Plea Deal
body: Tamaz Elizbarashvili, a prominent government-critical animal rights defender and businessman, was released from custody on October 22 after reaching a plea agreement with the Prosecutor’s Office in a case stemming from a confrontation at a Tbilisi restaurant involving staff of the pro-government Imedi TV channel. Under the agreement, Elizbarashvili, 63, was sentenced to nine months in prison, with the sentence suspended for a one-year probation period. He was also fined GEL 50,000 [approximately USD 19,300], according to IPN. Elizbarashvili pleaded guilty at the court hearing, saying: “I understand that what I said was a threat. Of course, I threatened them. I admit to the charge the Prosecutor’s Office brought against me,” media cited him as saying. “The defendant admitted guilt and voluntarily repented of the crime committed,” Goga Kakochashvili, the prosecutor in the case, said . “With the involvement of his lawyers, he wrote a statement and applied to the prosecutor’s office asking for a plea agreement,” which was approved by the agency. Elizbarashvili was initially detained on September 1 on administrative charges of disobeying police, as police first stopped his car and later searched his home as part of the criminal probe into making threats and illegal purchase and possession of firearms. Criminal charges of “making threats” were brought against him on September 3. On September 4, the Prosecutor’s Office released surveillance footage that it said showed Elizbarashvili returning to a restaurant and “presumably” concealing a weapon under his jacket before later “presumably” placing it in his car. The footage showed Elizbarashvili’s right hand hidden under his jacket near his chest, and later depicted his hand released and jacket open as he returned to the scene after walking to and leaning into his car. However, no weapon was visible in the footage. The proceedings also followed Elizbarashvili’s social media posts, including the August 31 Facebook post, where he addressed employees of the Imedi TV channel, saying they had “really crossed the line” during the encounter at a restaurant and demanding an apology by the end of the day. In a subsequent livestream, he said about eight people identifying as Imedi TV employees confronted him over his social media posts, accusing them of pressuring him to apologize. Elizbarashvili said he refused to apologize, left to take his wife home, and returned 25 minutes later to find the group gone. He repeated his demand for an apology during the livestream, warning: “If you don’t apologize, I will find you one by one, make you kneel and [f…] you in the mouth.” Media reports identified up to seven alleged victims in the criminal case. Among them were Shako Kutchashvili, Jaba Khubua, Sandro Gamsakhurdia and Nika Kldiashvili, who reportedly work for the pro-government TV Imedi. title: Zelensky: Russian ‘humanitarians’ launched a pointed attack on Kyiv immediately after talks
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky responded to the Russian military’s strikes on Kyiv overnight on October 22. “Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian ‘humanitarians’ since yesterday evening. They used 21 missiles. Unfortunately, numerous sites across the city have been hit and damaged,” he wrote on social media. Zelensky said the strike came “almost immediately after another round of talks” and that it showed “no real change in [Russia’s] attitude toward everything that is happening.” He called on allies to speed up deliveries of air defense systems to Ukraine and increase sanctions pressure on Moscow. Russian forces struck Kyiv with drones and ballistic missiles overnight on October 22. One person was killed and more than 20 were injured. The Ukrainian military, in turn, used drones to strike several regions of Russia overnight after the talks, including Moscow and the Moscow region. Two people were injured in New Moscow. title: WPL 2026/27: Army Ladies host Hasaacas; Ampem Darkoa face Northern Ladies
body: The first week of the 2026/27 GoldFields Women’s Premier League (WPL) season promises exciting fixtures with all 20 teams ready for battle. Defending champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies, having lost the Champion of Champions title to Hasaacas Ladies last weekend, will look to start their league campaign on a winning note. Charles Anokye’s side will face Northern Ladies in their opening game of the new season in the Northern Zone. Ampem Darkoa will be hoping to defend their title once again. The season kicks off at the Ohene Ameyaw Park on Friday, October 23, when Fosu Royal Ladies host newcomers Ashanti Ladies, with the kickoff set for 9:00am. Dormaa Candy Soccer Ladies will play as the host team against Dreamz Ladies at the Nana Agyeman Badu I Park on Sunday, while Tamale Super Ladies and Prisons Ladies battle at the Yendi Youth Resource Centre. The Bantama Astro Turf will also come in action, hosting the fixture between Supreme Ladies and Women’s Premier Super Cup champions, FC Savannah. In the Southern Zone, newly promoted side Immigration Ladies will square off with LadyStrikers at the La McDan Town Park. Hearts of Oak will rekindle their rivalry with newcomers, Rootz Sistaz at the Sechi Mthodist Astro Turf in Somanya, while the fixture of the weekend will see Army Ladies welcome Hasaacas Ladies to the El-Wak Stadium. Jonina Ladies will host Police Ladies at the Antie Aku Astro Turf before FC Samartex Ladies battle Epiphany Warriors on Sunday at the Nsenkyire Sports Arena.

title: Former DOH chiefs alarmed over proposed cut for health promotion in 2027
body: MANILA, Philippines – Former health secretaries sounded the alarm on the drastic cut to the health promotion budget in the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB) , as it supposedly violates the Universal Health Care (UHC) Law . Under the 2027 GAB , the House of Representatives allocated P275.85 billion for the Department of Health ‘s new appropriations, up from the P263.62 billion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). But the House, in its version, reduced the health promotion budget to P485 million, from the P2.5 billion in the NEP. On Thursday, October 22, Healthy Philippines Alliance warned that the House did not follow Section 30 of the UHC Law, which provides that “the cost of implementing health promotion programs shall be at least one percent (1%) of the DOH’s total budget appropriations.” “A budget cut of this scale undermines the mandate of the UHC Law. It is counterproductive to our goal of achieving a financially sustainable Universal Health Care which is fundamentally guaranteed to every Filipino,” said Dr. Manuel Dayrit, a health secretary during the Arroyo administration. Dayrit urged Congress to treat health promotion as a core investment rather than an expendable cost, as health promotion and disease prevention is the foundation of the UHC. Rappler reached out to Nueva Ecija 1st District Representative Mika Suansing , the House appropriations chairperson, for comment. Her staff said she is already on maternity leave. Rappler also reached out to Bataan 2nd District Representative Albert Garcia, the DOH’s budget sponsor, for comment. “Slashing funding for the prevention of noncommunicable diseases or NCDs will ultimately cost the government far more in secondary care and emergency hospitalizations in the future. Diabetes, heart and kidney disease, and hypertension are overwhelming Filipino families and draining our healthcare system,” said Dr. Jaime Galvez Tan, lead convenor of Healthy Philippines Alliance and health secretary during the Ramos administration. Dr. Esperanza Cabral, another health chief during the Arroyo administration, said the government cannot protect vulnerable communities in a “severely underfunded” health promotion budget. “When the budget for health promotion shrinks to P400 million, Filipino families, especially those from low-income households, lose the support and resources they need to protect them from preventable risks. It strips the poor of their right to services that can save their lives,” she said. The House’s budget amendments review subcommittee proposed budget realignments for the DOH amounting to P28.36 billion. Of the amount, P25 billion was added to the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program, which civil society groups have described as “soft pork.” Must Read Health groups to lawmakers: Increase PhilHealth budget, not MAIFIP funding Other DOH programs with higher funding figures were the Health Facilities Enhancement Program, nationally procured commodities for prevention and control of communicable disease, and operations of DOH regional hospitals. The Senate is still deliberating the 2027 budget proposal. A bicameral conference committee will be convened if there are differences in the versions of the House and Senate, before the proposed spending plan is brought to the President. – Rappler.com

title: OpenAI agents analyze mouse brain data in 32 minutes, a job that would take humans months
body:
OpenAI teamed up with PerturbAI and Scripps Research to deploy thousands of AI agents that analyzed biological data from millions of mouse cells. According to OpenAI , the agents ran on GPT-Rosalind and worked through a whole-brain CRISPR atlas, which maps how gene changes affect different cell types in the mouse brain.
The full analysis took 32 minutes. Each agent took on a single gene perturbation, analyzed how the cells responded, and searched the scientific literature for explanations. The team estimates that doing the same analysis by hand would take anywhere from several months to a year.
Among other findings, the agents turned up unexpected differences between two disease-related genes and a possible link between cholesterol regulation and neurodegeneration. In blind comparisons, human experts preferred the distributed agents' reports over those from a single agent 75 percent of the time. The resulting "Reasoning Atlas" is available on GitHub , and the accompanying paper is out on bioRxiv. Ad
OpenAI says these leads should help researchers decide which mechanisms to test in the lab first. Ad

title: Ministers restate plan for combined force of 13 Type 26 frigates
body: Ministers have restated that a combined force of thirteen Type 26 frigates with Norway is expected to enter service from the late 2020s, with five Type 31 frigates in service by the early 2030s, and that the Type 23 fleet will go through phased retirement, according to an answer given in Parliament. Andrew Rosindell, the Reform UK member for Romford, asked the Secretary of State for Defence whether he would make it his department’s policy to increase the lifespan of the Type 23 frigate fleet. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “As set out in the Defence Investment Plan, the Ministry of Defence will be implementing a phased retirement Type 23 Frigates after decades of proud and faithful service. “The Government is investing in: new autonomous surface vessels; autonomous sub-surface; an amphibious fleet with the Netherlands; future Common Combat Vessels; and delivering a combined force of 13 Type 26 frigates with Norway expected to enter service from the late 2020s; five Type 31 frigates expected to be in service by the early 2030s; and new Fleet Solid Support ships. “To avoid compromising operational security, the Ministry of Defence does not routinely disclose individual out of service dates or specific in-service dates for warships to avoid revealing elements of the Fleet’s long-term schedule. However, the Royal Navy continues to ensure that it has sufficient assets available to deliver operational outputs.” Norway selected the Type 26 this year, ordering at least five ships to replace its Fridtjof Nansen class and signing a strategic partnership with Britain that runs beyond the hulls to joint operations, shared support and common training. Britain is building eight at Govan and Scotstoun, and the thirteen figure counts both navies as one force, which is how the partnership has been presented since the Norwegian decision. The Type 23s are the ships carrying the burden in the meantime. Designed for a sixteen year life in the Cold War, several have served more than thirty years, and the general purpose ships have been leaving as their refits became uneconomic. Westminster and Argyll both went early after surveys found work that could not be justified, and the remaining hulls are the towed array ships that hunt submarines. The post Ministers restate plan for combined force of 13 Type 26 frigates first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Netherlands to provide Ukraine with EUR 26.5M for reconstruction
body:
Mykola Kalashnyk, Ukraine's Minister for Reconstruction, Infrastructure and Transport, announced this on Telegram following a meeting with Dutch Ambassador to Ukraine Roelof van Ees, Ukrinform reports.
"We discussed further cooperation in rebuilding Ukraine's infrastructure, strengthening the resilience of communities, and ensuring the stable operation of the transport sector. An important outcome of the meeting was confirmation that the Ukraine Partnership Facility (UPF) program will continue in 2027, with EUR 26.5 million in funding planned by the Netherlands," the statement said.
According to Kalashnyk, the parties agreed to explore ways to channel this funding into joint Ukrainian-Dutch infrastructure reconstruction and development projects. Priorities include ensuring uninterrupted water and heat supplies and strengthening the energy independence of communities.
The meeting also focused on Kyiv's needs for pumping equipment, generators, and energy storage systems, as well as opportunities for Dutch manufacturers to participate in temporary bridge construction projects.
Another area of cooperation is the development of ties between the ports of Odesa and Rotterdam. Amid continued Russian attacks on Ukraine's port infrastructure, such cooperation is important for maintaining international logistics routes. The minister also proposed that the Netherlands join the Ukraine Transport Support Fund.
As previously reported, the Netherlands has delivered diesel generators, portable generators, power transformers, and insulators to Ukrainian regions, with more than 50 tonnes of energy equipment shipped to the Khmelnytskyi, Poltava, Chernivtsi, Dnipropetrovsk, Chernihiv, and Mykolaiv regions.

title: [Rappler Investigates] High standards for the High Court
body: On Thursday, October 22, the Judicial and Bar Council began public interviews for those vying for the post that will be vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo , who is retiring on November 6. His replacement will be the country’s 28th chief justice (CJ) in a court still packed with Rodrigo Duterte appointees. At present, 12 justices out of 15 were appointed by the former president. You might want to read stories related to the CJ appointment. 5 Supreme Court justices vie to become next chief justice Appellate court justices, SolGen among candidates for next SC justice Incumbent President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s next choices for the Supreme Court (SC) will be his second and third, respectively — replacements for Gesmundo and Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier , who will retire on November 16. If you recall, Marcos’ first appointee was Associate Justice Raul Villanueva in 2025. Justice reporter Jairo Bolledo profiles the candidates competing to replace Javier in this first of a two-part report. Scheduled for CJ interviews on Thursday are Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen , appointed to the High Court in 2012 at age 49, and Associate Justice Benjamin Caguioa , appointed in 2016 when he was 56. Both were hand-picked by former president Benigno Aquino III. Thus far, Leonen is the second youngest justice to be appointed to the SC after Justice Manuel Moran, who joined the High Bench at age 45. Leonen had served as government’s chief peace negotiator with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, carved a name for himself in the field of human rights, was dean of the UP College of Law, and had even weathered an impeachment complaint in 2021. Critics, however, remember the Leonen-penned unanimous SC decision, which said in 2025 that the impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte was unconstitutional owing to a redefinition of the one-year bar rule and violation of due process. If you want to recall the reasons for that ruling, read more here . Of course, critics hit what they described as a “ grossly unfair ” decision that sounded very didactic and which imposed new requirements for impeachment. It fueled perceptions of an interventionist Supreme Court that did not respect separation of powers. More recently, Leonen, along with the majority, voted against a request for a temporary restraining order (TRO) sought by Senator Bato dela Rosa to block an arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity. Caguioa also voted against the TRO, saying in his closing statement: “This case will define the Court. For too long, power has found ways to outrun justice. It has hidden in office, in influence, in violence, and now, in the language of due process. That ends here.” The SC also recently voted unanimously against three petitions filed by supporters of the Vice President challenging the conviction threshold set by the impeachment court. Only 14 votes out of 20 active senator-judges will be required for a conviction of Sara Duterte, the impeachment court ruled. Citing procedural grounds, the High Court junked the petitions, saying they were premature since no final judgment had been rendered and there was lack of legal standing. One of the petitions argued that senators who are still in office should be allowed to vote even if they are in hiding (Bato dela Rosa), detained (Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta), or have medical conditions (Loren Legarda). Their inclusion would have set the voting base at 24 instead of 20 and raised the threshold to 16 for a Duterte conviction. The number 16 would be equivalent to two-thirds of “all the Members of the Senate” as required by the Constitution, the reasoning goes. Nothing stops the petitioners from refiling their petitions but the unanimous decision already sends a strong signal that cannot be ignored. The impeachment trial court should have the final say on the voting threshold, seems to be the underlying message if you read the fine print. Is the Supreme Court totally immune to political winds and oblivious to presidents? Perhaps not. But at a time when standards for choices of elective officials seem to be on the decline, many still look to the SC as a stronghold of justice and fairness to which high standards still apply. Has it lived up to those expectations? Let me know your thoughts. After today’s interviews, the next set of chief justice candidates is scheduled on Monday, October 26, and will feature Associate Justices Rodil Zalameda , Japar Dimaampao , and Jose Midas Marquez .
