title: West Darfur rallies express support for Tasis government
body: The leaders of the Transitional Peace Government and political alliances in Sudan’s West Darfur State have expressed support for the Tasis administration and its change agenda during public rallies in El Geneina, the state capital. They said the participation of citizens, particularly young people and women, reflected what they described as recovery, stability, and popular legitimacy. The Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasis) is an anti-governmental political and military coalition in Sudan formed by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), and 23 other allied political factions, armed movements, trade unions, and civil society groups. The rallies also featured calls for the establishment of a democratic civilian state founded on justice and equality, alongside demands for civilian protection and investigations into alleged violations in Darfur and Kordofan. Tijani Al-Tahir Karshoum, head of the civil administration in West Darfur, said the public turnout demonstrated residents’ support for the Tasis government and its vision of building a new Sudan based on justice and equality. “The rallies reflect a rejection of the old Sudan, which was characterized by injustice, marginalization and the plundering of national resources,” he said. “The demonstrations signal West Darfur’s recovery and will help strengthen security, stability, social cohesion and unity. The change agenda has been shaped by sacrifices and struggle, including the deaths of supporters and injuries to thousands of others.” Al-Tahir condemned attacks on civilians in Darfur and Kordofan, urging the international community to fulfil its responsibility to protect civilians. He also called for the establishment of an international investigative commission to examine alleged violations and hold those responsible accountable. Meanwhile, Ibrahim Fadl, head of the Qimam Alliance, said the rally was a continuation of previous revolutions in Sudan. He described the April 15 revolution as an ongoing movement, saying the large crowds demonstrated continued public support for it. “My alliance supported the Transitional Peace Government and rejects the government which targets civilians with aircraft and chemical weapons,” he said. “De facto Sudanese leader General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan does not represent the Sudanese people at international forums.” In a separate address, Carlo John, finance minister in the Transitional Peace Government, said the participation of young people and women reflected what he described as genuine recovery in West Darfur. “The Tasis Alliance is seeking to establish a new financial and economic system focused on easing the cost-of-living burden, improving access to essential services and providing free education,” he said. “The Tasis government’s economic programme is based on fiscal decentralization, granting regions and local administrations broad powers to manage their finances and resources, including revenue collection.” He said dismantling what he described as the centralized system that had dominated Sudan since 1956 was a key pillar of the change agenda. For his part, Decentralized Governance Minister Sila Musa said the public turnout demonstrated popular support for the Transitional Peace Government, adding that the people were its principal source of backing. Musa also praised the Tasis forces and what he described as their military victories. He called for investigations into alleged crimes he attributed to the Port Sudan-based army, urging cooperation with the government to achieve its objectives and restore education and healthcare services. The post West Darfur rallies express support for Tasis government appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Israeli forces kill disabled Syrian in raid on homes in Deraa
body: Israeli forces shot dead a civilian with disabilities during raids on homes in Syria 's southern governorate of Deraa, state news agency Sana reported on Thursday. Troops fired indiscriminately and snipers were positioned on roofs as the Israeli forces entered the village of Jamlah and searched homes, Sana reported. The man's body was transferred to Deraa National Hospital. A Syrian military official in Deraa told The National an Israeli military convoy entered Jamlah around 12.30am on Thursday. The man killed, Moaz Al Baeer, was on his way to a relative's house when he encountered Israeli forces at the entrance of the village, the official said. “When they stopped him he refused to comply, so they shot him.” The National viewed and verified an image of Mr Al Baeer's body. Israeli forces also shelled the outskirts of Abidin in the western Deraa countryside on Wednesday night. Two shells landed west of the town, with no reports of injuries or damage. Israeli attacks and incursions in Syria have escalated since the ousting of president Bashar Al Assad's regime in December 2024, with further intensification in recent months. Following the regime's fall, Israel declared the 1974 Disengagement Agreement void and moved to take control of the Syrian buffer zone, while also seizing positions beyond it . Israeli forces have continued to violate the agreement through repeated incursions into southern Syria, raids on civilian homes, arrests, land seizures and missile attacks, Sana reported. On Sunday, Syria's Foreign Ministry condemned an increase in Israeli incursions into Quneitra province and the Deraa countryside, alongside more frequent helicopter, reconnaissance and warplane flights over the south. These violations “undermine the prospects for achieving stability and security in the region in general and Syria in particular, and obstruct reconstruction and recovery efforts”, the ministry said in a statement. It called on the international community to halt the incursions and compel Israel to comply with international law and UN resolutions. In early October, the UN said Israel was holding 49 Syrians and had carried out 280 armed incursions into southern Syria in September. Released detainees alleged torture and ill-treatment, including beatings, prolonged forced standing and threats against their families, a statement by UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said.

title: MSI Defense Integrates LIONFISH 20 Weapon Systems on Ex-USCG Cutters for Hellenic Navy
body: Under a recent FMS program, MSI Defense announced it successfully integrated a 20mm LIONFISH weapon systems onto ex-USCG cutters bound for the Hellenic Navy. MSI Defense Solutions press release MSI Defense Solutions LLC (MSI) has completed integration of a next-generation 20mm weapon system onto a former U.S. Coast Guard Cutter being transferred to the Hellenic Navy under a Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program administered by the U.S. Coast Guard. MSI integrated the Leonardo LIONFISH® 20, a remotely operated, stabilized naval weapon system onto the vessel, delivering a modernized, mission-ready capability for transfer to an allied naval partner. The integration scope included structural reinforcement of existing ship components, turret mounting modifications, supporting electronics integration, and enhancements to the command and control station. The LIONFISH® 20 provides a 20mm machine gun with a coaxial sensor suite, daylight camera, infrared sensor, and laser range finder enabling autonomous surveillance, target identification, and precision aiming through a remote-control console. MSI developed and executed comprehensive integration, installation, and testing plans to ensure system performance and platform compatibility. Validation efforts included structural load analysis, recoil force assessments, sea state condition modeling, and vessel stability calculations associated with added system weight. Testing and evaluation activities were conducted OCONUS to verify operational safety and mission readiness prior to delivery. “This program reflects what MSI has been building toward since we began maritime integrations in 2021 — a proven, repeatable capability to modernize legacy naval platforms and deliver mission-ready lethality to allied partners. The technical complexity of integrating a stabilized remote weapon system within the structural and spatial constraints of a transferred vessel is significant, and our team executed with precision. This is the kind of deep integration work that defines MSI’s value in the FMS ecosystem.” — Nguyen Trinh, CEO and President, MSI Defense Solutions Lionfish 20 guns systems fitted aboard two Island-class ships of the Hellenic Navy. MSI Defense Solutions picture. Established Maritime Integration Capability MSI has been executing maritime weapon integrations since 2021, primarily supporting FMS cases involving excess U.S. government assets undergoing modernization prior to transfer to allied naval partners. The company’s experience spans remote weapon station integration, ammunition storage integration, electrical system upgrades, structural reinforcements, and C2 system development all engineered to operate within the spatial and stability constraints of legacy maritime platforms. MSI’s established track record with the Departments of Homeland Security, Navy, and Air Force combined with its expertise in complex system integration under firm fixed-price structures continues to support the successful execution of maritime modernization programs that demand both technical rigor and schedule discipline. MSI Defense Solutions remains focused on delivering intelligent maritime integration solutions that enhance platform lethality, safety, and operational effectiveness including within the tight spatial and structural constraints of legacy and transferred vessel designs. -End- Naval News comments: Four Island-class coastal patrol vessels were inducted into the Hellenic Navy in January 2025 . Leonardo’s LIONFISH remote gun systems are also present aboard the new FDI HN frigates of the Hellenic Navy. The post MSI Defense Integrates LIONFISH 20 Weapon Systems on Ex-USCG Cutters for Hellenic Navy appeared first on Naval News .

title: iNTTA 2026 to link tourism, agribusiness and investment across Ghana
body: The 6th Inter Tourism Expo and Conference (iNTTA 2026) is seeking to strengthen the links between tourism, agribusiness and investment to drive economic growth and create jobs across Ghana. The three-day event, scheduled for October 21 to 23, 2026, at the Ridge Royal Hotel in Cape Coast, will bring together tourism operators, investors, entrepreneurs, financial institutions and other stakeholders to explore business opportunities across the sectors. Executive Chairman of iNTTA and convener of the expo, Emmanuel Treku, said the initiative was designed to move beyond promoting Ghana’s tourism attractions to harnessing the sector as a driver of investment, industrial development and sustainable livelihoods. In a welcome message ahead of the event, he said Ghana’s cultural heritage, coastline, hospitality industry, creative industries and natural resources presented opportunities for enterprise development, capital mobilisation and export growth. The expo is being held under the theme: “The 24-Hour Africa Economy, Tourism, Agribusiness, Digital Sovereignty & AfCFTA Industrial Acceleration.” Mr Treku said the programme would seek to translate discussions into commercial partnerships and develop viable investment proposals that could generate measurable economic benefits. He called for stronger collaboration among the tourism, finance, trade, agriculture, transport, infrastructure, technology and industry sectors, with the private sector playing a key role in implementation. According to him, tourism must be treated as a strategic economic sector capable of supporting Ghana’s 24-hour economy, strengthening local value chains, attracting investment and creating sustainable employment. The programme will extend beyond Cape Coast to Greater Accra and the Savannah Region, with site visits scheduled for October 25 and 26. The Savannah Region engagements, to be hosted by the Yagbonwura, the overlord of Gonja land, are expected to showcase the connections between tourism, culture and commerce. Mr Treku said the expo would also provide opportunities for discussions on tourism infrastructure, access to finance, skills development, destination readiness and digital innovation. He urged investors, tourism operators, traditional authorities, the Ghanaian diaspora and international partners to use the platform to identify viable projects, open markets and establish partnerships that would continue beyond the conference. He said the broader ambition was to position Ghana as an investment destination and make tourism a stronger contributor to economic transformation.

title: Zelensky on Overnight Strike: ‘Russian ‘Humanists’ Launch 21 Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv in 3 Waves’
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia launched three waves of ballistic missile strikes involving 21 missiles against Kyiv after the latest round of negotiations.
In a statement posted on Telegram on Thursday, Zelensky said the strikes caused extensive damage across Kyiv, hitting residential buildings, energy facilities, railway station and metro infrastructure, shopping centers and industrial enterprises. A monastery was also among the damaged sites.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The attack came amid renewed US-led diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine. Russian President Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, where the Kremlin signaled willingness to resume trilateral negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
Witkoff sparked outrage among Republican lawmakers , after calling Putin a “humanitarian” as the Kremlin leader released American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been imprisoned in Russia for more than four years, as Washington sought to revive negotiations to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
“You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian – you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff told Putin during the televised meeting. “I commend you, and I thank you again.”
Republican lawmakers condemned the praise, citing Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, attacks on civilians and deportation of Ukrainian children.
“Since this evening, Russian ‘humanists’ have launched three waves of ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv, using a total of 21 missiles,” Zelensky wrote.
“Unfortunately, there have been numerous hits and significant damage across the city,” he said, adding that emergency services were working at all the affected locations.
Twelve Ukrainian regions came under Russian attack overnight , according to Zelensky. He said 34 people had been wounded in Kyiv and other regions, including five children, while two deaths had been confirmed.
“My condolences go out to their families and loved ones,” he said.
Zelensky added the attack came almost immediately after the latest round of negotiations, arguing that the strikes demonstrated Moscow had not changed its approach to the war.
“Almost immediately following the latest round of negotiations, Russia launched a demonstrative strike,” he wrote. “This indicates that there has been no genuine shift in their attitude toward the unfolding events.”
He said efforts to find a way to end the war must continue, but stressed that negotiations alone would not be enough without pressure on Moscow.
“It remains crucial to continue seeking the right solutions to bring this war to an end,” Zelensky said. “However, when Russian ballistic missiles serve as a response to negotiations, real pressure must be exerted on Russia to compel a different course of action – one that puts an end to the killing.”
He outlined several measures he said were essential to changing Russia’s behavior, including strengthening Ukraine’s air defenses, ensuring the rapid delivery of missiles, developing the capability to destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers and imposing sanctions over the war.
“Strengthening air defense, ensuring the rapid supply of missiles, gaining the capability to destroy ballistic missile launchers, and imposing sanctions for the war – all of this is essential,” Zelensky wrote.
He thanked those who recognize the situation and support Ukraine, emphasizing that the responsibility for the attacks lies with Russia.
“The aggressor deserves to be treated accordingly. Ukraine deserves support. Human lives deserve protection,” Zelensky said.
Russian forces launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv on Oct. 21–22, killing one person and injuring at least 24 others, including four children, according to Ukrainian officials.
The strikes damaged residential and non-residential buildings across six districts, as well as a monastery, a restaurant complex and other civilian infrastructure.
The attack also damaged part of the metro infrastructure on Kyiv’s Southern Bridge, prompting traffic restrictions, and hit an ambulance station in the Pecherskyi district, damaging six emergency vehicles. No medical personnel were injured, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 210 attack drones alongside Iskander-M, S-400, Zircon, and Oniks missiles, with Kyiv as the main target. By 9 a.m. on Thursday, Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or suppressed 181 drones, while Russian weapons struck 32 locations and debris from intercepted drones fell at eight others.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Kongsberg to arm Poland’s K2 tanks and support vehicles in NOK 700m Hyundai Rotem deal
body: Under the deal, Kongsberg will provide its Protector RS4 Remote Weapon Stations (RWS) for the K2 programme in Poland. The work covers three versions of the K2 rather than the tank alone. The RS4 stations will be fitted to the K2 Main Battle Tank (MBT) and the K2 Armored Recovery Vehicle (ARV). The third variant included in the contract is the K2 Combat Engineering Vehicle (CEV). Kongsberg expects to start shipping the first systems for integration into the vehicles in spring 2027. The contract also includes an Integrated Product Support (IPS) package, which covers initial spare parts, training and other support services. For Kongsberg, the order builds on an existing working relationship with the South Korean company. “This contract further strengthens the long-standing cooperation between KONGSBERG and Hyundai Rotem Company and reinforces Kongsberg’s position as a leading supplier of advanced remote weapon systems for international defence programmes,” said Kjetil Reiten Myhra, Executive Vice President, Kongsberg, and President of the Defence Systems division.

title: Russian forces preparing to resume mechanized attacks in southern Ukraine after months-long pause – military
body:
Anastasiia Shevchenko, Deputy Spokesperson for the Operation Task Force South, said this in a comment to an Ukrinform correspondent.
“According to our information, after a months-long pause, the Russians are now preparing to use armored vehicles again in southern Ukraine. Russian forces have completed preparations for mechanized attacks during the autumn period and are moving equipment into areas from which they plan to launch offensive operations,” she said.
Shevchenko noted that the Huliaipole sector is currently the hottest area in the operational zone of the Operation Task Force South, where the Ukrainian Defense Forces are facing one of the largest groupings of Russian invaders, comprising forces from several Russian combined-arms armies.
“On average, 10 to 20 combat engagements are recorded in this sector every day. The enemy is attempting to advance toward the settlements of Rybne, Nove Zaporizhzhia, Rivne, Kosivtseve, Ternuvate, Verkhnia Tersa, Hirke, Charivne, Zaliznychne, Omelnyk, Novoselivka and Yehorivka,” the Deputy Spokesperson said.
According to her, Russian forces have abandoned offensive operations along a broad front and are employing infiltration tactics. In addition, the enemy periodically attempts to conduct assaults with small groups supported by light motor vehicles, including motorcycles and quad bikes.
“This type of transport is maneuverable and fast,” Shevchenko added.
At the same time, she assured that the Russians should not expect to advance unimpeded.
“Our units control the enemy’s logistical routes and systematically detect and strike its equipment and personnel while they are still moving into position,” the Deputy Spokesperson emphasized.
Shevchenko also provided figures on Russian military losses in the operational zone of the Operation Task Force South.
“In terms of figures, since the beginning of October alone, units of the Operation Task Force South have eliminated more than 3,000 occupiers and 1,300 pieces of weapons and military equipment. Thus, the enemy is suffering significant losses in the operational zone of the Operation Task Force South,” she concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 21, Russian invaders attacked the positions of Ukrainian defenders 11 times in the Huliaipole sector. The enemy attempted to advance toward the settlements of Rizdvianka, Dolynka, Hirke and Yehorivka.

title: F1 title race explained: What Kimi Antonelli needs to become champion at the United States Grand Prix
body: A little over two years ago, just after his 18 th birthday, Kimi Antonelli crashed at Monza in his first-ever Formula One practice session. Today, he stands on the brink of the world championship and could become the sport’s youngest title winner in Austin, Texas, this weekend. Five drivers can still beat him on paper, even if most of them are clinging to the faintest of hopes. Six races remain, and all of them are traditional grand prix weekends as Singapore was the last Sprint weekend. Each GP win is worth 25 points, second place is 18, third is 15 and so on down to a single point for finishing 10th. That leaves a maximum of 150 points on the table. If two drivers finish the season level on points, the title goes to the one with more race wins. Teammate George Russell remains Antonelli’s closest challenger, while seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, four-time champion Max Verstappen, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and defending champion Lando Norris are still technically in contention. Here is what each of the six contenders needs to finish the season as world champion. Kimi Antonelli Where he stands: First on 340 points with eight GP wins. What he needs: Antonelli can win the title in Austin this Sunday if he wins the race and Russell finishes ninth or lower, and Hamilton finishes fifth or lower. Victory would take Antonelli to 365 points and nine GP wins this season. Even if Russell subsequently won all five remaining races to draw level on points, Antonelli would still prevail, as he has secured more race wins. If the Italian finishes second or lower in Austin, his next opportunity comes a week later in Mexico City, on November 1. View this post on Instagram George Russell Where he stands: Second on 238 points, 102 points behind. What he needs: Russell’s best-case scenario involves him winning all six remaining races, which would take him to 388 points. Even then, Antonelli would have to score 48 points or fewer across those six races, which is essentially finishing sixth every weekend. Russell began the year as favourite, considering his experience and the brilliance of the car, and things started brightly for the Briton, who won the opening race in Australia. Since then, reliability issues and his own style of driving have seen him usurped by his younger, more daring teammate. Lewis Hamilton Where he stands: Third on 229 points, 111 behind Antonelli. What he needs: If Hamilton wins all six remaining races, he will finish on 379 points. Antonelli would then have to score 38 points or fewer. In Austin, Hamilton would be eliminated from title contention if Antonelli wins and the Brit finishes fifth or lower. He is also out if Antonelli outscores him by 14 points or more. Hamilton’s second year at Ferrari has seen him be more competitive but he has still only won once this season. He would need six wins in a row and a total collapse from the young driver who replaced him at Mercedes for him to take the crown. Realistically, the chase for a record eighth title will have to wait another year. Six winners in 2026. Six still left in the fight. Can anyone hunt down Kimi? 🎯 #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/LwnEKW0ScR — Formula 1 (@F1) October 19, 2026 Max Verstappen Where he stands: Fourth on 221 points, 119 behind. What he needs: If Verstappen wins all the remaining races, he will finish on 371 points. Antonelli would then have to score 30 points or fewer, which is worse than seventh place every weekend. If Antonelli scored exactly 31 points, they would tie on 371 points with eight wins each and second places would settle it. In Austin, if Antonelli wins the race, Verstappen is eliminated from title contention wherever he finishes. There may be little hope for Verstappen. He spent most of the year struggling to get the car to compete and did not win a grand prix until October, in Sepang. Red Bull’s progress over the last few weekends has been exceptional, and the burst of form has dragged him back into the title conversation. Antonelli has admitted it unsettles him. It is a warning for next season, but it has probably come too late for this year. Charles Leclerc Where he stands: Fifth, on 215 points, 125 behind. What he needs: If Leclerc wins all six remaining races, he will finish on 365 points. Antonelli would then have to score 24 points or fewer, which is essentially finishing P8 in every remaining race. Leclerc has virtually no hope of winning the championship and his teammate Hamilton has produced better performances this season. His early exit at Monza, Ferrari’s home race, perfectly demonstrated how the season has drifted away from him. Lando Norris Where he stands: Sixth on 201 points, 139 behind What he needs: If Norris wins all six races, he finishes on 351 points. Antonelli would then have to score 10 points or fewer across six weekends. In Austin, Norris would need to outscore the Italian by at least 15 points just to remain in contention.

title: Aviation Authorities to Put Those in Contact with Ebola Disease on No-Fly List for 21 Days
body: Chinedu Eze The Minister of Aviation ad Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has directed aviation authorities to put anyone in contact with Ebola Virus Disease on no-fly list for 21 days. The Minister in his verified Facebook account stated that he held meeting with the Minister of Health, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, over the virus and how to contain its spread in Nigeria. The Minister said, “This evening (last night), I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge. He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the Aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest). “I have therefore directed the NCAA (Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority) to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development. I have also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports. Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the NCDC (Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention) following regional outbreak alerts earlier. Meanwhile, FAAN had earlier in a statement said it is working with NCDC, Port Health Services, NCAA and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts. The agency stated that the early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats. “FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public,” FAAN said The Authority, therefore urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials and advised the public to rely on verified informationand avoid spreading unconfirmed reports. “FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports,” the statement signed by the Director, Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Henry Agbebire, said.

title: Garmin Revamps and Opens Up Connect Developer API Program
body:
After some 7 months of being ‘closed’ to new entrants, Garmin has re-opened and revamped the Garmin Connect API developer program , focused specifically on 3rd-party platforms that want to receive data files from Garmin devices via Garmin Connect, or send certain types of data to Garmin devices. Things like receiving your completed activities/workouts, sending routes/courses or structured workouts to Garmin devices, receiving general health/wellness data, and so on. All of these leverage the Garmin Connect API today, and have for many years.
Before we get into the details of the new program, Garmin closed it to new applications back in March due to an overwhelming number of inbound applications. With the rise of AI-generated apps, Garmin went from a handful of (mostly legit) applications each week to a tsunami of new AI vibe-coded applications each day. Fun fact: Less than half of all applications that were requesting access even bothered to use it, once granted.
Of course, it’d be easy to blame vibe-coded AI apps for everything, but the reality was Garmin’s process was equally to blame. They treated every inbound request as if it were an enterprise-level company, rather than perhaps just a hobbyist developer or early-stage startup. That meant that everything from business case validation, policy validation, and such was all done at a level far beyond any other wearable in the space. Applications could take weeks to months (easily), compared with sometimes instant access to credentials from other companies like Polar, Wahoo, Suunto, and more. Garmin didn’t differentiate between the credential types: Everyone got the same full-fledged access, whether they really needed it or not.
That changes today, with three distinct tiers that essentially allow an app to ‘grow’ from hobbyist level, to startup level, to full ‘enterprise’ level access with 24×7 support/etc. The first two tiers are free, and greatly expand access to individuals wanting instant access to Garmin’s platform, effectively creating an MCP level of sorts…minus actually creating an MCP.
In short, Garmin Connect now has three different API levels, versions the previous level that required a bunch of paperwork and verifications. These three levels are now:
– Personal: Designed for a single person to have access to their activity and health data via the Connect API – Startup: Designed for organizations that need to support up to 1,000 users, adds more API areas – Enterprise: Everything above, plus more API areas, technical support, and historical data. Oh, and it costs money.
All of this is best shown in the chart below, which I’ve copied from Garmin’s Connect API site , but we’ll keep it here for long-term historical reference. Cause, if we know anything from the past, it’ll probably change again.
The key thing here is that both the Personal and Startup levels get both JSON summaries (which is what that means in this context), as well as full .FIT file with the activity data in it. Though, it does sound like Garmin is annoyingly stripping out some data they consider proprietary, whereas if you upload it manually from your watch/device, that data is there. I’m hoping they’ll change that, partially because it’s dumb, and partially because it just increases the ways things can go wrong and is overly complicated.
Still, I’m glad to see they’re offering the full .FIT file, as anything less would have mostly been useless when you start talking more interesting application ideas. Beyond that, you also get both general Health Data and Women’s Health Data JSON summaries (which is fine in this context, I think).
The process to create a Personal API key takes a few seconds in total.
I just did it again, end to end; maybe 8 seconds?
Meanwhile, stepping up to the ‘Starter’ level adds the Courses & Training API’s. These allow developers to *push* routes/courses to Garmin Connect, which can in turn end up on your device. And the same is true for structured workouts. Think things like Strava and Komoot Routes use this for routes, and TrainingPeaks or Final Surge uses this to send planned workouts. It sounds like approvals for this tier should be virtually instant.
Which then takes us to the ‘Enterprise’ level, which adds the Golf API that does small ball things, as well as, more notably, the Historical Data backfill. This means when someone connects a new account to their app, it’ll allow the user to backfill a predefined amount of historical data, versus just data from that moment forward. Further, it provides technical support and allows for more than 1,000 users.
But of course – there’s a catch. Once you hit that 1,000-user realm, you’re now in ‘pay-for-play’ land. Garmin is joining Whoop in charging a fee here. There’s essentially an initial $1,000 entry fee, which is a credit towards your monthly active user bill. That means as a company you’ll pay on a per-user basis, for “active monthly users” that are connected. That’s a big shift from the current ‘totally free’ realm that’s been the case for Garmin Connect since 2019, when they dropped the previous $5,000 entry fee .
Garmin is essentially saying they’re trying to recoup some of the costs of supporting the platform, while also being able to provide support at this higher tier. There’s also a reality here that many other companies are trying to build full businesses on the backs of Garmin’s platform (e.g. Bevel), and Garmin basically feels like if they want enterprise-level support, they should pay for it.
So what does that ‘monthly active users’ fee cost? Well, that’s to be negotiated on a per-company basis. It sounds like what Strava or Komoot would pay is undoubtedly different than what a smaller company would pay. However, for funsies, you may not know that the DCR Analyzer actually supports the Garmin Connect API today (along with Amazfit, COROS, Hammerhead, Polar, Suunto, Wahoo, Google Health, and Apple Health via HealthFit). So I asked what it’d cost us. We have roughly 20,000 total users, but a much smaller portion of those are monthly active users with Garmin Connections. While I can’t share the exact amount, it’s fair to say it falls within the rough category of ‘pennies on the dollar’.
This brings the next question: when will companies start to pay this? By April 1st, 2027. Between now and then, Garmin will work with existing Garmin Connect API partners to sort out that financial piece. By default, though, all existing partners become ‘Enterprise’ automatically. Further, no existing partner has to pay the $1,000 Enterprise entry fee.
I don’t love the idea of Garmin charging anything to access this data, and I largely feel like this should simply be the cost of doing business in 2026. If not, stick that cost into the marketing budget, because that’s what it is. It’s marketing for Garmin devices. Every single 3rd-party platform that integrates with Garmin is marketing for Garmin. That said, if I put on my DCR Analyzer hat, the cost here is pretty negligible – at least for one company. If a user wants to connect all of these platforms, then perhaps it’s slightly more notable, but even then, it still wouldn’t really matter to the bottom line.
Oh, and for lack of a better place to stick it, the existing Garmin Connect IQ program remains free and unchanged (that’s for widgets/apps/etc. on Garmin devices).
So what does the ‘API’ competitive landscape look like? Well, it depends. There’s no real question here that Garmin provides the most robust API in terms of features (e.g., routes, structured workouts, completed activities, health data, women’s health, etc.). That part honestly isn’t really debatable – it’s factually true. Equally, while platforms like Apple provide free access, they don’t offer a web-based API to push data into Apple Health. Meaning, a partner *has* to develop an iOS app to push/pull it there. That’s why for the DCR Analyzer we use HealthFit as our partner to pull data from Apple Health. The last thing I wanted to do was develop an app simply to get my Apple Fitness data; that solved our need.
Anyways, as for other device platforms – like COROS, Suunto, Wahoo, Polar, Amazfit, etc. – all of them today provide some level of API, but whether or not they provide it for the end-user to do something is heavily mixed. For example, COROS rolled out their MCP access for free for all COROS users. And Suunto announced the same thing last week for some time in the future. Wahoo and Amazfit have programs for companies, but those aren’t really available for individuals. Suunto and Polar also have programs for companies too, and both of those are pretty easy to access. In fact, fun tidbit: Out of all the API partners we implemented for the DCR Analyzer, by far Polar was the fastest and easiest to do.
Historically speaking, Whoop, for example, has charged for more detailed API access (such as the full workout files), while allowing free summary information. As an example, in the case of the DCR Analyzer, that’s not super useful, so we haven’t pursued it. Update: Whoop is no longer charging for API information, at any level, according to the company.
One of the things that companies are trying to avoid is ‘aggregator’ type platforms, such as Terra. Generally speaking, when I talk to platforms/companies in the sports tech realm, most have a strong disdain for Terra. It’s mostly for two reasons. The first is that most companies have felt that Terra consistently misleads their customers into thinking they have legit partnerships with the big platforms, when historically speaking, many of those platforms had never even heard of Terra. Second, Terra wasn’t using proper APIs (e.g. OAuth) for many of the sites they accessed, which makes it a notable security concern for the platforms in question. This 14-month-old community support question best exemplifies the issue in one efficient thread.
We saw this play out recently when Terra got themselves in a pickle as Garmin shut off access to the API for them, until they followed the rules that had been in place for years. Terra responded by asking people to e-mail Garmin’s CEO directly (and provided his e-mail address). Likewise, I got flooded with e-mails as well.
Still, Garmin’s shift here towards charging for API access will set a dangerous precedent for the industry. Especially for a company that bills itself as a (or the?) premium sports hardware provider. On the flip side, there’s simply no ignoring the flood of mostly AI apps that take up resources at Garmin and elsewhere to support. Heck, my inbox is flooded with these apps daily requesting reviews. It sounds like when Garmin shut off access to the API last spring, they were seeing inbound API requests at a daily scale that they’d previously only seen over a period of weeks. Simply put, there’s no good answer.
Ultimately, there’s sorta a few groups of winners and losers here. For hobbyists, this is a huge win. A massive one. This is the first time that Garmin has provided access (and instant access) to their API for individual users to grab and play with their own data without having to deal with manual .FIT file uploads/management. Likewise, those users can easily/instantly get into the ‘Startup’ category and do more things – all for free up to 1,000 users. So for companies trying to test out a theory, it’s all good news there.
Where things get fuzzier is the bigger companies, though of course, 1,000 users is hardly ‘big’. Strava has 200 million users, for context. At least now the gates are back open again, and companies can start working their way through the process accordingly. It sounds like part of the goal here is that by offloading the lower-tier access, they can increase the response time for enterprise tiers, minimizing the delay to get through that paperwork approval pile. Plus, those bigger companies can get proper technical support too.
P.S. – I found an old picture of Garmin’s Connect Developer Summit from 2019 when they first abolished the API fee. Seems appropriate here, even above.

title: SAF, RSF alliance claim contradicting military gains in Blue Nile
body: The Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasis) on Tuesday said it had taken full control of the strategic Al-Birka area and a military camp in Sudan’s Blue Nile region, amid conflicting claims from the Sudanese army and the alliance over the fighting’s outcome. The alliance is an anti-governmental political and military coalition in Sudan formed by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), and 23 other allied political factions, armed movements, trade unions, and civil society groups. In a statement dated 20 October 2026, the Tasis Alliance said its forces had seized several military vehicles, weapons, and ammunition. The alliance also vowed to continue its operations to capture additional positions across the region. Rapid Support Forces (RSF) field commander General Ali Al-Reno, speaking from inside Al- Birka, said his forces had established full control of the area after routing the defending troops and inflicting heavy losses on them. “Al- Birka is the backbone of the Blue Nile region, and my forces intend to advance towards Damazin, the regional capital,” he said. In a separate statement, the media office of the Sudanese army’s Fourth Infantry Division in Damazin said the army had dealt a decisive blow to RSF forces in Al- Birka, in the southern sector of the Blue Nile region. It described the operation as a specialized military action that inflicted heavy casualties and destroyed military equipment. The media office said the operation demonstrated the Sudanese Armed Forces’ readiness to respond decisively to any hostile movements targeting its positions or threatening the security of civilians and their property. Speaking to Radio Tamazuj, SAF General Jamal Al-Shaheed said fighting was ongoing, with clashes erupting in Al- Birka following an attack by RSF forces. “The fighting continued until the following morning, and the army seized six vehicles and combat equipment from the RSF,” he said. Gen. Al-Shaheed also said that, concurrently with the fighting in Al- Birka, the border area of Sali came under what he described as a large-scale attack involving a substantial number of troops. However, he said the Sudanese army and allied forces had repelled the assault. The post SAF, RSF alliance claim contradicting military gains in Blue Nile appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Gulf tour puts spring in Macron's step to tackle protests at home
body: A noticeable shift in mood was apparent during French President Emmanuel Macron's three-day tour of five Gulf states, from his sombre demeanour on arrival in the UAE to an upbeat, combative tone in Doha. Walking past the Emirati national guard at Abu Dhabi airport on Monday with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed, Mr Macron looked stern, his brow furrowed and his steps deliberate. The next day, after his plane landed in Doha flanked by Rafale jets, he greeted Qatar's ambassador to France, Sheikh Ali bin Jassim, with a hearty handshake. “How's the family?” Mr Macron asked the ambassador with a smile, before winking, as he often does, at the journalists watching from the sidelines. Such highly choreographed moments in international diplomacy are difficult to compare, but the change in demeanour reflected a broader shift that took place between Mr Macron’s departure from Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and his arrival in Doha a few hours later. By then, the key deliverable of his trip to the Gulf, which also included stops in Kuwait, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, had been announced. In the words of his advisers, France had secured in-kind compensation for its role as a reliable security ally to Gulf states, in the form of LNG shipments from Qatar and diesel sales from Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the UAE, equivalent to 10 per cent of French consumption. Regain control “When you have shown that you are there during difficult times, it is easier to gain visibility,” Mr Macron told reporters before departing Doha on Wednesday. The energy announcements were aimed at a domestic audience as France grapples with violent social unrest, fuelled in part by high energy prices following Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz . “I’ve had partners who understood that, as clients – as consumers – we have a need for this,” Mr Macron said. The Gulf gave Mr Macron a platform to regain control of the narrative at home. The President made it clear that he considered this exchange of services with Gulf states a political victory. “It was important for us,” he said. He also confirmed that defence co-operation had been high on the agenda, with an “important inter-governmental agreement” signed with the UAE to develop a joint strategy on the next generation of Dassault Rafale jets alongside deals with Qatar to upgrade its own Rafale jets. The last leg of the trip, to Saudi Arabia , was kept under wraps until his plane had departed Doha, most likely because of security concerns following Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s airport and critical infrastructure. The French presidency had adopted a similar communications strategy when Mr Macron travelled to Syria in July. An hour-long meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman secured further commitments to supply diesel to France for “as many months as necessary”, the Elysee Palace said. Ahead of the trip, Mr Macron's advisers had brushed aside persistent questions from journalists asking why Saudi Arabia was not included in the trip. There was no need, they argued, pointing to Prince Mohammed travelling to Paris in August. But such reasoning appeared unconvincing, given that the tour aimed primarily to secure oil and gas guarantees from Gulf states and accelerate investment in alternative export routes that bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Just before heading to the airport to fly to Riyadh, Mr Macron emerged from the Rosewood hotel in Lusail, Qatar, after taking questions from the press. He declined to answer questions about a hypothetical visit to Saudi Arabia. Support to Saudi Arabia Yet he appeared keen to highlight French military support to the kingdom, asking The National to repeat a question that had been drowned out by the media pack. The question referred to the UK announcing on Tuesday that it would send Typhoon jets to Saudi Arabia and asked for clarification about French support. “I think it is important for talks with the Houthis to resume and, obviously, for tensions to ease, because that would contribute to the same objective,” Mr Macron said. “Saudi Arabia has a very important pipeline that runs from the Arabian Gulf to the Red Sea, terminating at Yanbu. Several facilities have been destroyed by Houthi strikes. We have offered to help rehabilitate the site and, above all, secure it. For the past eight days, we have had personnel and capabilities deployed there.” This means French military support has been in Saudi Arabia since October 13. Mr Macron had said on September 24 that France would dispatch soldiers , radars and air defence systems to Saudi Arabia to protect the strategic Red Sea port of Yanbu. Contradictory information had since come out from the Foreign Ministry and the Elysee Palace about whether the mission had begun. The Defence Ministry has declined to give operational details. In March, France sent air defence systems to the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar. Yet despite the strength of France’s ties with Gulf states, its influence over continuing Iran-US negotiations remains limited. Questioned by a Qatari broadcaster on whether he had come with a concrete mediation proposal on the table in his meeting with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim, Mr Macron did not answer directly. Qatari mediation Instead, he pointed to the French-British initiative to station an international naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative has remained stalled since its announcement in April, as it requires a negotiated political solution to a conflict from which Europeans have been excluded. The French President said he had discussed “details and developments extensively” with Doha, and that “the coming hours and days would allow us to receive a response, particularly from Iran”. For a country that punches above its diplomatic weight and is grappling with a mounting debt crisis, France makes a point of keeping up appearances abroad. Unlike many other European presidents who travel with their entire delegations on a single plane, Mr Macron travels with three aircraft: an Airbus A330-200 for him, his ministers and senior members of his delegation, including chief executives; an Airbus A330 MRTT for more junior members of his delegation and journalists; and a Dassault Falcon for the handful of pool reporters with access to some restricted meetings. The National was part of the second group. Mr Macron took nearly a dozen questions from reporters in Doha, devoting the first half to the Middle East before switching to the French crisis. He had not spoken publicly about the violent protests that have shaken France for weeks since addressing the nation on Sunday night, before leaving for Kuwait, the first stop of his Gulf tour. His harshest words were for US President Donald Trump , who has blamed migrants for the protests. Mr Macron described his comments as “stupid”. “Does Mr Trump not like France?” Mr Macron was asked. “One cannot help but notice,” he said. “When I see leaders that are campaigning in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic and sometimes with credulity pick up AI content or relay what some spheres want to make believe is happening in France, they’re campaigning on our back, so we don’t need that.” With these comments, Mr Macron also appeared to be referring to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose relations with France have soured since Paris recognised Palestinian statehood alongside 10 other countries last year. The episode is a reminder that foreign policy – from relations with Israel, to the US and the Gulf – is playing an increasingly important role in French politics. What remains to be seen is whether the French public appreciates Mr Macron’s diplomatic efforts. Critics accused him of appearing disconnected from reality by pressing ahead with his Gulf tour despite the worsening situation in France. Mr Macron said he had no regrets. “What we are doing here is important for our citizens, so I decided to maintain it,” he said. More protests are planned for Saturday.

title: EU looks for someone to lead talks with Putin, with Finnish President Alexander Stubb among candidates, Politico reports
body: European Union officials are searching for someone to represent Europe’s position in negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Politico reported that discussion of candidates intensified after U.S. presidential special envoy Steve Witkoff met with Putin in St. Petersburg on October 21. “President Putin disregards the European Union as an authority,” Czech President Petr Pavel said in an interview with the Axel Springer Global Reporters’ Network, of which Politico is a part. “He doesn’t want to talk to [European Commission President] Ursula von der Leyen, he doesn’t talk to [the head of European diplomacy] Kaja Kallas. He stopped talking to other European leaders, including [French President] Emmanuel Macron,” he said. Pavel said the EU needs to “identify a person or a group of people who would speak for Europe.” These don’t necessarily have to be representatives of EU or NATO leadership, he said, but “simply leaders who would be given a mandate by the others to negotiate.” Finnish President Alexander Stubb is among those being considered as a potential lead negotiator for the EU. European diplomatic sources told Politico that Stubb has “the best relationship with Trump among EU leaders” cited Finland’s long border with Russia as another factor. Stubb took part in a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Witkoff in Oslo that preceded Witkoff’s trip to Russia, according to Politico. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also attended that meeting and is being considered as a key negotiator for the EU, Politico said. Another candidate is European Council President António Costa. Sources told Politico that it is critical for the EU to take part in the negotiations as a single entity rather than through the leaders of its individual member states. Russian President Vladimir Putin previously said that former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder, with whom he maintains a friendly relationship, could serve as a negotiator. WSJ sources reported a few days ago that Putin had proposed a trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S. and China to discuss ending the war between Russia and Ukraine. The outlet said EU representatives were not going to be invited to the meeting. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at reports@meduza.io . To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter .

title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2
body:
You can get a copy of the exploit from the ns2jb repository.
ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak for the Switch 2. It allows running arbitrary native code as any ordinary sysmodule, and as the built-in fs sysmodule. This lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO. To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2.
To demonstrate the capabilities of this jailbreak, Codex modded a Switch 2 exclusive, Mario Kart World. Thanks to my friends in Dabney House who helped me choose characters to add and playtest the game.
The very first thing I did was set up a harness around the Switch 1 and 2 so Codex could, ideally, jailbreak the Switch 2 without me:
Edit: Many people have been asking me if I actually used this prompt. No, it’s just a silly caption. I set a /goal for userland code execution, but that didn’t succeed. The jailbreak itself took substantial effort for ~2 weeks. The Mario Kart World, however, was entirely vibecoded in a day, and was just for fun.
The JetKVMs allow Codex to send controller inputs to the Switches over USB and receive video output over HDMI. We also need a way to press the power button—when the Switch 2 crashes, it needs a button press to restart.
That’s what the Bluetooth light switch flicker from Amazon is for. When the lever comes down, it presses the power button. Once the power button is fully pressed, the rest of the lever’s torque lifts the mechanism.
WebKit is a popular target for console jailbreaks, so it’s unsurprising that Codex has picked it for initial code execution.
It claims to have “native control-flow hijack” by taking advantage of a WebKit n-day loaded via a custom Wi-Fi captive portal.
We’d like to get code execution in microkernel services (or “sysmodules” on the Switch), so we can run homebrew, mod games, download saves, etc. Unfortunately, this approach of replacing one JavaScript function object with another doesn’t generalize beyond existing functions—we’d need a new way to make arbitrary IPC calls. That looks difficult.
Codex has reset the goal to complete these steps. It’s a side bet; it may succeed 1 , but let’s be real: the accessibility of WebKit and the Nintendo BBP reward have probably incentivized many before me to look here 2 .
While that runs, let’s explore other options.
My idea was to target Switch 1 games, for two reasons:
Maybe we can still get the upsides of the browser attack surface—orchestrating from JavaScript, using existing n-days, etc—while avoiding the downsides of WebKit mitigations by finding a Switch 1 game that embeds a browser? Something analogous to Electron, but for games, so we could pull off an exploit like this Discord RCE . I can’t disclose this approach’s findings publicly at the moment, but luckily, there are other Switch 1 games.
In particular, I’m interested in SmileBASIC . This is because it’s been pwned before, in smilehax , giving userspace code execution on the 3DS. It’s a giant C++ codebase; surely, if there was an exploitable memory corruption in the BASIC interpreter, there can be another.
Codex found a useful 32-bit integer overflow in the interpreter. When removing items from an array, the interpreter checked position + count <= array.length , but the sum could wrap and become negative. To fill the gap created by removing elements, it’s supposed to shift the remaining elements left, like so:
Say we have a string array R of length 4, and we run REMOVE R,&H60000000,&H3FFFFFFF . position + count wraps to 0x9fffffff . As a negative signed 32-bit integer, it’s less than array.length . The multiplications by 8 also wrap, so we end up performing memmove(backing, backing - 8, 32) , pulling the previous 8 bytes into the array. The command does report an Out of memory error, but it doesn’t matter, since the copy has happened already.
This is useful because the 8 bytes preceding any array in SmileBASIC contain a pointer to the array itself! After the REMOVE , operations on R[0] will treat the array backing as if it were a string.
Since a pointer occupies what would be the length field of R[0] , the string length is enormous, and we can perform reads and writes out of bounds. We read and write to memory by copying to and from substrings of R[0] .
This was a Switch 1 game, so the SmileBASIC agent could work on the exploit on my Switch 1, while the WebKit agent worked on the Switch 2. After some time, it got ROP.
Okay, now we need to compromise a more privileged process. We’re interested in ordinary sysmodules and built-in sysmodules .
Which sysmodule should we pursue? We don’t have their code, so it’s unclear which sysmodules have which privileges.
I gave a few Codex instances the goal of getting sysmodule code execution. Most chose to focus on audio and ldn . I think that’s because audio and ldn have had bugs on the Switch 2. Codex also looked at the NV service , probably because GPU drivers are generally fruitful?
In the meantime, I started looking at the built-in fs sysmodule , because:
The first reason is the most attractive to me. Even if we can’t get a useful jailbreak from fs , we can at least decrypt some of the other sysmodules so Codex can find bugs in them. Other sysmodules like ldr and ro look enticing because they have permission to map executable memory 3 , but they don’t have large attack surfaces, especially from SmileBASIC. We’ll come back to them later.
An IFileSystem handle has an IPC command, GetEntryType . This takes a path string, normalized with Path::Normalize .
Paths containing a parent-directory component with a backslash, like /..\ , call into a helper that allocates a temporary heap buffer of 0x301 bytes. Our path is copied in, but it can be larger than the buffer, causing a buffer overflow. lol
We’ll need a good victim allocation to overflow into. Codex found that the BufferedStorage object allocates a cache entry for its files. If that entry has its dirty bit set, reads and writes to the file follow a pointer to cached data. We can hijack that for arbitrary read/write 4 .
From here, I scanned through memory to find SmileBASIC’s connection object and set the saved PID to 1 . Now, my process has “FullPermission”, meaning I can perform privileged filesystem actions. I dumped internal storage and all ordinary sysmodule code, so Codex could perform offline analysis and I could understand where to go next.
Homebrew and modding typically rely on executing our own native code. Looking at the dumps, the only ordinary sysmodule with permission to map executable code is ro . All these sysmodules have CFI, PAC, and XOM. The interface for the module seems pretty minimal too. It seemed more fruitful to pursue a logic bug than to look for memory corruption in ro directly.
Let’s revisit that first point about fs serving decrypted code. This was useful for dumping the code for ordinary sysmodules. What’s the intended functionality of this interface? Loading programs?
Games and ordinary sysmodules are distributed as Nintendo Content Archives , or NCAs, containing a filesystem image called ExeFS. This contains a file for the main executable, main , and program metadata, main.npdm .
To load a program, the built-in ldr sysmodule asks fs to open ExeFS, and fs replies with an IPC handle to the filesystem. fs also provides two pieces of cryptographic information about the NCA header: the header’s SHA-256 hash and the developer’s signature of that hash. The loader uses this information to perform two signature checks:
Seems cryptographically sound to me, because, in theory:
In practice, however, I’m doubtful of that last claim, because it’s the responsibility of the fs module to ensure the served filesystem matches the NCA header’s filesystem hash, and we have ARW in it.
Indeed, with ARW, we can replace the ExeFS object behind the loader’s IPC handle with our own temporary filesystem. This filesystem still needs to serve a valid developer main.npdm for the loader’s first check, but the executable main itself can be arbitrary. The second check will pass because, by the time the loader opens the filesystem, fs has already submitted the valid NCA header hash and signature for the original filesystem.
These writes must happen after the loader requests the ExeFS filesystem but before fs processes the subsequent file requests. How do we ensure this?
The fs process maintains a list of its IPC connections. When a connection has a new IPC message, fs processes it. Using our arbitrary read/write, we can replace the handle fs waits on for the loader’s IPC connection with an event handle we control from SmileBASIC. That lets us control when fs processes a loader message.
With this, we can execute arbitrary code as any program we have a main.npdm for!
What main.npdm s do we have? Well, all of them. With ARW, we can use to the loader’s fsp-srv connection to copy the NPDM of any ordinary sysmodule or game.
We’ll use this capability to launch our own code using ro ’s NPDM. As mentioned earlier, ro ’s NPDM gives it permission to invoke kernel SVCs like SetProcessMemoryPermission , MapProcessCodeMemory , and MapProcessMemory . In this case, we’ll use MapProcessMemory to create a writeable view of fs ’s existing code. We can also dump fs ’s code by reading this view.
These calls, however, require a KProcess handle to the process. To get a handle to fs , we’ll use our ARW to overwrite IEventNotifier ’s 4-byte handle with 0xffff8001 and then call GetEventHandle from SmileBASIC. The kernel interprets this value to mean “the current process’s handle”, so SmileBASIC gets fs ’s KProcess handle.
We can then send this handle to our custom ro process, who patches fs ’s code.
Arbitrary code execution with any ordinary sysmodule’s permissions seems really powerful. We can investigate hardware without first exploiting each device’s driver. I’m hopeful this will help the homebrew community make progress toward CFW.
In the short term, there are a few next steps I think would be interesting:
For now, I’m excited to see all the upcoming Switch 2 homebrew, emulation, and modding.
It’s not inherently bad to attempt a WebKit exploit. Once we have a bug in a sysmodule we know to be valuable, it might make sense to go back and try to exploit it in WebKit with a data-only attack. This is because WebKit is accessible offline, meaning Nintendo can’t withdraw it like an eShop title. However, at this stage of our research, it’s not worth the cost to our iteration speed. ↩
I wonder if one day Nintendo will map ordinary sysmodules and even game code via encrypted blobs only the kernel or secure monitor can decrypt. Then, no userspace process could observe any code on the system—there can never be RX mappings in userspace. Even the loader module, which starts new processes, would ask a higher exception level to load encrypted blobs it supplies. There’d be tradeoffs, like games being unable to read their own code at runtime. However, Nintendo has already started removing dynamic code features, like the JIT sysmodule. I wonder if this is the direction the Switch is headed. Luckily, that day is not today. ↩
Initially, Codex’s read/write primitive repeated the buffer overflow on the cache object each time it wanted to change the backing buffer pointer. This hurts stability, especially when following many pointers consecutively, since each change is a chance to crash the system. We can use a similar trick to the one here . We can use some overflows to point the first cache entry’s backing buffer pointer at another cache entry’s metadata. Then we can replace the second cache entry’s pointer without risking more overflows. ↩

title: Defence Readiness Bill due before end of this Parliament
body: Legislation giving the government the powers it needs to respond effectively during escalation towards war is being developed and will be brought forward before the end of this Parliament, to be introduced when parliamentary time allows, according to an answer given in Parliament . Damien Egan, the Labour member for Bristol North East, asked whether the Secretary of State plans to introduce new legislation on defence readiness and national resilience during the current legislative session. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “The Government has accepted the 2025 Strategic Defence Review recommendation to introduce a Defence Readiness Bill to ensure the Government has the powers it needs to respond effectively during escalation towards war. Prospective legislation is being developed to be brought forward before the end of this Parliament and will be introduced when parliamentary time allows.” The Strategic Defence Review published in June 2025 recommended the bill as part of its whole-of-society approach, and the powers under discussion cover the things a government would need to do quickly in a crisis: directing industrial production, requisitioning assets, mobilising reserves at scale and moving forces and materiel across the country without the peacetime consents that normally apply. Much of the existing statutory framework dates from the Cold War or earlier. The timetable runs to the end of this Parliament, which gives the department until the next general election. This publication reported in the summer that the government was targeting the later part of the Parliament for the readiness bill , and today’s answer holds to that position while confirming that drafting work is under way. Ministers confirmed in separate answers the same day that government messaging on defence and security will continue to build ahead of Exercise ALBISTON SHADOW, a major United Kingdom home defence exercise, and NATO’s Crisis Management Exercise in spring 2027, with the Security Minister and the Minister for the Armed Forces chairing chief executive threat briefings for critical national infrastructure and industry leaders. A bill of this kind would attract scrutiny from across the House on the balance between emergency powers and ordinary liberties, which is the argument that slowed similar legislation in the past, and parliamentary time grows scarce in the back half of a Parliament. The department has roughly half of this one left to work with. The post Defence Readiness Bill due before end of this Parliament first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Drones attack military plant in Moscow region
body:
The Moscow Times reported this, according to Ukrinform.
The drone attack was reported by Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin. According to him, 630 drones had been heading toward Moscow since the evening, 163 of which were shot down during the attack on the city.
Two people were injured in the attack in the area of the village of Voronovo.
According to Astra, drones attacked the 75 Arsenal military plant in the city of Serpukhov. Footage recorded by eyewitnesses showed an explosion and fire at the facility following the drone strikes.
Residents of Serpukhov also reported in local chat groups that at least three missiles had hit the city.
The 75 Arsenal plant is subordinate to Russia’s Main Missile and Artillery Directorate (GRAU). It manufactures weapons and ammunition and repairs military equipment and armaments, including artillery systems and air defense systems.
As reported by Ukrinform, one person was killed and 24 injured, including four children, in Russia’s ballistic attack on Kyiv overnight on October 22. Fires and damage were reported in six districts of the capital.

title: iNTTA CEO urges government to prioritise tourism as a strategic economic sector
body: The Executive Chairman of the Inter Tourism Expo (iNTTA), Emmanuel Treku, has urged the government to treat tourism as a strategic economic sector capable of driving investment, job creation and national development. He said tourism should go beyond cultural promotion and hospitality to become a key contributor to Ghana’s 24-hour economy and broader industrial development agenda. In a welcome message at the opening ceremony of the 6th Inter Tourism Expo and Conference, on Wednesday, October 21, at the Ridge Royal Hotel in Cape Coast, Mr Treku said the country must take deliberate steps to harness its tourism potential. The expo, held under the theme “The 24-Hour Africa Economy, Tourism, Agribusiness, Digital Sovereignty & AfCFTA Industrial Acceleration”, seeks to connect tourism development with investment opportunities, agribusiness, digital innovation and industrial growth. Mr Treku said Ghana’s heritage, culture, coastline, hospitality industry, creative industries and natural resources offered opportunities for enterprise development, capital mobilisation and sustainable livelihoods. “Our message to Government is clear: tourism must be treated not merely as a cultural and hospitality activity, but as a strategic economic sector that can support the 24-hour economy, strengthen local value chains, attract investment and create sustainable employment,” he said. He called for stronger coordination among the tourism, finance, trade, agriculture, transport, infrastructure, technology and industry sectors, with the private sector playing a key role in implementing policies and investment initiatives. Mr Treku also invited government institutions, development partners, investors, financial institutions, tourism operators and entrepreneurs to use the expo as a platform to develop practical partnerships and identify viable projects. He said discussions at the event would focus on investment facilitation, tourism infrastructure, skills development, access to finance, destination readiness, digital innovation and removing barriers to business growth. Cape Coast, he noted, offered an appropriate setting for the discussions because of its historical significance, cultural heritage and coastal attractions, which could be leveraged to stimulate local enterprise and attract investment. The programme will also include engagements in Greater Accra and the Savannah Region, where participants are expected to explore the links between tourism, agribusiness and industrial development. Site visits to the Savannah Region are scheduled for October 25 and 26, with activities to be hosted by the Yagbonwura, the overlord of Gonja land. Mr Treku said the expo’s ambition was to establish lasting partnerships that would translate Ghana’s tourism potential into tangible economic opportunities. The 6th iNTTA is expected to bring together tourism stakeholders, business leaders, traditional authorities and international partners to explore opportunities for sustainable tourism development and economic cooperation.

title: Abu Dhabi's M42 launches AI platform to give doctors more time with patients
body: Abu Dhabi tech-enabled healthcare company M42 has launched Ossi, an AI platform designed to help with administration and give doctors more time with patients. The platform, announced at the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit, will be available at seven M42 centres in the UAE and Bahrain, and is estimated to help doctors spend up to 60 per cent more time with patients. Kareem Shahin, M42’s chief executive of Digital Health Solutions Platform and group chief digital officer, told The National that Ossi, launched in partnership with Microsoft, is “an AI platform that has been built by and for people here in Abu Dhabi”. It works alongside electronic medical record systems, bringing together AI agents, voice recognition and healthcare-focused large language models to support physicians before, during and after a consultation. “Before the patient arrives, the doctor can open Ossi, where the Patient Summary Agent provides a summary of the patient’s historical details and all of their medical details,” Mr Shahin said. “So during the patient appointment there is more time between the physician and the patient, and they are focused on the patient and their needs rather than checking all of the medical summaries. “Using AI to summarise medical history leaves nothing missed, so that the physician will see everything as per the most recent data, such as medications, lab results, radiology, and all of the recent appointments that the patient has had. The future of health care “It’s a cloud-based AI solution, and we’ve started implementing it across the network. We’re looking through the strategic partnership with Microsoft to host Ossi on Microsoft Azure cloud and take it globally, with many clients and many countries capitalising on the reachability of Microsoft worldwide.” The name Ossi comes from the ossicle bones in the human ear, which help to amplify and refine sound. “It listens to Arabic and English, and now we’re working even with our international partners to translate it into understanding Greek and other languages,” he said. Mr Shahin said that during the consultation with the patient, another of Ossi's AI agents listens in. “While the physician is interacting with the patient, the Scribing Agent listens to the consultation and transforms the conversation into a structured clinical note for the physician to review,” he said. “The physician can then use the Chat Agent to ask questions about the patient’s medical information and identify best practice based on available evidence and clinical guidelines. “Finally, the Coding Agent analyses the clinical documentation and suggests relevant medical codes, supporting the physician and coding workflow.” Together, the four agents work to provide AI assistance across the consultation, while keeping the physician at the centre of clinical decision-making. Working with instead of replacing hospital records Mr Shahin said that Ossi is designed to sit alongside, rather than replace, a hospital’s electronic medical records (EMR). “It doesn’t interrupt the EMR,” he said. “It is beside the EMR integrated within the doctor’s workflow.” “If a patient is going to see an oncology doctor, usually the doctor spends three to four hours before the patient visit to review the file. With Ossi and AI, this can be reduced to less than 10 to 15 minutes", as the doctor receives “the relevant summary of the file”. Mr Shahin described Ossi as part of Abu Dhabi’s wider digital health ecosystem, and M42’s government healthcare platforms were hosted on the UAE’s sovereign cloud, providing privacy for medical information. “We have security measures and we have a very robust security team aligned with the UAE Cyber Security Council, applying all of the guidelines and making sure our systems are updated as per the regulatory standard," he said. “Definitely at the end of the day, who will make the final decision is the doctor himself. But it’s a tool that can help to reduce time, to be more efficient, and not miss anything.” The seven M42 centres where Ossi is available are: Amana UAE; Amana Bahrain; Healthpoint; HealthPlus; Mubadala Health Dubai; Sheikh Sultan bin Zayed Hospital and Imperial College London Diabetes and Endocrine Centre in Abu Dhabi.

title: Voyant Successfully Demonstrates GNSS-denied Navigation for UK MoD
body: Voyant has successfully demonstrated its advanced navigation software to the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD), marking an important step in the development of resilient Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) capabilities for autonomous maritime systems operating in contested environments. Voyant press release In a real-life scenario, this capability would enable autonomous systems to continue navigating when satellite navigation has been lost or deliberately denied, supporting mission completion and the safe recovery of valuable assets. The demonstration took place aboard a Kraken K3 Scout autonomous surface vessel in the demanding littoral waters of the Solent. Operating in real time, Voyant’s software used advanced particle filter algorithms to compare live radar imagery with pre-existing reference maps of the terrain to enable the vessel to determine its position without relying on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS). The trial forms part of a wider MOD initiative to explore resilient technologies capable of supporting military operations in contested and congested GNSS-denied environments. James Norwood, CEO of Voyant, said: “Reliable navigation is fundamental to maritime operations, yet we are entering an era where access to GNSS can no longer be assumed.
