Working alongside Kraken and the Ministry of Defence, we have demonstrated a practical capability that supports the safe and effective deployment of autonomous maritime systems in challenging operational conditions. “The demonstration represents another milestone in the UK’s continued investment in sovereign technologies that strengthen resilience, enhance operational freedom and support the next generation of autonomous defence capabilities.” Modern military operations depend heavily on GNSS, including GPS, to provide PNT information for ships, aircraft, vehicles, missiles and autonomous platforms. However, satellite signals are increasingly vulnerable to jamming, spoofing and disruption, making resilient alternatives an increasingly important operational requirement. The challenge is particularly acute in the littoral environment, where coastlines, changing terrain and dense infrastructure can naturally reduce satellite reception – even before adversaries actively seek to deny it. Maintaining accurate navigation in these complex environments is essential to ensuring autonomous and crewed platforms can continue to operate safely, effectively and with confidence. Voyant’s software addresses this challenge by fusing radar data with advanced probabilistic algorithms to estimate a vessel’s position relative to its surroundings and provide an estimate of the uncertainty that is attributed to this estimate. Rather than relying on satellite signals, the system continually matches real-time sensor observations against known geographic features, providing trustworthy and resilient navigation even when GNSS is unavailable. As autonomous maritime systems become increasingly important across defence and security applications, technologies that enable safe and reliable operation in contested environments will be critical. – End – The post Voyant Successfully Demonstrates GNSS-denied Navigation for UK MoD appeared first on Naval News .

title: Governor Rimbasa decries Nagero, Lakamadi attacks and calls for peace
body: Western Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa has condemned recent attacks on government forces in Nagero County and in the Lakamadi Payam in Mundri East County, warned against further violence, and called on political actors to pursue power through peaceful and democratic means. He said government soldiers returning from Boo Bridge came under six separate ambushes in Bandala, Nagero County, but managed to reach Tambura safely on Monday morning. The governor also condemned an attack on a government outpost in Lakamadi on Tuesday, reportedly involving forces associated with the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM-IO) and the National Salvation Front (NAS). “We don’t want war in Western Equatoria,” Rimbasa said, warning forces loyal to former governor Alfred Futuyo against turning the state into a battleground. He urged political actors seeking leadership to pursue their ambitions through elections, stressing that the people should choose their leaders through the ballot rather than through armed conflict. However, Col. Wayi Godwill Edward, the SPLA-IO military spokesperson, in a press release on Tuesday said their position in Bandala, Nagero County, came under attack by SSPDF at 8 a.m. on Monday. “Our position came under a heavy, unprovoked and coordinated offensive by joint forces of the SSPDF, Wildlife Service, and elements designated as the East Africa Regional Force,” the statement reads in part. “The gallant SPLA-IO forces of Sector 6, under the decisive command of Governor Lt. Gen. Alfred Futuyo Karaba, Sector Commander, responded with bravery and valour. After eight hours of fierce combat, from 0800 HRS to 1600 HRS, the enemy was decisively defeated and repulsed towards Nagero and Tambura towns.” “The enemy casualties and losses include 15 personnel killed in action, 21 critically wounded in action, and assorted arms and ammunition recovered in good condition. On the SPLA-IO, 2 freedom fighters were martyred and 1 sustained minor injury,” the statement added. Radio Tamazuj could not independently verify the claims. Western Equatoria State Minister of Information and Communication Noah Issah Philip said some roads remain inaccessible following the recent security incidents, although residents in other areas continue with their normal activities. According to information from local authorities, the road linking Tambura and Nagero has reportedly remained unused since Tuesday, with no movement reported along the route on Wednesday. However, the road from Nagero towards areas reported to be accessible remains passable, allowing residents to continue their daily activities. In Mundri, the routes connecting Mundri to Amadi and Lui were reported to be safe, while the road from Amadi to Biti remained accessible. The route from Biti to Lakamadi, however, was reported to be inaccessible following a security incident earlier this week. Minister Issah said further information was needed to establish the security situation along some routes, particularly those leading towards Lakamadi. He reiterated the state government’s commitment to restoring peace and protecting civilians and their property. “The government wanted residents to return to their homes and farms and resume cultivation without fear of threats, harassment or intimidation,” he stated. A community leader in Nagero County who requested anonymity for security reasons described Monday’s security situation as tense following reported clashes between forces loyal to former governor Alfred Futuyo and the SSPDF. “We are not aware if some died, but we know someone died,” he said. “We cannot confirm if many died or were injured.” The source also reported seeing aircraft in the sky and said people were picked up in Tambura. However, the community leader could not establish the circumstances surrounding the reported movement or confirm the identities of those involved. The account reflects continuing uncertainty among residents about the clashes, the reported casualties and the wider security situation in the area. Efforts to reach representatives of the SPLM-IO, NAS and other relevant local authorities for comment on the reported attacks and the security situation were unsuccessful by the time of publication. The circumstances surrounding the reported attacks and the extent of the casualties remain unclear. The incidents have raised concerns about civilian safety, movement along key roads and the ability of communities to continue farming and other livelihood activities. The post Governor Rimbasa decries Nagero, Lakamadi attacks and calls for peace appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: 7 types of Toxic Colleagues at work: know them before they destroy your peace!
body: By Jonathan Kofi Appiah, Human Resource Consultant and Aviation Executive She was receiving pizza and drinks at work. Two colleagues thought they knew the story. They spread a rumour that nearly destroyed her reputation. But there was one thing they didn’t know: the man bringing her food was her biological father! Welcome to the workplace, where some people will help you meet your deadline, some will help you grow, and others will turn your innocent lunch into the biggest office scandal of the year! Let’s be honest. Sometimes, the biggest challenge in your career is not your workload, your boss, or your salary. It is the colleague sitting right next to you. Toxic colleagues can steal your ideas, damage your reputation, undermine your confidence, and make you dread going to work. In this article, I explore seven types of toxic colleagues, drawing on workplace experiences and lessons reflected in the first manuscript of my book, People Management Triangle: Managing Self, Staff, and Boss Effectively. One story reminds us why we must be careful about what we say, what we believe, and what we share. The Bank Teller, the Pizza, and the Rumour that went too far An illustrative story drawn from extracts of the first manuscript of my book, People Management Triangle. In a bank in Ghana, there was a female teller who often spoke about her achievements and the influential people she knew. She would sometimes mention that she knew people who could arrange to bring her lunch at work. Then something interesting began to happen. On several occasions, an elderly man, who appeared wealthy and drove a car, would arrive and hand over pizza and drinks to the security officer to be delivered to the young lady. The visits happened repeatedly. Two female colleagues noticed the pattern. Instead of minding their business or checking the facts, they began connecting the dots—except they were connecting them with imagination rather than evidence! Their conclusion? The teller was allegedly having affairs with bank customers in exchange for gifts. They even pointed to the fact that one of the men bringing her food was married. The story began to spread. Whispers turned into accusations. Speculation became accepted as fact. Before long, the young lady was being labelled a gold digger, and her character was being questioned. Imagine reporting to work every morning, serving customers professionally, and unknowingly becoming the subject of a scandal you never created. But wait. There was one important detail the gossipers did not know. The man was her biological father! The elderly man regularly passed through the area on his way to work. As a caring father, he would buy food and drinks for his daughter and arrange for them to be delivered to her at the bank. That was it. No affair. No secret relationship. No scandal. Just a father taking care of his daughter. Yet, two colleagues had taken an innocent act of parental love and turned it into a damaging workplace rumour. The question is: How many people’s reputations have we damaged simply because we thought we knew their stories? What if the rumour had affected her promotion? What if it had reached senior management or her family? What if it had damaged her marriage prospects or her standing in the community? And when the truth finally emerged, would those who spread the story have been willing to repair the damage? This story captures one of the most dangerous aspects of workplace toxicity: people can become so comfortable discussing other people’s lives that they forget they are dealing with real human beings. It also reminds us that what we see is not always what we think we see. Now, let’s look at seven types of toxic colleagues you may encounter at work. 1. THE GOSSIP: “I’m only telling you because I trust you!” This colleague always has the latest gist. They know who argued with the boss, who is having relationship problems, who is being considered for promotion, and who might lose their job. They may even begin the conversation with, “Please, don’t tell anyone I told you!” But somehow, the information travels across the entire office. The two colleagues in our bank story demonstrate how dangerous gossip can become when people spread assumptions as facts. Today’s gossip can become tomorrow’s accusation and you could be the next victim. How to deal with them: Avoid sharing sensitive personal information. Do not participate in conversations that damage someone’s reputation. Verify information before believing or repeating it. If there is a genuine concern about misconduct, report it through the appropriate channels. Remember: not every story deserves an audience. 2. THE CREDIT THIEF: “We did it!” You developed the idea. You did the research. You stayed late to complete the work. Then comes the presentation. Suddenly, your colleague stands before management and explains how they made everything happen. You are sitting at the back of the room wondering whether you attended the same project meetings! The credit thief is dangerous because they may not openly attack you. Instead, they quietly position themselves to benefit from your hard work. You do the work; they take the glory. Fraud or talent? How to deal with them: Keep records of your contributions. Send clear project updates to relevant stakeholders. Document responsibilities and decisions. Speak confidently about your work without belittling others. Hard work matters, but visibility and accountability matter too. 3. THE TWO-FACED COLLEAGUE: “My friend, you know I support you!” This colleague smiles at you during lunch, praises your ideas in private, and calls you a friend. But when promotion discussions begin, they suddenly question your competence. When you are around, they say, “You deserve that opportunity.” When you are absent, the story changes. Their words build trust, but their actions undermine it. Of course, not everyone who disagrees with you is two-faced. Healthy professional relationships allow disagreement. The problem arises when someone repeatedly pretends to support you while deliberately working against you. How to deal with them: Be friendly without trusting blindly. Judge people by consistent behaviour, not flattering words. Keep important professional discussions documented. Build relationships with people who can disagree with you honestly. You can be professional with everyone without making everyone your confidant. 4. THE PERPETUAL VICTIM: “Everybody is against me!” Nothing is ever their fault. They missed a deadline because nobody reminded them. They made a mistake because their supervisor did not explain properly. They failed to complete a task because the entire team supposedly refused to help. And somehow, you always end up being the villain. Let’s be fair: people face genuine challenges, and some employees are treated unfairly. The problem is a repeated pattern of refusing responsibility while blaming everyone else. How to deal with them: Clarify roles and expectations. Agree on deadlines and responsibilities. Keep records of important decisions. Show empathy without accepting blame for things you did not do. Being supportive does not mean becoming someone’s permanent excuse. 5. THE NEGATIVITY MERCHANT: “Who do you think you are?” You propose a new idea. “It won’t work!” You apply for a promotion. “You think you are better than everyone?” You achieve something meaningful. “You are showing off!” No matter what you do, this colleague finds a reason to discourage you. But here is the interesting part: sometimes, what looks like negativity is legitimate professional caution. A colleague who questions an idea because the numbers do not add up may be protecting the organisation. Someone who constantly belittles your ambition without offering constructive feedback may be protecting their own insecurity. The real question is: Are they challenging your idea to make it better, or attacking your confidence to keep you small? How to deal with them: Listen to constructive criticism. Ask for evidence and practical alternatives. Separate useful feedback from personal attacks. Keep pursuing your goals without becoming arrogant. You do not have to silence every critic. Sometimes, you simply need to distinguish a useful warning from unnecessary discouragement. 6. THE SABOTEUR: “I thought you knew!” This colleague knows about an important meeting but conveniently forgets to inform you. They receive a critical update but fail to share it. They withhold information you need to complete your assignment. Then, when things go wrong, they ask, “Why didn’t you do your job?” This is more than an unpleasant attitude. If deliberate and repeated, it can undermine performance, create unnecessary conflict, and damage your professional reputation. They hide the information, watch you struggle, and then blame you for the failure. How to deal with them: Confirm instructions and deadlines in writing. Request access to the information you need. Copy relevant stakeholders on essential updates. Raise repeated patterns of exclusion or information withholding with your manager or HR. Do not fight sabotage with sabotage. Protect yourself through professionalism, evidence, and clear communication. 7. THE JEALOUS COLLEAGUE: “It was just luck!” When you make a mistake, they are the first to notice. When you receive recognition, they suddenly become quiet. If you get promoted, it is favouritism. If you receive an award, it was luck. If management praises your performance, they claim you know how to impress the boss. Some colleagues find it difficult to celebrate another person’s progress because they measure their own worth against everyone else’s success. They are loud when you fail and silent when you win! How to deal with them: Focus on your performance rather than their reactions. Celebrate achievements without arrogance. Avoid unnecessary competition. Do not allow someone else’s resentment to control your confidence. Your colleague’s success does not have to be your failure. There is room for more than one person to shine. THE BIGGER LESSON: Don’t become toxic while fighting toxicity The bank teller’s story brings us back to a simple truth: you can see an event without understanding its meaning. You see someone receiving food and assume they are having an affair. You see someone speaking confidently and assume arrogance. You see a colleague questioning a decision and assume jealousy. Sometimes your interpretation may be correct. Sometimes it may be completely wrong. That is why mature professionals’ separate facts from assumptions. Before spreading a story, ask yourself: Do I know this to be true? Could there be another explanation? Am I helping solve a problem, or simply entertaining myself at someone else’s expense? Would I be comfortable if my own private life were discussed this way? These questions may save someone from unnecessary embarrassment, conflict, or reputational damage. Protect your privacy, but respect other people’s privacy too You do not owe every colleague an explanation of your family, relationships, finances, or personal affairs. Maintain healthy boundaries and share personal information only with people you trust. However, remember this: privacy is not guilt, and silence is not proof of wrongdoing. At the same time, do not label everyone who disagrees with you as toxic. Look for repeated patterns, consider the circumstances, and give people a fair opportunity to explain themselves. When toxic behaviour persists, respond wisely. Set boundaries, document serious incidents, seek appropriate support, and use formal reporting channels where necessary. Your goal is not to defeat everyone in the office. Your goal is to protect your peace, your reputation, your performance, and your integrity. A final thought from People Management Triangle The People Management Triangle emphasises three important leadership relationships: managing yourself, managing your staff, and managing your boss. Before you can manage difficult colleagues effectively, you must first manage yourself; your emotions, your assumptions, your words, and your reactions. You cannot always control what others say about you. But you can control whether you participate in spreading unverified stories about others. You cannot stop everyone from being jealous. But you can choose not to let jealousy dictate your behaviour. And you cannot build a healthy workplace by demanding integrity from everyone else while ignoring it in yourself. The strongest professional is not the person who knows everyone’s secrets. It is the person who can be trusted with them. Jonathan Kofi Appiah is a seasoned aviation executive with over a decade of experience in leadership roles. He is the Team Lead at Heritage Necessity Consult ( www.necessityconsult.com ) and the author of People Management Triangle: Managing Self, Staff and Boss Effectively. Previously, he held key positions at an Airline in Ghana, including Head of Commercial, Senior Manager of Organisational Effectiveness and Business Development, and Deputy Head of Human Resources. Jonathan.appiah@necessityconsult.com joojona@gmail.com

title: We are sorry for the erroneous tax compliance claims – GRA to Say Cheers
body: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has cleared Say Cheers of tax non-compliance and apologised to the business after a review confirmed it had met its tax obligations. The apology follows a previous VAT compliance exercise in September 2026 at the Accra Mall, where GRA officers were quite public in questioning the business’s compliance after reporting that no VAT invoices had been issued since 15th September, despite the business continuing to sell. The inspection was part of a national VAT compliance exercise by the GRA to improve tax collection by encouraging the issuance of VAT invoices. In the first exercise, the Commissioner of the Domestic Tax Revenue Division (DTVD), Dr Martin Kolbil Yamborigya, faulted Say Cheers, describing its invoicing practices as evidence of poor compliance and drawing public attention to the company’s tax status. However, the Authority’s own subsequent checks confirmed that the business had been compliant all along. This prompted the GRA, led by the Deputy Commissioner of Operations, Kwesi Eghan, to go back to Say Cheers to clarify their position in a public statement. Mr Eghan confirmed that the Authority’s e-tax monitoring system had verified the company’s compliance. Speaking to the press during the second visit on 21st October 2026, Mr Eghan said the Authority felt it needed to correct the earlier statement to avoid further damage to the company’s reputation. “We’ve checked the system. We’re very comfortable from our end. We have in fact checked the transactions that have been carried out and it’s absolutely clear that Say Cheers is in compliance, is in fact in compliance,” he said. He attributed the GRA’s initial concerns to miscommunication and a tax calculation error, not non-compliance by the business. Mr Eghan said the Authority revisited Say Cheers after the company invited the GRA to clarify concerns and demonstrate its compliance with tax requirements. He apologised for the earlier communication and acknowledged the need to correct the public record after the concerns attracted attention. “If there has been any miscommunication, we are mature enough to give you apologies and let the general public also understand that Say Cheers is compliant,” he said. He added that fairness in public communication required the Authority to clarify adequate visibility, particularly because the initial concerns were already public. The Say Cheers episode highlights the importance of checking tax records before making any public comment on a company’s compliance, given the potential impact on reputation and customer confidence.

title: [AINews] OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program is 1 of 2 parties to discover PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in core PHP affecting 70% of the web, using GPT-5.6 Sol; coordinated response over 2 months
body: Almost 2 months ago, OpenAI introduced Daybreak for Frontline Defenders , a $1B subsidy for access to Daybreak cyber models and products. That funding came into use almost immediately, as major vulnerabilities in PHP were independently discovered by two parties: Ryan Austin, a researcher at the security firm Calif, as part of the OpenAI “ Patch the Planet ” project in August 2026 using GPT 5.6 Sol: … as well as Wiz, recently acquired into Google Cloud (using Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol, as well as their own tool, Wiz Atlas). All high profile cyber disclosures are at least a little bit of marketing, and the degree to which this was a severely alarming vulnerability on the order of famous ones like log4shell and Heartbleed is up to some debate , but surely the coordinated response across the PHP Ecosystem is the developer community responding in its most ideal form. We should expect to be in for at least a year of finding such critical vulnerabilities; but it is the wrong move to blame the messenger for finding them; rather it is good to know that our critical software is generally getting the biggest security audit it has ever had in human history. AI News for 10/20/2026-10/21/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI Twitter Recap Top Story: PHP2Shell—chronology, core claims, and the complications behind the emergency response What happened Researchers disclosed two PHP-engine memory-corruption vulnerabilities, with demonstrated unauthenticated exploitation against major CMSs and an unusually broad coordinated response. The researchers named the vulnerabilities PHP2Shell and identified them as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Their technical description places the defects in PHP’s internal handling of out-of-memory conditions and fatal errors—not in a WordPress plugin or an application’s authentication logic. They report demonstrations of full remote code execution and “Heartbleed-style” memory disclosure. @sagitz_ The disclosed demonstrations included pre-authentication RCE against WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. The researcher’s announcement separately claims remote memory disclosure against any PHP application. These are researcher-reported exploit results; they should not be silently expanded into a claim that every deployment has an identical, immediately exploitable RCE path. @sagitz_ OpenAI says Calif researchers used its models to discover the flaws, while secondary reporting says Wiz independently found the same bugs. Posts identify GPT-5.6 Sol on the Calif/OpenAI side; a Wiz-affiliated account credits Gemini 4 Argon with discovery, exploit-chain development, detector creation, and patch validation. This is a multi-party discovery story, not evidence that one vendor alone found and fixed the issue. @TheRundownAI , @steipete , @ralucaadapopa OpenAI describes approximately two months of coordinated remediation before disclosure. It says the patch required a major PHP-engine change and coordination among maintainers, researchers, security providers, and governments. A participating researcher confirms work with the PHP Foundation to support and harden the patch. @OpenAI , @itszn13 Cloudflare deployed initial WAF mitigations before the scheduled patch release. Its CTO said rules covered known exploit vectors, were available to all customers including the free tier, and were being updated as early attacks emerged. He explicitly called the rules a stopgap and directed operators to patch at 14:00 UTC . @dok2001 The supplied NSA account advised preparation for an immediate update—and taking systems offline if timely mitigation was not possible. Later OpenAI messaging said upgrades were available; secondary reporting says details leaked before the patch. The supplied material does not establish precisely what leaked, when, or whether the release schedule changed. @NSACyber , @OpenAI , @TheRundownAI Reconstructing the chronology 1. Discovery and private coordination: approximately two months before public disclosure. OpenAI places the work under Patch the Planet and says it led a coalition preparing fixes and protections. Its security researcher Eric Wallace adds that internal teams worked on patching and detection rather than merely disclosing the bug, with confidential advance notification to governments and outside agencies. Greg Brockman reiterates the two-month coordination period. These are participant accounts, not an independently audited incident timeline. @Eric_Wallace_ , @gdb The distinction between program names matters: the posts associate the vulnerability with Patch the Planet , while researchers credit Daybreak model access for enabling security work. Those are related roles—remediation initiative versus access mechanism—not interchangeable descriptions of the same program. @OpenAI , @S1r1u5_ 2. Advance public warnings and a scheduled patch window. Japanese-language posts warned operators to prepare for a 23:00 JST, October 21 release, consistent with Cloudflare’s 14:00 UTC announcement. One correctly emphasized that a PHP-core vulnerability cannot be fixed merely by waiting for plugin developers. Another framed the event as a “15-minute” race after patch publication, but that number was a prediction—not a measured time to weaponization. @ds_nakajima , @expokun 3. Pre-release filtering and observed attack activity. Cloudflare’s post is the strongest firsthand operational evidence in the supplied record: mitigations were already deployed, known vectors were covered, and “early attacks” were appearing. It does not specify successful compromises, request counts, victim counts, payload provenance, or whether the traffic represented original exploit development versus reuse of leaked information. @dok2001 4. Research disclosure, government warning, and patch availability. The researcher’s public thread describes the exploit demonstrations and error-handling root cause. The NSA post calls for urgent preparation and conditional shutdown. OpenAI subsequently says every PHP site can upgrade safely. The supplied set contains no direct PHP Foundation release advisory, exact fixed-version matrix, distribution package identifiers, or patch commit. That missing primary-source layer prevents a reliable “upgrade to version X” instruction. @sagitz_ , @NSACyber , @OpenAI 5. Alleged premature exposure and widespread service disruption. The Rundown reports that details leaked early. A later viral compilation adds approximately 1.5 million servers , attributed to Censys, running versions without a fix; reported shutdowns involving Dutch institutions, government sites elsewhere in Europe, Wikipedia, Archive.org, Asana, GOG, and others; and a 05:55 warning from Japan’s prime minister. None of those individual claims is corroborated by its underlying advisory, measurement, or status page in the supplied material. Nor does the record establish whether each outage was a precaution, a patching interruption, an unrelated failure, or a compromise. @TheRundownAI , @fiveoutofnine SemiAnalysis separately reports that Japan’s prime minister urged PHP operators to patch immediately or temporarily disconnect if they could not. Its account contextualizes that response with an existing Japanese breach wave, rather than establishing that PHP2Shell caused those earlier incidents. @SemiAnalysis_ 6. Exposure-checking assistance followed disclosure. OpenAI published a repository containing a Codex skill intended to guide operators through checking whether their sites were affected. That is an assistance workflow, not a substitute for a vendor advisory, package verification, or evidence that every vulnerable runtime has been replaced. @OpenAI AI’s role: credible evidence, competing credit, and unresolved causality The affirmative case is stronger than a benchmark-only claim. Researchers describe working exploit chains, coordinated patch engineering, detectors, and patch validation. A participating researcher calls PHP2Shell the most consequential vulnerability they have helped discover. OpenAI characterizes it as an example of the “Defender’s Window” : advanced models finding a flaw before attackers, giving defenders time to prepare. Importantly, its wording is “to our knowledge” —not proof that no attacker previously knew the vulnerabilities. @itszn13 , @OpenAI Credit is distributed across humans, models, and infrastructure providers. Calif/OpenAI and Wiz/Gemini appear as separate discovery accounts; PHP maintainers supplied the upstream remediation path; Cloudflare supplied pre-release filtering. Google also advertises Wiz testing in which Gemini 4 Argon found more than twice as many vulnerabilities as baseline models , but the supplied promotional post does not expose the dataset, baselines, budgets, or false-positive accounting. It is not an independent comparative evaluation of PHP2Shell discovery performance. @TheRundownAI , @ralucaadapopa , @Google Researcher-access policy draws both praise and criticism. One researcher credits OpenAI’s Daybreak access with a portfolio of findings spanning PHP, GitLab, Chrome, WordPress, and other targets. Another sharply contrasts OpenAI’s vetted access with Anthropic’s restrictions; the claim that Anthropic contributed “zero value” is that author’s sweeping opinion, not established by the PHP record. A further post criticizes restrictions on Astra access and argues for giving 1,000 vetted researchers the best available models with intensive monitoring, rather than a rigid red/blue distinction. @S1r1u5_ , @migtissera , @S1r1u5_ The countervailing safety rationale appears in reporting that Anthropic delayed broad access to Mythos-class models for four months to strengthen cyber safeguards. That provides context for restricted access, but does not settle whether its implementation helped or hindered this particular remediation effort. @kimmonismus A burst of disclosures is not, by itself, evidence of a burst of AI-caused compromises. The supplied feed mixes defensive discovery, supply-chain attacks, credential theft, precautionary shutdowns, and unrelated vulnerabilities. Ethan Mollick interprets the moment as attack and defense accelerating beyond human response speeds; John Allard describes a capability “phase transition” while acknowledging that many recent findings came from white-hat programs. Both are interpretations of the pattern, not incident-level causal attribution. @emollick , @john__allard Operational complications: patching, shutdowns, and the temptation to “fix everything” The emergency is as much distribution and ownership as discovery. Operators need to locate PHP across managed hosting, containers, appliances, background workers, and old applications; obtain appropriate packages; deploy them; restart or replace affected processes; and verify the running build. One operator describes maintaining numerous PHP/WordPress sites and being exhausted by testing and updates. Another concludes that patch distribution is poorly coordinated. @ostrisai , @jd_pressman WAF deployment reduces immediate exposure but creates a false-confidence risk. Cloudflare’s own statement is narrower than the later advice to put all internet-facing services behind it: known vectors were covered, protections were evolving, and patching remained mandatory. Proxied coverage, alternate ingress paths, and the origin’s exposure must be checked rather than assumed. @dok2001 , @threepointone Shutdown guidance is conditional, not evidence that the entire internet should disconnect. The supplied NSA post recommends taking systems offline when immediate updating is infeasible until full mitigation is possible. For a specific operator, the relevant questions are affected-version status, exposure, available mitigations, and the consequences of continued operation—not the engagement score of an alarming post. @NSACyber “Use the RCE to auto-patch every server” is a proposal, not an authorized remediation plan. Marc Köhlbrugge raises the idea; J. D. Pressman suggests a presidential pardon for a lab or white-hat team attempting it. Unsolicited exploitation still risks unauthorized access, outages, incorrect fixes, destruction of evidence, and cross-jurisdictional liability. A speculative pardon does not provide universal authorization or eliminate civil and foreign legal exposure. @marckohlbrugge , @jd_pressman Update velocity has a supply-chain trade-off. One widely shared post captures the dilemma: updating constantly can expose users to compromised packages, while delaying updates leaves known vulnerabilities open. Pressman argues that endless patching is unsustainable unless the rate of new vulnerabilities and risky releases falls; he also notes that receiving no patch and discovering theft is worse than receiving too many updates. @xeophon , @jd_pressman , @jd_pressman The longer-term alternatives remain open questions. Sarah Guo reports CVEs increasing from roughly 4,000 per month to 15,000 since April , and asks about formal verification, safer distributions, and organizations without red teams. The counts are not independently verified here, and disclosure volume is not a direct measure of successful exploitation. Other posts ask what a full-codebase security sweep would cost and recast the challenge as hardening mundane infrastructure rather than debating only abstract catastrophe. @saranormous , @saranormous , @teortaxesTex , @mimi10v3 For an incident team, the defensible sequence is to obtain the authoritative PHP and distribution advisories, inventory exposed runtimes, apply temporary protections where justified, deploy authenticated fixed packages, verify running processes, and investigate evidence of exploitation separately. Updating closes a vulnerability; it does not establish that credentials or data were never exposed. Public reactions: practical caution versus unsupported escalation The precautionary perspective stresses that interconnected services are fragile and remediation can be costly. Joshua Achiam compares the moment to March 2020 , speculates about internet lockdowns, recommends backing up valued internet material, and suggests printing important records. Pressman says remediation costs exceeded his expectations. These are preparedness judgments—not evidence of impending systemic collapse. Paper copies may help continuity but are not inherently tamperproof logs. @jachiam0 , @jachiam0 , @jachiam0 , @jd_pressman The alarm-skeptical perspective asks for specificity. Alex Johnson argues that warnings about bank accounts being arbitrarily emptied obscure the distinction between unauthorized transfers and scams in which customers authorize payment. He invokes U.S. Electronic Funds Transfer Act protections with timely reporting; those protections are jurisdiction-, account-, and circumstance-dependent, not a universal guarantee. Kelsey Piper separately warns about the psychological cost of living under constant annihilation framing. @AlexH_Johnson , @KelseyTuoc Broad personal-security advice needs to be separated from the PHP fix. Password managers, unique credentials, strong MFA, patching, carrier port-out protections, and U.S.-specific credit or tax identity safeguards can reduce downstream harm. But enabling 2FA does not prevent exploitation of an unauthenticated PHP-engine bug. Likewise, viral advice to avoid all online payments the next day is not supported by a demonstrated scope assessment. @peterwildeford , @StillMare_ The broader threat context is real but not interchangeable with PHP2Shell. SemiAnalysis reports 18 Japanese companies disclosing breaches since September 25, including exposures of approximately 6.6 million Times Car accounts , 11.18 million Burger King Japan app records , and potentially 22.5 million Sourcenext records . It attributes findings about AI-assisted scanning and API attacks to JPCERT/CC. Another post quotes an August 19 advisory concerning AI-assisted tooling against internet-exposed Siemens PLCs. These are separate reported incidents and advisories; neither establishes PHP2Shell as their entry point. @SemiAnalysis_ , @AndrewCurran_ The key unresolved evidence gaps are concrete: exact affected and fixed versions; CVSS vectors; deployment prerequisites; the independent discovery timeline; what leaked before release; successful exploitation versus scanning; validated exposure counts; and the cause and duration of each reported shutdown. The supplied viral incident compilation cannot answer those questions merely by placing PHP, GitLab, LiteLLM, Railway, certificate-authority failures, and government warnings in the same narrative. @fiveoutofnine Other News Flint and Automated Research: Local Coding Models, Smaller Teams and Scientific Workflows Flint launches with broad local-serving support : Recursive released an Apache-2.0 coding MoE with roughly 40B total parameters, 2.5B active parameters and a 262K-token context window. LM Studio says it requires approximately 24GB locally. Recursive positions it as an on-device complement to—not a replacement for—frontier cloud agents ( launch , specifications ). Claimed results : Recursive reports 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89.7% on SWE-bench Pro v2 and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified. These are release claims, not independent replication ( results ). Performance : Advertised short-context speeds exceed 125 tokens/s on a MacBook Pro and 150 tokens/s on RTX Spark. A separate user measured 114–132 output tokens/s on an M5 Max with int4 MLX; that is useful corroboration of speed, not a controlled capability evaluation ( local measurement ). Research contribution : Recursive says its Eureka Machine participated across ideation, implementation and validation, contributing sparse architecture choices, low-bit training and kernels. It claims a 71% size reduction with almost no quality loss and development from scratch in under four months ( method ). Availability : Day-zero integrations span local frameworks and hosted access. vLLM reports 500 tokens/s on one GB200 at 100K context using NVFP4 without speculative decoding; OpenRouter offers free launch access ( vLLM , OpenRouter ). Mirendil claims one-researcher pretraining at scale : Mirendil says its first base model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months for less than $10M in compute, including research experiments and the final run. It discloses unusually broad parameter ranges—100B–500B for Base, 500B–2T for Large and 2T–10T for XL—rather than precise configurations. Independent evaluations, post-training results and API access are still forthcoming, so this is a consequential efficiency claim awaiting external validation ( announcement ). JOLT jointly trains the teacher and student : Perplexity and NVIDIA’s post-training work addresses a weakness in self-distillation: a privileged teacher can exploit shortcuts unavailable to its student. JOLT trains the teacher using outcome rewards while penalizing excessive divergence from the student. The authors report matching GRPO on MATH with 6.5× fewer training tokens; JOLT+, which adds student outcome rewards, beats GRPO across five evaluated benchmarks ( method and results , benchmark summary ). GPT-Rosalind generates testable biological hypotheses : OpenAI reports thousands of agents linking gene-expression results from millions of mouse-brain cells with literature in 32 minutes. One proposed mechanism connects DCTN1 disruption to impaired cholesterol transport; another examines differences between TSC1 and TSC2 disruption in cerebellar neurons. These are hypotheses for experimental follow-up—not demonstrated treatments or validated drug targets ( DCTN1 work , TSC2 follow-up ). Inference Systems: DeepInfer Economics, Native TPU Support and Power-Aware Capacity DeepInfer exposes production scheduling techniques : DeepSeek’s released framework combines speculative decoding, dynamic prefill sizing, decode balancing by request count and KV length, and overlapping CPU scheduling with GPU execution. A particularly reusable idea is adjusting speculative verification length using predicted draft acceptance and measured hardware throughput, making batches more regular instead of allowing slow replicas to determine completion time ( technical analysis ). Cache accounting : A deployment-report summary cites 1.5M input tokens/s per prefill accelerator including cache hits , versus 60K excluding hits at a 96% cache-hit rate; decode is reported at 14K output tokens/s per accelerator. These are materially different throughput quantities ( report summary ). Economics caveat : The same summary describes approximately $38 per accelerator-hour as revenue , not profit. Server, electricity, cooling and staffing costs remain outside that figure. Independent benchmarking remains contested : SemiAnalysis says DeepInfer is absent from InferenceX because essential serving components are missing and reconstructing them would require too many assumptions. Its subsequent profitability comparison drew criticism for mixing hardware generations, peak versus off-peak prices, and revenue versus profit. The criticism is itself an attributed analysis, not a settled replication result; the practical requirement is matched hardware, workload, cache assumptions, SLOs and pricing before comparing economics ( benchmark limitation , comparison critique ). TorchTPU opens a native PyTorch path : Google open-sourced TorchTPU for training and serving through familiar PyTorch tooling. SGLang’s plugin is reportedly powering production inference at Meta and supports several current open models; its custom MegaKernel reaches a claimed 770 decode tokens/s for Muse Spark Open at batch size one on an 8K-input/1K-output workload. vLLM-TorchTPU adds prefix caching, speculative decoding and disaggregated serving ( Google , SGLang , vLLM ). GTC emphasizes deployment speed and power utilization : NVIDIA’s DSX POD packages AI infrastructure into containerized building blocks, with coverage claiming capacity expansion in days rather than months. More concretely, Lambda demonstrated 19 HGX B200 nodes operating within the power budget of 16 using DSX MaxLPS. Treat deployment timelines as product claims and the node result as a proof of concept, not fleet-wide capacity already delivered ( DSX POD , Lambda demonstration ). Evaluation Integrity and Agent Engineering: Measure the Harness, Not Just the Model Medical reasoning exposes completeness–accuracy tradeoffs : Artificial Analysis revised MLCR-AA’s prompts, reference answers and three-model judging panel. Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra tie at 41.7%, with no model exceeding 42% under the combined completeness-and-accuracy requirement. Claude leads completeness; OpenAI leads record-grounded accuracy. Revised scores are not directly comparable with the previous methodology ( results , methodology ). Length confound : A cross-benchmark analysis finds Claude answers approximately 4–6× longer than OpenAI’s; each added claim creates another opportunity to contradict the record. Raw rubric scores, completeness and length-adjusted quality therefore produce different rankings ( comparison ). SWE-bench Multimodal faces an ablation challenge : An independent investigation argues that v2 does not meaningfully require images; a separate researcher highlights running the benchmark without images as the essential sanity check. This is a substantive critique of what the benchmark measures, not proof that its underlying coding tasks lack value ( investigation , ablation discussion ). Evolved harnesses and interfaces improve fixed executors : Two papers strengthen the case for optimizing the environment around agents. OO-Harness : Specialized subclasses, execution-derived design lessons and routing raise AutomationBench from 61.6% to 77.4% with the same Gemini 3.5 Flash executor; Workspace-Bench rises from 25.5% to 39.5% ( paper summary ). Agent S4 : A meta-agent builds tools from trajectories without success labels. The reported open-27B OSWorld V2 result reaches 21.3%, 3.8× the same model with hand-built interfaces; ScienceBoard rises from 41.4% to 58.6%. These are paper-reported system results, not model-only comparisons ( summary ). SuperMimic targets cheaper humanoid training : Researchers report training across 129,514 motions using one GPU for three hours, versus a cited state-of-the-art setup of 128 GPUs for seven days. The mechanism combines a learned, differentiable world-model surrogate with backpropagation through time. The claimed >1,000× GPU-hour reduction concerns this motion-control training setup, not robotics learning generally ( results , mechanism ). Agent Products, Retrieval Models and API Distribution Claude Duet enters research preview : Anthropic opened a waitlist for an Opus-5.5-powered proactive assistant; reported initial access is for U.S. Pro and Max users. Examples include monitoring Slack, preparing questions and making purchases after a request. Stripe describes Link-wallet purchasing and MCP-based invoicing, refunds and revenue analysis. Availability is preview-stage, with no separate pricing disclosed in the supplied posts ( Anthropic executive , access , payments integration ). Retrieval releases target precision and context cost : Cohere launched Rerank 5 in Pro and Fast tiers. Its opt-in Context Focus returns scored passages rather than whole documents, claiming up to 41% lower token consumption while maintaining accuracy. Separately, ParseBench reports NVIDIA’s sub-1B Nemotron 3.5 Parse taking first place across its document-understanding benchmark ( Cohere feature , availability , ParseBench ). Kling 4.0 rollout reaches API access : fal initially announced UI/agent access with API support forthcoming; Kling subsequently announced its official API rollout. Claimed improvements center on complex-motion stability, reference consistency and cinematic control. The later announcement supersedes the earlier “API coming soon” status ( fal launch , API rollout ). Enterprise model access expands while Claude versions its API : OpenAI announced frontier models and Codex workflows coming to Google Cloud Model Garden. Separately, Anthropic’s API version 2026-10-21 removes temperature , top_p and top_k from Messages; new major SDKs default to it, while 2023-06-01 remains supported. Teams upgrading SDKs should explicitly review migration behavior ( Google Cloud distribution , version changes , SDK defaults ). Industry and Governance: Researcher Speech and Public-Benefit Oversight Non-disparagement clauses draw scrutiny : Posts citing BBC reporting allege that Google employment contracts restrict public criticism indefinitely, discouraging discussion of AI safety and military uses. Former employee accounts and researcher commentary describe a chilling effect. These are attributed contractual and workplace claims; the supplied material includes no company response or legal determination ( report excerpts , researcher account ). Anthropic updates benefit governance : Anthropic published its annual Public Benefit Report and appointed experimental physicist and former Harvard science dean Christopher Stubbs to its Long-Term Benefit Trust. This is a governance development, separate from the company’s model evaluations and product launches ( report , trust appointment ). Top tweets (by engagement) NSA: prepare PHP updates; take systems offline if mitigation is impossible — 80,000 OpenAI: coordinated PHP2Shell discovery and remediation — 19,600 OpenAI: Codex skill for checking PHP2Shell exposure — 10,500 NVIDIA: Microduck sim-to-real demonstration — 7,800 Richard Socher: Flint local coding model launch — 7,600 OpenAI: GPT-Rosalind’s neurodegeneration hypothesis — 7,500 Cloudflare CTO: free WAF mitigations are a stopgap—patch PHP — 7,000 Nous Research: Hermes orchestrates robot-training workflow at GTC — 6,400 AI Reddit Recap /r/LocalLlama + /r/localLLM Recap 1. Open-Source Inference Speedups: DeepInfer, EAGLE-4, RTX 3090 BF16 Unlock New from DeepSeek - DeepInfer - (Activity: 441): The image is a screenshot of DeepSeek’s X announcement that DeepInfer, its in-house large-scale inference framework, is now fully open source: image , GitHub repo , X post . DeepSeek describes DeepInfer as the production inference stack behind DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, optimized for high-throughput, low-latency serving to reduce compute cost and energy use; a linked Zhihu source claims a single cluster reaches 155 trillion tokens/day and about $38/card/hour revenue at off-peak pricing. Commenters framed the open-sourcing as unusually aggressive compared with Anthropic, OpenAI, or Meta , with one saying those labs “would never do this.” Some users were still unclear on the practical role of the framework, asking simply: “What do it do?” A linked Zhihu source claims DeepInfer enables high-throughput, low-latency inference for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash , reporting single-cluster throughput of 155 trillion tokens/day and revenue of $38 per card per hour at off-peak pricing: https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/2095560295930508953 . Commenters highlighted this as unusually aggressive public disclosure compared with companies like OpenAI , Anthropic , or Meta . One technical concern was whether DeepInfer is a truly general-purpose inference framework or primarily tuned for DeepSeek’s own model architecture . A commenter noted that flashy framework launches tied to a flagship model often hide architecture-specific optimizations that may not transfer cleanly to other LLMs. A performance figure mentioned in the thread was roughly 256 tokens/s × 100 users , which commenters characterized as extremely high concurrent serving throughput. The implication is that DeepInfer may be targeting production-scale multi-user inference rather than single-request latency benchmarks alone. Eagle-4 Released: Faster than DFlash2 & DSpark (Activity: 306): EAGLE-4 is a source-available speculative decoding stack using hardware/workload-calibrated draft trees, with eagle-harness integration paths for SGLang, vLLM, and TokenSpeed; current reported support/benchmarks center on Qwen3.8-27B. The post cites speedups over vanilla decoding of 2.22× for MTP, 2.57× for DSpark, 2.80× for DFlash 2, and 3.59× for EAGLE-4, while the repo reports SPEED-Bench gains on 4× NVIDIA B300 of 3.42× SGLang, 2.83× vLLM, and 3.09× TokenSpeed at single-request concurrency; gains reportedly shrink at higher concurrency ( EAGLE-4 ). Commenters also point to LiLiCorr, used by Nemotron Bolt, as a competing speculative decoder with more granular benchmark reporting ( paper ). Commenters questioned whether the DSpark/DFlash comparisons are representative because aggregate averages can hide workload sensitivity—e.g. MTP may do better on structured outputs such as code/JSON —and asked for breakdowns by workload type. Another concern was practicality: the EAGLE-4 draft model is reportedly about 3 GB larger than DFlash2 , making it less attractive for VRAM-constrained deployments. Several commenters questioned whether Eagle-4’s reported speedups over DFlash2 and DSpark are representative across workloads. One noted that averaged results may hide large variance, since MTP can perform better on structured-output tasks such as code or JSON, and asked for acceleration broken down by workload type rather than aggregate benchmarks. A practical deployment concern was raised around memory footprint: Eagle-4’s draft model is reportedly about 3 GB larger than DFlash2 , which may make it unsuitable for VRAM-constrained local inference setups already at capacity. Commenters pointed to competing or adjacent speculative decoding work, especially LiLiCorr , used by Nemotron Bolt , whose paper reportedly provides more granular benchmark analysis: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20530 . There was also interest in comparing Eagle-4 against HyperQwen or whether HyperQwen could integrate it: https://github.com/syv-ai/HyperQwen . Now that 3090 frenzy warning post makes sense. (Activity: 405): The image is a screenshot of an X/Twitter post claiming an RTX 3090 “gpu-unlock” kernel/module can raise BF16 tensor math throughput substantially, e.g. 82→155 TFLOPS for BF16 tensor pipe and 64→99 TFLOPS for cuBLAS BF16 GEMM, allegedly by removing an NVIDIA-imposed limitation on FP32-accumulate tensor ops. In context, the Reddit OP asks whether this explains a prior “3090 frenzy” warning and whether old anti-mining or product-segmentation restrictions might still affect LLM workloads, but commenters note that synthetic BF16/GEMM gains may not translate to real inference/training speedups. Commenters are skeptical of the market-hype angle: one calls predictions of used 3090s becoming more expensive than 5090s “delusional,” while another links a prior refutation arguing the hack has not shown practical workload gains. The dominant view is cautious: the benchmark claims are interesting, but “1.9× faster” may amount to much smaller end-to-end improvements. Several commenters argued that the rumored RTX 3090 “hack” is being overhyped because the measured benefit appears limited to a narrow workload slice: roughly 10–12% prefill improvement , not a broad 1.9x real-world LLM inference speedup. One linked the prior thread’s top refutation , emphasizing that the apparent low-level BF16 gains do not yet translate into practical end-to-end workloads. A technical concern raised was that BF16 operations may be only a small fraction of inference time , so accelerating or unlocking BF16 paths on RTX 3090 would have limited impact unless the bottleneck is actually BF16 compute rather than memory bandwidth, KV-cache access, sampling, or other kernels. Another commenter noted adoption would depend on whether the modification can be made safely and remain stable across CUDA and NVIDIA driver updates . On pricing, commenters were skeptical that used RTX 3090 values would materially spike from this news, arguing that GPU pricing is driven more by broader industry supply contracts and new-card positioning than by niche LLM hobbyist demand. One comparison cited a new Radeon RX 9700-class 32 GB card around ~$2k as potentially better value than an inflated used 3090, though the exact product naming/value claim was not deeply benchmarked in the thread. 2. New Open Models: Ornith-1.5, Flint, Tiny Voice-Cloning TTS ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-122B (Qwen finetune) (Activity: 438): Ornith AI released Ornith-1.5-122B , a 122B MoE reasoning model fine-tuned/continued from Ornith-1.0 on a Qwen 3.5 / Gemma-derived lineage, with a self-improvement loop that jointly optimizes task generation, scaffold construction, and solution rollouts via RL rather than using only fixed human-curated tasks. Artifacts include GGUF , unsloth GGUF , and NVFP4 variants; the model card claims strong coding/agentic benchmark performance, 262K context with optional YaRN scaling toward ~ 1M , and serving support via vLLM/SGLang/OpenAI-compatible APIs plus llama.cpp/Ollama-style GGUF paths. Commenters questioned the choice of a Qwen 3.5 122B base versus newer “Next Flash”-style bases, arguing it may already be behind newer architectures. One technical concern was inference speed: because it is based on Q3.5 122B with A10B active parameters and lacks sparse attention, a commenter estimated it will be roughly 2× slower than Q3.8fn-style models with A6B active parameters. A commenter notes the finetune is based on Qwen 3.5 122B , implying A10B rather than A6B behavior for q3.8fn users and no sparse attention , which they estimate will make inference roughly 2× slower for that setup. There is technical skepticism about the base-model choice: one commenter asks why it was not built on Ornith Next Flash , arguing that while Qwen 3.5 is a strong base, it has been “left in the dust” relative to newer alternatives. RecursiveSI/flint (40B A2.5B) · Hugging Face (Activity: 784): RecursiveSI/flint is an Apache-2.0 decoder-only MoE coding-agent model on Hugging Face , with 39.8B total parameters but only ~ 2.5B active per token. It uses 49 layers, 256 routed experts per MoE layer with 6 selected per token, mixed sliding-window/full attention, and a documented 262k context; Recursive reports 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89.7% on SWE-bench Pro v2, and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified, targeting SGLang serving on B300/H200 GPUs with OpenAI-compatible tool use. Commenters framed it as roughly the “ 35B-A3B ” class model people wanted from Qwen 3.8, but noted that the existence of Qwen3.8-27B makes the release feel less surprising; otherwise, the benchmark screenshot was the main technical discussion point. Commenters position Recursive Flint as a 40B MoE with only 2.5B active parameters, roughly matching the class of “ 35B-A3B ” sparse models some users wanted, but now competing against newer small-active MoEs like Qwen3.8-27B . The thread notes that without Qwen’s recent release, this would likely be viewed as a much more significant drop. A technical NVIDIA GTC Berlin announcement frames Flint as a local coding model optimized for RTX Spark , claiming over 220 tokens/s on a 64GB RTX Spark and strong results on agentic coding benchmarks including SWE-Bench Pro v2 , Terminal-Bench 2.1 , and SWE-bench Verified : https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/local-ai-gtc-rtx-dgx-spark-station-sync/ NVIDIA says Flint was built using Recursive’s Eureka Machine , an automated AI research loop that proposes ideas, implements them, runs experiments, and selects follow-ups. The cited post claims this system produced specialized kernels that improved Flint generation speed on RTX Spark by 55% without changing model weights , and notes Apache 2.0 open weights plus support for post-training via NeMo Automodel SFT/LoRA and NeMo RL GRPO. Pocket TTS which supports voice cloning is now just 1.9 million parameters (Activity: 561): Kyutai released Pocket TTS-small , compressing a CPU-real-time voice-cloning TTS stack from ~ 100M parameters down to 18.2M , 6.9M , and 1.9M variants. The compression pipeline uses distillation from a ~ 300M teacher, single-pass baked-in classifier-free guidance, a PCA-derived 64-D backbone–head latent interface, structured transformer pruning, separate backbone/head/codec distillation, and optional reward fine-tuning; reported CPU throughput reaches ~ 9.9× real time for the 18.2M model and ~ 25× real time for the 1.9M model, with the 18.2M model matching or slightly exceeding the original on WER/UTMOS. Commenters focused less on the compression method and more on an apparent profanity filter in the released model/demo—e.g. “What the fuck” being rendered as “What the dee”—though an update says the team fixed the issue. Others asked for more rigorous benchmarks on naturalness, real-time factor, and cross-speaker voice similarity, especially for fully local inference. Several users reported an apparent text censorship/regression in the TTS output: phrases like “What the fuck” were synthesized as “What the dee” . The top commenter later noted that the team addressed the issue and poste

title: Dimango M/A Basic School: Crumbling classrooms, two teachers for eight classes, but hope arrives
body: Imagine a school where two teachers are responsible for eight classes, where four grade levels are merged into a single classroom, and where the building itself is literally collapsing around the pupils. This is the reality that has defined Dimango M/A Basic School in the Nkoranza South Constituency for years. But today, a new chapter begins. A School in Crisis: Infrastructure on the Verge of Collapse The physical structure of Dimango M/A Basic School tells a painful story. The school’s main building, which has served the community for years, was partly ripped off by torrential rains, leaving sections of it collapsed and dangerously unsafe for young learners. For years, pupils have been forced to study in these dilapidated conditions—exposed to the elements and learning in an environment that poses serious health and safety risks. The crumbling walls and damaged roofing sheets are a constant reminder of the neglect that rural schools continue to face across Ghana. The situation is compounded by the terrible road network connecting Nkoranza to Dimango. During rainy days, the roads become nearly impassable, cutting off teachers and students from the school entirely. Two Teachers, Eight Classes: The Teacher Deficit If the infrastructure is a crisis, the staffing situation is nothing short of alarming. Headmaster Samuel Yaw Amankwa Junior revealed that the school currently has only two teachers managing eight classes—from kindergarten to primary six. To cope with the shortfall, teachers are forced to combine four different classes at a time, a practice that is severely undermining academic progress. “Top on the list of the school’s challenges is the lack of teachers,” Mr. Teri told Joy News. “We have two teachers taking care of eight classes. We combine four classes at a time, and this is affecting academic work badly.” The headmaster explained that the combination of multi-grade teaching and poor infrastructure has created an environment where meaningful learning is nearly impossible. “How can one teacher effectively teach four different grade levels in a single classroom? The children are suffering, and their futures are at stake.” He appealed to the Ghana Education Service and the Ministry of Education to urgently post more teachers to the school, noting that without adequate staffing, even the best infrastructure will not translate into quality education. The MP’s Intervention: A Three-Unit Classroom Block Recognizing the urgent need, the Member of Parliament for Nkoranza South, who doubles as the Minister for Labour, Mr Emmanuel Agyekum, has stepped in with a tangible solution. Today, the MP handed over a brand new three-unit classroom block to the school, providing pupils with a safe, modern, and conducive learning environment for the first time in years. Speaking at the handover ceremony, Mr Agyekum emphasized that the project is part of his commitment to improving education in the constituency. “The move is to provide the pupils with a decent education infrastructure in order to prevent the young children from walking several kilometers to neighboring communities to school,” he said. “This is to bring better education closer to the pupils, who are the future of the country.” The MP noted that investing in rural education is essential for bridging the gap between urban and rural communities, and he assured the community of his continued support. A Community’s Hope The handover ceremony was met with joy and relief from parents, community elders, and students who have long advocated for better conditions at the school. For the people of Dimango, the new classroom block is more than just a building—it is a symbol of hope and a sign that their children’s education matters. However, the community is acutely aware that infrastructure alone will not solve the problem. The Headmaster’s appeal for more teachers remains unanswered, and the road network continues to be a barrier to consistent attendance. What Lies Ahead The new classroom block is a significant step forward, but Dimango M/A Basic School still faces an uphill battle. The community is calling on the government, the Ghana Education Service, and other stakeholders to address the teacher deficit and improve the road network. For now, the pupils of Dimango have a safer place to learn—and a renewed sense of hope that their future is brighter than their past.

title: Russian attacks kill at least 9, injure 57 across Ukraine as Kyiv hit by mass missile, drone attack
body:
Russian attacks have killed at least nine people and injured 56 others across Ukraine over the past day, as Russia launched a mass missile and drone attack primarily targeting Kyiv, local authorities said on Oct. 22.
In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles struck transport and medical infrastructure in several waves overnight on Oct. 22, killing at least one person and injuring 24 others, according to city authorities.
Russian forces launched a mass combined attack overnight with Iskander-M, S-400, Zircon, and Onyx missiles, as well as 210 drones of various types, including 110 jet-powered drones, the Air Force reported. Kyiv was the main target of the attack. Ukrainian air defenses shot down 181 drones, including 87 jet-powered ones, according to the Air Force. Strikes were recorded at 32 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at eight others.
In Kharkiv Oblast , one person was killed and 15 others, including three children, were injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv and 11 other settlements, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
In Sumy Oblast , one person was killed and four others injured in Russian drone attacks over the past day, the regional military administration said. Russian forces carried out nearly 60 attacks against 26 settlements across 14 communities.
In Donetsk Oblast , two people were killed, in Druzhkivka and Kramatorsk respectively, while nine others were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, local Governor Vadym Filashkin said.
In Zaporizhzhia Oblast , three people were killed and three others injured in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding district, local Governor Ivan Fedorov said. Russian forces launched 862 attacks against 48 settlements across the oblast over the past day.
In Chernihiv Oblast , one person was killed and another injured after Russian forces twice attacked an enterprise in Chernihiv with Banderol drones, regional governor Viacheslav Chaus said. A Russian drone also struck an agricultural enterprise in Semenivka overnight, setting a warehouse and other buildings on fire.

title: Russia strikes Kyiv hours after Putin meets with Trump envoy Witkoff, killing one and injuring more than 20
body: Russian forces struck Kyiv overnight on October 22 with drones and ballistic missiles. In the Dniprovskyi district, the strikes damaged homes and vehicles and set residential and non-residential buildings on fire, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said. One person was killed and five others, including a child, were injured. In the Darnytskyi district, the strikes damaged transportation infrastructure. In the Obolonskyi district, two people were injured. In the Pecherskyi district, eight people, including three children, were injured. In the Holosiivskyi district, six people were injured. The strikes also damaged non-residential buildings, ambulances, and a monastery. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the strikes damaged part of the metro system’s infrastructure at the South Bridge. He did not provide further details. Russia’s Defense Ministry said the strikes in Kyiv hit “Ukrainian military-industrial facilities involved in the production and storage of long- and medium-range cruise missiles and drones, as well as transportation infrastructure sites.” In the Odesa region, Russian forces struck a food production facility, Ukraine’s public broadcaster Suspilne reported . A fire broke out, destroying the administrative building. No one was injured. Russia’s Defense Ministry said the strikes targeted “port infrastructure facilities in the Odesa region and vessels used in the interests of Ukraine’s Armed Forces.” Russia strikes Kyiv with drones and various types of missiles daily. The latest attack, on October 22, came just hours after U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg to meet with Vladimir Putin for talks focused on ending the war between Russia and Ukraine. title: EU strategy to end war based on ‘peace through strength’ formula – Kubilius
body:
Andrius Kubilius, European Commissioner for Defence and Space, said this in an interview with Ukrinform .
“Our peace strategy, as I understand it, is really an implementation of the formula ‘peace through strength’. And strength should be on Ukrainian side in order to achieve a just peace,” Kubilius said.
He added that this strength could largely be provided through European support, as Ukrainians have already mobilized all their domestic resources. Ukraine now needs all possible additional strength and support from its partners.
“The European Union here is most important supporter. That's what I considers real peace plan,” the European Commissioner stressed.
At the same time, he believes that U.S. partners should not be forgotten. Ultimately, the U.S. President also believes that peace can be achieved through strength, although he probably sees it differently from the Ukrainians.
“Trump is also speaking about ‘peace through strength’ formula, but he may understand it in a different way really,” Kubilius noted.
He is convinced that sanctions against the aggressor country should continue. Such sanctions are being imposed not only by European partners but also by Ukraine itself.
“Russia needs to feel what this war means. And Russia should not have possibilities to have any profits from selling oil or gas products. That is what we are trying to achieve with our legal sanctions. Ukrainians are making their sanctions,” Kubilius said, describing strikes deep inside Russian territory against oil refining facilities as the most effective sanctions against Russia’s energy sector.
As reported by Ukrinform, Andrius Kubilius recently called for the development of an independent European peace strategy for Ukraine, saying that it was no longer possible to rely on the U.S. administration to establish peace in Ukraine.

title: Poland deputy FM meets Araghchi in Tehran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 22 (MNA) – Polish Deputy Foreign Minister Wojciech Zajączkowski met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who blamed insecurity in West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz on US and Israeli aggression.
Poland's Deputy Foreign Minister Wojciech Zajączkowski, who traveled to Tehran for the third round of political consultations between Iran and Poland, met Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday evening.
Araghchi noted the positive historical ties between the Iranian and Polish peoples and the discussions held with his Polish counterpart on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, stressing the importance of planning to use existing capacities in both countries to strengthen interaction in various fields in line with mutual interests.
Araghchi explained Iran's positions on developments in West Asia and described the insecurity in the region and the Strait of Hormuz as stemming from the aggressive actions of the United States and the Zionist regime. He criticized some European countries for complicity in or inaction toward the blatant military aggression against Iran and stressed the need for all countries, including European governments, to take a principled stance in condemning the military aggression against Iran and the crimes committed during it.
The foreign minister also stressed that Iran, as it has been steadfast in using the tools of diplomacy to secure regional peace and security, will not hesitate to defend its national sovereignty and territorial integrity against any threat or aggression.
The Polish deputy foreign minister, for his part, expressed satisfaction with his visit to Iran, presented a report on his talks with his Iranian counterpart and explained his country's positions on regional and international developments.

title: Warnings Against Sharing Sensitive Information With AI Chatbots
body: AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot are growing increasingly popular, but cybersecurity company ESET warns users to think carefully before sharing personal, medical, financial or confidential information with these tools. As artificial intelligence becomes part of everyday life, understanding what information to keep private has become an essential digital skill. ESET cautions that users may not always know how chatbot providers handle the information they share, particularly when they seek advice on mental health, medical conditions, legal matters or other personal issues. Before choosing an AI platform or model, users should review the provider’s data policies and privacy settings to understand how it collects, stores and uses their information. Although some platforms emphasise privacy and data sovereignty, users should remain cautious. Companies can change their policies, terms of service and priorities, potentially allowing information shared today to be used for AI training in the future. Five Types of Information You Should Keep Private ESET identifies five categories of information that users should avoid sharing with AI chatbots. 1. Passwords and account credentials Users should never disclose passwords, login credentials, recovery codes or answers to security questions that could provide access to their accounts. 2. Sensitive personal information Identity and passport details, home addresses and financial information can expose individuals to identity theft, fraud and other risks if they fall into the wrong hands. 3. Confidential workplace information Internal reports, customer records, product plans, source code and other non-public business information should remain confidential unless an organisation has explicitly approved the AI tool for that purpose. Uploading a confidential document for an AI-generated summary may seem like an efficient way to save time. However, if the tool lacks the necessary approval or appropriate agreements between the employer and provider, sharing the document could breach company policies, contractual obligations or data protection requirements. 4. Medical and highly sensitive personal data Medical records, test results, treatment details and other health information require particular care because of their sensitive nature. 5. Information about other people Users should avoid sharing colleagues’ details, customer records, private conversations, contact information and other personal data belonging to third parties without appropriate authorisation. Before submitting any information, ESET recommends asking three questions: Is it publicly available? Am I authorised to share it? Would I feel comfortable if it became exposed in a data breach? How to Use AI Chatbots More Safely If users need to share information with an AI chatbot, ESET recommends taking steps to minimise potential risks. These include removing names and other identifying details, using fictional or anonymised examples instead of real cases, and summarising sensitive documents themselves before asking AI for assistance. At work, employees should use approved corporate AI tools with appropriate data protection safeguards whenever available. Users should also check which classifications of information their chosen tools can process, whether conversation history and memory features are enabled, and whether external plugins, links or web-search functions could transfer information outside their organisation’s controlled environment. Anonymisation and Deleting Chats May Not Be Enough ESET warns that AI chatbots may infer personal information from a user’s prompt history, even when the user has anonymised the information entered. Deleting a conversation also does not necessarily guarantee that all associated data or copies have disappeared. While deletion may reduce exposure, users should not assume that it removes every trace of the information. Understanding each provider’s data retention policies and how it handles collected information is therefore essential, including whether it may use that information to train AI models. What to Do If You Have Shared Sensitive Information If users have already disclosed sensitive information, ESET recommends deleting the conversation where possible, removing any relevant stored memories and revoking access to connected applications where appropriate. Anyone who has exposed passwords, recovery codes or other account credentials should change them promptly. If the disclosure involves company information, customer records or data belonging to third parties, users should report the incident to their employer or organisational security team rather than attempting to manage it independently. As AI chatbots become more widely used, ESET’s advice highlights the importance of treating personal and confidential information with care before submitting it to an AI tool.
