title: DSS, Police, Other Security Agencies Protecting Vulnerable Communities in Plateau, Youth Groups Assert
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja A coalition of indigenous youth organisations in Plateau State has asserted that the Department of State Services (DSS), the Mobile Police Force and Operation Rainbow are working to protect vulnerable communities in the state. At a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday, the coalition dismissed a recent petition and viral videos accusing security operatives of bias and criminality as deliberate attempts to undermine counter-insurgency efforts. The coalition’s spokesperson, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, Esq., President of the Berom Youths Moulder-Association and Coordinator of Indigenous Youth Nationalities, Northern Zone, accused the petitioners of seeking to undermine joint security operations through petitions and social media campaigns. He called on the Federal Government to protect the security agencies from political and criminal pressure. The coalition, comprising Afizere, Anaguta, Atakar, Atten, Bache, Berom, Gamai, Irigwe, Kunlere, Mushere, Mwaghavul, Ron, Pan, Tarok and other ethnic youth organisations, said the campaigns could distract security operatives and benefit militants. It cited a petition dated 5 October 2026, signed by Mujahid Abdullahi, Esq., on behalf of Plateau chapters of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), the Gan Allah Fulani Development Association of Nigeria (GAFDAN), the Fulbe Youth Development Association (FUYODA) and other organisations. The petition allegedly accused the DSS of discriminatory operations against its communities and blamed it for killings, abductions, cattle rustling and attacks on livestock. The coalition maintained that the allegations were intended to mislead the Federal Government and the public. It claimed that joint security operations had exposed links between cattle grazing and armed militants responsible for attacks on communities. The group alleged that at least 152 hamlets, villages and communities had suffered attacks, while security operatives had also been targeted in several ambushes. However, it called for a thorough investigation into allegations of misconduct, compromise and collusion involving some military personnel. The coalition urged President Bola Tinubu and other Federal Government authorities to sustain security operations, strengthen inter-agency collaboration and investigate any credible allegations of wrongdoing. “We smell a rat,” it said, describing the petition and videos as “ploys and strategies of distraction”. It urged the government to support security agencies rather than withdraw them from Plateau State.

title: NIS Raises Alarm Over Human Trafficking, Travel Fraud, Says Border Controls Alone Cannot Stop Irregular Migration
body: Michael Olugbode in Buja The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has warned that misinformation, false promises and inadequate access to reliable migration information are exposing Nigerians to human trafficking, migrant smuggling and travel fraud, declaring that border controls alone cannot address the growing challenges of irregular migration. The Service called for coordinated action by government agencies, security institutions, development partners, community leaders, civil society organisations and the media to close information gaps and ensure that prospective migrants can make informed decisions about travelling abroad. The Comptroller-General of the NIS, Kemi Nandap, gave the warning in a speech delivered by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency Directorate, Franca Nwanneka, at a Stakeholder Sensitisation and Engagement Seminar in Abuja on Wednesday. The seminar was themed, “Bridging the Information Gap: Promoting Informed, Safe and Regular Migration.” Nandap said although people migrated in pursuit of education, employment, safety and better opportunities, decisions influenced by misinformation, deceptive promises and limited awareness of lawful migration pathways could expose them to serious risks and devastating consequences. “Human trafficking, migrant smuggling, travel fraud, and irregular migration highlight the risk of inadequate information and intelligence sharing among operational stakeholders,” she said. The Comptroller-General stressed that tackling the problem required more than enforcement at the nation’s borders, insisting that prospective migrants must have access to accurate, timely and reliable information before making decisions that could affect their safety and future. “Preventing these risks requires more than border control. It begins with equipping prospective migrants with accurate, timely, and reliable information to make informed decisions and pursue safe, lawful migration pathways,” she said. The warning places public awareness and access to trustworthy information at the centre of Nigeria’s migration management efforts, with the Service seeking stronger collaboration among institutions responsible for border security, migration governance and public sensitisation. Nandap said the NIS was strengthening its operational capacity through institutional reforms, modern border management technologies, intelligence gathering and improved service delivery. She cited the recent deployment of the border control and immigration management system and other technology-driven platforms as part of efforts to build a modern, responsive and intelligence-led immigration service. However, she acknowledged that technology and stronger border controls could not independently resolve the factors driving irregular migration. “Nevertheless, we recognise that even the most sophisticated border management systems cannot on their own address the underlying factors that encourage irregular migration,” she said. The Comptroller-General therefore urged stakeholders to move beyond discussions and adopt coordinated, practical measures to counter misinformation and ensure that reliable migration information reaches communities, particularly those most vulnerable to exploitation. She specifically called on government agencies, security institutions, development partners, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, educational institutions, transport operators and the media to take greater responsibility for public sensitisation. “Migration sensitisation is a shared responsibility that cannot be left to the Nigeria Immigration Service alone,” she said. According to her, the seminar was designed to help stakeholders examine existing approaches, identify institutional gaps and explore how innovation, community participation and inter-agency cooperation could improve migration management. She expressed confidence that the presentations, roundtable discussions and technical sessions would generate practical recommendations towards a safer and more coordinated migration management system. The NIS chief also commended partner institutions, development partners, resource persons and participants for their contributions to strengthening migration governance in Nigeria. Also speaking at the seminar, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its partnership with the NIS to promote regular migration and address migration-related challenges. Nnenna Onuoha, Senior Programme Associate of IOM Nigeria, who represented the organisation’s Chief of Mission, Sharon Dimanche, said the partnership between the two institutions had continued to grow stronger and produce tangible results. “The relationship and the partnership between IOM and NIS have been and have continued to grow stronger and have produced tangible results,” Onuoha said. She described the engagement as an opportunity for stakeholders to deliberate on how collective action could make regular migration more accessible and commonplace in Nigeria. Onuoha conveyed Dimanche’s goodwill to the participants and expressed the IOM’s hope that the discussions would lead to fruitful deliberations and actionable outcomes. The collaboration reflects a shared emphasis on stakeholder engagement and better-informed migration decisions, with the NIS focusing on its statutory responsibilities for immigration control and migration management and the IOM supporting cooperation on migration-related issues. The challenge ahead, however, is to translate the commitments made at the seminar into sustained public education, improved access to reliable migration information and effective coordination among relevant institutions. For the NIS, the objective is to ensure that prospective migrants can distinguish legitimate migration opportunities from deceptive offers and understand the lawful pathways available to them before embarking on potentially dangerous journeys. The seminar brought together representatives of security and law enforcement agencies, regional and international organisations, border management institutions, civil society groups, non-governmental organisations, community-based organisations, academic institutions and other stakeholders. Nwanneka formally declared the seminar open on behalf of Nandap, expressing the Service’s expectation that the deliberations would advance a safer, smarter and more coordinated migration management system in Nigeria.

title: Greece Achieves First Successful Laser Link with Low-Earth-Orbit Satellite
body: Greece has achieved its first successful optical laser communication link with a low-Earth-orbit satellite, as the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA) and Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (AUTH) established a connection between the Greek ERMIS-3 nanosatellite and an optical ground station on Mount Holomontas. The achievement marks one of the first stable laser links internationally between a CubeSat nanosatellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and a ground-based optical telescope. The system uses an infrared laser beam, a technology that can support secure, high-volume data transmission. NKUA’s Department of Aerospace Science and Technology designed and built the ERMIS-3 nanosatellite, while AUTH’s Laboratory of Theoretical Mechanics and Astrodynamics, within its Department of Physics, developed the Holomontas Optical Ground Station in collaboration with Lithuanian company Astrolight and the European Space Agency (ESA). The achievement also marks Greece’s first successful optical communication link with a low-orbit satellite travelling at high speed across the sky. Laser technology delivers high-speed data transmission The ATLAS-1 laser device aboard ERMIS-3 currently supports data transmission at speeds of 1 gigabit per second (Gbps). Link-budget calculations indicate that the system could potentially support speeds of up to 10 Gbps. Both ATLAS-1 and the Holomontas ground station received their first signals during the satellite’s first active pass over the station. By the third pass, engineers had fully calibrated both systems, enabling them to operate autonomously according to a predetermined schedule. Since then, the satellite and ground station have regularly established two optical links per day. Initial results demonstrate that the system can transmit data reliably during both daytime and nighttime operations, including under partial cloud cover, at low satellite elevation angles and even when clouds or trees intermittently obstruct the optical path. The equipment received signals at elevation angles below 10 degrees above the horizon. Following calibration, link availability exceeded 85% of the available time, indicating potential for operational and commercial applications. New opportunities for telecommunications and national security Scientists say laser-based optical communications could enable the transmission of enormous volumes of data for 5G networks, artificial intelligence applications, inter-satellite links and highly secure government and military communications. The technology could also support national security and defence applications by providing a highly secure alternative to conventional telecommunications. Researchers say laser communications open new possibilities for Greece to develop advanced quantum communications technologies, which remain available in only a limited number of countries. The successful experiments strengthen cooperation between NKUA and AUTH in space technology. Astrolight developed both the satellite’s laser transmitter and the receiver at the ground station. The experiments received support from the European Space Agency, Greece’s Ministry of Digital Governance and Artificial Intelligence, and the Hellenic Space Centre. Minister highlights national space programme Digital Governance and Artificial Intelligence Minister Dimitris Papastergiou said Greece’s National Microsatellite Programme was turning the country’s investment in space into practical technical expertise. “The successful optical targeting between a CubeSat and a national observatory demonstrates how Greek universities and technology companies can jointly use new infrastructure, multiplying the value of the national programme and opening pathways for the satellite communications of tomorrow,” Papastergiou said. He added that the programme also offered young scientists and engineers valuable opportunities to gain training and practical experience with cutting-edge technologies. Researchers highlight international significance Professors Vaios Lappas and Antonis Paschalis of NKUA, the scientific leads of the ERMIS project, described ERMIS-3 as one of the most advanced CubeSat satellites developed in Europe. They said the use of ATLAS-1 as a laser communications terminal had enabled a unique collaboration and the establishment of some of the first stable laser links from a nanosatellite worldwide. They added that the achievement created new opportunities for secure communications involving small satellites within the European space ecosystem. Kleomenis Tsiganis, a professor in AUTH’s Department of Physics and the university’s lead for space situational awareness and optical ground station activities under the HolOGS programme, called the experiment a major milestone for his team and optical communications in Greece. He emphasised the significance of establishing the link from AUTH’s Holomontas facilities with ERMIS, a satellite developed in Greece by NKUA. He also praised Astrolight’s technical expertise and contribution to the collaboration. Frederic Rouesnel, head of ESA’s Resilience Initiatives Implementation Management Office, said the achievement demonstrated Europe’s ability to deliver world-class innovation through close cooperation between industry, academia and public institutions. He noted that an 8U CubeSat developed by the University of Athens had connected directly with Earth through a laser link for the first time, using a compact optical terminal developed by Astrolight and a corresponding receiver at AUTH’s Holomontas ground station. Rouesnel said ESA had provided programme management, technical oversight and support throughout the project, helping turn an ambitious concept into a pioneering demonstration of in-orbit resilience. The ERMIS programme forms part of Greece’s National Microsatellite Programme. The European Union’s Recovery and Resilience Facility, under NextGenerationEU, and the Ministry of Digital Governance fund the programme, with support from ESA and the Hellenic Space Centre. A video demonstrating the ERMIS laser satellite link is available here . title: US Declines to Take Position on Turkey-Libya Maritime Deal
body: The US State Department has called for good-faith negotiations to resolve maritime disputes, responding to a question about the eastern-based Libyan House of Representatives’ ratification of the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum. The US State Department did not explicitly comment on the memorandum’s legality or the Libyan parliament’s decision. Instead, it highlighted the benefits of resolving maritime disputes for investment and exploration across the region, while encouraging Greece and Turkey to address their differences bilaterally. “We encourage our partners in the Eastern Mediterranean to resolve their maritime disputes through good-faith negotiations,” the department said. “Resolving maritime issues serves the interests of all sides and opens the way for commercial investment and exploration that will benefit the entire Mediterranean region,” it added. Addressing relations between Athens and Ankara, the State Department noted that “Greece and Turkey are both NATO allies” and encouraged the two countries to hold bilateral discussions to address any disagreements. The Libyan House of Representatives approved the 2019 maritime delimitation memorandum between Turkey and Libya on 20 October. Greece rejected the decision, arguing that the memorandum violates international maritime law and infringes on the sovereign rights of countries in the region. The European Union also expressed strong dissatisfaction with the ratification. In a statement issued on 21 October on behalf of the EU, the High Representative reiterated that the memorandum violates the sovereign rights of third countries, conflicts with the law of the sea and cannot produce legal consequences for third countries. title: Meta Sued in Australia Over Social Media Harm to Children
body: Meta and its platforms, Instagram and Facebook, are facing a class-action lawsuit in Australia over allegations that their design encourages addictive behaviour and creates harmful dependencies among children. Eight people filed the lawsuit in the Federal Court of Australia, the country’s second-highest court, seeking compensation for exposure to harmful content or social media addiction they experienced before turning 18, law firm MinterEllison said in a statement on Wednesday. The case could be the first lawsuit in Australia to hold social media platforms responsible for the harmful effects of their services on users, particularly children and teenagers. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Sydney-based court issued an order on Monday prohibiting the disclosure of details about the proceedings or the identities of the class-action plaintiffs, according to court documents. In August, Meta agreed to pay just over $17 billion in the United States to settle a lawsuit that accused the American company of deliberately designing its platforms to encourage addiction among young users. The Australian case comes amid growing tensions between the government and major technology companies following the country’s world-first ban on social media use by children under 16. The government has also recently proposed rules that would allow users to disable algorithmic feeds. title: Police Confirm Deaths in Rivers Boat Tragedy as Kula Community Demands Probe
body: . Contractor denies allegations linking Ibeto to incident Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt The Rivers State Police have confirmed an incident involving a boat accident in Kula Kingdom, Akuku-Toru Local Government Area of the state, in which 10 people were reportedly killed. The police spokesperson, ASP Agabe Karborlo said investigations were ongoing to establish the exact number of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The Rivers State Police Command is aware of the incident in Kula Kingdom, Akuku-Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State, which reportedly resulted in the loss of lives. Investigation is ongoing to ascertain the exact number of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the incident,” she said. The incident reportedly occurred on Tuesday evening amid tensions over the planned recovery of a vessel, Anambra Basin FSO, and a dispute involving allegations of oil pollution in the community. Community sources alleged that residents had opposed the removal of the vessel over concerns about the environmental impact of a reported oil spill. Sukubo Sara-Igbe, a native of Kula and President of the National Youth Council of Nigeria, alleged that six gunboats arrived in the area during the operation. He said that a boat conveying community members capsized during the confrontation, leaving several people feared dead. “The top boat capsized the boat the community came with, and 10 lives were lost,” he said, adding that efforts were being made to recover the bodies. He also alleged that two local security personnel were among those feared dead. The police have yet to establish the identities of the casualties or independently confirm the circumstances described by community sources. A former spokesperson of the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) Chief Anabs Sara-Igbe, also called for an investigation into the incident, saying the community had raised concerns over the reported pollution and the vessel’s removal. The incident has heightened community concerns, with calls for the authorities to establish what happened, determine responsibility where necessary and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the reported deaths are fully investigated. However, Max Shipping Services Limited, the owner of Anambra Basin FSO and a subsidiary of Ibeto Group, denied allegations linking Ibeto to the incident in a statement dated October 21, 2026. The company said it owned the vessel but was not the operator of the oilfield or the underlying petroleum operations in Kula. According to the statement, the vessel was hired to Menal Technical Services Limited under a Marine Equipment Hire Agreement dated September 20, 2024, subsequently amended by an addendum. Max Shipping said Menal had assumed specified contractual responsibilities relating to operational requirements, community settlements, security and demobilisation. The company explained that it sought to retrieve its equipment following prolonged outstanding hire payments, adding that the crude oil previously stored in the vessel had been discharged before the demobilisation effort. It cited tank inspection documents issued by Checkirem and GSV Inspection Services Limited in September 2026, which it said recorded that the inspected tanks were free and clean of crude oil at the time of inspection. The company also said its representatives had met with community leaders on several occasions to explain its contractual relationship with Menal and seek a peaceful resolution. “We are deeply saddened by reports that a community boat capsized and that allegedly lives may have been lost,” the statement said. It urged the media and the public to distinguish between ownership of the vessel and the operational responsibilities of the hirer and other parties involved in activities at the oilfield. Max Shipping called for calm and urged the relevant authorities to investigate the incident and establish the facts. Meanwhile, the police investigation is expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding the boat capsizing, the reported deaths and the events leading to the confrontation.

title: UFC Abu Dhabi: Merab Dvalishvili has new plan for Petr Yan and promises ‘domination’
body: For a former UFC champion, the fighter with the most takedowns in company history and a man whose face is plastered across billboards around Abu Dhabi advertising UFC 333, Merab Dvalishvili hardly needed to introduce himself to the assembled media. He did it anyway. “Hello everybody. My name is Merab Dvalishvili.” The Georgian cut a suave figure in a brown tailored suit, an expensive watch and a permanent smile. He was jovial and playful, joking about riding motorcycles and horses with Sean Strickland. It was in stark contrast to his opponent. If Dvalishvili’s vibe was light, Petr Yan’s was heavy. Dressed in a black baseball cap and UFC apparel, Yan exuded a brooding, smouldering intensity. He said Dvalishvili should not even be in line to face him this Saturday for a shot at his UFC bantamweight belt. “ Song Yadong is really more deserving of a title fight, to be honest,” the Russian champion said through a translator. “I do not choose my opponents. Whoever the company gives me, that's who I fight.” Make no mistake, Dvalishvili and Yan do not like each other. One does a passable job of disguising his disdain; the other wears it like a badge of honour. If all fights are personal, in the sense that both combatants are trying to inflict maximum pain and damage on each other, this one carries an extra edge. The two meet for the third time in their careers at Etihad Arena on Saturday , with one win apiece. It is billed as the co-main event but could easily headline the card, with no disrespect intended to Alexander Volkanovski and Movsar Evloev . Trash talk dominated the build-up to their first two encounters, and there have been plenty of barbs fired this time around, too, mostly from Yan. UFC 333 build-up - in pictures “I'm really excited to fight Petr Yan; the title is secondary,” said Dvalishvili. “His trash talk and his disrespect doesn't bother me because the most important thing is to get the win against him and answer that way. “I'm not here to show who is the better person. I'm here to show who is the better fighter.” Abu Dhabi will bring the trilogy - which began three years ago - to a close. Back then, Dvalishvili took a unanimous decision over Yan, a result the Russian heavily disputed. Before that bout, Dvalishvili had made the extreme claim that he would kill himself if he lost to Yan. Having suffered defeat the last time the two met, the Georgian has adopted a much more measured approach this time around. “No, the first fight was very important; it was really personal. But right now I'm a different person, at a different stage [in life]. That time it was a different situation,” Dvalishvili said. “But right now, I just want to win the fight. I can see now if I lose, it's gonna just be a loss. And it's possible, of course. Petr Yan is a dangerous guy. “Even when we fought the last time, I was the one who said he deserved the fight with me. He's the most dangerous guy. “And of course, I knew I could lose this fight, but I still take this risk. I'm not saying that I'm not gonna lose. Every time I fight, there is a chance that I lose. It's possible. But I'm not gonna kill myself.” Yan produced the performance of a lifetime when the two met last December at UFC 323. He literally took the breath away from Dvalishvili with crunching body shots and broke his opponent's spirit by repeatedly denying his takedown attempts. Dvalishvili had taken that bout just two months after beating Corey Sandhagen. It was his third successful title defence, bringing him level with his good friend Aljamain Sterling, who was in attendance to support him and will also corner Dvalishvili on Saturday. The Yan rematch was Dvalishvili's fourth fight of 2025. Most champions defend their belts no more than twice a year. Dvalishvili admitted in an earlier interview with The National that it had been a mistake to take on Yan so soon after his win over Sandhagen. A fighter renowned for his cardio and work ethic simply ran out of steam. Dvalishvili conceded that he knew he was losing the fight after the second round. He said he would take a different approach to Saturday's contest. “I'm not really focused on the takedown. I have a different strategy. I think it's gonna be domination this time, like it was the first time. I have a different game plan, and I can't wait to show everyone, and I can't wait to raise my hand.” Yan said that, regardless of what Dvalishvili brings to the octagon, he will emerge victorious. “He has his own thoughts, his own ideas, his own plan,” he said. “I'm not really interested in what he has to do. I have a plan, and my plan is to come out there and win.” Yan underwent major back surgery in January following his win over Dvalishvili. Sean O'Malley, who knows both fighters well having faced Dvalishvili twice and Yan once, believes Yan has made a mistake by taking the fight and needs more time to recover. “If I am here, I am 100 per cent ready to fight,” Yan snapped when asked for his thoughts. There is no need for either man to raise the stakes. They have already fought twice, shared one victory apiece and spent the best part of three years trading blows and barbs. On Saturday, at Etihad Arena, there will be nowhere left to hide.

title: examining the macOS gcc binary
body:
if you’ve ever written C(or c++) on a mac, you’ll know that the so-called gcc is just clang in disguise
most people(fairly) assume that this is just an alias, but this is not true! it’s a binary!
now, what is this binary? i naively assumed that it would just be shelling out to clang but it turns out the answer is more interesting than that.
there’s some interesting stuff here(for example special logic for checking if it’s being run as c++ or llvm-gcc specifically), but the key thing we’re interested in is this line of code:
this is a function from libxcselect.dylib, but it’s basically the same thing as running xcrun .(fun fact: the xcrun binary basically just calls this function ) if you disassemble any xcode-installed developer tool, you’ll see this exact same binary ,meaning all the developer tools that xcode-select installs on macOS are actually just being run through xcrun. 1 but that raises the important question: what does xcrun do ? i’ve certainly never heard of it before this. well, checking the manpage we can see that it calls developer tools from the developer tool directory. this gives us an important bit of info: the location of the actual gcc binary that’s being called. thankfully for us, there is a --find command that can give us exactly this.
looking in this directory, we can see that: c++, llvm-gcc, llvm-g++ aren’t in this directory, that’s why they’re hardcoded into the binary itself cc and clang++ are just alises to clang but most interestingly, g++ is an alias to an actual gcc binary that’s in the same directory: well, what does that gcc binary do, then? opening it in my disassembler, we see that it… shells out to xcrun and calls clang(or clang++ depending on how it’s called)
if you’re wondering why this is, my guess is because of SIP. /usr/bin is a protected directory on macOS and i assume apple can’t update it without requiring a restart, and you can update the xcode tools without having to restart your mac. as for why they dont just add the developer tools directory to path, my guess is that they want the freedom to change this directory whenever they want ↩︎

title: Terrifying Virus Threatens the Global Internet with Cyberattacks
body: Government websites across Europe and other regions suspended operations on Wednesday after authorities identified serious security vulnerabilities in PHP, raising concerns about potential cyberattacks targeting websites and their databases. The alert first emerged on Tuesday, when developers responsible for PHP, one of the world’s most widely used programming languages, disclosed two critical vulnerabilities and began working on an updated version to address the problem. However, a broader security alert followed on Wednesday, despite the release of a version considered more secure. Reports suggested that some websites could not easily apply the necessary fixes, while hacker groups were allegedly coordinating efforts to exploit the vulnerabilities. Attackers could potentially gain access to website administration systems, deface pages, steal large databases or use compromised websites to launch wider cyberattacks against infrastructure. Cybersecurity authorities and some government leaders in Europe, the United Kingdom, Japan and Australia urged PHP users to take immediate precautions, including temporarily disabling websites that relied on vulnerable versions of the software. Several countries, including the Netherlands and Finland, reportedly took websites offline, while French authorities announced that vulnerable websites had entered maintenance mode. PHP and WordPress underpin much of the internet PHP is an open-source programming language that powers approximately 75% of websites for which the underlying technology can be identified. It also underpins WordPress, the world’s most widely used content management system, which supports around 43% of all websites. These range from personal blogs and small business websites to government services, news platforms and online shops. A report by The Wall Street Journal said artificial intelligence helped researchers identify the vulnerabilities, described as the most significant to emerge in PHP in more than a decade. The White House reportedly linked the discovery to the importance of US leadership in superintelligence, adding that it had known about the security issue since the previous Friday. title: Oil prices gain more than $1 after Yemen strikes on KSA
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 22 (MNA) – Oil prices rose by more than $1 a barrel on Thursday as more Yemen attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke concerns over a broader escalation of regional conflict and further disruptions to West Asia supplies.
Brent crude futures gained $1.93, or 1.8 percent, to reach $110.75 a barrel as of 04:42 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude climbed $1.43, or 1.5 percent, to trade at $98.58.

title: War update: 187 clashes on front line over past day, Pokrovsk sector remains hottest
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, this was stated by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine in a Facebook post on the situation as of 8:00 on Thursday, October 22.
The enemy launched one missile strike and 88 airstrikes, dropping 289 guided aerial bombs. In addition, the invaders deployed 10,414 kamikaze drones and carried out 2,604 attacks on settlements and Ukrainian troops positions, 67 of them using multiple-launch rocket systems.
The enemy shelled, among other areas, the settlements of Bezsalivka, Korenok, Tovstodubove, Oleksiivka, Kucherivka, Rohizne, Mala Korchakivka, Bachivsk, Mohrytsia, Pysarivka, Volfyne, Khrapivshchyna, Sukhodil, Vovkivka, Luzhky, Hirky, Ulanove, Fotovyzh, Novokostiantynivka, Zarichne, Baranivka, Korchakivka, Shalyhyne, and Obody in the Sumy region, as well as Khrinivka in the Chernihiv region. Airstrikes hit the settlements of Pysarivka, Kyianytsia, Pustohorod, and Novokostiantynivka.
Over the past day, Ukrainian Defense Forces aviation, missile forces and artillery struck three clusters of enemy personnel and equipment.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk sectors, the Russian invaders launched two airstrikes using six guided aerial bombs and carried out 47 shelling attacks on Ukrainian troop positions and settlements, one of them using multiple-launch rocket systems.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna sector, Ukrainian forces repelled five enemy attacks. The invaders attacked near the settlements of Starytsia and Vovchanski Khutory as well as toward Izbytske.
In the Kupiansk sector, the enemy made nine attempts to improve their position, conducting offensive operations toward Radkivka.
Attempts to break through the Ukrainian defenses were repelled in the Lyman sector, where Russian forces launched nine assault actions, including near the settlements of Kolodiazi and Zarichne as well as toward Hlushchenkove, Derylove, and Lyman.
In the Sloviansk sector, the enemy launched two attacks near Ozerne and toward Mykolaivka.
In the Kramatorsk sector, the enemy conducted no offensive operations.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, seven attacks were recorded. Russian forces conducted offensive operations near Kostiantynivka and toward Novopavlivka.
In the Pokrovsk sector, the enemy launched 21 attacks. The invaders attempted to advance near Sofiivka, Dobropillia, Bilytske, and Molodetske as well as toward the settlements of Vilne, Kucheriv Yar, Hannivka, Svitle, Krasnopodillia, Serhiivka, and Muravka.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, the enemy launched one attack toward Ternove.
In the Huliaipole sector, Russian forces attacked Ukrainian positions 11 times attempting to advance toward Rizdvianka, Dolynka, Hirke, and Yehorivka.
In the Orikhiv sector, the enemy made two attempts to attack toward Pavlivka.
In the Dnipro River sector, the Russian invaders conducted one assault.
In the Volyn and Polissia sectors, no signs of the enemy forming offensive groups were detected.
As reported by Ukrinform, total combat losses of Russian forces from February 24, 2022, to October 22, 2026, reached approximately 1,571,820 personnel, including 2,250 Russian troops lost over the past day.

title: Another Azerbaijani citizen found in Armenia after illegally crossing the border, reportedly a shepherd who got lost
body: Azerbaijani shepherd crosses into Armenia A new incident has occurred on the Armenia – Azerbaijan border after an Azerbaijani citizen entered Armenian territory illegally. Armenia’s National Security Service confirmed the incident on 22 October. Yashar Ali Gasimov, born in 1968, reportedly lost his way on 19 October. “ Appropriate steps are being taken to return the Azerbaijani citizen ,” the National Security Service said. Armenian media had been reporting since 19 October that an Azerbaijani shepherd had crossed the border illegally and been taken to military police. Some reports claimed he was carrying a white flag. On 21 October, Azerbaijan’s State Border Service responded to a query from Azerbaijani media, saying that “ no such incidents have occurred in the territory under its control ”. The incident has caused concern in both countries following another recent border incident. On 1 October, Azerbaijani serviceman Nasimi Musayev was detained in Armenia. According to Armenian investigators, he illegally crossed the border, entered a house in the village of Shaki in Syunik province, opened fire and wounded a woman. Criminal proceedings have been launched against Musayev. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said he would stand trial in Armenia. He also said Azerbaijan had not requested his transfer and stressed that Yerevan and Baku had agreed to handle cases involving servicemen separately from other matters. title: Show HN: Kuron – An LLM acts as your app so you can try ideas before building
body:
Write an idea in one line — even one that would take ~50 hours to build. Within about a minute it is running on minimal screens and you can use it by hand, so you can find out whether it is worth building. Nothing is generated per idea: the LLM sets the system up, then is the system on every action.
The code is only a set of generic tools exposed over MCP — store and read data, define a screen, notify, look through the camera, listen to the mic, play and shape sound, speak, draw, set timers — plus a minimal renderer. Every tool checks the shape of its input and answers in words; the LLM corrects itself. There is no business logic, no word list, no per-idea exception in the code.
When a prototype behaves wrongly, you don’t patch it: you tell it how it should behave (“urgent patients go first”), and the request agent rewrites its own brief, screens and checks.
One English idea file for a small clinic: reception tablet, doctor’s PC, stock PC, patient’s phone and waiting-room display. Claude set it up from the idea in 65 s with 16 tool calls (about $0.41) , then acted as the system on every button. Each reply below is what it actually did; only the waiting time between steps is shortened.
Recorded on an M1 Max through Claude Code: Claude Sonnet 5.5 for setup and requests, Claude Haiku 5.5 for button presses. The screens are drawn by the same renderer the tool uses. The raw recording is replay.json .
A prototype where the LLM does everything is dangerously convincing. So during setup the LLM also estimates, for every action, how a shippable version would do it — ordinary code , a model , an outside service , or not yet possible — with an error rate and a delay. Flip Ideal → Existing tech and the system behaves that way: late, sometimes wrong, sound leaking past the earphones.
After you have tried it, kuron turns what the system actually did into a spec — data, screens, golden examples taken from real tool calls, this table — and an implementation plan for a coding agent.
UI and app generators (Lovable, v0, Figma Make…) build the screens and the code behind them, and prototypes usually fake the judgement with fixed data. kuron builds the behaviour : the face stays minimal, while the judgement, the data and the hand-offs between roles really happen.
Open kuron on claude.ai . It starts with the clinic above already set up; press any button, ask for a change, flip to existing tech, or write your own idea. It runs on your own Claude account (you are asked once), so you need to be signed in to claude.ai. The browser version has no microphone and runs timers when you press them.
Needs Node.js 20+ and Claude Code (logged in). No npm dependencies.
Pick an example — a task list, an IoT fridge with a phone app, a sales deal desk, earphones that let only important sounds through — or press + New and write your own idea in one line. Each example sets itself up the first time you open it (about a minute).
--preset local runs everything on Ollama with tool calling instead of Claude. The tools are a plain MCP server, so any MCP client can drive the same system: node bin/kuron.js hands --url http://127.0.0.1:4870 .

title: ‘Red Line Crossed’: Germany Raises Russian Sabotage Threat to ‘Significant’ for First Time
body:
Germany’s armed forces have classified the threat of Russian sabotage against its troops and facilities as “significant” for the first time amid rising concerns over Russian hybrid warfare.
The classification is the second-highest level on the internal threat scale of the Germany’s military, news outlet Süddeutsche Zeitung reported on Wednesday.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The reclassification was triggered by the discovery in mid-September of a crashed drone carrying high explosives near the Wunstorf air base in Lower Saxony, according to the newspaper, citing an internal military document.
Germany’s defense ministry spokesperson confirmed the assessment, saying “We are noting that we face a significant sabotage threat overall for the Bundeswehr,” Germany’s armed forces.
The military report, reviewed by Süddeutsche Zeitung, states that Russia had crossed “a previously anticipated red line of harmful intent involving kinetic and/or lethal effects” against Germany and the Bundeswehr through the use of weaponized drones.
Last month, Berlin said Russia was responsible for the attempted drone attack at the Leipzig airport in August.
An explosives-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft used for military supplies at the airport in eastern Germany, a key hub for NATO and Kyiv.
According to the German military assessment, investigators believe that while similar drones were used in both the Wunstorf and Leipzig incidents, the Wunstorf drone was aimed at Bundeswehr aircraft, whereas the Leipzig incident targeted civilian cargo aircraft.
The report also cited a pattern of suspected Russian reconnaissance across Germany, including drone overflights of the Arrow 3 missile defense site in Saxony-Anhalt, as well as a camouflaged camera found filming a strategically important railway station in Minden, Westphalia.
Intelligence services expect the situation to worsen in the short term, with further actions likely in the near future, the document noted.
The defense ministry spokesperson said preventive measures were being tailored to individual sites and could range from increased guard patrols to additional technical security such as infrared ⁠cameras and fence surveillance systems.
Europe has been on high alert in recent weeks following intelligence assessments warning that Russia could test NATO through actions ranging from sabotage, cyberattacks and drone activity to a limited military operation.

title: Future German F128 Frigates To Receive MSI-DS Seahawk Light Gun Systems
body: The German Navy is in the process of procuring eight F128 anti-submarine frigates in two production batches, replacing the aborted F126-effort. The F128-program intends rapid introduction into the German Navy from 2029, in order to compensate for delays resulting from the cancellation of F126. The equipment-contract for MSI-DS further reflects this urgency, as the MSI Seahawk 30 mm gun system is commercially available for quick integration into F128. Germany previously ordered this design as part of the F123B frigate modernisation. Information published on a British investment platform reveals that UK-based MSI Defence Systems Ltd has secured a contract worth £ 29.7 million, approximately US$ 40 million in relation to the new German frigate program. MSI-DS will supply twelve DS30M naval gun systems, also termed Seahawk DS by the company, equipping four F128 frigates. The publication does not specify a delivery timeframe, only stating that MSI-DS expects “Delivery of the systems (…) to take place in accordance with the programme schedule over the coming years.” Follow-up order for more MSI-DS weapon stations likely The order volume likely relates to the procurement structure of F128 for the German Navy. Germany after parliamentary approval initially ordered four F128-frigates in July. The German parliament in the beginning of October then approved the second batch for another four frigates. Therefore, a follow-up contract for MSI supplying gun systems for the remaining F128 frigates in the near future appears plausible. MSI DS30M-based Mark 38 Mod 4 30mm naval gun system on display on MSI Defence stand at Sea Air Space 2022. The MSI-DS DS30M is a remote controlled weapons mount which can accommodate light autocannons in the 25-40 mm calibre range. Additionally, the design can fit a 7.62 mm machine gun or missile launchers in a co-axial configuration, if so desired. MSI offers three different turret configurations dubbed DS Remote, DS A1 and DS A2, depending on the sensor and fire control-specification. The design most widely adapted by multiple navies is a version using the 30 mm Mk 44 Bushmaster II cannon. The United States since 2022 is acquiring the MSI-design under the designation Mk 38 Mod 4, with several design changes, including accommodation of a co-axial M2 .50 BMG heavy machine gun. German Navy phasing out older autocannons due to drone threat The choice of the MSI-design follows a decision by the German Navy in 2024 to purchase the 30 mm gun system for the comprehensive modernisation of the older F123 Brandenburg-class anti-submarine frigates. On F123 the MSI Seahawk will replace the existing Rheinmetall MLG 27 “Marineleichtgeschuetz”. The selection of MSI-DS for F128 further underscores a previously reported emphasis on significant commonality between F123B and the new frigates. The MLG 27, with a 27 mm gun derived from the Mauser BK27 fitted to a wide range of fighter jets, established itself as the primary light gun system for the German Navy since introduction in the early 2000s. The weapon then replaced various outdated light autocannons onboard both combatants and auxiliaries of the German Navy. However, in the wake of deployments in the Red Sea and with the wider emergence of drone-based airborne and surface threats the German Navy considers the MLG 27 obsolete. Instead, the service seeks a replacement enabling modern ammunition choices such as air burst munitions, and more advanced sensor- and fire control-capabilities. Rheinmetall MLG 27 weapons mount onboard Elbe-class tender in 2007. Image Wikipedia/public domain (author Rebell18190). Rheinmetall will likely consider the selection of the MSI Seahawk a further blow to company-efforts promoting its own solutions replacing the MLG 27, notably the Sea Snake 30 mm gun mount the company previously sold to Brazil and Sweden. Whether the German Navy will further expand the adaption of the MSI Seahawk DS beyond the F123B- and F128 frigate-fleet remains to be seen. The post Future German F128 Frigates To Receive MSI-DS Seahawk Light Gun Systems appeared first on Naval News .

title: Russian Attacks Kill 4 Civilians, Injure at Least a Dozen Across Ukraine in Overnight Drone Strike
body:
Russian attacks killed four civilians and injured at least 14 others in Donetsk , Kharkiv and Chernihiv regions over the past 24 hours, while overnight drone strikes sparked fires and damaged civilian property and businesses across several regions, local officials and emergency services reported on Thursday, Oct. 22.
Vadym Filashkin, head of the Donetsk Regional Military Administration (OVA), said Russian forces killed two residents of the region on Oct. 21, in Druzhkivka and Kramatorsk. Another nine people were injured over the same period.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv OVA, reported a 42-year-old woman was killed by Russian shelling in the village of Lymanivka in Lozova district. Four other people were injured, including boys aged 10 and 13. Medics provided the injured with the necessary assistance.
Vyacheslav Chaus, head of the Chernihiv OVA, said Russian forces attacked an enterprise in Chernihiv twice with drones on Oct. 21. A 61-year-old man was killed in the second strike, while a 54-year-old man suffered acoustic barotrauma.
Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov reported several Russian drone strikes across the city, including attacks on residential areas and other civilian infrastructure.
At around 2:16 a.m. on Thursday, a Russian jet-powered drone struck a residential area in the Slobidskyi district, setting an outbuilding on fire and damaging several private homes. No casualties were reported at the time.
A strike was also recorded in the Osnovianskyi district, in the central part of the city, with the impact initially under assessment.
In the Kholodnohirskyi district, a jet-powered Shahed drone struck a parking lot, setting several private vehicles on fire. Emergency crews and municipal services were dispatched to the scene.
At 7:47 a.m., Terekhov reported another drone strike in the Osnovianskyi district. The drone hit the ninth floor of an office building next to residential buildings. No casualties or fires were reported following that strike.
At 8:48 a.m., the mayor reported another Russian strike on the same district.
In Sumy, a Russian first-person view (FPV) drone struck a vehicle, sparking a fire and damaging other vehicles, according to the State Emergency Service (DSNS).
The blast wave shattered windows in a five-story residential building. Despite the threat of further attacks, rescuers extinguished the fire.
One person was reportedly injured, according to preliminary information.
Russian forces also attacked Kropyvnytskyi district in Kirovohrad region on the evening of Oct. 21, setting warehouse facilities on fire, the DSNS reported.
The large scale of the fire and the threat of follow-up strikes complicated firefighting efforts. Rescuers eventually contained the blaze and remained at the scene.
According to preliminary information, no one was killed or injured in the attack.

title: Announcing DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS “Cinnamon Teal”
body:
TL;DR: The DuckDB team is happy to announce that today we're releasing DuckDB version 2.0.0 LTS, codenamed “Cinnamon Teal” (Spatula cyanoptera). This is our biggest feature release so far, and it ships a polished version of the Quack protocol, asynchronous I/O, a first-class VARIANT type, agent mode, triggers, an extensible SQL parser, and much more, built from close to 20,000 commits since DuckDB 1.5.
Update 2.0.0 packed so many features that we published a followup blog post titled “Gems of DuckDB 2.0.0” .
We are proud to release DuckDB 2.0.0, codenamed “Cinnamon Teal” after the Spatula cyanoptera , a strikingly reddish-brown duck found in the western Americas.
While DuckDB 1.0 was all about stability and backward compatibility, DuckDB 2.0 is above all a feature release. In this blog post, we summarize the highlights and then walk through the breaking changes and how to migrate. We showcased many of the new features in “A Preview of DuckDB v2.0” , which covers each one in more depth. For the complete release notes, see the release page on GitHub .
Tip To install the new version, please visit the installation page .
With this release, there are currently three DuckDB lines available. DuckDB 2.0 is a long-term support (LTS) release with support until at least October 2027. The previous LTS release, version 1.4, is still supported until November 17, 2026. To ensure a smooth transition and allow sufficient time for testing, we extended the support period of DuckDB 1.5 until March 2027, effectively also turning it into an LTS release. For details, see the release calendar .
To find your way around the documentation for all of the new features, we also published a “What's New in the Docs for 2.0” page that links each feature below to its documentation.
DuckDB has been an in-process database since day one. In DuckDB 1.5.3 , released in May, we introduced the Quack protocol that lets you run DuckDB in a traditional client-server setup, along with the quack extension , which implements DuckDB's native protocol, so any DuckDB process can serve its databases .
DuckDB 2.0.0 ships a polished version of the Quack protocol with substantial performance and stability improvements. It also introduces the new CONNECT statement that allows attaching and switching to a remote database in a single command for better ergonomics:
For simplicity, this example runs the server and the client on the same machine. By default, the server only listens on localhost . To accept connections from other machines, keep the server on localhost and put it behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy . The allow_other_hostname option , which exposes the server directly, is only meant for testing.
The CONNECT statement is not limited to Quack: it points your session at any remote database that supports it , including PostgreSQL and MySQL. For these, the new remote pushdown optimizer ships queries directly to the remote server instead of pulling tables over the wire.
The CLI also has shortcuts for setting up a Quack client-server pair: the new -serve and -connect arguments start a Quack server or connect to one directly from the command line:
DuckDB 2.0 introduces asynchronous I/O for reading Parquet and CSV files, as well as DuckDB's native storage format . The I/O layer now scales independently from the query processing layer, issuing reads in the background and keeping multiple requests in flight. This means far more parallelism for remote reads and dramatically faster queries on object storage such as s3:// .
We described the design in detail in a dedicated blog post . In that post, we showed the network throughput over the course of a query with and without asynchronous I/O:
Network throughput. Higher utilization and shorter runtime are better.
The VARIANT type stores semi-structured, schema-less data such as JSON while keeping the performance of columnar execution. So you can think of it as JSON on steroids: a VARIANT column can store differently shaped data in every row, but unlike JSON it is not a text format.
DuckDB 1.5 already introduced VARIANT , but DuckDB 2.0 fully integrates it. DuckDB 2.0 detects the common structure in your data and “shreds” it, so it compresses well and executes fast. The pipeline works end to end, from shredded execution straight out of storage to shredded VARIANT reading and writing for Parquet, backed by a family of variant_* functions . For example:
Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor increasingly drive the DuckDB CLI on their users' behalf. The 2.0 CLI detects when it is being run by an agent and switches to agent mode : it prints compact Markdown tables instead of padded boxes, says clearly when a result was truncated, stops runaway queries early, and reports errors as JSON.
Long-running SQL queries report their expected cost prior to running, so the agent can decide whether to wait. In our experiments on TPC-H, agent mode cut the amount of DuckDB output the model had to read by 59%. You can turn it on for manual testing using the -agent flag or instruct your agent to turn it off using the -no-agent flag.
DuckDB has always used a parser derived from PostgreSQL's. In 2.0, our own modern, extensible PEG-based parser , which debuted as an opt-in feature in DuckDB 1.5 , becomes the default. Extensions can now hook into the grammar itself (an idea we first explored in our research on runtime-extensible parsers ), so expect extensions that expose entirely new SQL syntax. Error messages now come with precise source locations. For details, see the PEG parser documentation . The new parser is designed to be compatible with the old one, apart from a few deliberate changes listed in the migration guide . If you notice any other differences, please file an issue. In the meantime, you can switch back to the old parser using the legacy_parser extension by running SET enable_legacy_parser = true ; .
The old parser had served DuckDB since its first commit in 2018. Its grammar was generated with YACC/Bison, which produces an LALR(1) parser, so as DuckSQL grew, even small additions could collide with existing rules and raise shift/reduce or reduce/reduce conflicts. A PEG grammar avoids this by trying alternatives in the order they are written, so adding syntax no longer risks breaking unrelated rules. Python itself moved to a PEG-based parser in version 3.9 for the same flexibility.
DuckDB 2.0 ships a revamped C API v2 , which is considerably more powerful than its predecessor and exposes components such as file systems and table functions to extensions. Before marking it as stable, we would like to test it in the field, so please give it a try and send us your feedback !
You can also register and host your own trusted extension repositories, so an organization can host and sign its own extensions and have them install and load just like the built-in ones:
A repository is a name, a URL prefix, and one or more RSA public keys that are trusted to sign the extensions served from it. The prefix can point at anything DuckDB can read: a local path, https , s3 , you name it. At CREATE time, DuckDB fetches the repository's public keys and pins them into the repository definition, printing each key's SHA-256 fingerprint so you can compare it against one published out of band.
This feature is still a work in progress and its syntax may change in future releases. For more details, see the Extension Repositories page .
DuckDB's core extensions are also shipping several new features, fixes, and performance optimizations. These are too numerous to all list here, so we only highlight a few of them and will cover them in dedicated blog posts in the coming weeks:
DuckDB 2.0 delivers triggers: the CREATE TRIGGER statement with BEFORE and AFTER triggers, FOR EACH ROW and FOR EACH STATEMENT , transition tables via REFERENCING OLD/NEW TABLE , multiple triggers per event, RETURNING on triggered tables, and DROP TRIGGER . The classic use case is audit tables, where a trigger records what changed in response to a table modification. Some combinations, such as BEFORE ... FOR EACH ROW and UPDATE ... FOR EACH ROW triggers, are not yet supported; see the limitations .
Triggers can also maintain materialized views incrementally! For example, to keep track of the average age of people per nationality in a table age_statistics , you can use two triggers – one for insert and another for delete operations – and store the sum and the count alongside the average.
On insertion, we aggregate the new rows per nationality and merge them into age_statistics , adding a row for each new nationality:
On deletion, we subtract the deleted rows and drop a nationality once its last person has left:
Triggers bring us one step closer to materialized views, a long-standing item in the “future work” section of our roadmap .
As always, DuckDB's friendly SQL dialect keeps growing. A few favorites from this release cycle:
There is more: DuckDB 2.0.0 supports the SQL-standard FETCH FIRST and allows UNNEST in the GROUP BY clause . It also ensures well-defined MERGE and UPDATE ... FROM semantics for cases when multiple rows are matched.
DuckDB 2.0 comes with a small set of breaking changes. For most users, upgrading is straightforward, but complex deployments running many DuckDB processes need more care. The storage format is the most likely source of problems: DuckDB versions before 2.0 cannot read database files created by DuckDB 2.0. DuckDB 2.0 can still read and write your existing database files, and these remain readable by older versions. We recommend testing 2.0.0 on a shadow system before switching production over. And, if your workload is mission-critical, you may want to wait for the first patch release, coming in November .
For the full details, see the migration guide .
Following DuckDB's long stint on C++11, DuckDB 2.0 now requires a C++17 compiler .
We also switched to Clang as the default compiler for our release builds. On Linux and macOS, both DuckDB and its core extensions are built with Clang. On Windows, the CLI is built with Clang, while most core extensions are still built with MSVC. We may move more Windows builds to Clang in the future, but this requires further changes.
Timezone-aware timestamps, calendars, and collations have always been powered by the ICU library. In 2.0, the ICU library is gone entirely: the icu extension now implements timezones, calendars, and collations itself, with the timezone data built directly from the IANA database and compressed down to around 45 kB.
Everything keeps working exactly as before, and the native implementation is also faster. If you find any issues, please let us know !
The old single-arrow lambda syntax ( x -> x + 1 ) is now disabled by default. Use the Python-style syntax instead:
You can temporarily re-enable the old syntax with SET lambda_syntax = 'enable_single_arrow' ; . Both the flag and the single-arrow syntax will be removed entirely in v2.1.
The amalgamation build , which bundles DuckDB's entire source code into a single header and a single source file, is now deprecated. The amalgamation has grown too large to be realistically useful in most cases.
We are gradually phasing out osx_amd64 from the list of fully supported platforms . For the time being, DuckDB and core extensions are still built and supported, but community extensions are only built for this platform on a best-effort basis. DuckDB 2.1 will stop supporting osx_amd64 .
These were a few highlights, but there are many more features and improvements in this release. There have been almost 20,000 commits by many contributors since DuckDB 1.5, shipping smaller features as well as performance and usability improvements. The full release notes can be found on GitHub .
We would like to thank our community for the detailed issue reports and feedback that have driven this release, and our special thanks go to our contributors!

title: Russian ballistic attack leaves one dead, 22 injured, causes damage in six Kyiv districts
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said this in a post on Facebook .
“Since the evening of October 21, Russian forces have launched ballistic strikes on six districts of the capital. Fires broke out and damage was reported,” the statement said.
In the Dniprovskyi district, one person was killed and a child was hospitalized. Residential buildings and cars were damaged, while residential and non-residential buildings caught fire. Five other people were injured.
In the Darnytskyi district, transport infrastructure was damaged. There were no casualties.
In the Sviatoshynskyi district, a non-residential building and a restaurant complex caught fire. The fire, which covered an area of 1,100 square meters, was extinguished.
In the Obolonskyi district, non-residential buildings were damaged and fires broke out. Two people were injured. The fires were extinguished.
In the Pecherskyi district, buildings, ambulances and a monastery were damaged. Eight people were injured, including three children.
In the Holosiivskyi district, six people were injured after a non-residential building was hit.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russia launched a ballistic strike on Kyiv overnight on October 22. At the time, 15 people were reported injured, including two children.
