Local media reported that when she confronted the manager, he acknowledged that the phone belonged to him. The incident was initially discussed in reviews on the restaurant’s Google page, where the restaurant said the manager had been dismissed.
● A video circulating on social media showing a man publicly humiliating his wife on a bus has sparked widespread outrage. A female passenger intervened, leading to a heated argument, and forced the couple to leave the bus. Police became involved and arrested the man. She filmed the incident on her mobile phone, accompanied the footage with profanity, and later posted the video online. Both social media users and investigators considered her words and actions potentially disruptive to public order. The investigation is ongoing.
● Azerbaijan has called on the UN and other relevant international organisations to step up their involvement in the search for missing persons, the development of forensic expertise and support for their families. Speaking at a meeting of a UN General Assembly committee, Azerbaijan’s representative Shahriyar Hajiyev said that more than 4,000 Azerbaijanis remain missing in connection with the former conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia. Since the end of the conflict, 32 mass graves containing the remains of 253 people have been discovered. Hajiyev reiterated his call for Armenia to open its archives, disclose information about burial sites and collect witness testimonies so that families can learn the fate of their missing relatives.
● The Azerbaijani public association Families of Missing Persons in Karabakh is holding a peaceful demonstration outside the European Parliament in Brussels, calling for the fate of more than 4,000 Azerbaijanis who went missing during the first Karabakh war to be established. Participants displayed photographs and personal belongings of the missing and urged Armenia to provide access to its archives and information about mass burial sites.
● Prison sentences have been sought for two more civil society activists. The prosecutor is seeking 12 years in prison for Imran Aliyev, head of the Meclis.info platform, and 11 years for Elgiz Gahraman on charges including smuggling, money laundering and tax evasion, as well as other alleged offences. Both categorically deny the charges and say they are being persecuted for criticising the authorities. The prosecutor’s closing statement was interrupted after a third defendant, Tamilla Musayeva, became unwell and lost consciousness. The hearing at the Baku Court of Grave Crimes was postponed until 2 November.
Since late 2023, more than 30 journalists and activists have been arrested in Azerbaijan on smuggling charges. The defendants say the cases are linked to their professional activities, while the authorities deny that there are political prisoners in the country. According to human rights organisations, 328 political prisoners are currently held in Azerbaijani jails.
● The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) has requested explanations from the Azerbaijani government over a complaint filed by NIDA movement activist Elmir Abbasov, who was sentenced to 12 years in prison in the Toplum TV case. Abbasov was previously accused of drug possession. He maintains that the drugs were planted on him and that his arrest was punishment for accusing President Ilham Aliyev of corruption in Facebook posts. The activist also alleges that he was subjected to police brutality and that his complaints were not effectively investigated.
Arrests in the Toplum TV case began in March 2024. The defendants were initially charged with smuggling, but the charges were later expanded. All the activists and journalists deny wrongdoing and say their arrests were politically motivated. On 27 July this year, sentences were handed down: Akif Gurbanov, head of the Institute for Democratic Initiatives, and Ruslan Izzatli, a co-founder of the institute, received 15 years in prison. Toplum TV co-founder Alasgar Mammadli and activist Ali Zeynal were sentenced to 14 years. Institute for Democratic Initiatives staff members Ramil Babayev and Ilkin Amrakhov, along with Toplum TV video editor Mushfig Jabbar, received 13-year sentences. Journalists Farid Ismayilov and Elmir Abbasov were sentenced to 11 years, 11 months and 28 days. The court also ordered the confiscation of their cars and apartments.
● BP Azerbaijan has announced that the $2.9 billion Shah Deniz Compression project, designed to increase gas production, has entered the offshore construction phase. BP has installed four piles with the largest diameter the company has ever used in the Caspian Sea. The project is expected to yield an additional 50 billion cubic metres of gas and 25 million barrels of condensate. Construction is scheduled for completion in 2029.
● Hungary has invested around $2 billion in Azerbaijan’s economy. Hungarian companies MOL and MVM have acquired stakes in major oil and natural gas fields, while MVM is also a shareholder in the Shafag solar power plant. Hungarian Ambassador to Azerbaijan Tamás Torma announced the figures, noting that the two countries have maintained an expanded strategic partnership since 2023. They cooperate in energy, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and water management, including through the green energy corridor project. Torma also highlighted Azerbaijan’s contribution to Europe’s energy security and its role in international transport projects.
● Cargo transit through Azerbaijan has reached a five-year high. Since the beginning of the year, transit volumes have increased by 14.5%, exceeding 12 million tonnes. Container traffic through the country’s ports has risen by 29%.
● President Ilham Aliyev has signed a decree establishing Karabakh National Park, covering 88,418 hectares of state land in the Aghdara, Khojaly, Kalbajar, Shusha and Lachin districts. The stated aim is to protect biodiversity and the natural heritage of territories that Azerbaijan says were liberated from Armenian occupation during the Second Karabakh War of 2020.
● The National Cybersecurity Agency has warned of widespread cyber fraud targeting, among others, relatives of government officials. Scammers posing as government employees and law enforcement officers use caller ID spoofing, WhatsApp, psychological pressure and AI-generated voice impersonation to steal money and personal data. The agency urged the public to verify information through official channels and never share sensitive information with strangers.
● The Foreign Ministry has advised Azerbaijani citizens to refrain from travelling to France amid an increase in unrest, violence and civil disobedience in the country in recent days.
● Azerbaijan’s Prosecutor General’s Office has placed seven people living and working in Turkey on an international wanted list over allegations of publicly calling for the violent seizure of power in Azerbaijan, a change to the constitutional order and the incitement of religious hatred in the country. Those named in the case include Haksöz author Rıdvan Kaya, Değişim TV presenter Zekeriya Ceran and Analiz Merkezi founder Fatih Tezcan. According to investigators, the seven published relevant material on social media and online platforms between 25 September and 18 October. Kaya and Ceran also spoke at rallies outside Azerbaijani diplomatic missions in Istanbul and Ankara. A court in Baku ordered all seven to be arrested in absentia. The authorities are using international legal assistance mechanisms, including cooperation with the relevant Turkish authorities.
● The Azerbaijan Press Council accused several Turkish media outlets and social media users of spreading biased and inaccurate information about Azerbaijan, including claims that the country had introduced a hijab ban in schools. According to the council, the school uniform rules have been taken out of context and portrayed as an issue of religious confrontation, with old and fake photographs and videos also being used. “The published material openly crosses the boundaries of criticism and freedom of speech by giving a platform to dangerous calls for the violent change of Azerbaijan’s constitutional order and the unlawful seizure of power,” the statement said. The Press Council urged Turkish media to avoid spreading disinformation that could damage relations between the two countries, which are based on the principle of “one nation, two states”.
● Detained Meydan TV journalist Aynur Elgunash has finally been transferred to a clinic, her lawyer said. Her family and friends had been urging the authorities to arrange medical treatment for some time, citing serious concerns about her health. According to her lawyer, Elgunash had undergone 17 operations on her leg and was preparing for another surgery when she was arrested. Her most urgent health problem is now related to her kidney, which requires immediate surgery, the lawyer said. The authorities have not commented on the situation.
Aynur and 11 other journalists and activists have been arrested in the “Meydan TV case” on charges including currency smuggling. They all deny wrongdoing and say the case is linked to their critical reporting on the authorities.
● Military representatives from NATO member states and partner countries conducted a joint assessment in Baku to determine whether Azerbaijan’s military capabilities meet alliance standards, the Swedish Embassy in Azerbaijan reported. The process is aimed at improving interoperability and expanding defence cooperation. Among those who visited Baku were John Mead, Deputy Commander of NATO’s Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum, and Air Commodore Jeff Brock. They held meetings with the leadership of Azerbaijan’s General Staff.
● A delegation from the United Arab Emirates (UAE), led by Chief of Staff of the UAE Armed Forces Lieutenant General Issa Saif bin Ablan Al Mazrouei, is visiting Azerbaijan. He met Azerbaijani Defence Minister Zakir Hasanov and Chief of the General Staff of the Azerbaijani Army Karim Valiyev. The discussions focused on expanding military cooperation, regional security and the joint air-tactical exercise “Falcon Encounter 2026”, currently taking place in Azerbaijan. The delegation also visited the Azerbaijani Air Force’s Joint Air Operations Centre.
● NVIDIA, Apple and Microsoft topped the State Oil Fund of Azerbaijan’s technology stock portfolio in 2025. Over the year, the fund’s investments in telecommunications and IT company shares rose by 18.8%, reaching nearly 9 billion manats (around $5.3 billion). Seven technology companies featured among the fund’s ten largest stock investments, compared with five a year earlier.
● Czech company Škoda Group has said it is ready to become a key partner in modernising public transport in Baku, other Azerbaijani cities and territories regained by Azerbaijan, according to Roman Sorkin, the company’s vice-president for sales in Central Asia and the South Caucasus. The company sees the Baku Metro as a strategic project and is also interested in developing tram systems and light rail, as well as supplying electric traction vehicles for the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route. Read more here.
● Cooperation between Azerbaijan and Ukraine in education, law enforcement and regional ties was discussed during a series of meetings involving Azerbaijani Ambassador to Ukraine Seymour Mardaliyev and Ukraine’s ministers of education, interior and justice. Mardaliyev also met the mayor of Ivano-Frankivsk and the head of the Ivano-Frankivsk regional military administration.
● Another video about the 2020 Second Karabakh War has been published on Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s account on X. The video shows footage from the more than 30-year period of Armenian occupation of Karabakh and surrounding Azerbaijani territories, including the mass displacement of local Azerbaijanis during the First Karabakh War in the early 1990s, as well as the destruction and desecration of mosques. It also features Armenian leaders who supported the occupation over the years. Footage of meetings at the UN and EU institutions accompanies a narrative accusing the international community of inaction and applying double standards towards Azerbaijan. The video then shows scenes from the Second Karabakh War and states that Azerbaijan restored its territorial integrity on its own. Aliyev goes on to discuss the peace process, saying that Azerbaijan did not seek revenge for the suffering of its people but instead offered Armenia peace, which, he says, remains fragile and needs to be protected and strengthened.
● Azerbaijan exported goods worth $23.45 million to Armenia from January to September 2026, while its indirect imports from Armenia amounted to just $96,500, according to the State Customs Committee.
● Since the beginning of the year, Georgia has increased its imports of fuel and lubricants from Azerbaijan by more than 23%. Azerbaijan is now Georgia’s second-largest supplier of these products.
● Since the beginning of the year, 25 main telecommunications lines with a total length of more than 1,000 kilometres have been built in the Karabakh region, state-owned Aztelecom reported. Telecommunications infrastructure has been established in 11 cities and 54 villages and settlements, with 12,267 subscribers connected to the network.
● Football fans are preparing for this evening’s match in Baku between Azerbaijani club Sabah and Germany’s Borussia Dortmund, part of the third round of the UEFA Champions League’s league phase in the 2026/27 season. The match will kick off at 20:45. Free buses to the stadium will be provided from different parts of the city at the initiative of Sabah FC and with the support of the Land Transport Agency.
● Popular Formula TV presenter and journalist Vakho Sanaia has been sentenced to 30 days of administrative detention. The Interior Ministry accused him of publishing social media posts and videos containing obscene insults directed at political figures. Sanaia was arrested at his home after failing to attend the court hearing, which he had described as absurd. The Media Advocacy Coalition said the judicial system was being used to silence critical voices and punish journalists. Read more here.
● European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand said in Brussels that the EU was closely monitoring the lawsuit filed by Georgia’s ruling party with the Constitutional Court seeking to ban five opposition parties. He said this case, together with legislative amendments, pointed to the alarming use of the judicial system for political purposes and threatened fundamental freedoms and political pluralism. The European Commission is calling on the Georgian authorities to immediately release politicians, journalists and activists who have been unjustly detained and repeal what it calls “repressive legislation”.
● Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili named the lawmakers who will defend Georgian Dream’s position before the Constitutional Court: Archil Gorduladze, Giorgi Kakhiani, Tengiz Sharmanashvili and Tornike Cheishvili. In their lawsuit, 88 ruling party MPs are seeking to ban five parties: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia – Lelo, the Federalists and Gakharia for Georgia. Hearings are scheduled for 21–23 October, while the opposition has announced plans to hold rallies in Tbilisi and Batumi.
● The case against former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili, who has been convicted of corruption, has been referred to court for consideration on its merits. The Prosecutor’s Office has brought additional charges against him, accusing him of receiving a large bribe as part of a group. The offence carries a prison sentence of 11 to 15 years. The court rejected as evidence a public letter from Gharibashvili in which he alleged that former Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze was involved in the case. Gharibashvili has already been sentenced to five years in prison under a plea agreement in a separate case involving the laundering of illicit income.
● The Prosecutor’s Office is negotiating a plea agreement with Zurab Chavchanidze, who was sentenced to five years in prison in connection with the alleged attempt to seize the Presidential Administration on 4 October 2025. Under the proposed agreement, Chavchanidze would serve one year and one month in prison, followed by a two-year suspended sentence. If the Tbilisi Court of Appeals approves the agreement, he will be released from prison in early November. Anton Vardanidze, who was convicted in the same case, has also asked the Prosecutor’s Office to conclude a plea agreement.
● Georgia’s exports totalled $6.15 billion in January–September, up 19.6% from the same period last year, according to the National Statistics Office of Georgia (Geostat). Imports rose by 5.3% to $14.38 billion, leaving a trade deficit of $8.23 billion. China, Russia and Turkey were Georgia’s largest export markets, while crude oil and petroleum products were among its main export goods.
● Georgian wine exports fell by 0.6% in value and 6% in volume in January–September, reaching $188.7 million. According to Geostat, Russia still accounted for 63.4% of the total value of wine exports. Poland and Ukraine ranked second and third.
● Enguri Hydropower Plant has prepared a report on the large-scale power outages that affected the country on 24–25 July. The report says the control systems and voltage regulators of four of the plant’s generators failed to operate properly. The company had previously signed a €560,000 contract with Voith Hydro to upgrade these systems without holding a tender. The State Security Service is investigating the causes of the outages as a possible act of sabotage. The findings have not yet been made public.
● Internally displaced people who have not received housing or financial compensation from the state can apply for compensation of 10,000 lari (around $3,000) per family member. Applications are being accepted at Public Service Halls and community centres until 2 November. Payments are to be made within 45 days at the latest.
● Seasonal flu vaccination will begin across Georgia on 21 October. According to the Ministry of Health, the country has purchased 200,000 doses of the French-made Vaxigrip vaccine. Vaccination is free for all citizens.
● A meeting chaired by the prime minister discussed progress on the Academic City programme. This major state project aims to create a unified technology hub bringing together universities, research organisations and other educational institutions in a modern environment. Minister of Education, Science, Culture and Sport Zhanna Andreasyan presented the concept of consolidating higher education institutions and outlined plans to cooperate with leading international universities in specific areas of the programme. She also presented an estimate of the costs of developing the necessary infrastructure.
● New appointments have been made at the Ministry of Defence. Taron Yeghiazaryan has been appointed head of the Armament and Technical Support Department, while Norayr Mkrtchyan will head the Armed Forces’ Moral and Psychological Support Department.
● Construction waste was found to have been dumped into Lake Sevan using heavy machinery. The incident damaged 580 square metres of a specially protected area and polluted 33 square metres of the lake’s water surface. The damage is estimated at 946,404 drams (around $3,000). A report of a suspected crime has been sent to the Prosecutor General’s Office.
● Another lawsuit seeking compensation for damage caused to the state by unpaid taxes has been upheld. Once the court rulings take effect, 39,128,615 drams (around $110,000) will be confiscated from an individual.
● A silver commemorative coin dedicated to the natural monument known as the “Symphony of Stones” will be issued into circulation today. Located in the Azat River gorge near the ancient Garni Temple, around 30 kilometres from Yerevan, the formation consists of symmetrical basalt columns that resemble the pipes of an organ. The site is included on the list of specially protected natural areas.
● Police have uncovered cannabis cultivation and drug production on a plot of land near the home of a 37-year-old local resident.
● Holding COP17, the UN’s international environmental conference, in Armenia is raising the country’s international profile and boosting tourism, Economy Minister Gevorg Papoyan told journalists. According to the minister, the number of flights to Armenia has increased sharply during the conference, and an additional 10,000–15,000 tourists are expected to visit the country. Papoyan also said that events of this kind help improve the investment climate and create opportunities to attract new investment.
● Azerbaijan has exported goods worth $23.45 million to Armenia since the beginning of the year, while indirect imports from Armenia into Azerbaijan totalled just $96,500, according to Azerbaijan’s State Customs Committee.
PHOTO: Two young bezoar goats, a species listed in Armenia’s Red Book, were found and seized from the yard of a house in the village of Tsakhkunk. The animals were estimated to be around four to five months old: one male and one female. The damage caused to wildlife is estimated at 3 million drams (around $8,300). The Environmental Protection and Mining Inspection Body has referred the case to the Investigative Committee.
● The 17th UN Biodiversity Conference has opened in Yerevan. COP17 will run from 19 to 30 October. The event’s official opening ceremony has taken place. Following the high-level presidential summit “Leaders for Nature”, held on 16 October, world leaders have already adopted the Yerevan Declaration. It reaffirms countries’ political commitment to deepening international cooperation to restore ecosystems and protect nature.
● Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called on the international community to move from declared commitments to concrete action to preserve biodiversity. He made the statement at the opening ceremony of the 17th COP17 conference in Yerevan. “Let Yerevan mark a new stage of political determination. Let this be the moment when we move from words to action, from division to cooperation,” Pashinyan said.
● The former “Public Council of Karabakh” expressed outrage over remarks made by UN Secretary-General António Guterres at COP17, which is being held in Yerevan. “Guterres spoke about the rights of indigenous peoples, biodiversity conservation and the responsibility of the international community, but did not mention the forced displacement of the indigenous Armenian population of Artsakh or their right to return to their homeland. We condemn this silence. In September 2023, more than 100,000 Armenians from Artsakh were forced to leave their homeland as a result of Azerbaijan’s military actions and the prolonged blockade that preceded them. How can one speak about protecting the rights of indigenous peoples while in a country that has provided refuge to tens of thousands of people forcibly expelled from their homeland, yet ignore their right to return?” the statement said.
● UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany, who is in Armenia to attend the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), visited the Zvartnots Temple, which is included on the UNESCO World Heritage List. El-Enany stressed the importance of proper management of historical monuments and their use for cultural and educational purposes.
● Asoghik Karapetyan, Director of the Museums and Archives of the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin and a member of Armenia’s National Commission for UNESCO, expressed outrage that a visit to Zvartnots Temple had been arranged for the UNESCO Director-General, but not to the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin. “If it was possible to visit Zvartnots, why not visit the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin? Why not showcase the magnificent, fully restored and lavishly decorated cathedral? It was the nomination of the cathedral that was included on the UNESCO World Heritage List, whereas Zvartnots Temple was only part of that nomination. Such a decision is a clear indication of a lack of state consciousness,” Karapetyan said.
● Armenia’s delegation to the United Nations took part in an interactive dialogue with UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, held as part of the UN General Assembly. It was emphasised that Armenia remains firmly committed to promoting lasting and sustainable peace in the region. The delegation also stressed that resolving humanitarian issues is crucial to building trust and promoting reconciliation, particularly in relation to detained persons and missing people.
● Relations between Russia and Armenia are going through a period of seeking a new balance, Russian Ambassador Sergey Kopyrkin said at an event marking the 70th anniversary of the public organisation Union of Veterans of Armenia named after Marshal Baghramyan. “Regardless of how the political situation changes, our shared history, joint victories and the figure of Marshal Baghramyan remain powerful unifying factors for our peoples. It was through unity that we won the most difficult war, and it is unity that we must rely on to meet the challenges of today,” Kopyrkin said.
● An analytical centre for Armenia’s mining and metallurgical sector will be established. The centre will serve as a platform for research and for strengthening dialogue between the public and private sectors.
● Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan received a delegation led by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, who arrived in Armenia on his first official visit to the country. “There is significant potential for developing practical cooperation in trade, transport, agriculture, information technology, education and tourism. One important outcome of the talks will be the signing of a broad package of documents,” Japarov said.
● The European Union Mission in Armenia (EUMA) presented a photo exhibition exploring the links between peace, security, biodiversity conservation and the well-being of local residents. The exhibition features more than 40 photographs taken during routine patrols and visits to local communities in the Syunik, Vayots Dzor, Tavush and Gegharkunik provinces.
● The ruling Georgian Dream party held meetings of its Political Council and parliamentary majority, attended by the party’s founder and honorary chairman, billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili. According to the officially released information, Ivanishvili reviewed a series of corruption-related arrests within the party’s ranks and said the problems had been overcome. Parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia and head of the government of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara Zurab Pataradze were added to the Political Council as new members. Speaking to journalists, Kirtskhalia dismissed rumours that Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze would soon resign. Kobakhidze himself said that no personnel matters had been discussed at the meetings, including the possible release from prison of former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili, who was convicted of corruption. Read more here.
● Several people convicted in the “4 October case” of 2025, concerning an alleged attempt to seize the Presidential Administration, have been released from Gldani prison under plea agreements.
● The body of Lasha Broladze, a Georgian citizen killed while fighting against Russian forces in Ukraine, has been brought to Tbilisi. He will be buried in the village of Natanebi, in the Ozurgeti district.
● The European Union Monitoring Mission in Georgia said it would no longer fund the country’s government because of the deterioration of democratic processes, but would continue supporting the population and allocate €38 million for new projects in 2026. Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili said that, with this statement, the European Union had effectively abolished Georgia’s statehood and that “this disgrace must soon be washed away”. On 17 October, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze proposed that the European Union begin an open and public dialogue at the political level.
● A court denied bail and remanded criminal underworld figures Vato Kipiani, Avtandil Bilanishvili, also known as “Katsro”, and Shota Kipiani in custody. According to the Prosecutor’s Office, on 14 October they beat a 65-year-old man at a restaurant in Tbilisi’s Vake district. They are charged with group violence, an offence carrying a prison sentence of up to two years. Bilanishvili is frequently described in the media as a friend of Bera Ivanishvili, the son of billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili, who is widely regarded as the country’s shadow ruler. The alleged links of all three suspects to elite circles have long been widely discussed in Georgian media and on social media, and their arrests have caused a major stir.
● Nana Keinishvili, a member of the National Bank of Georgia’s board, has left her post amid an investigation into her activities. According to the Prosecutor’s Office, the case was opened following testimony from executives of BitExchange, who accused her of illegal business activity. Keinishvili strongly rejects the accusations and says she stepped down to protect the interests of the state and the reputation of the National Bank.
● On 16 October, Swiss Foreign Minister and current OSCE Chairperson-in-Office Ignazio Cassis visited Georgia. Georgian Foreign Minister Maka Bochorishvili said that Georgia had applied to chair the OSCE in 2027. Cassis said that a broad consensus was needed for next year’s chairmanship and that the aim was to find a solution by the end of November, although he could not guarantee the outcome. Gigi Tsereteli, chairman of the opposition European Georgia party, described the government’s initiative as a PR stunt.
● Kobakhidze met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Yerevan on the sidelines of the UN COP17 biodiversity conference. According to the Georgian prime minister, they discussed bilateral relations and the current situation in the Middle East. US Republican Congressman Joe Wilson commented on news of the meeting, describing the Georgian government as an “America-hating regime” and Iran as a “terrorist state”.
● Applications for a cash compensation programme for internally displaced persons (IDPs) will open on 19 October. According to the Ministry of Health, an IDP family that has not yet received housing or compensation from the state can receive 10,000 lari (around $4,000) for each family member. Applications will be accepted at court buildings until 2 November. Georgia’s independent Social Justice Center said that the programme’s low compensation amount could put families at risk of homelessness.
● Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili said that during a meeting in Rome, he had explained to the president of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) that the Georgian delegation would not participate in the assembly’s work as long as PACE continued to violate Georgia’s sovereignty.
● Tbilisi hosted the 44th “Saturday March” as part of the continuous pro-European protest movement that has been ongoing for almost two years. The march’s main slogan was “No torture in prisons!”, with participants demanding an end to degrading treatment in prisons and by the police. Former President Salome Zourabichvili joined the march and delivered a speech criticising the authorities’ intention to ban five opposition parties. The Constitutional Court is reportedly due to hear the ruling party’s lawsuit on 21–23 October. Watch all the videos in the “Protests in Georgia” podcast here.
● A major scandal continues over the municipal shelter for stray animals in the city of Gori. Footage posted on social media showed hundreds of puppies kept in a single cramped, dirty enclosure, reportedly with very little food and water. Dozens of animal rights activists arrived at the shelter, sparking mass protests. Many people took puppies home, while private shelters took in several dozen. Many of the animals were already seriously ill, and some died on the way. A number of veterinary clinics joined the rescue effort, offering free treatment to the rescued animals. Hundreds of appeals demanding immediate action have been posted on social media and in the media, calling on local authorities and the country’s leadership to investigate the situation.
● Azerbaijan marked Restoration of Independence Day on Sunday. Congratulations were extended to the country by the European Union Delegation, the embassies of the United Kingdom, Belgium, Ukraine, Latvia and the Netherlands, Turkey’s Foreign Ministry and the Organisation of Turkic States.
● Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan congratulated Azerbaijan on Restoration of Independence Day, writing on X: “We are always united, in sorrow and in joy.”
● On Sunday, Azerbaijan marked the sixth anniversary of taking control of the 13th-century Khudafarin Bridge over the Araz River, near the Azerbaijan–Iran border in the Jabrayil district, during the Second Karabakh War in 2020. Local media recalled that on 18 October 2020, two other historic villages in the same district were also liberated from more than 30 years of Armenian occupation.
● The hacking group “313 Team” has claimed responsibility for DDoS attacks carried out between 13 and 15 October against the information resources of Azerbaijani government agencies, media outlets and foreign diplomatic missions in Azerbaijan. The incident was reported by the National Cybersecurity Agency.
● The ruling Yeni Azerbaijan Party announced that it had expelled Ramiz Mehdiyev, the detained former head of the Presidential Administration, from its ranks. He is accused of treason, attempting to seize power by force and laundering criminal proceeds.
● The Prosecutor’s Office announced that the investigation into the cases of detained opposition figures Ali Karimli and Mammad Ibrahim, leaders of the Azerbaijan Popular Front Party, had been completed. Their case was initially linked to the investigation into Ramiz Mehdiyev, but the proceedings were later separated. Karimli and Ibrahim have also been charged with attempting to seize power by force, an offence punishable by up to 20 years in prison or life imprisonment. Both deny the charges and consider their prosecution politically motivated.
● Turkish commentator Celal Çiftçi, who has been placed on Azerbaijan’s international wanted list, has apologised to the Azerbaijani state and people for his publications. He is accused of calling for the violent seizure of power in Azerbaijan and disseminating material inciting religious hatred and enmity. Çiftçi had protested against restrictions on wearing hijabs in Azerbaijani schools and posted on social media a video generated using artificial intelligence, showing an armed man in military uniform knocking over a street sign bearing an image of President Ilham Aliyev. In a post on X, Çiftçi wrote that he had “gone beyond what hehe intended to say” and acknowledged that “decisions about the future of Azerbaijan fall within the competence of the Azerbaijani people and the country’s own constitutional institutions”.
● A book entitled “Factors Creating Serious Difficulties for Students in Azerbaijani-Language Schools in Georgia in Learning Their Native Language” was presented in Tbilisi. Its author is Aygul Isayeva, head of the public organisation Maarif. Among the main problems she identified were the reduction in the number of native-language lessons, the abolition of the graduation examination in the subject, errors in textbook translations and a shortage of qualified teachers. The study notes that the suspension of admissions to the Azerbaijani Language and Literature programme at Ilia State University in 2006 had a negative impact on the training of qualified specialists.
● Mass brawls broke out before and after the Qarabag–Neftchi football match in Baku, and 19 people were detained. The match ended in a high-scoring 3–3 draw. The Disciplinary Committee of the Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan imposed fines on both clubs and ruled that their next home matches must be played behind closed doors.

title: How Ukraine outmaneuvered Russian troops in Operation Vivaldi
body:
Soldiers from the 21st Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment Kraken, who go by their callsigns "Cooper" and "Admin," prepare to launch a Darts mid-range strike drone in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, on Oct. 8, 2026. (Lisa Bukreyeva / The Kyiv Independent)
Editor's note: Most of the Ukrainian soldiers and commanders interviewed are identified by their callsigns, in accordance with military protocols.
KHARKIV OBLAST — Ukrainian soldier Oleksandr had already narrowly survived crossing a mine-strewn field and a river in the crosshairs of Russian artillery when the swarm of first-person-view (FPV) drones began hunting him.
"If I'm honest, I was convinced they were going to kill us," the 37-year-old told the Kyiv Independent while chain-smoking cigarettes in the safety of his base in Kharkiv Oblast .
"I was already like, 'everyone goodbye, I love you all, everything is good,' but (the commanders were saying) on the radio, 'don't even think about it, everything will be fine.'"
Oleksandr was part of Operation Vivaldi , which lasted until mid-October and, until recently, was a top-secret counteroffensive in the Lyman sector in the northern part of Donetsk Oblast .
By pushing forward this spring, Ukrainian brigades under the Third Army Corps aimed to improve defensive positions in the area, which is critical to holding on to the remaining Ukrainian-held strongholds in the Donbas ahead of the winter, multiple commanders who took part said.
As well as liberating 277 square kilometers (107 square miles) of land and 16 villages as of Oct. 14, the operation proved something potentially even more important — that on today's drone-saturated and largely stalemated front line, it's still possible for Ukraine's infantry to advance in significant numbers.
The first task was making it through a dense minefield. Survive that, and then there was the river to cross. Survive that, and there was a chance the village of Shandryholove could be liberated from Russian forces.
The first group of three soldiers that attempted the crossing barely made it, Battalion Commander Sergii Galchenko said. Two groups that followed were forced to turn back after setting off mines.
"The enemy couldn't figure out where we were."
Those that made it needed reinforcing as soon as possible, no easy task when the few wooden bridges crossing it were destroyed, and Russian drones and artillery monitored the area constantly.
The soldiers initially waded through the water, but used wood and logs to create a makeshift crossing, according to Galchenko.
"We had a very serious problem with logistics when it came to bringing in our own reinforcements," Galchenko, who goes by his callsign "Psycho," said at his command post not far from the front.
The best way to stay alive was to keep moving, not staying in one place long enough for Russian drones and artillery to zero in on their positions.
"The enemy couldn't figure out where we were," Galchenko said.
Galchenko's battalion was assigned to enter Shandryholove from the south and move northward, clearing the central street as they went.
Two tactics proved vital — using drones wherever possible, and using a blockade tactic whereby infantry sneaked behind Russian lines to isolate Moscow's troops from the rear and block their escape.
Taking Shandryholove — a village only 0.17 square kilometers (0.066 square miles) in size — took more than a month.
"The enemy heavily mined (the area), abnormally heavily, because it understood that it couldn't stop us any other way," Galchenko said.
Anti-personnel mines were everywhere and accounted for 80% of casualties, Galchenko said, without disclosing the total number of Ukrainian casualties during the operation.
To minimize the risk to Ukrainian lives while advancing, the most important thing for the commanders was to rely on drones as much as possible, striking Russian positions ahead of the advancing troops. Soldiers on the ground would then go in to look for survivors.
"We did everything we could to prevent the infantry from encountering the enemy there," Galchenko said.
Units of the 66th Brigade advanced northward along the treeline toward heavily mined Shandryholove. The village had long been destroyed by years of heavy fighting in the area.
Oleksandr, who goes by his callsign "Marine," was in the first group of three soldiers to enter.
It was eerily quiet at first. The trio cleared a building as instructed and were approaching a church when they were spotted likely by a Russian FPV drone. A swarm soon followed.
For around four hours, the trio ran in zig-zags through the ruins of the village in a desperate attempt to avoid the drones above, while trying to stick to the concrete streets to avoid the mines below.
All three survived, but were not unscathed — one drone slammed into a door that Oleksandr had slammed shut behind him, peppering them all with shrapnel and dealing each a concussion.
The challenge in liberating Shandryholove was that Russian troops had prepared an extensive underground defensive network, primarily utilizing basements.
With the houses mostly destroyed in the village, it was difficult to assess from drone footage whether there was a basement under all the rubble, according to a company commander of the 125th Heavy Mechanized Brigade, who goes by his callsign "Ed." He estimated that there were about 50 houses in Shandryholove.
Instead of storming straight into Shandryholove, the majority of Ukraine's troops advanced along the treelines around the village to cut off the Russian troops inside, according to Ed. He said that his 125th Brigade moved roughly in parallel with other Ukrainian units, including the 66th and 60th mechanized brigades, with one advancing at a time and the others then playing catch-up.
What helped initially was that Russian troops in the village had been worn out by the cold weather when the offensive began, with some appearing to have died from exposure, Ed said.
"This really played in our favor," he added.
Shandryholove was just one of many such tiny villages that needed to be liberated for the counteroffensive to succeed. In between them, Ukrainian forces advanced along treelines, continuously changing the timing and routes of assaults to keep Russia's troops guessing.
Sometimes the soldiers would move in the dead of night, wearing anti-thermal blankets, while on other days they would switch it up to the gray hour before sunrise or daytime, according to Ed.
The pace of advance varied day to day. Galchenko said that his soldiers from the 66th could advance two kilometers (1.2 miles) in a day, while sometimes it took four days to advance 200 meters.
The vanguard of the advance was made up of soldiers sent usually in pairs to conduct the blockade maneuver, sneaking behind enemy lines to block logistics and prevent Russian infantry from being reinforced or running away to the rear, according to "Judo," a battalion commander with the 60th Mechanized Brigade.
The dense spring foliage in the forest served as a double-edged sword. This helped the infantry hide from Russian drones, but also made it difficult for friendly drones to conduct reconnaissance of the area.
It was crucial for the infantry to serve as the "ears," letting their commanders know where they heard voices and movement.
Galchenko stressed that it was important to enter the Russian positions quietly so the Russian soldiers inside wouldn't have time to warn their higher-ups that the Ukrainians were advancing.
"They knew that the quieter we entered, the more chance that the enemy would not be able to pass on (the information) to his higher-ups."
"We knew that the quieter we entered, the greater the chance the enemy would not be able to pass on (the information) to his higher-ups that we are advancing," Galchenko said.
"Then we have more chance to advance without any (potentially dangerous) moments."
As the 66th and 125th brigades were working on liberating neighboring Shandryholove in spring, the 60th was tasked to move behind the smaller village of Derylove to the south to cut it off so another unit could retake it, Judo said. When trying to infiltrate, the objective was to establish a defensive line inside Russian-held territory by carefully sending in one group after another, he explained.
The commander told his unit that they should only open fire if they were fully certain that they could kill Russian soldiers, waiting until they got as close as five meters.
"The enemy was moving through what he believed was his territory, and our group let the enemy in and completely destroyed them," Judo said.
"Their bodies were then camouflaged, in order for the enemy not to detect our group by finding the bodies of its soldiers from drones."
The soldiers would try to penetrate five kilometers (3.1 miles) into the Russian rear. He admitted that 30 to 40 percent of the time the soldiers would still be spotted by drones, then had to shoot the drones down themselves or rely on their unit to deploy countermeasures remotely.
Despite the risks, Judo said the operation went successfully, with the unit taking "minimal" casualties. He believes that there would have been many more casualties if the positional war had continued and his unit had remained on the defensive.
Russian troops responded differently to the Ukrainian offensive each day. Russia could react with an extremely heavy barrage of artillery and drone strikes, and by scattering mines, but it could also suddenly go quiet for a couple of days, according to Ed.
Stepping on a mine was the most common cause of injury, followed by FPV strikes, and then gunshot wounds, Ed said.
"On one day there could be up to two mine blasts, and then three days without any," Ed said.
Evacuation proved to be difficult, and the mines that injured advancing troops were also a threat to those that tried to rescue them. They were difficult to spot in the long grass that had appeared with the arrival of spring.
Ed recalled one incident when a soldier was dragging a wounded comrade on a stretcher when it struck a mine, killing the wounded man.
Much has been made of the rapid advances in unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) and their potential for evacuations on the battlefield, but during Operation Vivaldi, their slow speed made them prime targets for Russian drones, according to several commanders.
"If Russia sees a UGV, then I will say that there is a very high probability — 90% — that it will try to hit it," Galchenko said.
Galchenko recalled one incident when six Ukrainian soldiers were running across a field to assault a forested area when they were attacked with about 35 fiber-optic FPV drones, 12 fixed-wing Molniya drones, and heavy artillery over the course of two hours.
One appeared to have been killed outright and the other five were injured, one so severely that commanders monitoring the assault via a drone feed thought he was dead. When he regained consciousness, a UGV was sent in to bring him back without the need to send another soldier into an area already the target of so much Russian fire.
After struggling aboard, the wounded soldier made it around 1,500 meters away from the front line when a Russian drone struck, killing him.
Away from the fighting on the ground, another critical aspect of Operation Vivaldi was Ukraine's middle-strike drone capability, which hammered Russian logistics about 200 kilometers (124 miles) away.
For the 21st Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment Kraken, the targets included ammunition depots, repair bases, and fuel storage sites in occupied territories of Luhansk Oblast, according to "Dolyna," one of the unit's high-ranking commanders.
He linked the quieter days mentioned by Ed to successful strikes on Russian ammunition depots which, at least temporarily, deprived Russian artillery of shells.
Perhaps more crucially, these strikes helped deprive Russian infantry of the basic things they needed to survive — food, water, and ammunition.
"(Russian troops) were demoralized," Dolyna said at a middle-strike drone launch site in Kharkiv Oblast.
"It's hard to stay motivated when you are cold, hungry, and have nothing to keep you warm."
Operation Vivaldi had retaken 277 square kilometers (107 square miles) of territory, including 16 settlements, as of Oct. 14, according to the Third Army Corps. The unit claimed that Russian forces had suffered around 8,000 personnel losses, with over 250 soldiers captured by Ukraine as of this month. The Kyiv Independent couldn't independently verify the claimed battlefield figures.
Ukraine's casualty ratio compared to Russia's has been one to seven, with the majority of Ukrainian losses being injuries while Russia faced more fatalities, Brig. Gen. Andrii Biletskyi, the corps' commander, claimed during a briefing, as cited by Ukrainian media Hromadske.
When announcing the end of the fourth stage of Operation Vivaldi, Biletskyi said, "four seasons of 'Vivaldi' are over, but the music continues."
Commanders said in early October that they believe that Ukraine has already achieved its main objective of the counteroffensive and expect the pace of the counteroffensive to gradually slow, particularly with the arrival of winter.
"(Going on the offensive) is in our blood," Judo said.
"We don't have any intention of withdrawing or retreating. Our only goal is to fight for our territory."
Hi, this is Asami, the author of this article. Thank you for reading it until the end. While reporting on an ongoing operation such as this one is difficult due to OPSEC concerns, what allows us, as local reporters, to tell their story in depth is gaining the commanders' and soldiers' trust. My goal has always been to shed light on the reality on the ground and to tell the stories as humanly as possible, because assaulting in the current drone-dominated phase of the war can be extremely deadly.
No matter how difficult the situation gets in Ukraine, we will continue to do our best to report from these front-line regions and provide a reliable window into the war. Please consider supporting our reporting , which is available without a paywall thanks to the support of our members.
Asami Terajima is a reporter at the Kyiv Independent covering Ukrainian military affairs and front-line developments. She is the co-author of the weekly War Notes newsletter. She previously worked as a business reporter for the Kyiv Post, focusing on international trade, infrastructure, investment, and energy. Originally from Japan, Terajima moved to Ukraine during childhood and completed her bachelor's degree in Business Administration in the U.S. She is the winner of the Thomson Reuters Foundation's Kurt Schork Award in International Journalism 2023 (Local Reporter category) and the George Weidenfeld Prize, awarded as part of Germany's Axel Springer Prize 2023. She was also featured on the Media Development Foundation's 2023 "25 under 25: Young and Bold" list of emerging media makers in Ukraine. She is among the finalists for the U.K.'s One World Media Award 2026 in the Print category and the French Bayeux Calvados-Normandy award 2025 for war correspondents in the Young Reporter category.

title: Russian forces lose another 2,250 soldiers in war against Ukraine over past day
body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
The Russian army also lost 12,439 (+3) tanks , 25,594 (+8) armored fighting vehicles, 51,447 (+44) artillery systems, 2,229 (+1) multiple launch rocket systems (MLRS), 1,719 (+3) air defense systems, aircraft—449, helicopters—356, ground-based robotic systems—2,997 (+7), operational-tactical-level UAVs—575,142 (+1,750), cruise missiles—5,138, ships and boats—35, submarines—2, vehicles and tankers—165,641 (+363), and specialized equipment—4,846 (+2).
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 21, as of 10:00 p.m., there were 165 combat engagements between the Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian invaders on the front lines, with the heaviest fighting taking place in the Pokrovsk direction.

title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
body: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection. Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services . title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
body: To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Train, Adapt and Optimize Models With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T, Alpamayo, QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Multiview and multisensory video data generation for evaluating policies in closed loop simulation. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ADNOC-Cosmos.mp4 The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
body: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready , helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention. Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope. Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid. Explore the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and the Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design . title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
body: European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image, about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine.
