title: FG, States, Agencies Rally Nigerians in Early Fight against Ebola
body: • Keyamo puts 44 contacts on ‘no-fly’ list •Atiku demands accountability on N10bn preparedness fund Emmanuel Addeh, Olawale Ajimotokan, Michael Olugbode, Sunday Aborisade, Juliet Akoje in Abuja and Ayodeji Ake in Lagos The federal government, state governments, the National Assembly and public health institutions yesterday intensified efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola in Nigeria, mobilising health workers, strengthening disease surveillance and urging Nigerians to adopt precautionary measures following confirmation of an imported case in Abuja. The response came as the Senate and House of Representatives called for the immediate release of emergency funds to strengthen the country’s preparedness, while the West African Health Organisation (WAHO) stepped up regional surveillance and coordination. Besides, the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) urged persons suspected of infection to stay away from congregational prayers pending medical assessment. In the same vein, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has demanded accountability for the N10 billion reportedly approved for Ebola preparedness, questioning how much had been released and how the money had been spent. Health authorities have identified 44 contacts linked to the confirmed case and are tracing them for monitoring and appropriate medical intervention, as public health officials warn that early detection, contact tracing and strict infection prevention measures are critical to preventing further transmission. Also, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday convened its first Incident Management Meeting following the official declaration of the outbreak, bringing together its leadership and key partners to coordinate response activities. The development has prompted heightened vigilance across states, with Niger State placing public and private health facilities on alert and directing them to report suspected cases immediately. Medical experts have also urged Nigerians to avoid unnecessary physical contact, practise regular handwashing and seek prompt medical attention if they develop symptoms or suspect exposure. FG Assures Nigerians of Containment Strategies The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats yesterday evening assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola disease recently discovered in the country. Chairman of the Task Force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said this while speaking to newsmen after the group’s emergency meeting at the State House, Abuja. Gbajabiamila said the Task Force has been working behind the scenes since it was inaugurated in June this year adding that this informed why it was easy to detect the index case discovered yesterday. “It’s very important to note this. Since the issue of Ebola came up in June, there have been about 44, 000 flights in and out of Nigeria. So, it’s because of what the Ministry of Health, the task force and all the agencies have been doing. All hands have been on deck. “The passenger with the disease showed no symptoms, which came four days after the woman got into Abuja, and it was the identification process and the protocols that were put in place that enabled the quick identification. That also speaks to the country’s capacity and ability to deal with this disease as best as we can,” he added. He assured Nigerians that the Task Force would strengthen whatever needed strengthening, the protocols, and ensure more rigorous enforcement moving forward. “The Task Force is on top of it. NCDC is on top of it; everyone is on deck. We must build community trust and avoid panic, but it’s also important to state clearly that this is a collaborative effort between the government and the people,” he stated. Also speaking, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate, said Nigeria has competent health authorities, including private hospital operators and agencies, Immigration, Aviation, Interior, and subnational actors, who have put surveillance systems in place across the country, ready to respond. “We have been conducting contact tracing diligently and isolating those contacts of the index imported case in this country. We will continue to do that, and we want to reassure Nigerians that the federal government, alongside its technical partners, the World Health Organisation, the Africa Centre for Disease Control, and our own Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, have activated the incident management system across the various pillars. “They are working day and night diligently, and our hospital capabilities are also activated, such that we can aim to contain this case, as has been the case in other countries, but we will not relent. Our population should respect public health directives. “Most of our states have adequate response plans. We have the resources, and we’re mobilising those capabilities. And we’re also confident that if we continue on this path, we should be able to dent this outbreak,” he stated. He further urged citizens to avoid misinformation while combating the virus. “The key also for the population is to avoid spreading misinformation or baseless rumours, which can cause unnecessary panic. The Task Force leadership has met. WHO and Africa CDC are working closely with the team. “In addition to our exceptional public health physicians who had successfully tamed this virus in 2014, and had contributed to other countries, we are confident that if we continue in this direction, we will emerge from this crisis in a much stronger place,” Pate assured. Senate Demands Immediate Release of Emergency Funds The Senate yesterday called on the federal government to release emergency funds from the Service Wide Vote to strengthen Nigeria’s disease surveillance and response system, following confirmation of the Ebola case in Abuja. The upper chamber, however, rejected a proposal for relevant Senate committees to visit major international entry points to assess the country’s preparedness, after Senate President Godswill Akpabio questioned the necessity of the exercise and raised concerns about exposing lawmakers to possible infection. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Francis Faduyile, representing Ondo South, who called for mandatory health screening at international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. Faduyile, a professor of medicine, warned that Nigeria could not afford to take chances with its public health infrastructure, particularly as the strain responsible for the outbreak had no approved vaccine. He urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, NCDC and Port Health Services to enforce compulsory screening for international arrivals, including health declaration forms, temperature checks and symptom assessments. He also advocated enhanced screening for travellers who had visited or transited through affected areas within the preceding 21 days, irrespective of their nationality or country of departure. The senator called for the provision of trained port health officers, thermal scanners, personal protective equipment and properly equipped isolation rooms at entry points, while urging the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria and the Nigeria Immigration Service to ensure that adequate personnel and facilities were available. He further recommended the establishment of functional isolation and treatment centres in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, alongside stronger contact tracing and surveillance mechanisms. Faduyile also called for a review of the Quarantine Act of 1926 to bring the legislation in line with contemporary public health realities and the International Health Regulations. He proposed that Senate committees on Health, Primary Healthcare, Development and Disease Control, Aviation, Interior, and Appropriations visit major entry points and submit a report within four weeks. However, Akpabio opposed the proposed visits, questioning whether lawmakers needed to travel to the entry points when the immediate priority was to strengthen the agencies responsible for disease surveillance and control. The Senate President subsequently put the proposal to a vote, with the majority of lawmakers rejecting the visits while retaining support for measures to strengthen the country’s response. Contributing to the debate, Senator Ekong Sampson, representing Akwa Ibom South, stressed the need to strengthen Nigeria’s health system to protect citizens against Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. Senator Sadiq Umar, representing Kwara North, called for the deployment of appropriate technology to improve contact tracing, while Senator Adamu Aliero, representing Kebbi Central, urged the federal government to release emergency resources without waiting for previously approved budgetary allocations to become available. Senator Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North, also supported calls to amend the Quarantine Act. House Seeks Strategic Action The House of Representatives has called on the federal government to immediately mobilise public and private health agencies across the country and place them on high alert following a reported Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) case involving a woman who arrived in Abuja from Uganda. The call followed a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Hon. Amobi Ogah on October 21, 2026 seeking stronger preventive and emergency medical measures to curb the spread of the disease in Nigeria. Ogah expressed concern over the reported case which he said was confirmed on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 involving a woman who arrived from Uganda and tested positive for the virus in Abuja. The lawmakers noted that Ebola Virus Disease is a severe and potentially fatal infectious disease that requires prompt detection, effective infection prevention and control measures and coordinated public health interventions to prevent transmission and save lives. They warned that delays in identifying suspected cases, conducting appropriate laboratory investigations, isolating confirmed cases, tracing contacts and providing timely medical care could increase the risk of transmission and place additional pressure on Nigeria’s healthcare system. The House further expressed concern that inadequate public awareness, insufficient infection prevention and control supplies, gaps in healthcare workers’ preparedness and limited emergency response capacity could undermine efforts to prevent and contain the outbreak. It emphasised the critical roles of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, state ministries of health, port health authorities and other relevant stakeholders in strengthening the country’s epidemic preparedness and response mechanisms. The lawmaker also acknowledged the importance of collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO) and other relevant international and regional public health institutions to ensure that Nigeria’s preventive and emergency response measures are guided by current scientific evidence and international health regulations. Consequently, the House resolved to mandate the federal government to immediately mobilise all relevant private, state and federal health agencies and place them on high alert to contain the disease. It also urged the federal government, through the Ministry of Finance, to urgently release all outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies to enable them to effectively discharge their responsibilities. In another resolution, the lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to immediately assess the funding expected to be released in order to strengthen Nigeria’s preparedness and response capacity against the disease, in line with current epidemiological evidence and public health guidance. Atiku Demands Accountability for N10bn Fund Former Vice President Atiku has demanded a detailed account of the N10 billion approved for Ebola preparedness, alleging that Nigeria’s response to the confirmed case has exposed gaps in surveillance, emergency funding and the protection of healthcare workers. In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku called on President Bola Tinubu’s administration to disclose how much of the announced funding had been released, the dates of disbursement, contracts awarded, beneficiaries and items delivered. “Ebola is a grave public health threat. Nigerians deserve urgent action, competent leadership and the truth,” he said. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered,” Atiku added. He argued that announcing emergency funding was insufficient without verifiable evidence of disbursement and utilisation, calling for a formal audit to establish how the money had been spent. The former vice president also questioned the timeline of the reported case, alleging that the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, while the government publicly confirmed the case on October 20. He demanded explanations about the handling of the 44 contacts reportedly associated with the case and alleged that private healthcare workers lacked adequate protective equipment. Atiku also questioned the leadership structure of the response, recalling that Tinubu announced a Presidential Task Force chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, in June. He maintained that medical experts, including epidemiologists, doctors and public health professionals, should lead the technical response, with the authority and resources required to manage the outbreak. The former vice president further alleged that the Minister of Health’s planned press conference was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and participating in voting. He warned that the outbreak could worsen economic pressures if the response disrupted movement, livelihoods and commercial activities. WAHO, NCDC Step Up Surveillance The West African Health Organisation (WAHO) has intensified regional disease surveillance and coordination among West African countries following the confirmation of the imported Ebola case in Abuja, amid concerns about possible cross-border transmission. The ECOWAS health institution disclosed that Nigerian authorities confirmed the case on October 20, involving a woman who had recently arrived from Uganda. According to WAHO, the patient developed symptoms on October 7 and received treatment at a private health facility in Abuja on October 11, before laboratory tests confirmed the infection on October 20. The organisation said it was monitoring the situation in collaboration with the NCDC, national health authorities and regional epidemiological surveillance mechanisms. As part of the response, WAHO yesterday held a briefing with directors of the National Public Health Institutes of ECOWAS member states to reinforce regional vigilance and coordination. It stressed that early detection, prompt notification of suspected cases, effective epidemiological surveillance and coordination among health services were critical to containing epidemic-prone diseases. The organisation advised the public to wash their hands frequently with soap and clean water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers. It also urged Nigerians to avoid direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of sick or deceased persons, as well as contaminated clothing, bedding and personal belongings. WAHO warned against handling the bodies of people who died from suspected causes, recommending that safe and dignified burials be conducted by trained teams. It further advised against handling or consuming bushmeat and cautioned against contact with sick or dead animals, including bats and primates, urging people to ensure that meat was thoroughly cooked. People experiencing symptoms consistent with Ebola, including sudden fever, severe fatigue, body aches, vomiting, diarrhoea or bleeding, were advised to contact or seek assistance from a health facility immediately. WAHO also urged travellers to avoid non-essential journeys to affected areas and comply with official health guidance where travel was unavoidable. Warning against misinformation during public health emergencies, the organisation urged Nigerians to rely on official sources and refrain from circulating rumours or unverified reports. It reaffirmed its commitment to working with the health ministries of ECOWAS member states and technical and financial partners to strengthen regional health security. The organisation said its specialised Regional Centre for Surveillance and Disease Control, based in Abuja, would continue monitoring developments and sharing relevant information in coordination with the appropriate health authorities. Besides, the NCDC yesterday convened its first Incident Management Meeting following the official declaration of the outbreak in Nigeria. The meeting brought together the agency’s leadership and key partners to align response efforts as the Incident Action Plan was being finalised. NCDC teams were also conducting case management and response activities, with emphasis on enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and coordinated risk communication. The measures are intended to strengthen the detection and management of suspected cases, identify people who may have been exposed to the virus and limit potential transmission. The agency reaffirmed its commitment to a timely, coordinated and evidence-based response, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders. WHO Urges Nigeria, Others to Strengthen Measures The World Health Organisation (WHO), has advised countries in Africa to strengthen control measures, including case investigation, contact tracing, infection prevention and control. This followed reported import of Ebola into Nigeria’s federal capital territory, Abuja. WHO said it was working closely with, “partners and health authorities to strengthen control measures, including case investigation, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and provision of essential supplies including personal protective equipment for health workers. In a statement, the organisation urged all countries in the region to sustain a high level of readiness as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to evolve. “Kenya has reported nine cases linked to an imported case in recent weeks. Countries should maintain strong disease surveillance and rapid alert investigation, ensure laboratories can safely test suspected cases, keep rapid response and clinical teams ready for immediate activation, reinforce infection prevention and control in both public and private health facilities, and pre-position essential supplies, while actively engaging with communities. “They should also heighten monitoring at points of entry, with response plans in place. Sustained readiness is essential to detect cases early, prevent onward transmission and protect health workers and communities. “WHO advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries, and continues to closely monitor and, where necessary, verify travel and trade measures in relation to this event. “WHO risk assessment is being regularly reassessed, to incorporate the latest developments related to this event.” NSCIA Bars Suspected Ebola Carriers from Prayers The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) has urged persons suspected of Ebola infection to refrain from attending congregational prayers pending medical assessment, as part of measures to prevent the spread of the disease. The council, under the leadership of its President General and Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, made the call in a public health advisory issued yesterday following the reported laboratory confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory. In the advisory signed by the NSCIA Secretary General, Prof. Is-haq Oloyede, the council urged Muslims to comply with medical guidance and prioritise the preservation of life. It called on chief imams, Islamic scholars, state councils for Islamic affairs and Muslim organisations to intensify public awareness through Friday sermons, religious gatherings and community engagements. The council also advised anyone experiencing symptoms associated with Ebola, particularly following possible exposure, to seek prompt medical attention and avoid close contact with others while awaiting professional guidance. It warned that Ebola could spread through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of infected persons who had developed symptoms, contaminated materials or the bodies of people who had died from the disease. The NSCIA identified fever, severe headache, weakness, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in some cases, unexplained bleeding as symptoms requiring attention. It urged Nigerians to wash their hands regularly, avoid contact with suspected cases and promptly report suspected infections to the appropriate health authorities. The council also called on the federal and state governments to strengthen disease surveillance, contact tracing, public enlightenment and healthcare facility preparedness, while ensuring adequate protection for health workers and timely dissemination of accurate information. Emphasising the religious basis for the measures, the NSCIA said the preservation of life, known in Islamic jurisprudence as Hifz al-Nafs, was one of the fundamental objectives of Islamic law. It referenced Qur’an 2:195, which cautions against throwing oneself into destruction, and recalled the Prophet Muhammad’s guidance on precautions during infectious disease outbreaks. The council urged the public to avoid spreading unverified information and to refrain from stigmatising affected individuals and their families. It reaffirmed its readiness to mobilise mosques, Islamic organisations and community leaders nationwide to support public health education and disease prevention. The NSCIA urged Nigerians to remain calm and act responsibly, stressing that faith, prayer and appropriate medical care were complementary in responding to public health emergencies. Expert Urges Nigerians to Avoid Physical Contact President of the Academy of Medical Sciences, Prof. Oladapo Ashiru, yesterday urged Nigerians to avoid handshakes and hugs, maintain strict personal hygiene and promptly report suspected cases to prevent the spread of Ebola. Ashiru made the call during an interview with Arise News, where he described the situation as serious but manageable, stressing that public awareness, early detection and strict adherence to infection prevention measures would be critical to containing the threat. He recalled Nigeria’s successful response to the 2014 Ebola outbreak in Lagos, saying the country could draw on that experience to prevent further transmission. “It can be managed. And the way we manage this depends on how we respond to this situation,” he said. “We successfully managed this in 2014 when there was an index case in Lagos, and it was critically managed and contained,” he added. Ashiru said the circumstances surrounding the current infection, including whether it occurred during transit or originated from Uganda, remained unclear. “Right now, we have one case confirmed in Abuja. Whether in transit or from Uganda, we don’t know,” he said. He explained that Ebola differed from COVID-19 because it was not airborne and was primarily transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of an infected person. “In the case of Ebola, the difference between Ebola and COVID-19 is that Ebola is not airborne, whereas COVID-19 is airborne,” he said. He identified contact with the bodily fluids or secretions of an infected person, particularly after symptoms developed, as a major route of transmission. “The major way you can get it is by contacting the body fluid or secretions of somebody showing the signs of Ebola,” he said. The medical expert advised Nigerians to suspend customary greetings involving physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, while preventive measures were strengthened. “This is a time for Nigerians, as the Academy of Medical Sciences has stressed, to refrain from shaking hands and hugging,” he said. The expert urged public and private hospitals, clinics and other healthcare facilities to strengthen surveillance and remain alert to patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of Ebola. He said healthcare providers must act promptly when they encounter a patient with fever or other symptoms that raise suspicion of infection. “The private clinics must be on high alert in terms of once you recognise a case with fever or you suspect it, you have to be proactive in suspecting such cases,” he said. Ashiru particularly cautioned health workers about the risks associated with removing personal protective equipment after attending to suspected or confirmed cases. Niger Ramps Up Surveillance The Niger State Government has placed public health organisations across the state on heightened alert following confirmation of the Ebola case in Abuja. The government said the measures were precautionary and intended to strengthen surveillance, early detection and rapid response capacity, particularly because of the frequent movement of people and volume of trade between Niger State and neighbouring Abuja. The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Murtala Bagana, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists in Minna yesterday, reassuring residents that no Ebola case had been detected in the state. He said the state government was collaborating with the NCDC, the World Health Organisation and other international partners to strengthen preparedness and ensure a coordinated response. According to him, public and private health facilities across the state had been directed to report any suspected case immediately. Bagana said Local Government Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers and response teams had been deployed to strengthen contact tracing, clinical assessment and safe referral protocols. He added that infection prevention and control measures had been reinforced across health centres to protect frontline workers and patients. The commissioner appealed to residents to remain calm, avoid panic and observe basic hygiene, particularly frequent handwashing with soap and water or alcohol-based hand sanitisers. He also advised residents to avoid direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of anyone exhibiting symptoms and warned against spreading unverified rumours or stigmatising individuals being assessed by public health officials. Bagana stressed that living in or travelling to Niger State did not, in itself, constitute exposure to the virus. He advised anyone exhibiting symptoms or suspecting possible exposure to isolate themselves and contact public health authorities through designated emergency hotlines before visiting a medical facility. The state government said the heightened alert was intended to ensure that suspected infections could be identified promptly and referred for appropriate medical assessment, while surveillance and response systems remained on standby.

title: Mbah Backs Tinubu on Fuel Subsidy Removal, Says a Return Inconceivable
body: • Maintains subsidy return will create panic among investors • Insists he has delivered good governance to Enugu Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order. Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu yesterday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors. He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy. “If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued. “We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that. “Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. That would take us back. It is going to create panic in the system. It is going to get investors to pull back. “Those that are coming in today to invest in that sector will become jittery. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said. He said the nation should focus on how to further encourage private capital to flow, noting the growth the nation had experienced in the stock exchange space. He added that Tinubu’s policies had stabilised the macro indicators, thus encouraging foreign direct investment. “You can see quite a lot of funds coming into our country, not just portfolio investments, but also direct investments. It is also going to strengthen because the macro indicators are right,” he stated. Mbah maintained that whereas fuel subsidy removal enables the government to target the less privileged, fuel subsidy as earlier practised benefited the rich more. “By the way, I do not think the subsidy we practised before the President removed it was even the right one for the country because even the people we were looking at benefiting from it were only insignificantly benefiting from it. It was largely beneficial to our wealthy folks. “But now, you can almost notice that the government is doing that in targeting the poor, using proceeds from subsidy removal. The government is aggressive on cash transfers. There is also the programme where the government is targeting 1,000 persons per ward across the entire country to be able to provide seed capital for them to become productive,” he added. Meanwhile, on his stewardship so far, Mbah said his administration had kept faith with the people of Enugu State, delivering good governance across all sectors in line with his campaign manifesto. He said the people of the state only needed to imagine where the state was before his inauguration as governor and where it is currently headed. “Let us imagine the Enugu we knew four years ago. Let us just imagine an Enugu without Hotel Presidential. Let us imagine an Enugu without the International Conference Centre. Let us imagine an Enugu without Enugu Air. Let us imagine Enugu without the transport terminals, the 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres. “You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the International Hospital. You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the CNG buses, the Nigergas. I think the list is endless. “But I even think that we can stretch that imagination further because the work ahead will be more profound. Just imagine an Enugu where our children are receiving education that prepares them for the world because they have been imbued with evolving 21st-century skills. Imagine again an Enugu where you do not have any part of the city with an unpaved road. “Also, imagine an Enugu in four years’ time that generates 660 megawatts of electricity; where we are able to provide 24-hour power supply; where you cannot come into your house and have the light off; and where people can run their businesses for a whole week without worrying about the cost of diesel. “Just imagine an Enugu where you generate electricity and the people of Enugu are buying that at 120 naira because they own the coal that feeds the power plant. “Imagine an Enugu where you now have to ride, not just on our CNG buses, but you have the monorail that can take you from point A to point B. Imagine an Enugu where you can fly from here to the United Kingdom, to the United States and other parts of the world,” he stressed. Mbah urged the people to keep faith with the journey of greatness, growth and development, defending the gains of his first term and guaranteeing the promises of his second term by working for his re-election. “If these imaginations capture our fancy, then we have a duty to fight for it. We do have a duty to continue to make sure that the bar does not come down and that the standard we have set in Enugu is sustained,” he noted.

title: Fertiliser Summit: Experts Proffer Measures to Boost Food Security
body: Agricultural experts, researchers and policymakers have called for greater investment in soil intelligence, digital technology and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations to improve farm productivity and strengthen food security in Nigeria. The call was made at the 2026 Nigeria Fertiliser Summit on Phosphorus and Food Security, held in Abuja, where more than 280 participants from across the agricultural sector examined ways to improve nutrient management and ensure farmers obtain better returns from fertiliser application. The summit was organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, in partnership with the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) and the Fertiliser and Inputs Support Services Department of the federal ministry of agriculture and food security. Speaking at the opening session, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Aliyu Abdullahi, represented by the Director of Agricultural Land and Climate Change Management Services in the ministry, Mr Oshadiya Olanipekun, emphasised the importance of soil data, soil testing and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations in improving farmers’ productivity. He also acknowledged the contribution of the Regional Hub for Fertiliser and Soil Health for West Africa and the Sahel, noting that collaboration with the initiative would enable Nigeria to benefit from regional expertise and technical support for site-specific fertiliser recommendations. Similarly, the Vice Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Prof. A.S. Bamire, said improving agricultural productivity required more than increased fertiliser application, stressing the importance of responsible nutrient management, research, innovation and stronger partnerships. A member of IAR&T and one of the summit organisers, Prof. Vincent Aduramigba-Modupe, said agricultural transformation depended on applying the appropriate nutrients in the right quantities and under suitable conditions. “Improving crop productivity is not only about applying fertilizer. It is about ensuring the right nutrient is applied in the right amount, at the right place, and under the right conditions,” he said. Participants identified soil intelligence as a critical component of efforts to improve fertiliser-use efficiency, highlighting the importance of digital soil maps, soil information systems, laboratory services, site-specific nutrient recommendations and digital advisory tools. A visiting scientist with the Regional Hub and Professor of Soil Science at Bayero University, Kano, Prof. Jibrin Mohammed Jibrin, described soil intelligence as fundamental to achieving food security. “The basis of food production and food security is the soil. You need healthy soil to produce well and feed the nation with nutritious food. To do that, you need soil intelligence,” he said. Presentations by the Regional Hub highlighted ongoing efforts to strengthen evidence-based nutrient management in Nigeria and across West Africa through digital soil mapping, support for national soil information systems, laboratory assessments and the validation of fertiliser recommendations tailored to specific soils and crops. The Hub’s Senior Agronomist, Dr Bello Shehu, said improving phosphorus management required a better understanding of the nutrient needs of different soils and crops. “It is about understanding what different soils and crops need and ensuring that farmers have access to the right products and the right advice,” he said. The summit also underscored the need for stronger coordination among stakeholders to address fragmented approaches to soil health and fertiliser management. Participants noted that although several initiatives were already underway, improved collaboration was necessary to prevent duplication, align priorities and accelerate implementation. They highlighted the roles of technical working groups, the Coalition of the Willing and Nigeria’s National Technical Team, which serves as an interface between the country and the Regional Hub, helping to align national priorities with regional expertise and support. “If we want to achieve our goals, we have to work together. Too many initiatives have been implemented in silos. Real progress will come when stakeholders align, collaborate and follow through on agreed actions,” Jibrin said. The summit further highlighted the Regional Hub’s role as a technical resource and coordination platform supporting fertiliser and soil-health priorities across West Africa and the Sahel. The Hub works with a consortium comprising the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, the International Fertiliser Development Center, OCP Africa, the International Soil Reference and Information Centre, the African Plant Nutrition Institute and Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, alongside national technical teams, country focal points and research institutions across the region. In a goodwill message, the incoming Director of the Regional Hub, Bastiaan Huesken, said the initiative was established to help countries translate scientific evidence into practical solutions for farmers. “The Hub was created to turn soil data into recommendations, and recommendations into products and advice that farmers can use,” he said.

title: Akume: North-south Power Rotation Good for National Unity
body: Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, has urged political stakeholders to respect the North-south power rotation arrangement, saying the principle is essential to Nigeria’s national stability, fairness and democratic consolidation. He made this known yesterday in Abuja when he received a delegation from the Order of the Knights of St. Mulumba (KSM), Nigeria, led by its Supreme Knight, Sir Steve Adehi. Akume said the arrangement, which emerged from consultations among political leaders ahead of the return to civilian rule in 1999, remained an important framework for promoting national cohesion and ensuring equitable distribution of political power between the two regions. The SGF recalled that political leaders, who met in Kaduna in 1999 had agreed that presidential power should alternate between the North and the South in eight-year cycles, beginning with the South, as part of efforts to address concerns about political exclusion and strengthen national unity. He explained that the arrangement was conceived to promote political balance, build mutual trust and safeguard the country’s territorial integrity by ensuring that neither region felt permanently excluded from the nation’s highest political office. Akume insisted that power rotation should not be regarded as a temporary political convenience but as a fundamental political understanding anchored on fairness, mutual respect and national stability. He also expressed concern over attempts by Northern aspirants to contest the presidency before the completion of the South’s current eight-year cycle, insisting that the established sequence should be respected. According to him, following the eight-year administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, the current presidential tenure held by a Southerner should be allowed to run its course in accordance with the principle of alternating power between the two regions. He argued that respecting the arrangement would reinforce confidence in the democratic process and help sustain the understanding among Nigeria’s diverse political and regional interests. Akume further emphasised the need for greater collaboration among the federal, state and local governments to address the country’s economic and social challenges, noting that ongoing reforms and development initiatives should be assessed against both immediate economic realities and long-term national objectives. He commended the Order of the Knights of St. Mulumba for its charitable interventions aimed at improving the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians. Earlier, Adehi said the organisation had undertaken several humanitarian initiatives, including supporting medical treatment for patients, assisting inmates with outstanding financial obligations to facilitate their release from correctional facilities, providing boreholes, renovating schools and supporting hospitals. He explained that the interventions were informed by the recognition that the government alone could not address the numerous social and economic challenges facing the country. He also urged greater collaboration between government and private organisations through philanthropy, partnerships and community-based initiatives to alleviate poverty and improve living conditions Umahi Seeks Support for Tinubu’s Second Term Bid, Cites Infrastructure Drive Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja The Minister of Works, David Umahi, has urged Nigerians to support President Bola Tinubu’s second term bid, arguing that continuity in leadership would sustain the administration’s infrastructure drive and consolidate the gains of its economic reforms. Umahi made the call at a town hall meeting in Kano, ahead of the commissioning of major road projects in the state, including outstanding works on Section I, Lot 1 (Zaria-Kano) of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Expressway, the ministry said in a statement. The minister, who also called for the re-election of Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, said the federal government’s infrastructure investments and difficult economic decisions were laying the foundation for sustainable growth and prosperity. “The worst is over. The darkest part of the morning is the dawn. We are moving into prosperity as a result of the hard decisions occasioned by the reforms,” he said. He identified the removal of petroleum subsidy and other economic policy changes as necessary measures to reposition the Nigerian economy, urging citizens to remain patient as the benefits of the reforms increasingly translated into development projects across the country. Umahi also dismissed the perception that the South-east was opposed to Tinubu’s administration, reaffirming the region’s commitment to national unity and calling for support for the president’s second-term ambition. The minister commended Yusuf for his leadership, particularly his efforts to promote peace, unity and inclusive governance, while praising the state’s environmental sanitation standards. “I am yet to see another state that is beating Kano in cleanliness. In all the streets we passed through, you could pick a pin,” Umahi said. He attributed the level of cleanliness to purposeful leadership and the effective use of public resources, adding that Kano’s example reflected the standard of environmental responsibility and governance Nigerians deserved. Umahi also praised the governor for bringing together political leaders, former governors, prominent indigenes and other stakeholders, describing the gesture as evidence of mutual respect and a commitment to the collective progress of the state. He urged Kano residents to support Yusuf’s second-term bid, arguing that continuity would help sustain the governor’s development initiatives and strengthen the state’s contribution to national progress. The minister further advocated greater representation of engineers in leadership positions, saying their technical expertise, professional training and problem-solving abilities could improve governance and infrastructure delivery. He expressed appreciation for the peaceful atmosphere and unity he witnessed in Kano, noting that the experience had positively influenced his perception of the state and prompted him to reconsider his departure date. Earlier, Yusuf commended the federal government for its infrastructure investments, particularly the road projects expected to improve transportation, connectivity and economic activities in Kano and the wider North-west region. The governor described the scheduled commissioning of outstanding works on the Zaria-Kano section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Expressway as a significant milestone in the country’s infrastructure development. He thanked Tinubu for the interventions and other support extended to Kano State, expressing optimism that the commissioning ceremony would be successful. The Federal Ministry of Works said it remained committed to delivering durable, safe and quality road infrastructure across the country under the federal government’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

title: Tinubu Felicitates Kwankwaso at 70, Says He’s a Friend and Progressive Politician
body: • Hails his contributions to nation, as Obi, NDC vow to rescue Nigeria, celebrate ally Deji Elumoye and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has rejoiced with the vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, on his 70th birthday, describing him as his friend and progressive politician. Tinubu acknowledged the contributions of Kwankwaso, whom he described as an influential figure, in different capacities, as ex-governor of Kano State, and ex-defence minister and former Senator. Tinubu, in a seven-paragraph tribute, stated, “My warm congratulations to my friend, Dr Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, former Governor of Kano State, one-time Minister of Defence and former Senator representing Kano Central Senatorial District, on his 70th birthday on October 21, 2026. “Senator Kwankwaso and I have longstanding association, dating back to our time in the National Assembly in 1992, he in the House of Representatives and I in the Senate, and later in 1999 when we both emerged as governors of our respective states. “As members of the Class of ‘99 Governors, we both played pivotal roles in laying the foundation for the democracy the nation enjoys today. “Shaped by different political choices, our political paths differed until we coalesced in 2013 to form the All Progressives Congress. Since then, history and service have kept us intertwined. “I must acknowledge Senator Kwankwaso’s immense contributions to Kano State and Nigeria as a two-term Governor, former Minister of Defence, former Senator, former presidential candidate, and now a presidential running mate. “Senator Kwankwaso remains an influential figure and a progressive politician. That we are in different political parties and competing on different platforms in the January 2027 election will not remove my affection for Senator Kwankwaso. “As the former governor marks this milestone, I wish him good health, personal fulfilment, and many more years of engagement in the nation’s democratic process.” Obi, NDC Celebrate Kwankwaso, Vow to Rescue Nigeria from APC in 2027 Elections Presidential candidate of NDC, Peter Obi, and the party’s leadership celebrated Kwankwaso on his 70th birthday, describing him as an experienced public servant and a key partner in their quest to transform Nigeria. In a separate birthday tribute, Obi expressed confidence in his partnership with the former Kano State governor, saying their shared commitment to national development could help rescue the country from the consequences of poor governance. NDC also praised Kwankwaso’s record in public service, citing his experience in the legislature, the executive arm of government, and Kano State politics as important assets to the party’s presidential ticket ahead of the 2027 general election. Obi said their relationship had deepened through conversations and a shared determination to build a country that offers opportunities to all Nigerians. He stated, “With the passage of time, I have come to appreciate the bond between us deeply, the many conversations we have shared, and the common commitment to Nigeria that continues to shape our service. “As you mark your 70th birthday on October 21, I honour not only an accomplished public servant but also a very dear elder brother, friend, and partner whose life has been dedicated to serving our people.” Obi said Kwankwaso’s career had taken him through the legislature, the Federal Executive Council, the governorship of Kano State, and other responsibilities in national public life. According to Obi, those experiences represent decades of engagement with the Nigerian people and provide a foundation for continued service to the country. The NDC presidential candidate said, “Turning seventy is not merely a significant milestone; it is a moment to look back with gratitude on a life devoted to service, the wisdom gained through experience, and the opportunities that remain ahead. “As we continue to hope for and work toward a better Nigeria, I remain grateful for our partnership, and for our shared conviction that our nation can become a place where no child is deprived of opportunity, no family is left in poverty, and every Nigerian can live with dignity, security, and hope. “My dear brother, may God bless you with renewed strength, good health, wisdom, and many more productive years. May the years ahead be filled with peace, fulfilment, and the satisfaction of seeing the values we cherish take firmer root across our nation.” In its statement, NDC, through its National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses, congratulated Kwankwaso on behalf of the party’s National Executive Committee, National Working Committee, members, and supporters in Nigeria and the diaspora. The party described the former Kano State governor as a symbol of courage, progressive politics, and people-centred leadership. It said his record in Kano State and his service at the national level had established him as an influential figure in Nigerian politics. “At 70, you remain a towering symbol of courage, selfless service, progressive politics, and people-centered leadership,” the party said. NDC recalled Kwankwaso’s tenure as governor of Kano State, where he promoted the Kwankwasiyya political philosophy, and his service as a senator, minister, and national political leader. It stated that his experience and grassroots support had strengthened the party’s presidential ticket, which pairs him with Obi. “As our vice presidential candidate, you have brought uncommon energy, loyalty, capacity, and grassroots appeal to the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) ticket,” the statement said. The party added that Kwankwaso remained a dependable partner in its campaign to build a new Nigeria that works for all citizens.

title: The Curator: *Spooky* home smells & how to fix them
body:
The Curator independently decides what topics and products we feature. When you purchase an item through our links, we may earn a commission. Promotions and products are subject to availability and retailer terms.
In Canada, every October means Thanksgiving, pumpkins, and the annual closing of the windows, the annual cranking of the heat, and all the smells that we could previously waft outside are now staunchly inside with nowhere to hide. That means mystery, funky smells can start to emerge, and it starts to get a little…spooky. Right in time for Halloween, of course!
And with spooky smells, you can’t just cover them up. These freaky odours can’t be overcome by a vanilla cookie candle or spring mist room spray. The real fix is to find the source and deal with it. Here are five seasonal smells that haunt our homes this time of year, what’s causing each one, and how to get rid of it (dare I say…exercise it?!) for good. Let’s go through these horrors one by one.
When the temperature drops, mice start looking for somewhere warm to snuggle into, and a gap the size of a dime is all they need. The first sign of a settler – besides the scratching sound – is usually the smell: sharp, stale, and ammonia-like, and it hangs around long after the mice are gone. Mouse urine contains urea, which bacteria break down into ammonia, and the musky “mousy” smell comes from a compound that releases slowly over time, which is why it never seems to leave. No one wants that.
Fall walks can leave a dog smelling like a pond by the time you get through the door. Woof! What makes up that wet dog smell? Yeast and bacteria live in its fur and constantly produce smelly compounds. When the fur gets wet, the water knocks those compounds loose and sends them into the air, and the longer your dog stays damp, the longer your couch smells like it (eww!). The fix is to dry the pup fast and fully, right at the door.
You know the leggings. They come out of the wash smelling clean, and the second you sweat, the stink comes back from the dead. That’s called odour rebloom. Odour-causing bacteria grow better on polyester than on cotton, and synthetic fabrics hold on to body oils that a regular wash doesn’t always remove. Your body heat wakes up whatever was left behind. First, don’t toss sweaty gear straight into the hamper; let it air dry fully first.
Bamboo Charcoal Bags Odour Absorber – $5.39
Waterless Nebulizing Essential Oil Diffuser – $99.95
You turn on the bathroom tap and get a whiff of something musty and damp or just…rotten. Gross! Often, it’s not the water. It’s the drain. Soap, toothpaste and hair build up a slimy layer called biofilm on the underside of the sink stopper, inside the drainpipe, and inside that little overflow hole near the top of the sink. Pull the stopper out and scrub it (brace yourself, as this part can be a Nightmare on Elm Street in and of itself), then clean the overflow with a slim bottle brush and hot soapy water.
I always say the car is like a microcosm of the house, which means this is the time the car windows get rolled up, too. This seals in all the moisture, odours and guck that gets stuck in the car during the colder months. What’s in there? Wet boots, gym bags, hockey bags, half-eaten snacks, you know the deal. Moisture plus organic material, like sweat, crumbs, and mud, feeds odour-causing bacteria, and a closed cabin traps all of it. Yummy. Start by removing the source: take the floor mats out to dry, clear out the food and garbage, give the car a good vacuum, and stop storing gear in there (do your best here, gear can make a car so, so stinky).

title: Kremlin Confirms Lukoil Negotiations With Washington
body:
The Kremlin confirmed Wednesday, Oct. 21, that Russia and the US are discussing the future of sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil’s overseas assets, valued at approximately $22 billion, as economic negotiations between Moscow and Washington expand alongside efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov disclosed the talks following Russian President Vladimir Putin’s meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, saying the two governments were considering a broad range of economic projects, including the fate of Lukoil’s international holdings.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The disclosure came as the US Treasury Department extended authorization for negotiations over the sale of Lukoil’s foreign assets until Nov. 21, allowing potential buyers more time to reach agreements that would still require separate US approval.
The developments provide further confirmation that Washington and Moscow are discussing major commercial interests despite American sanctions imposed to restrict Russia’s energy revenues and pressure the Kremlin over its invasion of Ukraine.
Speaking to Russian state television following Putin’s meeting with Witkoff, Ushakov said Moscow and Washington were reviewing numerous economic proposals, including several major projects.
Among them were discussions concerning US sanctions on Lukoil and the potential sale of its international assets.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov separately confirmed that the US Treasury authorization needed for the sale could be extended if necessary, describing the proposed divestment as a commercial matter.
Lukoil placed its international assets on the market after Washington sanctioned the company in October 2025 over Russia’s war against Ukraine.
US private equity firm Carlyle Group agreed in January 2026 to acquire the assets but subsequently abandoned the deal after it failed to secure regulatory approval. Other prospective buyers have included ExxonMobil.
The portfolio, initially valued at approximately $22 billion, includes oil production interests, refineries and fuel distribution businesses across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Central Asia.
The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control extended its authorization for negotiations over Lukoil International GmbH and its subsidiaries until Nov. 21, 2026.
The extension allows prospective buyers to conduct due diligence and negotiate conditional purchase agreements. However, it does not authorize the actual transfer of assets or lift sanctions on Lukoil.
Any completed sale requires separate OFAC approval. The Treasury Department has stipulated that the transaction must sever ties with the sanctioned Russian company, prevent it from receiving immediate financial benefits and keep any proceeds owed to Lukoil blocked until sanctions permit their release.
The Lukoil negotiations emerged as Witkoff publicly acknowledged that the US Treasury Department was working directly with Putin’s economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
During Wednesday’s meeting, Witkoff also discussed future US-Russian economic cooperation, while Putin outlined plans for diesel shipments to the US and offered supplies of Russian fertilizer.
The expanding economic dialogue comes as Russia continues its invasion of Ukraine and Washington seeks to revive trilateral peace negotiations.

title: US, Israel plan renewed Iran strikes after US midterms, focusing on short, intense attacks - report
body: The US and Israeli militaries have drawn up detailed plans for renewed strikes on Iran following the US midterm elections on November 3, The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening, citing American officials familiar with the discussions.According to the report, the plans focus on a short, intensive military operation that could last approximately three days and include strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure, and missile and drone capabilities.The two countries have stepped up joint military exercises, including flights over Iraq to rehearse potential strikes. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also discussed the plans with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during his visit to Israel this week.The US and Israel reportedly came close to launching an attack earlier this month, but US President Donald Trump decided to postpone it at the last minute.According to the report, Trump has not yet approved a new military operation, while diplomatic efforts to reach an agreement with Iran are ongoing.Iranian officials have threatened that any renewed attack would trigger a broader response, including strikes on data centers and undersea communications cables.The large-scale operation that never took placeAccording to a Financial Times report published on Tuesday, Netanyahu had pushed for a large-scale offensive against Iran, with the IDF preparing for a multi-day bombing campaign over the weekend of October 10.The operation did not go ahead because Trump opposed resuming hostilities ahead of the US midterm elections.The FT further reported that the planned operation was intended to target power plants and other civilian infrastructure, along with nuclear facilities and sites associated with the Iranian regime.The strikes were expected to be more intensive than those carried out by Israel and the US at the beginning of their joint military campaign in February.However, The Jerusalem Post learned from IDF sources that the military was not planning to strike Iran on October 10.Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Defense Minister Israel Katz, nor any other government official had told the IDF to prepare to attack in the way that such orders were handed down leading up to the June 2025 and early 2026 conflicts with Iran.In that sense, sources have told the Post that the premise of the Financial Times report – that Trump blocked Israel from an attack on Iran while it was about to carry out – is wrong, because Israel was not about to do that.Sources have speculated that the so-called leak of a “potential attack” on Iran to the FT could have been designed to impact the Israeli election by pushing the idea that Netanyahu claimed he was ready to attack Iran a third time but that Trump then prevented him from doing so.Israeli military preparations continueMeanwhile, Fox News reported on Tuesday that Israeli fighter jets had flown toward Iran over Syria and Iraq during an exercise conducted overnight between Monday and Tuesday.According to Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst, the aircraft were deployed eastward during the exercise.Middle East Eye also reported, citing local sources, that Israeli fighter jets had been spotted over southern Syria and later over Muthanna Governorate in southern Iraq.Trump had already made clear on October 8 that the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections."We are having productive talks with the Islamic Republic of Iran," he said at the time."I want to make it clear to everyone that although Iran is in very bad shape, both economically and militarily, and although the blockade will remain fully in effect, we will not attack Iran at any point before the midterm elections, which will take place in the United States on November 3."Despite the ongoing military preparations, it remains unclear whether the plans will lead to an attack after the elections.According to the reports, while some officials believe renewed strikes could take place in the coming weeks, others believe the military preparations are intended to pressure Tehran during negotiations.Iranian officials have also warned that any further attack would prompt a broader response, including strikes on data centers and undersea communications cables.US warning and disagreements in negotiationsMeanwhile, the Lebanese newspaper Al-Akhbar reported on Tuesday that Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, had conveyed a US warning during a visit to Tehran, demanding that Iran make concessions on its nuclear program or risk a large-scale military attack.The report, based on leaks and unofficial information, specifically raised the possibility of strikes on nuclear facilities at Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran.According to the newspaper, Munir's visit was intended to revive Pakistan's mediation channel between Washington and Tehran.The Lebanese report said significant disagreements remained between the two sides over the order in which issues should be addressed during negotiations.Iran remains unwilling to give up enriched nuclear materialsWhile the US is demanding progress on the nuclear issue as a condition for continuing talks, Iran wants to prioritize ending the war and the blockade, as well as arranging the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The report also stated that Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei had made clear to Munir that Iran's enriched nuclear material would remain on Iranian territory.Alongside the Pakistan-mediated talks, Trump has reiterated that he will not allow Iran to acquire nuclear weapons. However, no public decision has been announced on resuming military strikes.The possibility of a military operation following the US midterm elections remains on the table, alongside ongoing efforts to reach a diplomatic agreement.Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: UK accounts for over half of FDI into Oman, says London Mayor
body:
Muscat: The United Kingdom accounts for more than half of foreign direct investment into Oman, the Lady Mayor of London said. Addressing a banquet in the City of London held in honour of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, she pointed to the strong presence of British and Omani businesses at the event as evidence of the depth of their commercial relationship. “The remarkable number of British and Omani businesses represented here tonight is itself a testament to the strength of our economic ties,” she said. Highlighting opportunities for further cooperation, she said the UK-Oman Sovereign Investment Partnership was helping channel investment in both directions. “The UK-Oman Sovereign Investment Partnership is helping channel investment in both directions,” she said, adding that the opportunities ahead were even greater. The Lady Mayor also highlighted the potential for collaboration in emerging technologies, pointing to the Oman Investment Authority's investments in British university spinouts working in artificial intelligence and robotics through Cambridge Innovation Capital and Oxford Science Enterprises. She described the investments as a way of turning research into commercial opportunities, saying: “It’s turning ideas into industries. Research into discovery. And the ambitions of one generation into opportunities for the next.” She also referred to the landmark free trade agreement between the UK and the Gulf, saying it was “opening doors to new markets and partnerships”.

title: Ukrainian forces reportedly strike Moscow Oblast weapons plant
body:
Ukrainian forces struck a weapons plant in Serpukhov, Moscow Oblast, overnight on Oct. 22, monitoring channels reported.
Eyewitnesses claimed that drones followed by missiles struck the site, known as the 75th Arsenal, according to independent Russian outlet Astra.
The site produces weapons and ammunition for the Russian army and also repairs Russian military equipment, according to the channel.
The facility has been sanctioned by Ukraine, the U.S. , and the EU for its role in Russia's war.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 630 drones headed towards Moscow Oblast, claiming that the majority were intercepted, with 163 destroyed as they approached the city of Moscow.
In the Voronovskoye settlement, which is administratively part of Russia's capital city, two people were injured as a result of the attack, Sobyanin added.
Reports could not be immediately verified by the Kyiv Independent.
Earlier in the night, Ukrainian drones struck the Russian city of Lipetsk , according to monitoring channels.
Multiple explosions were reported in the city, and a residential building was allegedly struck, monitoring channel ExileNova Plus wrote.

title: Atyrau University, UTAS Ibra discuss international cooperation
body:
As part of efforts to strengthen international cooperation and exchange academic expertise in the higher education sector, Dr. Salamat Idrisov, Chairman of the Board and Rector of Khalel Dosmukhamedov Atyrau University in the Republic of Kazakhstan, received Dr. Saud Al-Busaidi, a lecturer at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS) in Ibra, Sultanate of Oman. During the meeting, both sides discussed ways to develop international cooperation in higher education, focusing on several key areas. These include joint research projects, the implementation of scientific research and initiatives serving mutual interests, and the enhancement of partnerships between faculty members at both universities to share successful experiences and expertise. As part of his academic program in Kazakhstan, Dr. Saud al Busaidi is visiting the Faculty of Multilingual Education at Khalel Dosmukhamedov Atyrau University from October 17 to 30. During his visit, he is delivering a series of lectures and training workshops for students and faculty members, highlighting the latest scientific and methodological practices and expertise.
