title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
body:
Protect your projects from malicious packages
The LiteLLM 1.107.0 ⁠ (opens in new tab) release on PyPI carries a credential stealer and a remote code execution backdoor. All seven wheels (Linux, macOS, Windows) install them as three files in site-packages . Both run when any Python process starts on the host, even one that never imports litellm . The upstream GitHub source does not contain them.
LiteLLM confirmed the compromise in its incident report ⁠ (opens in new tab) , which lists remediation steps. PyPI removed the release by 13:23 UTC on 2026-10-21. The Docker images v1.107.0 , latest , main-latest , and main-stable on Docker Hub and GHCR also carried the malicious code between 11:46 and 14:20 UTC.
Versions 1.106.2, 1.107.0rc1, and 1.107.0rc2 are clean. The companion packages that 1.107.0 pins, litellm-proxy-extras==0.4.110 and litellm-enterprise==0.1.78 , are also clean.
Installing litellm==1.107.0 places three files in site-packages . Python loads two of them each time it starts.
The pyproject.toml in the 1.107.0 source distribution (sdist) has one extra line in the maturin build section:
The maturin data = "cook" setting copies a cook/ folder into litellm-1.107.0.data/purelib/ in the wheel. pip installs that folder into site-packages .
The sdist leaves out the cook/ folder, so this line is the only visible change. No public commit in BerriAI/litellm ⁠ (opens in new tab) contains data = "cook" or a cook/ folder.
The wheel RECORD lists the three added files:
LiteLLM’s incident report ⁠ (opens in new tab) says the attacker held the GitHub CLI credentials of three developers. LiteLLM believes the attacker took them from the logs of an internal LiteLLM deployment exposed to the internet. With an organization owner’s token, the attacker bypassed branch protection and pointed the private release workflow at a lookalike repository, Berri-AI/litellm . The attacker then passed the approval gate with a second developer’s credential, and the official pipeline built, signed, and published the artifacts.
At startup, Python runs each line that starts with import in a .pth file in site-packages . cook.pth contains import cook , so the stealer runs in every Python process on the host: the application, pip, IDE language servers, and CI jobs.
cook.py wraps about 61 KB of Python in one layer of exec(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode('...'))) . The decoded code starts with this configuration:
Python imports sitecustomize at startup, so this file also runs in every Python process.
The attacker can point the daemon at a new server by editing domain.txt . Each infected host runs whatever that server returns as codepy .
At 13:40 UTC, the GitHub account letters9813 and its repository returned 404, about two hours after the release. The backdoor now finds no server address and does nothing. Hosts that ran the daemon before the deletion could have received and run second-stage code. SafeDep could not recover the server address.
All times are UTC on 2026-10-21, from LiteLLM’s report unless noted.
LiteLLM’s report lists this digest for berriai/litellm on Docker Hub and ghcr.io/berriai/litellm .

Meta says it’s issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday , the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
“The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant,” Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new class of shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”
Meta has poured billions of dollars into the AI race as it builds ( and promotes ) sprawling data centers, poaches top talent from other companies like OpenAI, and builds AI models capable of rivaling those from other tech giants. The company expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion and $145 billion estimate.
It’s been a busy past few weeks for Meta, which launched its AI agent, Muse , in September. Like other AI agents, Muse can do things like clean out your email inbox, book restaurant reservations, and plan trips. The Muse app shot to the top of app stores shortly after its rollout, and hit 10 million downloads in the US this week. Meta also rolled out its Muse Wonder model this week .
Muse’s launch hasn’t come without some snags. Amid concerns about user privacy , a tech YouTuber reported that the agent gave out his address to a stranger on Facebook Marketplace. The company has also had to pause Muse’s conversation-sharing feature after researchers discovered chats publicly available on the web.

This guide adds EYG scripting to an Erlang application my_counters . Just want the code look at example .
Embedding EYG in Erlang gives you a scripting environment with tight controls over what can be accessed. With this control you can:
EYG's toolkit consists of a set of composable parts, for this guide install the following.
Below is the simplest Erlang module that will run EYG code.
Start an Erlang shell, with this module loaded, and run your first scripts.
This is everything needed to run any self-contained, pure EYG program. We will add two affordances that make it easier to work with.
First we will pretty print the errors. Each EYG package has its own pretty printing functions. The code below will handle formatting parser errors as well as runtime values and errors. The return value from this function is now a binary that can be presented to the user.
All the examples in this guide we are running from the erlang shell so it's convenient for our run function to accept charlists as well as binaries.
Now a runtime errors prints useful output.
EYG programs in this first runner cannot perform any side effect. This is already good enough for a configuration script but for anything more we need to add effects. Running a simple hello world currently fails.
Any error interpreting an EYG program returns the reason for the break and the full program state. An unhandled effect is one type of break.
For an explanation of what an algebraic effect is check out this post
When execution stops at an unhandled effect, the Erlang host can implement it and resume the EYG program with the reply value. We update the run function so the initial result from executing the expression is passed to a loop function that will keep running the program for every break that can be handled.
The implementation of loop matches on an unhandled_effect . If the extrinsic implementation of the effect succeeds the loop recurses.
Effects can be implemented at any level of abstraction. They can be core utilities like logging or more specific to the application. The counter example has additional utilities Random and Now as well as three effects for managing the counter application.
Before running an EYG we can check that it has no runtime errors. The type inferences is sound, any program that passes type checking has no runtime errors. An effect context is passed to type checking ensuring that a program has no errors including trying to call effects that are unavailable.
In this type checking loop we start with a pure context and extend it with just the the Log effect.
Replace the successful parse branch in run/1 with the following. If type checking succeeds, run the program; otherwise, return the formatted diagnostics.
You now have an EYG scripting environment that checks programs before running them and has the full power of Erlang available for implementing effects. To expose more of your application, add effect handlers and their corresponding types to the inference context.

title: Poland reportedly suspends major arms shipment to Ukraine over regional tribute to Ukrainian Insurgent Army, whose fighters took part in WWII massacres of Poles
body: Poland has suspended delivery of a large weapons package to Ukraine over the Lviv Regional Council’s decision to declare 2027 the year of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army ( UPA ), a source told the news outlet RBC Ukraine. Lviv Regional Council members voted at an October 20 plenary session to declare 2027 the year of the UPA, its commander Roman Shukhevych, and Ukrainian political figure Oleh Olzhych. The source told RBC Ukraine that the Lviv regional authorities had “managed” to hold the vote just as Poland was preparing to send Ukraine a large military aid package. “Their irresponsible actions have now put delivery of this package on hold. Intensive efforts are underway through back channels to resolve a problem that was created out of nothing,” the source said. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the Lviv Regional Council’s decision “unwise” and said it “harms Ukraine itself.” Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called the decision unacceptable, saying it “deepens divisions” between the two peoples. “The Ukrainian authorities must distance themselves from this position,” he said. Polish Deputy Foreign Minister Marcin Bosacki said Ukraine had assured Poland that the Lviv Regional Council’s decision would not take effect. He said the resolution had disappeared from the council’s website after Poland intervened. The Lviv Regional Council’s Facebook post announcing the year of the UPA is now unavailable . Issues surrounding the Ukrainian Insurgent Army regularly strain relations between Poland and Ukraine. The most recent such dispute arose in the spring of 2026, when Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree awarding the honorary title “Heroes of the UPA” to the Separate Special Operations Center North, part of the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ Special Operations Forces. The decision drew sharp criticism in Poland because UPA fighters took part in the Volhynia massacres of 1943–1944, in which an estimated 30,000 to 60,000 Poles and 20,000 to 30,000 Ukrainians were killed. After Poland condemned the decision, Zelensky promised to open the archives on the Volhynia massacres. title: NYC high school faces backlash over ‘intifada’ post
body: INTIFADA FLARE UP: One of New York City’s most prestigious public high schools is facing backlash because a school-based socialist youth group co-signed a social media post declaring “Intifada Until Victory!” The Young Democratic Socialists of America chapter of Stuyvesant High School — along with YDSA chapters at Hunter College, the New School, City College and Lehman College — all signed onto an Oct. 8 Instagram post that accused the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter of silencing student activists who wanted to protest Mayor Zohran Mamdani over Israel. The groups accused the democratic socialist mayor of betraying the Palestinian cause and blasted his decision to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch in her position, referring to her as a “Zionist billionaire.” The term intifada — which refers to violent uprisings against Jews in Israel — is viewed by many Jews as a call to violence against them. Moshe Spern, president of United Jewish Teachers — an advocacy group representing Jewish teachers and students across the city — is demanding the posts be removed immediately and that the YDSA group provide a public apology to the school community. “NYC public schools have seen hundreds of antisemitic and anti-Israel incidents since October 7, 2023,” he wrote in an email yesterday to Stuyvesant Principal Seung Yu and New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels. “When a school-recognized club amplifies this rhetoric, it risks contributing to a hostile environment.” In the missive, Spern invoked Title VI — the federal law that bans discrimination based on race, shared ancestry and national origin — and demanded a review of the YDSA chapter’s charter, faculty adviser and recent activities for compliance. Spern also cited a chancellor’s regulation that states that student clubs operate under the principal’s supervision and must remain consistent with the school’s educational goals. Yu did not respond to requests for comment. Mamdani’s Department of Education also did not respond to Playbook. Spern told Playbook today that he has yet to receive a response from Yu. “To flat out ignore it is extremely irresponsible,” he said. The NYC-DSA defended the organization. “We support the right to organize,” NYC-DSA co-Chair Gustavo Gordillo said in a statement. “NYC-DSA did not organize or endorse this particular rally, but red scare tactics have never been effective tools for engaging with student movements.” The social media uproar is the latest flashpoint in ongoing tensions in the city over Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the war that followed. Mamdani, a longtime critic of Israel, was reluctant to condemn the term “globalize the intifada” on the campaign trail last year before finally saying he will not use the term . He also drew bipartisan backlash over his statement marking the third anniversary of the attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu labeled the mayor an antisemite , which Mamdani has denied. Mamdani, though, has also simultaneously faced backlash from pro-Palestinian activists who accused him of betraying the Palestinian cause by retaining Tisch, who’s Jewish and a self-described Zionist. Those critics have also criticized him for not doing enough to prevent local synagogues from holding events that promote land sales in Israel, some of them in the occupied West Bank. — Madina Touré From the Capitol Q’S LATEST: Gov. Kathy Hochul has a 55-41 lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, a Quinnipiac University poll released this afternoon found. That 14-point advantage is narrower than the 19-point lead Quinnipiac gave Hochul last month. But it’s more in line with the numbers from other pollsters: Marist found Hochul up by 11 two weeks ago, Emerson had Hochul up 12 in early October, and Siena measured her lead at 9 points last month. Despite Hochul’s lead, the Q Poll concluded Blakeman has an enthusiasm advantage. A total of 65% of his backers were “very enthusiastic” to support him, while only 33% of Hochul’s supporters said the same. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL LANDER DETAINED: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained today by Israeli security officials while harvesting olives in the West Bank. Lander, a self-described liberal Zionist and critic of Israel , said he went to the West Bank as part of the “Protect the Harvest” coalition to support Palestinians gathering crops. Rabbi Jill Jacobs, CEO of T’ruah, a progressive rabbinical organization, said she was also detained Wednesday, along with “approximately 80 American, Israeli, and international volunteers providing a protective presence for Palestinian farmers.” According to a press release from T’ruah, there were “approximately two hours of peaceful harvesting” until “Israeli forces declared the area a closed military zone” and detained them to transport them to a police station, despite the volunteers agreeing to leave. An Israeli military official told POLITICO that officers from the Israel Defense Forces and Border Police, along with local police, arrived at the scene because Palestinians did not submit a request to coordinate harvesting in that area, which is required ahead of time. The official added that the farm in question “requires only a small number of harvesters to collect its produce” and “the security establishment views the arrival of dozens of activists as an act intended solely to provoke, which undermines the harvesting process.” Lander was released “once the matter was brought to our attention” that he is a congressional candidate, the official said. Lander confirmed in a social media post that he was released with a “warning” because of his “public profile.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO . IN OTHER NEWS — MUSK: Elon Musk has spent more than $500,000 to support Rep. Mike Lawler’s reelection bid against Democratic challenger Cait Conley. ( Gothamist ) — STOP: New York City deployed 600 red light cameras to intersections, the maximum number allowed under state law. ( New York Daily News ) — MEASLES: In the wake of a measles crisis, the state Health Department remains locked in a court battle with Amish schools over religious vaccine exemptions. title: OCIUS’ New Bluebottle Hybrid USV Demonstrates Capability at Maritime Big Play Pacific
body: Two diesel-hybrid variants of Ocius’ renewably powered Bluebottle Uncrewed Surface Vessel (USV), ‘Bluebottle Hybrid’, are participating in the US Navy-led Maritime Big Play Pacific exercise, which runs throughout October. Ocius press release The exercise will mark the first time the Bluebottle Hybrid has participated in a Navy exercise anywhere in the world. The vessels will carry ThayerMahan Outpost® acoustic intelligence payloads with TransparenSea® processing software, enabling the detection and tracking of undersea threats as part of an integrated suite of maritime capabilities. Maritime Big Play is an AUKUS Pillar II exercise and experimentation series bringing together Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States to accelerate the operational use of autonomous and uncrewed systems in the maritime domain. The exercise uses realistic operational scenarios spanning anti-submarine warfare, maritime strike and seabed operations, allowing defence, science and industry teams to test emerging technologies in operationally relevant conditions. default The Bluebottle Hybrid variant supplements the platform’s renewable energy sources with a diesel generator, providing additional power when required. This enables persistent operations in low-light environments, including high-latitude winters, while also supporting payloads with higher power demands. Ocius’ renewably powered Bluebottles are currently in operation with the Royal Australian Navy, Royal New Zealand Navy and in the US via Ocius partner ThayerMahan. Under the Royal Australian Navy’s SEA1200 program, Ocius selected the ThayerMahan Outpost® acoustic intelligence payload with TransparenSea® processing software to integrate with the Bluebottle USV to support undersea intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance/anti-submarine warfare capabilities. In the United States, Ocius Bluebottles are integrated with ThayerMahan sonar systems and operate as Outpost® systems. Previous participation by the renewably powered Bluebottle in US Navy exercises has focused on submarine detection, demonstrating the platform’s endurance and resilience in demanding operating environments including through two hurricanes. Quotes attributable to Robert Dane, Chief Executive Officer of Ocius Technology: “Bluebottle Hybrid’s participation in Maritime Big Play Pacific 2026 is another demonstration of the increasingly important role autonomous and uncrewed systems are playing in the maritime capabilities of AUKUS nations. “We are proud to showcase the Bluebottle Hybrid for the first time and demonstrate the flexibility of the platform in environments where additional power is required, including northern hemisphere operations and missions involving higher-power payloads. “Maritime Big Play Pacific also gives us the opportunity to demonstrate Bluebottle operating as part of an integrated suite of tri-nation capabilities in realistic operational conditions.” – End – The post OCIUS’ New Bluebottle Hybrid USV Demonstrates Capability at Maritime Big Play Pacific appeared first on Naval News .

title: Some KC-135s Damaged by Iran Still in Depot: AFMC Boss
body: At least two KC-135 Stratotankers that were seriously damaged during Operation Epic Fury are still undergoing extensive maintenance depot repairs, the head of Air Force Materiel Command said Oct. 21. Six of the Air Force’s six-decade-old refueling tankers received varying degrees of damage in the opening weeks of the war against Iran. One KC-135 was involved in a collision with another Stratotanker over western Iraq on March 12 and lost part of its tail. The other tanker in that collision was completely destroyed, killing all six Airmen aboard. Another five KC-135s were hit during an Iranian missile strike on Prince Sultan Air Base , Saudi Arabia. During an event with the Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies, AFMC boss Lt. Gen. Linda Hurry said her command sent an aircraft battle damage repair team to the Middle East to make temporary repairs to some KC-135s and “get them back into the fight,” Hurry said. Others were patched up enough to fly back to depots in the U.S., she said. She did not specify how many planes fell into each category. Photographs emerged online showing one KC-135 flying with a transplanted tail, and others landing in the United Kingdom with patches covering the fragmentation damage that peppered their skins. At least two Stratotankers “received much more significant damage” and are still in depot, Hurry said. She applauded the work the repair team did on these planes to get them airworthy enough to get back to the U.S. “One had many, many, many holes in the side,” Hurry said. The repair team was “able to patch it up and get the authority to have it [make] a one-time flight back to the depot. It was just phenomenal that they were able to actually save that aircraft. Now they’re rebuilding it.” Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach told lawmakers in June that all of those salvageable KC-135s would eventually return to service, although the most heavily damaged could take a year or two to be completely fixed. Tinker Air Force Base, Okla., serves as the main KC-135 depot. Depot Hiring In addition to Tinker, the Air Force has depots at Warner-Robins Air Force Base, Ga., and Hill Air Force Base, Utah. Officials have called them “national treasures” for their work in repairing critical assets, but there have been concerns about manning and funding for years now. AFMC as a whole is seeing widespread manpower shortages, Hurry said, with about 8,200 billets—including maintainers, engineers and contracting professionals—currently vacant. The Air Force Sustainment Center, which is part of AFMC and oversees those depots, specifically has a shortage of 2,600 billets, she said. In response, AFMC is looking to hire depot artisans—the most highly-skilled civilian mechanics, technicians, and engineers—and other maintainers to keep the depots fully staffed, Hurry said. The command is trying to do more targeted and streamlined hiring to fill the gaps, including by hosting hiring events where they can extend temporary job offers “right there on the spot,” and getting new hires on the job faster, she said. AFMC is also looking at offering retention benefits and targeted incentives to hold on to vital employees with critical skill sets, “to make sure we’ve got the right artisans to care for some of these airframes that are older than probably most of us on the line,” Hurry said. But sometimes, Hurry said, the Air Force doesn’t have to wait for a plane to get to one of its three main depots to do some of that necessary work. Airmen have proposed ideas for “a speed line” to push maintainers forward to the field and get the work done on-site, she said. That would not just help keep planes flying, Hurry said, but also could help with morale and retention. “They can see what they’re doing would have a direct impact to [U.S. Central Command] operations or operations around the globe,” Hurry said. “It really, really makes a difference. The sense of pride, the sense of purpose, the sense of commitment to our mission has really helped some of our retention.” When a plane like a KC-135 goes through the depot process, Hurry said, maintainers routinely tear it “down to its ribs to build it back up again, to send it back out to the fight.” “It is amazing how far we break down the aircraft to build it back up again as part of the routine depot maintenance cycle,” Hurry said. The post Some KC-135s Damaged by Iran Still in Depot: AFMC Boss appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Zelensky Confirms Trilateral Talks With US, Russia Could Take Place by Early November
body:
Russia has signaled support for trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the US, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday, Oct 21, confirming that the meeting could take place no later than early November.
Kyiv received the message from Washington after senior US envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg earlier in the day, Ukrinform reported. The Ukrainian, American and Russian teams will continue communications to prepare the agenda further, although the exact date has not been set yet.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The American side proposes to do this [organize the meeting] as soon as possible. We support that,” Zelensky said, adding that ending the war remains in focus.
Zelensky told reporters that the Ukrainian delegation would support proposals for a ceasefire, an energy truce and humanitarian initiatives, including the return of prisoners of war (POWs).
According to Ukrinform, the president had also expressed hope that Russia would honor its commitments to the trilateral format.
Although Moscow has signaled openness to the discussions, it showed very little willingness for a partial truce. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov earlier said Putin was not considering an energy ceasefire .
“Russia needs peace, not a ceasefire,” he said, rebuking US President Donald Trump’s recent announcement of an energy truce between the Kremlin and Moscow.
Following the talks, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said that Putin had told Witkoff Russia was “in principle, ready to resume” trilateral negotiations around mid-November, with a focus on postwar security arrangements.
The proposed trilateral meeting – including Ukraine – appears to be separate from a possible meeting between Trump, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of next month’s APEC summit in Shenzhen, which Ushakov said Beijing was already preparing.
Speaking ahead of the meeting with Witkoff in Oslo, Norway, Zelensky said the three leaders were free to meet. However, any talks about Ukraine’s future could only be discussed with Kyiv present “at the table of negotiations.”
On Tuesday, Oct. 20 Trump said that he was willing to meet Putin and Xi in China next month, possibly without Zelensky. He suggested Ukraine should have someone else negotiate on its behalf.
The renewed push toward peace talks comes as diplomatic ties between Kyiv and Washington appear to be recovering from more than a week of escalating tensions.
Trump’s rhetoric, however, has continued to cast doubt on that recovery. Speaking in the Oval Office on Oct. 20, as the Oslo talks were underway, he claimed that Russian forces “just keep marching forward” in Ukraine and that the US had given Kyiv $350 billion while getting nothing back, other than grief and high diesel.
Kyiv Post found both claims to be false .
The rift began on Oct. 9, when Trump announced an abrupt, controversial diesel deal with Putin while a Ukrainian delegation was holding peace negotiations with Trump’s administration in Miami.
In the days that followed, Ukraine faced unannounced restrictions on Starlink terminals and a week-long pause in US intelligence sharing .
Trump also called for Ukraine to elect a new president, prompting Zelensky to respond that only Ukrainian citizens could decide on his removal.
For the occasion, Kyiv proposed a 60-day ceasefire, but Moscow rejected the proposal, offering only a one-day truce on the day of the elections itself.
Trump also announced an immediate energy ceasefire on Oct. 11 , claiming both sides had agreed to it – although neither formally did. While Ukraine abided by the truce, Peskov claimed Trump’s energy truce was never defined, so Russia cannot be accused of breaking it .
Following discussions in Oslo on Oct. 20, Zelensky confirmed US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has resumed , adding that Kyiv could see results within the next 48 hours on Patriot interceptors and Starlink restrictions.
The latest round of diplomacy builds on Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner’s previous visits to Moscow and Kyiv on Sept. 5-6, where they held three hours of discussions with Putin followed by an informal dinner, before heading to Ukraine for the first time during their tenure.
Although all three sides described the negotiations as substantive and positive, no breakthrough was reached.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Sisi says Egypt would defend Saudi territory but rules out attack on Houthis in Yemen
body: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said Egypt's military support for Saudi Arabia would be limited to defending the kingdom's territory and borders and would not include an attack on Yemen, the presidency said on Wednesday, as the Iran-backed Houthis intensify attacks on the kingdom.Sisi's comments came as Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh, Saudi state news agency SPA said. Abdelatty delivered a written message from Sisi to King Salman, and the two sides discussed bilateral ties and regional developments, SPA said.Any Egyptian military backing for Saudi Arabia could mark a significant escalation in the broader Middle East conflict, which has threatened global energy supplies and pushed oil prices higher since the US and Israel struck Iran in February.Egypt would also defend the territory of any other Arab country if asked, Sisi said, but its military effort would not extend beyond Egyptian territory or that of an Arab state whose security and stability Cairo was seeking to protect.On Monday, Egypt's parliament delayed until October 26 a vote on authorizing the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, lawmakers said.Saudi-Houthi conflict escalates over recent weeksFighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa and much of the north, has escalated in recent weeks.Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, including the United Arab Emirates, provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central bank deposits and investments after the 2013 military overthrow of Islamist President Mohamed Mursi. Sisi became president a year later.Egypt, a regional military power, previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 in support of the government against the Houthis, though it played a limited combat role in the civil war.

title: The only candidate from Russia’s Komi region to call for peace in last month’s parliamentary elections has been detained on suspicion of ‘justifying terrorism’
body: Oleg Mikhailov was detained in Moscow on suspicion of “justifying terrorism,” the Telegram channel Novaya Respublika and the BNK news agency reported. The regional branch of Russia’s Communist Party confirmed his detention to BNK. Novaya Respublika reported that Mikhailov was charged with “justifying terrorism” over a 2024 post about sociologist Boris Kagarlitsky, who was sentenced that year to five years in a penal colony, also for “justifying terrorism.” Mikhailov is being held in a temporary detention facility. A court will decide on October 22 whether to keep him in custody or impose other restrictions pending trial. The provision he is accused of violating, Part 2 of Article 205.2 of Russia’s Criminal Code, carries a fine or five to seven years in prison, according to Novaya Respublika. Oleg Mikhailov heads the Communist Party’s regional branch in Komi and is a former member of the republic’s State Council. In September 2021, he won a State Duma seat in a single-member district. After Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the European Union, Canada, New Zealand, the United States, and Ukraine imposed sanctions on him. The United States sanctioned him over the passage of a law against “fake news” about the military, even though he had not voted for it. In the 2026 State Duma election, Mikhailov finished second in the Syktyvkar single-member district, losing to a candidate who had fought in the war. During the campaign, Mikhailov was the only candidate from Komi to call for peace. A month and a half before the vote, there was an attempt to remove him from the ballot. title: Air Force starting to game out sustainment framework for CCA drones
body: Air Force officials are in the early stages of developing a sustainment plan for Collaborative Combat Aircraft so that the enterprise is ready when the next-generation drones are fielded, according to the head of Air Force Materiel Command. The service plans to field 500 CCA platforms by 2032, and expects the robotic fighter jets to fly alongside its manned fifth- and sixth-generation planes and add capacity to the fleet. Anduril and General Atomics have been tapped to produce the first increment of systems for the program, and Shield AI and RTX subsidiary Collins Aerospace were selected to provide mission autonomy capabilities for the initiative. Once the unmanned systems are fielded, the Air Force will need its maintenance enterprise to help keep them flying and ready for combat. “Honestly, we’re just starting to develop the sustainment framework for the CCAs,” Lt. Gen. Linda Hurry, commander of Air Force Materiel Command, said Wednesday during a Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies event. “The good news is we’re starting very early, and we’re going to connect with the sustainment center, with our supply chain professionals, and the providers of our aircraft right now to make sure that we have a good, solid understanding of what our [Life Cycle Sustainment Plan] might look like, the whole collective sustainment plan. It is not fully fleshed out at this point, but like I said, the good news is we’re starting early to make sure that we understand where we’re going so that we can establish the right supply chain, the right second- and third-order tier suppliers to make sure they’re all lined up, so that if the Air Force chooses to buy a certain number of aircraft, we can be ready when that time comes,” Hurry said. Meanwhile, the Air Force’s sustainment enterprise is facing challenges and shortages as it tries to boost the readiness of the service’s existing aircraft. “One of the things that we’re really focused on right now is hiring our depot artisans and our maintainers there. Right now, our sustainment center is about 2,600 billets short, but we’re hyper focused not only at the depot but throughout AFMC on our hiring activities,” Hurry said. “Holistically, AFMC’s got about 8,200 vacant billets right now. That’s maintainers, that’s engineers, that’s contracting professionals, you name it. And so, what we’re trying to do is do more targeted hiring activities and streamlined hiring activities.” The service is also facing a $14 billion “hole” when it comes to spare parts, she noted. “One, we have got to get money for spares, and then two, we’ve got to get those spares on our shelves and then out to where our mechanics actually need” them, Hurry said. “Getting the right parts is critical, and it’s a direct correlation to your readiness. If we don’t have the parts, we don’t have ready aircraft [and] we don’t have the readiness our nation needs.” The Air Force is tapping into new technology like AI and quantum capabilities to boost its sustainment enterprise, according to Hurry. “In the past, we have been grossly inadequate … in our ability to forecast. Well, we’ve got quantum computing capabilities, and if we do quantum optimization, we can actually figure out the best parts by repair for our entire supply chain, and we’re using that right now to make sure that we’re getting after the right parts for the right aircraft, and we can ingest or increase readiness as much as we possibly can, all through quantum computing,” she said. Hurry noted that the service also has a system called Predictive Analytics and Decision Assistant, or PANDA. The AI tool is geared toward predictive maintenance. The tech is part of the Air Force’s “Condition Based Maintenance Plus” initiative. “If we can actually put this into a system and predict where the next failure is going to be, and then link it with the supply chain so that the parts are actually available, we can optimize those precious hours of our maintainers,” Hurry said. “We know our aircraft are getting older, but if we can use the PANDA system — and we are in fact using it — we can predict … when do we have to take a jet down, and we can actually control our own destiny a little bit.” The post Air Force starting to game out sustainment framework for CCA drones appeared first on DefenseScoop .

title: Bigger Than a Cessna, Smaller Than a C-130: Air Force Funds Blended-Wing Body Concept
body: As the Air Force wrestles to solve the logistics of dispersed operations in the vast Indo-Pacific, it’s investing $3.5 million to help develop a new kind of aircraft: a blended-wing body freighter that’s smaller than a C-130 but larger than a Cessna for “sub-tactical” lift. The startup firm behind the new aircraft, Natilus, thinks it could answer questions the Air Force faces about fuel, cargo space, and range to make its Agile Combat Employment concept work, an executive told Air & Space Forces Magazine. The Pentagon’s Operational Energy-Innovation Directorate and the office of the Air Force’s assistant secretary for energy, installations, and environment funded the $3.5 million contract with Natilus, which will go toward development of the firm’s KONA aircraft, including “full-scale flight testing” starting in late 2027 or early 2028, Chief Operating Officer Nolan Giblin told Air & Space Forces Magazine in an interview. There is also a demonstration planned during a joint force exercise, likely in the Pacific. Blended-wing body aircraft are halfway between the traditional tube-and-wing and the flying wing designs, with the wings and fuselage blending together to help create lift. Its shape makes it more aerodynamic and fuel efficient, while increasing the size of the cabin in the fuselage. “When you couple the aerodynamic efficiency of about 30 percent reduction in fuel with the added volumetric capacity, it really boils down to moving more for less,” said Giblin. In 2023, the Air Force launched a BWB demonstrator/prototype program with startup JetZero, who is partnering with Northrop Grumman. That aircraft, dubbed Z4, is expected to fly in 2027. But while the Z4 is a large aircraft on par with a KC-46 or C-17, KONA is far more modest and meant for an entirely different use, Giblin said. JetZero has pitched the Z4 as a potential future aerial refueler for the Air Force, with a wingspan approaching 185 feet and a maximum operating weight of 362,000 pounds; Giblin said KONA is focused on smaller airlift and has a wingspan of 85 feet and a max takeoff weight of 19,000 pounds. Still, the Air Force’s support for the Z4—the service has invested about $235 million in the project—encouraged Natilus that there are “tailwinds” for BWB aircraft in the Pentagon, Giblin said. Originally, Natilus developed KONA for “short-haul cargo operations and e-commerce,” according to its website. Companies like FedEx, DHL, and Amazon rely on massive “hub-and-spoke” networks , and a small BWB aircraft could move loads to smaller spokes more efficiently compared to a larger, tube-and-wing airframe. Besides being more fuel efficient, a BWB aircraft’s shape provides more total volume in the cabin, Giblin noted. “Today’s tube-and-wing aircraft that they’re flying at the spoke-level of the hub and spoke are [maxing] out on volume before they top out on weight, and so they’re literally leaving revenue on the ground every time they take off. And so there’s an interest for a more volume-centric platform” Giblin said of commercial firms. The Air Force is looking to build its own hub-and-spoke model—agile combat employment calls for dispersing small teams of Airmen and aircraft from large hubs to remote or austere airfields to make it harder for adversaries to target them. Ensuring those forces can move efficiently and are supplied at their new locations, however, is no small feat. That’s especially true in the Pacific, where the distances are vast and mostly covered by water. The Air Force has about 270 C-130 tactical airlifters, which can haul 40,000 pounds of cargo, but service officials have shown an interest in more flexible solutions. That’s led industry to develop an onslaught of small cargo drones —some are Cessna 208s modified to fly autonomously, others are clean-sheet designs. They range in payload capacity from 500 pounds to a few thousand. KONA is at the high end of that range, capable of carrying payloads up to a little more than 8,000 pounds with a range of 800 nautical miles. Its capacity in particular is greater than the modified Cessnas other firms are working on, filling what Giblin described as a “capability gap” between the light utility aircraft and the C-130. Like the smaller Cessnas, though, KONA will be “optionally manned.” For commercial operations and inside the U.S. under the FAA’s jurisdiction, Giblin said, a human pilot will likely fly. But for the Air Force, autonomy is a key attribute, especially when flying in contested airspace. “We do have our own homegrown [autonomy] software stack. However, we also have optionality to partner with folks that are already looking at this in a serious way,” Giblin said. “ … And so, we have a couple different paths towards achieving autonomous flight.” Natilus is already building its demonstrator—the Air Force contract will accelerate that production. Giblin said the “vertical tails, flight control surfaces are already built, the cargo loading system was delivered by Raytheon a couple weeks ago, we just put on order used PT6 engines.” Still to come are the wing shipset and the fuselage. The post Bigger Than a Cessna, Smaller Than a C-130: Air Force Funds Blended-Wing Body Concept appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
